jobs.title: Flight Software Engineer 1
jobs.description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

SPACE SYSTEMS

At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets — we're building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, and more.

Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. The team has built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help them get to space — our world class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions. 

FLIGHT SOFTWARE ENGINEER I

We are currently seeking a Flight Software Engineer I for our team based out of our Littleton, CO site. In this role, you will play a key role in supporting the development of flight software for our Space Systems programs. You’ll spend your days participating in all aspects of software design and development, from requirements definition through coding and testing. And when we say test, we mean your software will be on orbit within weeks and months, not years. Thanks to having our own rockets and launch sites, we have frequent opportunities to test and operate our software on orbit. To be successful in this role, you must want to see your software make a big impact on the way we explore space and use it as a platform for discovery and innovation. Join a driven team of pioneers relentlessly tackling challenging projects, delivering on the impossible, and making an impact on the future of space!

WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO: 

• Develop application software to run within a Real Time Operating System (RTOS) and/or embedded Linux

• Develop hardware drivers to interface to Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs), Star Trackers, Reaction Wheels and other spacecraft sensors and actuators

• Develop and maintain comprehensive unit tests to run within a Continuous Integration framework

• Collaborate with hardware-in-the-loop test engineers to verify and validate combined software and hardware functionality

• Collaborate with systems engineers and embedded systems engineers in developing, documenting and validating requirements

• Participate in review of source code changes and ensure all changes meet company coding standards

• Participate in design reviews such as a PDR and CDR

• Assist with on-orbit (and interplanetary!) flight operations

 YOU'LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor's degree in aerospace engineering, computer science, electrical engineering, or equivalent technical degree

• Experience in embedded software development

• Proficiency in C and C++ languages 

• Experience with Real Time Operating Systems (RTOS) or with Embedded Linux

• Active Secret security clearance OR ability to obtain and maintain one

• U.S. citizenship is required, due to program requirements

THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE:

• Active TS/SCI security clearance

• Experience with Rust language

• Advanced Degree

• Experience developing software and drivers with CAN/CAN-FD and/or UDP/TCP within an embedded system

• Experience developing software for autonomous vehicles operating in harsh environments, such as satellites or autonomous vehicles

This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas.
Anticipated annual equity grant value is designed around function, level, experience, and other factors; realized value depends on vesting and stock-price performance.

Join one of the world's fastest-growing space companies and own a piece of it. In addition to competitive base pay, you'll receive company stock as part of your total compensation package, giving you a direct stake in our success. As we expand to new launch sites, groundbreaking missions, and global markets, your ownership has the opportunity to grow alongside the company.

Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans, dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, 401(k) retirement plan with company match, and other discounts and perks.

The expected salary range for the position is displayed in accordance with the Colorado Equal Pay for Equal Work Act. Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Total Compensation (base and equity)

locations: New York, NY; San Francisco, CA
jobs.description:
At Scale, our mission is to develop reliable AI systems for the world's most important decisions. Our products provide the high-quality data and full-stack technologies that power the world's leading models, and help enterprises and governments build, deploy, and oversee AI applications that deliver real impact. We work closely with industry leaders like Meta, Ernst & Young, Mayo Clinic, Time Inc., the Government of Qatar, and U.S. government agencies including the Army and Air Force.

Scale's Machine Learning Research team builds the foundation for the next generation of AI systems — pushing the boundaries of what's possible with frontier models while ensuring safety, reliability, and alignment at every step. Our work spans generative AI, reinforcement learning and advanced post-training methods, scalable oversight, synthetic data pipelines, red teaming, and evaluation science.

We are developing a large-scale hybrid human-machine system to power machine learning pipelines for dozens of industry-leading customers. These models and systems form the backbone of Scale's long-term strategy, enabling billions of tasks monthly and supporting some of the most complex and advanced use cases in the AI ecosystem.

As an intern, you'll work on a combination of deeply technical ML applications in production and cutting-edge research problems, with mentorship from world-class researchers and the opportunity to collaborate with leading teams across industry and academia. Interns own real, published or shipped work — not side projects.

Example Projects

• Measure the dangerous capabilities of frontier models and conduct preparedness research

• Research the science and creation of new benchmarks for frontier models

• Develop new methods for training models to excel on extremely difficult reasoning problems that require long chains of thought

• Research reinforcement learning and post-training methods that improve model reliability on high-stakes tasks

• Research scalable oversight protocols that enable humans to produce and quality control reasoning chains beyond their native capabilities

• Study the boundaries of model generalization and capabilities to inform data-driven advancements

• Research synthetic and hybrid data with humans in the loop to scale up high-quality data generation

• Take models currently in production, identify areas for improvement, improve them using retraining and hyperparameter searches, then deploy without regressing on core model characteristics

• Create post-training or agentic solutions that integrate into our ability to deliver applications for enterprise and public sector clients

Required to Have

• Currently enrolled in a BS, MS or PhD program with a focus on Machine Learning, Deep Learning, or Natural Language Processing, with a graduation date in Fall 2027 or Spring 2028

• Available for a Summer 2027 internship (May/June start dates) in San Francisco Or New York.

• Prior research experience or a track record of publications on LLMs, NLP, multimodal models, agents, safety, evaluation, alignment, or a related field

• Experience with one or more general purpose programming languages, including Python, Javascript, or similar

Ideally You'd Have

• A previous internship in Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Natural Language Processing, Adversarial Robustness, Alignment, Evaluation, or Agents

• Experience as a researcher — through internships, full-time roles, or at a lab

• Publications at top-tier venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, ACL, EMNLP or AAAI, or contributions to open source projects

• Hands-on experience with reinforcement learning, agentic systems, or evaluation infrastructure

How We Work

Our credos shape how we make decisions and work as a team:

• Earn Customer Love — trust is earned with every interaction, every delivery, and every problem we solve

• Team Flow — ideas, energy, and support move freely across teams; optimize for the whole

• Quality is Our Cheat Code — the systems that deliver quality consistently are a structural advantage

• Find the 20% — find the inputs that drive the outcomes and execute them completely

• Write the Market — our research puts us at the frontier, and we bring our partners there first

• Three Moves Ahead — consider the consequences of consequences, and plan accordingly

Scale employees in eligible roles are also granted equity based compensation, subject to Board of Director approval. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for your preferred location during the hiring process, and confirm whether the hired role will be eligible for equity grant. You'll also receive benefits including, but not limited to: comprehensive health, dental and vision coverage, retirement benefits, a learning and development stipend, and generous PTO. Additionally, this role may be eligible for additional benefits such as a commuter stipend.

jobs.title: Vehicle Software Engineer Intern
jobs.description:
Advanced Reentry Technologies

Who We Are:

Inversion is an aerospace and defense company pioneering advanced reentry technology to enable next-generation capabilities from space. By combining high-performance materials, precision aerodynamics, and mission-driven autonomy, Inversion is transforming reentry into an operational capability for an entirely new class of missions.

The company’s highly maneuverable reentry spacecraft, Arc, is designed for rapid global cargo delivery, hypersonic testing, and other national security missions that require precise, controlled flight through the atmosphere. Arc creates an entirely new transportation domain, unlocking unprecedented speed and global reach.

Headquartered in Los Angeles, Inversion designs, manufactures, and integrates its spacecraft under one roof, enabling the company to move rapidly from concept to flight. The company is backed by leading investors including Y Combinator, Spark Capital, and Lockheed Martin Ventures, with customers across the U.S. government and commercial space industry.

Position Overview:

As a Vehicle Software Engineering Intern at Inversion, you will help develop the software systems that enable our next-generation reentry vehicles to operate reliably, both in space and on the ground. You will work alongside experienced flight and ground software engineers to build, test, and deploy software that directly supports spacecraft development, qualification, and mission operations.

Unlike traditional internships focused on smaller assignments, you will take ownership of a meaningful engineering project, driving it from initial requirements and design through implementation, testing, and delivery. Your work could involve flight software, ground systems, hardware integration, or automated testing infrastructure, depending on team priorities and your interests.

This is a hands-on opportunity for students passionate about software engineering, embedded systems, robotics, or aerospace to build production-quality software that will continue to be used long after their internship ends.

Key Responsibilities

• Own a well-scoped software engineering project from requirements definition and technical design through implementation, validation, and deployment.

• Design, develop, and test software that supports spacecraft flight systems, ground operations, or engineering test infrastructure.

• Develop and integrate software with physical hardware, simulation environments, or existing flight and ground software systems.

• Write automated tests and contribute to software verification using unit testing, software-in-the-loop (SIL), hardware-in-the-loop (HIL), or processor-in-the-loop (PIL) environments.

• Collaborate with flight software, avionics, simulation, and other engineering teams to solve challenging technical problems.

• Participate in software design reviews, code reviews, debugging, and integration testing.

• Document technical designs, test results, and software functionality, and present your completed project to the engineering team.

Required Qualifications

• Currently pursuing a bachelor's, master's, or doctoral degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Robotics, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

• Demonstrated software development experience through personal projects, engineering teams, research, open-source contributions, or previous internships.

• Experience programming in at least one language such as C, C++, Rust, or Python.

• Strong understanding of fundamental software engineering concepts, including debugging, testing, data structures, and software design.

• Familiarity with collaborative development tools and practices such as Git, code reviews, or automated testing.

• Strong problem-solving skills, curiosity, and the ability to independently work through unfamiliar technical challenges.

• Ability to communicate technical ideas clearly and collaborate effectively with engineers across disciplines.

Desired Qualifications

• Experience developing software that interacts with physical hardware, embedded systems, or robotics platforms.

• Familiarity with Linux development environments and command-line tooling.

• Experience developing test automation, simulation software, or continuous integration pipelines.

• Familiarity with networking concepts and communication protocols such as TCP/IP, UDP, Ethernet, CAN, UART, or SPI.

• Experience with embedded Linux, device drivers, or low-level systems programming.

• Hands-on experience with spacecraft, rocketry, CubeSats, robotics, Formula SAE, autonomous vehicles, or similar engineering projects.

Our office headquarters is located in Playa Vista, CA. This position requires in office presence for the duration of the internship.

The California annual base hourly rate for this role is currently $38-$41. Pay Grades are determined by role, level, location, and alignment with market data. Individual pay will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: interviews and an assessment of several factors that are unique to each candidate, job-related skills, relevant education and experience, certifications, abilities of the candidate and internal equity.

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

jobs.description:
ABOUT NU

Nu serves more than 140 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services.

 

Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Its business model thrives on customer love and lower costs, feeding a flywheel of growth and profitability.

Visit our Institutional Page https://www.nu.com/2026-en


ABOUT THE PROGRAM

The Nu AI Core Summer Internship Program is a research-focused internship for PhD students working at the frontier of artificial intelligence and machine learning.

Over about 12 weeks, interns collaborate with engineers, applied scientists, and researchers on complex AI challenges. Each intern leads an end-to-end research or applied AI project that combines research methods with large-scale production environments.

The program builds long-term relationships between industry and academia and with emerging AI research talent.



PROGRAM STRUCTURE

 - Duration: ~12 weeks

 - Start dates: May–June, aligned with US university calendars

 - Location model: Remote, with one in-person week at Nu's Palo Alto office in Silicon Valley, fully covered by us.

What you get

 - Dedicated research mentor

 - Ownership of a scoped AI research project

 - Access to large-scale datasets and compute infrastructure

 - Research talks and technical seminars

 - Final research presentation to leadership and AI teams


RESEARCH AREAS

Interns may work on projects related to:

 - Machine learning and deep learning

 - Large language models and generative AI

 - Recommender systems and ranking models

 - AI infrastructure and model optimization

 - Responsible AI and model evaluation

Projects typically combine research experimentation with applied system development, including model design, experimentation, and large-scale evaluation.



CANDIDATE PROFILE

This program targets PhD students conducting research in AI and machine learning who are interested in applying their work to real-world systems.

Applicants are typically pursuing a PhD in fields such as:

 - Computer Science

 - Machine Learning

 - Artificial Intelligence

 - Statistics

 - Mathematics

 - Computational Linguistics

 - Electrical Engineering

 - or related quantitative disciplines.



BASIC QUALIFICATIONS (APPLICATION/ SCREENING FILTERS)

 - Currently enrolled in a PhD program

 - Research focus in machine learning, AI, statistics or related areas

 - Strong programming skills in Python or similar languages

 - Experience working with machine learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow)

 - Experience designing experiments and evaluating models

 - Experience working with large datasets or training ML models
   


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

Strong candidates may also demonstrate:

 - Publications at top AI/ML conferences (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, KDD, RecSys, CVPR, CIKM or equivalent-conferences for related fields)

 - Experience working with large-scale ML systems or distributed training

 - Experience with LLMs, generative AI, or foundation models

 - Open-source contributions in AI or ML

 - Experience collaborating in interdisciplinary research environments



WHAT WE VALUE

We are particularly interested in candidates who demonstrate:

 - Strong research rigor and experimental methodology

 - Ability to translate research ideas into practical systems

 - Track record of identifying novel research directions or reframing existing problems

 - Intellectual curiosity and independent problem solving

 - Collaboration with engineers and cross-functional teams

 - Interest in deploying AI systems with real-world impact




BENEFITS

 - Top Tier Medical Insurance

 - Top Tier Dental and Vision Insurance

 - Life Insurance and AD&D

 - Extended maternity and paternity leaves

 - Nucleo - Our learning platform of courses

 - NuLanguage - Our language learning program

 - NuCare - Our mental health and wellness assistance program

 - 401K

 - Saving Plans - Health Saving Account and Flexible Spending Account



LOCATION FOR THIS OPPORTUNITY

Remote, but only for USA PhD students




Our recruitment process may involve the use of artificial intelligence–enabled tools, such as automated interview transcription and analysis, to support the evaluation process. Artificial intelligence is not used to make final hiring decisions; all decisions are made by human reviewers.

Appian Intern (Paid Internship)

Must hold at least a Bachelor’s degree

Location: Hybrid (Washington, DC Metro Area Preferred)
Compensation: $20/hour (40 hours per week)
Duration: 4 Weeks (with potential for full-time employment.

Citizenship: This position requires U.S. citizenship. 

Who We Are:

Horizon Industries Limited (Horizon) is a dynamic IT and Management Consulting firm based in the Washington, DC area. Founded in 1996, Horizon Industries Limited (Horizon) has evolved into a company of highly qualified professionals that provides full-cycle IT consulting and Management support in both the private and public sectors.

Horizon’s culture is based on our core values, and we PRIDE ourselves on a diverse, employee- and family-centric approach.

Launch Your Career in Low-Code Development

Are you passionate about technology and eager to build solutions that make a real impact? Horizon Industries is looking for motivated and ambitious individuals to join our Appian Internship Program—an immersive, paid opportunity designed to prepare you for a career in low-code application development and digital transformation.

As an Appian Developer Intern, you'll develop technical and professional skills, collaborate on real-world projects, and gain exposure to the consulting environment supporting Federal Government clients.

This internship is more than just a learning opportunity. It's a pathway to a full-time career. Successful interns who meet performance expectations and are based on business needs will receive an offer to join Horizon Industries as a full-time Appian Consultant.

What to Expect

Your internship begins with a structured four-week training program designed to accelerate your learning:

• Week 1: Horizon-sponsored, instructor-led virtual Appian training (Monday–Friday, 9:00 AM–5:00 PM)

• Weeks 2–4: Hands-on internal training focused on Appian development, consulting methodologies, Agile practices, and professional skills

Throughout the program, you'll receive mentorship from experienced Appian professionals while building the foundation needed to launch your consulting career.

What You'll Do

As an Appian Intern, you will:

• Learn the fundamentals of Appian low-code application development and business process automation.

• Shadow experienced consultants to gain real-world insight into designing, developing, and implementing Appian solutions.

• Assist in building Appian applications, workflows, interfaces, reports, and business processes under the guidance of senior developers.

• Participate in application testing, quality assurance, and defect resolution activities.

• Support the integration and configuration of Appian applications with enterprise systems.

• Research Appian best practices, emerging technologies, and industry trends, and present findings to the team.

• Create and maintain technical documentation, configuration guides, and user documentation.

• Assist in troubleshooting and resolving application issues.

• Participate in Agile ceremonies, team meetings, knowledge-sharing sessions, and collaborative problem-solving activities.

• Develop training materials and resources to support end-user adoption.

• Continuously expand your technical knowledge while developing consulting, communication, and presentation skills.

What We're Looking For

We're looking for individuals who are curious, motivated, and excited to build a career in technology consulting.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Software Engineering, or a related technical field.

• Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving skills.

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

• Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to collaborate effectively in a team environment.

• Highly organized with exceptional attention to detail.

• Self-motivated, adaptable, and eager to learn new technologies.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

• Demonstrated leadership through academic, extracurricular, or professional experiences.

• Passion for software development, automation, and emerging technologies.

Preferred Qualifications

• Basic knowledge of object-oriented programming concepts.

• Familiarity with Java, Python, JavaScript, SQL, or another programming language.

• Understanding of databases, web technologies, or software development methodologies.

• Experience with Agile or Scrum environments is a plus.

• Resides in the Washington, DC metropolitan area.

Why Horizon Industries?

At Horizon Industries, you'll join a collaborative team dedicated to delivering innovative technology solutions for Federal Government clients. We invest in our people through mentorship, structured training, and continuous learning opportunities. Many of our full-time consultants began their careers through our internship program.

If you're ready to build in-demand technical skills, work alongside industry experts, and launch your consulting career, we'd love to hear from you.

Horizon is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer, and it is our policy to consider all applicants for employment. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, or national origin.

Who You Are:

Ai2 is seeking passionate, early-career researchers to join us for an internship. PhD graduate students in AI-related fields are invited to apply for full-time research internships with us year-round. Our research covers the full spectrum of robotics ranging from low-level control, scaling simulation to solve real-world robotics challenges, world models, RL, and investigating agentic systems for robotics. We are looking for applicants that are experienced and passionate about a particular aspect of robotics. International candidates are welcome to apply. Pay is competitive, and visa sponsorship is available.

Who We Are: 

Ai2’s Robotics team is looking for PhD student interns to join our team. 

As a research intern in the Robotics team, you’ll have the unique opportunity to support the development and investigate core research problems in foundation models and skills for robotics, contribute to the development of completely open data sets, benchmarks, and models, and experiment with robots in the real world.

Your Next Challenge:

At Ai2, you will be working with world-class AI researchers and talented software engineers. We perform team-based, ambitious research, with a mandate to strive for big breakthroughs, not just incremental progress, in an exciting and interactive workplace. 

All interns are paired with a mentor and will participate directly in Ai2's groundbreaking work. There are no restrictions on publications based on internships. 

Ai2 Research Interns will have the opportunity to do the following tasks:

• Conducting AI research under the guidance of a mentor, which may include building AI systems or system components, developing datasets, and/or conducting experiments.

• Reading the scientific literature to investigate and understand AI research.

• Meeting with the mentor to discuss research progress and ideas.

To see more about our current, future, and past interns at Ai2, check out the internship page on our website!

What You’ll Need:

Minimum Qualifications:

• Pursuing a PhD in robotics, machine learning, or related fields.

• Have an interest and experience in cutting-edge artificial intelligence and robotics research.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Proven track record of publishing at robotics and AI conferences, such as CoRL, ICRA, IROS, RSS, and Neurips. 

• Strong software engineering skills in physics simulation, machine learning, and robot control.

Physical Demands and Work Environment:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by a team member to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the functions.

• Must be able to remain in a stationary position for long periods of time. 

• The ability to communicate information and ideas so others will understand. Must be able to exchange accurate information in these situations. 

• The ability to observe details at close range.

• Can work under deadlines.

A Little More About Ai2:

Ai2 is a Seattle based non-profit AI research institute founded in 2014 by the late Paul Allen. Our mission is building breakthrough AI to solve the world’s biggest problems. We develop foundational AI research and innovation to deliver real-world impact through large-scale open models, data, robotics, conservation, and beyond.

In addition to Ai2’s core mission, we also aim to contribute to humanity through our treatment of each member of the Ai2 Team. Some highlights are:

• We are a learning organization – because everything Ai2 does is ground-breaking, we are learning every day. With a wide variety of world-class AI experts as guest speakers, and our commitment to your personal on-going education, Ai2 is a place where you will have opportunities to continue learning alongside your coworkers. 

• We value diversity - We seek to hire, support, and promote people from all genders, ethnicities, and all levels of experience regardless of age. We particularly encourage applications from women, non-binary individuals, people of color, members of the LGBTQA+ community, and people with disabilities of any kind. 

• We value inclusion - We understand the value that people's individual experiences and perspectives can bring to an organization, and we are building a culture in which all voices are heard, respected and considered.

• We emphasize a healthy work/life balance – we believe our team members are happiest and most productive when their work/life balance is optimized. While we value powerful research results which drive our mission forward, we also value dinner with family, weekend time, and vacation time. We offer generous paid vacation and sick leave as well as family leave.

• We are collaborative and transparent – we consider ourselves a team, all moving with a common purpose. We are quick to cheer our successes, and even quicker to share and jointly problem solve our failures.

• We are in Seattle – and our office is on the water! We have mountains, we have lakes, we have four seasons, we bike to work, we have a vibrant theater scene, and we have so much else. We welcome interest from applicants from outside of the United States.

• We are friendly– chances are you will like every one of the 200+ (and growing) people who work here. We do.

Benefits:

• Team members are able to enroll in our health savings account plan, our healthcare reimbursement arrangement plan, and our health care and dependent care flexible spending account plans.

• Team members will receive $125 per month to assist with commuting or internet expenses and will also receive $200 per month

jobs.description:
Legend Biotech is a global biotechnology company dedicated to treating and, one day, curing life-threatening diseases. Headquartered in Bridgewater, New Jersey, we are advancing the next generation of cell therapy through a portfolio of innovative technologies, including autologous, allogeneic, and in vivo cell therapy approaches. Our research spans chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T), T-cell receptor (TCR-T), natural killer (NK) cell-based therapies, and other emerging platforms designed to transform the treatment of serious diseases. From our global network of research and development sites, we are committed to discovering and developing safe, effective, and cutting-edge therapies for patients worldwide.

Legend Biotech entered into a global collaboration agreement with Johnson & Johnson to jointly develop and commercialize CARVYKTI® (ciltacabtagene autoleucel; cilta-cel). Through this strategic partnership, we combine complementary expertise and capabilities to advance innovative immunotherapies for patients living with multiple myeloma.

Legend Biotech is seeking a Data Intern as part of the Information Technology team based in Bridgewater, NJ.

Role Overview

The Data Intern will support the Data & Analytics team in collecting, organizing, analyzing, and visualizing data to enable business decision-making. The intern will gain hands-on experience with enterprise data, business intelligence tools, cloud data platforms, data quality, and documentation within a regulated life sciences environment.

Working with IT, business, and data teams, the intern will contribute to reports, dashboards, data processes, analytics, automation, and AI-enabled initiatives. This opportunity is well suited for a student interested in gaining practical experience in data analytics, data engineering, and business intelligence.

Key Responsibilities

• Assist with collecting, cleaning, transforming, and analyzing structured and unstructured data from multiple business systems.

• Perform exploratory data analysis to identify trends, patterns, anomalies, and potential data quality issues.

• Develop and enhance dashboards, reports, and visualizations using tools such as Microsoft Power BI.

• Write SQL queries to retrieve, analyze, and validate data from databases and cloud data platforms.

• Support data engineering activities, including data ingestion, transformation, validation, and reconciliation.

• Assist with preparing analytics-ready datasets and support the development of data and semantic models.

• Support enterprise data platform initiatives using technologies such as Snowflake, Microsoft Azure, Microsoft Fabric, or similar cloud platforms.

• Assist with documenting data sources, transformations, lineage, metadata, and business rules.

• Perform data quality checks and support the resolution of data inconsistencies.

• Support discussions with business stakeholders to understand and document reporting and analytics requirements.

• Assist with analytics, automation, and AI-enabled solutions where appropriate.

• Participate in testing and validation of reports, dashboards, datasets, and data pipelines.

• Prepare technical documentation, presentations, and analytical summaries.

• Follow organizational requirements for data privacy, cybersecurity, data governance, and the appropriate handling of confidential information.

• Perform other data and analytics-related activities as assigned.

The Data Intern works under the guidance of the Data & Analytics team and may independently perform assigned analysis, prepare reports, document findings, and identify data quality issues. The role may recommend process improvements and highlight risks or issues but does not have authority to make architectural, compliance, financial, or strategic decisions without management approval.

WHAT TO EXPECT

Heron Power is a startup company building cutting-edge power electronics for the 21st-century grid. We aim to debottleneck the growth of electricity generation and consumption with scalable, innovative, and less costly hardware solutions, accelerating the electrification of everything.

Our first focus goal is to build better converters (inverters & rectifiers) to connect large-scale renewables, storage, and loads to the grid. Heron Power’s leadership team is made up of seasoned veterans who have designed and shipped gigawatts of power conversion products over the past decade.

We understand that no one individual knows everything. We will all learn a lot together and from each other. You can expect to work in a dynamic and collaborative environment, driven by first principles engineering, solving difficult problems.

As an Intern, Firmware Engineering, you will be responsible for developing and testing embedded firmware for our power conversion products. Additionally, you will help with hardware bring-up, test automation and development tooling, working alongside experienced firmware and hardware engineers.



HOW YOU WILL CONTRIBUTE

 - Write and debug embedded C firmware for microcontrollers

 - Implement test cases and automate test execution, including unit tests, hardware-in-the-loop tests and real hardware bench tests

 - Hardware bring-up and firmware debugging using lab/debugging tools

 - Improve build, test and development tooling

 - Write clear documentation and take part in code reviews



WHAT YOU WILL BRING

We have a short list of must-have requirements. We prioritize a strong grip on first principles, hands-on skills, and a sense of initiative. Domain-specific knowledge and experience will help determine the career level for each hire.



MUST-HAVE REQUIREMENTS

 - Currently pursuing a BS or MS in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science or a related field

 - Good C/C++ programming skills

 - Some embedded experience from coursework, clubs or personal projects

 - Basic Python for scripting

 - Familiarity with Git, or any version control tools


NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Experience with microcontrollers and common peripherals (ADC, PWM, UART, SPI, CAN)

 - Familiarity with any RTOS or real-time programming

 - Lab tools such as an oscilloscope or debugger

 - Interest in power electronics or energy

If you are passionate about technology and enjoy working in a fast-paced environment, we would love to hear from you. Join us in accelerating the electrification of everything at Heron Power.

Amplify helps teachers bring delight and rigor to students every day. We have become a leader in K–12 literacy, biliteracy, math, and science by building inspiring teaching and learning experiences based on research. The Amplify Classroom platform combines curriculum, assessment, and supplemental learning into one coherent high-quality instructional system. A pioneer in education since 2000, Amplify has developed deep relationships in states and districts by partnering with educators to drive implementation quality and improved outcomes. Today, Amplify serves more than 18 million students and teachers across all 50 states and on six continents. For more information, visit Amplify.com http://amplify.com.


CREATE AN IMPACT BY SHAPING THE WORLD OF EDUCATION!

Amplify is seeking a curious and driven AI Scientist Intern to join our team this summer and help us build intelligent, data-informed experiences for the educators, students, and families who use our innovative educational products. This paid, remote 10-week internship offers the chance to make a real impact on products used by millions of students and teachers.

If you’re comfortable with machine learning, data modeling/applied AI and are genuinely passionate about making learning better for teachers and students, then this role could be a fit for you! The ideal candidates will love digging into large datasets, bring a collaborative, ask-questions-first energy to your work, and feel excited to build intelligent systems that move the needle for K–12 learners.

 - Contribute to documentation, technical reports, model performance analyses, and research presentations

 - Track and analyze model outputs to spot patterns, anomalies, and optimization opportunities

 - Join product demos and Data Science/Product Manager meetings to build knowledge of Amplify's AI-driven products

 - Real-world challenges affecting educators, students, and families

 - Collaboration with Data Science, Engineering, and Product teams

 - Contributions to meaningful AI research and model development in a mission-driven environment

 - Mentorship from industry professionals at the forefront of AI in education

 - Exposure to Machine Learning, NLP, Adaptive Learning, and AI Ethics

 - Hands-on training in a fast-paced, agile environment

The firm pursues investment strategies primarily within the global fixed income markets with the objectives of capital preservation and absolute return without significant correlation to equity, interest rate and foreign exchange markets. Established in 1994, Bracebridge manages private investment funds that serve endowments, foundations, pension funds and other institutional and high-net-worth investors.

Approximately 170 employees operate from our office located in Boston’s historic Back Bay. The entrepreneurial and collaborative culture at Bracebridge rewards and supports motivated, dedicated, enthusiastic and intellectually curious individuals. We believe our firm’s greatest asset is the people who work here.

Bracebridge is seeking to hire a talented graduate student as a co-op in our Quantitative Research department. • Build out the data acquisition framework for new providers and asset classes
• Improve product documentation

• Experience with .NET development platform preferred
• Experience with C# or Java
• Strong object-oriented programming skills
• SQL skills
• Ability to critically evaluate and improve current processes

• Intellectual curiosity and an eagerness to learn

With over £74 billion of assets under management, we secure the pensions of nearly one million people and pay out, on average, approximately £355 million in pension payments each month.

To do that, we need the very brightest original thinkers to bring creativity as well as rigour. Rothesay is a rewarding place to work, where quality people can thrive and prosper. We pride ourselves on the connections our people build, many of whom have been with us for over ten years.

Rothesay is the UK’s largest pensions insurance specialist, purpose-built to protect pension schemes and their members’ pensions. Our internship programme is designed to provide hands on work experience within a fast-pace financial services environment, allowing you to develop the key skills to jump-start your career. 

The 8-week structured programme will start with a fundamentals week offering insight into Rothesay, your team and the financial services industry. Throughout the programme there will be both on-desk and off-desk technical and business skills training, providing career building exposure to accelerate your future after you graduate. The engineering team at Rothesay develops and supports systems used by front office (trading, risk, strats, capital, pricing) and middle office (operations, finance).

This is a great chance to work with and learn from Rothesay’s team of extremely highly regarded, experienced and friendly software engineers. At Rothesay every employee has the opportunity to make a real impact to the business. Our engineering team is open to new technologies and creative ideas.

Quantitative Researcher Intern
jobs.description:
At Graviton, every strategy, model and edge begins not with instinct, but with someone asking a better question than everyone else.

As a Quantitative Research Intern, you'll spend 10-12 weeks working on research that directly shapes how we understand markets and build trading strategies. You'll collaborate with researchers and technologists to investigate market behaviour, test hypotheses, build predictive models and solve problems where the answers aren't obvious.

This isn't an internship where you observe from the sidelines. Outstanding work has the potential to shape production strategies and generate real, measurable returns.

Ideal candidates are quantitatively sharp, practically minded problem solvers, programmers, mathematicians and scientists who are excited to solve the hardest problems in our field, across our offices in the US, Singapore, Amsterdam and London.

What You'll Work On

You'll work on real research problems, not simulated exercises, discovering predictive patterns from billions of market events, designing statistical models, and applying machine learning to open research problems. Your work would include:

• Discovering predictive patterns from billions of market events

• Designing statistical models that identify trading opportunities

• Applying probability, optimization and machine learning to open research problems

• Building AI-powered research agents that accelerate experimentation

• Developing infrastructure for rapid, large-scale research

• Designing experiments and backtests to evaluate hypotheses

• Translating research into production-ready trading signals

• Exploring new ML, AI and quant finance techniques to find the next source of alpha

What You'll Learn

Beyond the technical exposure, you'll learn how experienced researchers approach hard problems: breaking them down, questioning assumptions, and deciding based on evidence rather than intuition. You'll be paired with a mentor, reporting manager and buddy, with regular code reviews and feedback throughout the internship.

What Success Looks Like

Successful interns leave having delivered a complete research project from hypothesis to evaluation, built statistically rigorous models, and demonstrated curiosity, ownership and the ability to solve open-ended problems.

Who We're Looking For

We're looking for exceptional students who genuinely enjoy solving hard problems.

• Full-time undergraduate, Master's or PhD student in a quantitative discipline (math, physics, computer science, statistics, or a related field), graduating 2028

• Strong programming skills in Python and/or C++

• Grounded in probability, statistics, linear algebra and optimization, with experience in machine learning, statistical modelling or data analysis, whether through coursework, research or personal projects

• Comfortable working with large, complex datasets, with strong analytical thinking

• A passion for applying quantitative thinking and rigorous research to solve open-ended problems in markets

• Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain complex ideas clearly

Our Culture

More than specific technologies, we care how you think. We look for people who are curious enough to question assumptions, analytical enough to separate signal from noise, persistent enough to keep searching past the first answer, humble enough to keep learning, and excited by problems without textbook solutions.

At Graviton, researchers sit alongside engineers to solve problems where milliseconds matter and better models create real competitive advantage. You'll get meaningful ownership from day one, in a culture built on intellectual honesty and continuous improvement. Your contribution won't be measured by hours spent, but by the quality of your thinking.

Markets are among the most complex systems humans have ever created. Every day, someone discovers a better answer. This summer, that someone could be you.

jobs.title: Quantitative Researcher
jobs.description:
At Graviton, we don't believe the best trading strategies come from following established playbooks. They come from asking better questions. Why does a pattern exist? What is driving it? Is it real or just noise? Can it be explained, modelled and turned into an edge?

As a Quantitative Researcher, you'll work on those questions every day. You'll investigate market behaviour, develop quantitative models, build and test hypotheses and turn insights into trading strategies, working alongside researchers and technologists in an environment where an idea on a whiteboard can reach live trading quickly.

This isn't a role where the answers are in a textbook. The problems are open-ended, the data is enormous, and finding the answers is the job.

Ideal candidates are rigorous thinkers who genuinely enjoy mathematics, programming and figuring out things that aren't obvious, based in our Singapore, London, Amsterdam or US offices.

What You'll Work On

You'll work across quantitative research and systematic trading, taking ideas through the full lifecycle: question, hypothesis, experiment, model, validation, strategy, production. Depending on your team and research interests, your work would include:

• Discovering predictive patterns and sources of alpha from billions of market events

• Formulating hypotheses about market behaviour and designing experiments to test them

• Applying probability, statistics, optimization and machine learning to build predictive models and quantitative signals for systematic trading

• Designing robust backtests and statistical tests to distinguish genuine signals from noise

• Working with large and complex datasets to uncover patterns that aren't immediately visible

• Investigating market microstructure and how markets behave at different timescales

• Evaluating strategy performance, identifying weaknesses and continuously refining models

• Developing research infrastructure and AI-powered tools and agents that make experimentation faster and analysis deeper

• Working closely with technologists to translate research ideas into efficient, production-ready systems

• Exploring new techniques in machine learning, statistics and quantitative finance to uncover new sources of edge

No two research problems are the same. Good research finds patterns. Great research understands why they exist.

What Success Looks Like

Successful researchers at Graviton discover new sources of alpha and turn them into robust trading strategies, build models that hold up under real market conditions and not only in backtests, develop a deep understanding of market behaviour, create research frameworks and tools that make the broader team more effective, work with technologists to take ideas from research into production, and communicate complex quantitative ideas clearly and rigorously. Your impact isn't measured by how many models you build. It's measured by the quality of the ideas you discover and what those ideas enable.

Who We're Looking For

We're looking for exceptional problem solvers who genuinely enjoy mathematics, programming and figuring out things that aren't obvious.

• Degree in a quantitative discipline such as mathematics, physics, computer science, statistics, operations research or machine learning

• No active backlogs

• Strong programming skills in Python and/or C++

• Solid grounding in probability, statistics, linear algebra and optimization, with experience in machine learning, statistical modelling or data analysis, whether through coursework, research or personal projects

• Comfort working with large, complex datasets, and strong analytical thinking

• A passion for applying quantitative thinking and rigorous research to solve open-ended problems in markets

• Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex ideas clearly

Prior exposure to quantitative research, algorithmic trading, market microstructure, competitive mathematics or machine learning is valuable, but we care more about how you think than whether you've worked in finance before.

Our Culture

More than specific tools or techniques, we care how you think. We look for people who are curious enough to keep asking why, analytical enough to separate signal from noise, persistent enough to pursue difficult problems, intellectually honest enough to abandon an idea when the evidence says so, and humble enough to keep learning.

At Graviton, researchers sit alongside technologists on specialized trading teams that operate with significant autonomy. You'll have meaningful ownership of research problems from day one: forming your own hypotheses, challenging existing approaches and following the evidence wherever it leads, with the infrastructure and datasets to test ideas at scale, competitive compensation, and a culture where the best idea wins regardless of who proposed it.

Markets are among the most complex systems humans have ever created, and they never stop changing. Neither should our thinking. Every day, someone asks a better question and finds an answer nobody had. That someone could be you.

jobs.description:
Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all. 
Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.

At Micron, we are transforming how the world uses information to enrich life. The High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) Design team develops industry-leading memory solutions that enable advances in Artificial Intelligence, high-performance computing, graphics, and data-center applications. Our engineers collaborate across global teams to deliver innovative memory architectures and semiconductor technologies that power next-generation computing systems.

As an HBM Design Engineer Intern, you will work alongside experienced memory engineers and gain hands-on experience in semiconductor design, simulation, verification, and analysis. This internship provides exposure to industry-standard design methodologies, EDA tools, and cross-functional collaboration throughout the product development lifecycle. You will also have opportunities to apply AI-Assisted and AI-Enabled workflows to improve engineering productivity, debug efficiency, and design quality.

Responsibilities
• Assist with the design, simulation, analysis, and verification of HBM memory and logic circuits using industry-standard semiconductor design tools.
• Support RTL development, circuit implementation, timing analysis, power analysis, and functional validation activities.
• Develop scripts, automation solutions, and AI-Assisted workflows to improve design productivity, debug efficiency, and design-flow quality.
• Collaborate with Design, Verification, Physical Design, CAD, and Product Engineering teams on technical reviews, debug activities, and project deliverables.
• Document technical work, experimental results, AI-Enabled insights, and design methodologies to support knowledge sharing and continuous improvement.

• Currently pursuing a Bachelor's, Master's, or Ph.D. degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field.
• Completed coursework in Digital Logic Design, CMOS Circuits, Computer Architecture, VLSI Design, Semiconductor Devices, or related subjects.
• Demonstrated understanding of combinational and sequential logic design concepts.
• Experience with Verilog, SystemVerilog, or VHDL through academic, research, or project work.
• Programming experience in Python, Perl, Tcl, C/C++, or similar languages, with strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Preferred Qualifications
• Knowledge of memory architectures such as DRAM, SRAM, DDR, LPDDR, or HBM.
• Experience with RTL design, simulation, synthesis, timing analysis, verification methodologies, or functional coverage concepts.
• Familiarity with Linux/Unix environments, scripting, and automation techniques.
• Exposure to semiconductor EDA tools such as VCS, Xcelium, Questa, PrimeTime, Innovus, Virtuoso, or similar platforms.

Leidos Defense Systems is seeking a talented Electrical Hardware Design Engineering Intern to join a diverse team in summer 2027 to create unique solutions for complex problems. We have offices across the United States that provide responsive, cost-effective engineering, scientific, and IT solutions in the defense, space, cyber, and commercial fields. The ideal candidate will thrive in a learning environment that encourages leadership and technical growth.

At Leidos, our mission is to reach, equip, and teach students with an interest in the field of defense and aerospace. Running for over two decades, the internship program has been a staple at Leidos, giving interns hands-on experience in their future career path. With no shortage of work available, interning with Leidos promises growth, experience, and unrivaled opportunity across the US.
 
This position is an Electrical Hardware Design Engineer Summer Intern in the Electrical Systems Department. Interns are provided with opportunities to participate in a wide range of design engineering activities that include concept development, architecting, implementing, and testing printed circuit board assemblies (PCBAs) including power supply, mixed-signal, FPGA, microcontroller designs. There are also additional skill development opportunities through participation in printed circuit board layout, signal integrity analysis, power distribution network design, technical trade studies, and evaluation of technology improvements. The selected candidate will work closely with their assigned mentor on tasks that are beneficial to the intern's skills development and valuable to the programs with which they are working. The ideal candidate will thrive in a learning environment that encourages leadership and technical growth.
 
Primary Responsibilities
• Assist in the design, simulation, modeling and testing of hardware solutions.
• Working with design tools such as Mentor Graphics, Altium for PCB design, SPICE, and Visio.
• Develop and execute hardware verification plans.
• Debug hardware using test equipment such as oscilloscopes and signal generators.
• Collaborate with team members on hardware projects.

• Currently enrolled in an accredited college/ university and currently working towards a degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field.
• Holds a GPA of 3.0 or higher.
• Includes resume and unofficial transcripts in application.
• Demonstrates problem solving, teamwork, and communication skills.
• Basic understanding of circuit theory and design.
• Exposure to at least one programming language (Python, MATLAB, or C/C++).
• Must be a US Citizen and be able to obtain and maintain a DoD Secret security clearance.
• Able to work onsite in Huntsville, AL during summer 2027.
 
Preferred Qualifications
• Coursework or project experience with:• Multi-layer PCB design or layout
• Digital logic design (VHDL/Verilog, FPGAs, or microcontrollers)

jobs.title: AI Co-op
jobs.description:
At Manulife John Hancock, we believe in investing in the future – starting with you. Our AI Co-op Program is your launchpad to success, offering the support, structure, and exciting opportunities you need to thrive and make your mark. Our co-op program offers more than just experience; you'll join a vibrant community, participate in engaging events, and benefit from personalized mentorship. 

As an AI Co-op, you’ll gain hands-on experience applying data science and machine learning techniques to solve real-world business problems. You’ll work with modern tools and datasets to explore and prepare data, develop predictive models, and generate insights that drive decision-making. Join a supportive team and experience a values-first culture where your career development and well-being are prioritized alongside your job impact. You’ll receive guidance from experienced practitioners while gaining exposure to the end-to-end lifecycle of data science, machine learning, and emerging AI solutions in an enterprise environment. 

We are currently looking for highly motivated students to join us in our Toronto, Ontario, Canada office for a 4-month co-op, running from January 5th – April 22nd, 2027. This is a hybrid position, where you are expected to be in the office Tuesday–Thursday, with the opportunity to work remotely on Mondays and Fridays. 

Position Responsibilities: 

• Explore, prepare, and validate data while ensuring data quality and consistency for analysis and modeling 

• Build and evaluate machine learning models using a range of techniques, with thoughtful experiment design and documentation 

• Support feature engineering, model development, and performance optimization 

• Prototype generative AI solutions (e.g., prompting, retrieval-based methods) with a focus on safety and effectiveness 

• Develop reproducible code and workflows for data processing and modeling using tools such as Python and SQL 

• Communicate insights through clear visualizations, reports, and presentations for both technical and non-technical audiences 

Required Qualifications: 

• Currently pursuing an undergraduate degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related field 

• Experience with at least one programming language (e.g., Python, R, Java) and familiarity with data manipulation techniques 

• Familiarity with machine learning concepts and tools (e.g., scikit-learn, PyTorch, or similar frameworks) 

• Experience working with SQL or other data querying languages 

• Understanding of version control systems (e.g., Git) and collaborative coding practices 

• Interest in machine learning, data science, and emerging AI technologies 

Preferred Qualifications: 

• Exposure to machine learning techniques such as regression, tree-based models, neural networks, or time series methods 

• Familiarity with generative AI concepts (e.g., prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation) 

• Experience with cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud) or data tools (e.g., Databricks, Spark) 

• Exposure to data visualization tools (e.g., Power BI, Tableau) and ability to present insights clearly 

• Strong problem-solving and communication skills, with the ability to apply technical solutions to business challenges 

When you join our team: 

• We’ll empower you to learn and grow the career you want.  

• We’ll recognize and support you in a flexible environment where well-being and inclusion are more than just words.  

• As part of our global team, we’ll support you in shaping the future you want to see.  

• As part of our co-op program, you will gain early access to Manulife John Hancock’s premier early talent program, GRO, tailored to graduating students! This program is designed to launch your career with the support, structure, and opportunities you need to thrive. 

Application instructions: 

• Submit your resume, cover letter, academic transcript, and work term evaluation (if any) in one PDF file. 

 Please note the salary range is expected to be between $54,600 CAD to $72,150 CAD. 

The actual salary will vary depending on local market conditions, geography, and relevant job-related factors such as knowledge, skills, qualifications, experience, and education/training. The annual salary will be pro-rated based on the length of the work-term

jobs.title: AI Data Science Intern
jobs.description:
About Marvell 
Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities. 

At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead. 

Your Team, Your Impact

The Data Office, part of Marvell’s CIO organization, builds the data and analytics foundation that helps the company make faster, better decisions across supply chain, finance, engineering, sales, and operations. Our team engineers the data pipelines that bring Marvell’s core enterprise systems together on modern platforms such as Databricks, Snowflake, and Power BI, and turns that data into trusted datasets, dashboards, machine learning models, and AI agents. Our work helps Marvell predict supply risk, improve product development efficiency, and put AI-driven insights in the hands of business leaders. As an intern, you will work on real projects that go into production and are used by teams across the company.
What You Can Expect
• Build and maintain scalable data pipelines (ETL/ELT) in Databricks and Snowflake that ingest, clean, and transform data from enterprise systems, with automated data quality checks
• Develop, evaluate, and deploy machine learning models and AI applications, including LLM-based and agentic workflows, that solve real business problems in areas such as supply chain, engineering productivity, or finance
• Analyze large, multi-source datasets to uncover trends, anomalies, and opportunities for improvement, and define the metrics that measure them
• Design interactive dashboards and visualizations in Power BI that communicate insights to business stakeholders
• Document pipelines and models, and present findings and recommendations to your mentor, the Data Office team, and business partners at the end of your internship
This is a hybrid role. You will be paired with a technical mentor and will meet regularly with the team to review progress and get feedback.

What We're Looking For
• Currently pursuing a Master’s Degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Statistics, Data Engineering, or a related field with an expected graduation date between Fall 2027 – Summer 2028
• Proficiency in Python for data processing, analysis, and modeling (e.g., pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn), and strong SQL skills for querying, transforming, and modeling large datasets
• Understanding of data engineering fundamentals, including ETL/ELT design, data warehousing, data modeling, and pipeline orchestration concepts
• Solid foundation in statistics, machine learning, and exploratory data analysis, with familiarity with modern AI models such as large language models (LLMs)
• Ability to communicate technical findings clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences
• Preferred: Hands-on experience with data platforms and tools such as Databricks, Snowflake, Spark/PySpark, Delta Lake, Airflow, or dbt
• Preferred: Experience building dashboards and reports in Power BI, Tableau, or similar BI tools
• Preferred: Hands-on experience building AI applications with LLMs and agentic frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, or similar, including RAG, prompt engineering, and tool integrations (e.g., MCP)
• Preferred: Prior project, internship, or research experience in data engineering or data science, with familiarity with cloud platforms (AWS or Azure) and Git/CI/CD

Expected Base Pay Range (USD)
32 - 63, $ per hour.
The successful candidate’s starting base pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location and market conditions. The expected base pay range for this role may be modified based on market conditions.

Additional Compensation and Benefit Elements 
Marvell is committed to providing exceptional, comprehensive benefits that support our employees at every stage - from internship to retirement and through life’s most important moments. Our offerings are built around four key pillars: financial well-being, family support, mental and physical health, and recognition. Highlights for our interns: medical, dental, and vision coverage, perks and discounts, robust mental health resources to prioritize emotional well-being, and paid holidays. Additional compensation may be available for intern PhD candidates. We look forward to sharing more with you during the interview process.
All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status.

Any applicant who requires a reasonable accommodation during the selection process should contact Marvell HR Helpdesk at TAOps@marvell.com.

These tools must not be used to record, assist with, or enhance responses in any way. jobs.title: Research Intern - Context and Knowledge Systems for AI
jobs.description:
Job Requisition ID #

26WD101097

Autodesk Research – Intelligent Construction
Summer 2027 | 12 weeks

Position Overview
Modern AI systems increasingly depend on their ability to access and use the right context at
the right time. An important research challenge is how large, evolving bodies of information
should be represented to support reliable inference.
Autodesk Research provides a distinctive setting for this work. Construction projects are rich,
complex information environments whose state changes continuously over time, making
them a compelling domain for studying context and knowledge systems for AI.
As a Research Intern, you will own a focused research problem in this area. You will
investigate new approaches to building and retrieving structured context, develop
experimental prototypes, and evaluate how effectively they support downstream AI
reasoning.
You will work closely with Autodesk researchers and engineers and have substantial freedom
to bring ideas from your own research. Strong contributions may form the basis of an
academic publication and future Autodesk research.

Responsibilities
• Conduct original research in context and knowledge systems for AI. Investigate
methods for representing and retrieving information to support reliable contextual
inference
• Develop new approaches to context construction. Explore how relevant knowledge
can be identified and assembled dynamically from large and evolving information
environments
• Build research prototypes. Implement experimental systems using graph-based,
semantic or hybrid approaches and apply them to realistic project information
• Design and conduct rigorous experiments. Develop suitable research questions,
baselines and evaluation methods to understand the strengths and limitations of
proposed approaches
• Collaborate with Autodesk researchers and engineers. Work across AI research,
software engineering and domain expertise to refine ideas and translate them into
experimental systems
• Communicate research findings. Present results within Autodesk Research and
contribute, where appropriate, to research papers, technical reports and
demonstrations

Minimum Qualifications
• Currently enrolled in a PhD program in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence,
Data Science, Information Science or a closely related field, with at least one
academic term remaining after the internship
• Research experience in an area related to knowledge representation, information
retrieval, data management or contextual information systems for AI
• Strong programming skills and experience developing experimental research
software
• Understanding of contemporary AI systems and how retrieval and contextual
information support modern reasoning or agentic workflows
• Experience formulating research questions and designing empirical evaluations.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills

Preferred Qualifications
Research experience in one or more of the following areas would be valuable:
• Knowledge graphs or graph-based information systems
• Advanced information retrieval and hybrid retrieval methods
• Retrieval-augmented generation, including GraphRAG or related approaches
• Context engineering or memory architectures for AI systems
• Semantic and structured knowledge representation
• Temporal, provenance-aware or evolving data systems
• Heterogeneous data integration at scale
• Graph machine learning applied to representation or retrieval
A strong research publication record in a relevant area is desirable

Prior experience with architecture, engineering or construction is not required. We are
particularly interested in candidates with deep technical expertise who are motivated by the
opportunity to test their research against a complex real-world information environment.

About the Team
Autodesk Research explores technologies that may shape how the world is designed and
made. We work across fundamental and applied research, developing new ideas and testing
them against problems grounded in professional practice.
The Intelligent Construction team investigates how emerging forms of AI can support a more
connected and adaptive construction industry. An important part of that challenge is
understanding how fragmented project information can become a coherent and evolving
source of knowledge for intelligent systems.
You will join a multidisciplinary research environment with expertise spanning AI, data
systems, software engineering and construction. You will work closely with experienced
researchers while having substantial ownership of your own research problem.
Expected Research Outcome
This is a focused 12-week research internship. The research question will be developed with
the successful candidate to make use of their existing expertise while addressing a problem
relevant to the team's research direction.
By the end of the internship, we expect the intern to have developed and evaluated an original
approach to a clearly defined research problem. This should include a working research
prototype, rigorous experimental evidence and a clear account of the findings and limitations.
The work will be shared within Autodesk Research. Where the research contribution warrants
it, we would expect to develop the work toward publication at an appropriate academic
venue.

Learn More

About Autodesk
Welcome to Autodesk! Amazing things are created every day with our software – from the greenest buildings and cleanest cars to the smartest factories and biggest hit movies. We help innovators turn their ideas into reality, transforming not only how things are made, but what can be made.

We take great pride in our culture here at Autodesk – it’s at the core of everything we do. Our culture guides the way we work and treat each other, informs how we connect with customers and partners, and defines how we show up in the world.

Are you a problem solver looking for a hands-on internship position with a market-leading company that will help develop your career and reward you intellectually and professionally?

About Analog Devices
Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI) is a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge. ADI combines analog, digital, AI, and software technologies into solutions that combat climate change, reliably connect humans and the world, and help drive advancements in automation and robotics, mobility, healthcare, energy and data centers. With revenue of more than $11 billion in FY25, ADI ensures today's innovators stay Ahead of What's Possible. Learn more at www.analog.com and on LinkedIn and X.

At ADI, you will learn from the brightest minds who are here to help you grow and succeed. During your internship, you will make an impact through work on meaningful projects alongside a team of experts. Collaborating with colleagues in an environment of respect and responsibility, you will create connections that will become a part of your professional network.

ADI’s culture values aligned goals, work-life balance, continuous and life-long learning opportunities, and shared rewards. The internship program features various lunch-and-learn topics and social events with other interns and full-time employees.

At ADI, our goal is to develop our interns so they are the first to be considered for full-time roles.

Apply now for the opportunity to grow your career and help innovate ahead of what’s possible.

The High-Speed SAR ADC Group in Newbury, UK, has an established reputation for developing industry-leading high-speed, precision analog-to-digital (A/D) converters. The group has been responsible for the development of several flagship SAR ADCs, including the AD7626, AD7960, AD4020, AD4696, AD4080, and AD4880. Its engineers have also published extensively in leading journals and conferences, including IEEE JSSC, ISSCC, ESSERC, the VLSI Symposium, and IEEE TCAS.

As an intern, you will have the opportunity to contribute to the design, verification, layout, and evaluation of analog and mixed-signal circuits used in precision A/D converters. You will work alongside a highly skilled team of engineers, gaining hands-on experience with real-world IC design challenges and contributing to the development of our next generation of products.
This role offers an excellent opportunity to develop practical experience in analog and mixed-signal IC design, while learning from experienced engineers in a collaborative development environment. The position is available for internship durations ranging from 3 to 12 months.
 
Core Responsibilities
 
• Design of circuits to be used in high precision (16-20bit resolution, >10MSps) analog to digital (A/D) converters
• Verification of the designed circuits with A/D converter
• Modelling and evaluation of signal chain driving the A/D converter
 
The Candidate
 
The ideal candidate should have a solid understanding of the basic principles of analog and digital design. The candidate should be enrolled in a related study program such as Electrical and Electronic Engineering. Any programming knowledge, MATLAB, Verilog and Labview experience is also relevant to the position. The candidate should be highly motivated, keen to learn from peers and able to demonstrate strong initiative.

Why Join our Team?
• Very Competitive Salary
• Strong mentoring from a group of well-established experts in Precision, High-Speed ADC design
• Variety of Networks/ Social Clubs
