jobs.title: Software Engineering Intern
jobs.description:
Software Engineering Internship Program

Location: Remote (US)*

Duration: 4 months (start in late February 2027)

Hours: 40 hrs/week paid experience

Application Deadline: All interested applicants must apply by November 20, 2026.

The Wikimedia Foundation is the non-profit organization that operates Wikipedia – one of the most popular websites in the world, accessed by over 1.8 billion unique devices every month. It is the only non-profit in the top 50 websites, supported by a community of millions of individual donors around the world.

We are looking for graduates, non-graduates, or those seeking a career change who are interested in developing software engineering skills through an immersive “learn on the job” internship program. As an intern, you will be embedded into an engineering team within our Product and Technology departments and assigned a primary project with clear deliverables. Alongside your manager and dedicated mentor, you will learn the inner workings of our open source code that helps to create “a world in which everyone can freely share in the sum of all knowledge”. You will work with software that serves over half a billion page views per day through Wikipedia (and other Wikimedia projects). The outcome of your work will impact how all people everywhere discover, share, and contribute to free knowledge.

Additionally, you will have the opportunity to learn about various departments at the Foundation and connect with the wider volunteer movement and community.

Applicants who identify from a group that is underrepresented in the global conversation of technology advancement are encouraged to apply. We’re also welcoming applicants from communities where access to free knowledge and Wikimedia projects are just emerging.

PROGRAM DETAILS

Successful candidates must be able to commit to a four month, 40hr/week internship which will fall between late February to late June 2027. We will provide laptops and necessary software installed for the duration of the program. This role is 100% remote, and in some cases there may be potential opportunities to participate in in-person events to meet other fellow interns and teams.

POTENTIAL TEAM OPPORTUNITIES

Mobile Apps Engineering Team
The Mobile Apps team's primary objective lies in constructing native Android and iOS applications for the Wikimedia Foundation.

Editing
The Editing team is part of the Contributors group. They work on tools for editing across MediaWiki, principally VisualEditor, DiscussionTools, and Edit check. The team is currently working on Suggestion Mode, a feature for the VisualEditor that proactively suggests actions that people can consider taking to improve Wikipedia articles.

Data Platform Engineering
The Mission of the Data Platform Engineering team is to empower Wiki Communities and the Wikimedia Foundation to gain insights, conduct research, and build compelling user experiences, through access to privacy-aware data and data platform services. The Data Platform is a collection of systems and services providing end-to-end capabilities for our data producers and consumers to collect, discover, and use data.

Release Engineering
The Release Engineering team enables developers to confidently build, test, and deploy code changes across Wikimedia projects, including Wikipedia, by creating the tools, infrastructure, and automation that keep software delivery fast and reliable.

Connection team

The Connection team is part of the Contributors group. They aim to improve how contributors connect and understand their impact. The team was formed in 2021 to focus on the needs of campaign and event organizers and participants and hopefully improve the experience of Wikimedia campaigns.

Tools Infrastructure (with Observability)

The mission of the Tools Infrastructure team is to provide a free, reliable, secure and scalable Cloud hosting platform to support Wikimedia contributors and developers to run tools, bots, data pipelines, and services that support Wikipedia and its sister projects. 

The Observability team’s mission is to provide insight into the health, performance and behaviour of production code and systems for teams within the Wikimedia Foundation and for volunteers at large.

As we form our internship cohort, we are looking for candidates who possess:

• Basic experience with at least one back end or front end programming language (e.g PHP, Javascript, Python) OR a mobile app language (Kotlin, Swift), OR a demonstrated interest in cybersecurity and/or privacy.

• Basic experience with databases.

• Basic experience with at least one scripting language.

• For some roles:

• Basic querying and data manipulation with SQL or other query languages

• Linux/command-line knowledge

• Understanding of networking, operating systems, or distributed systems concepts (latency, throughput, error rates). 

• Ability to work independently and be resourceful in solving problems.

• Ability to stay accountable to deliverable requirements deadlines.

• Effective and inclusive communication skills with diverse cultural and language communities.

• Willingness and hunger to learn, a positive attitude, empathy, and a sense of curiosity.

• The ability to flourish in a highly transparent and collaborative environment.

• A desire to make meaningful contributions to knowledge equity, free culture, and open access to global education.

About the Wikimedia Foundation

The Wikimedia Foundation is the nonprofit organization that operates Wikipedia and the other Wikimedia free knowledge projects. Our vision is a world in which every single human can freely share in the sum of all knowledge. We believe that everyone has the potential to contribute something to our shared knowledge, and that everyone should be able to access that knowledge freely. We host Wikipedia and the Wikimedia projects, build software experiences for reading, contributing, and sharing Wikimedia content, support the volunteer communities and partners who make Wikimedia possible, and advocate for policies that enable Wikimedia and free knowledge to thrive. 

The Wikimedia Foundation is a charitable, not-for-profit organization that relies on donations. We receive donations from millions of individuals around the world, with an average donation of about $15. We also receive donations through institutional grants and gifts. The Wikimedia Foundation is a United States 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization with offices in San Francisco, California, USA.

As an equal opportunity employer, the Wikimedia Foundation values having a diverse workforce and continuously strives to maintain an inclusive and equitable workplace. We encourage people with a diverse range of backgrounds to apply. We do not discriminate against any person based upon their race, traits historically associated with race, religion, color, national origin, sex, pregnancy or related medical conditions, parental status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, genetic information, or any other legally protected characteristics.

The Wikimedia Foundation is a remote-first organization with staff members including contractors based in 40+ countries*. Salaries at the Wikimedia Foundation are set in a way that is competitive, equitable, and consistent with our values and culture. The anticipated annual pay range of this position for applicants based within the United States is US$34.32 to $42.13 per hour with multiple individualized factors, including cost of living in the location, being the determinants of the offered pay. We neither ask for nor take into consideration the salary history of applicants. The compensation for a successful applicant will be based on their skills, experience and location.

*Please note that we are currently able to hire in the following US States for these internship roles: Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, District of Columbia*, Flor

About the role

Muon is seeking Ground Software Engineering Interns to help build the software that powers high-performance satellite constellations. The Software Engineering team at Muon is responsible for software on the spacecraft, at ground stations, in the cloud, and visualization and simulation. As an intern, you won't be on the sidelines, you can look forward to owning a project from start to finish which could involve enabling a new type of task for the spacecraft, simulating a new component, writing the software for a new piece of hardware, or deploying new algorithms for processing images and other sensor data from the spacecraft.

Muon is a fast growing company which offers interns the experience to get direct mentorship and have real impact on our programs. You'll collaborate with a dynamic team in a startup environment and have the chance to learn from some of the most accomplished and experienced aerospace professionals in the industry, in an experience where your decisions and contributions play a pivotal role in driving Muon's success. Summer internships will range between the months of May and September depending on university schedules, and the internship is full-time and on-site in Mountain View or San Jose, CA.

Responsibilities

• Own a well-scoped software project from design through implementation and testing, with mentorship from experienced engineers at each stage.

• Develop and contribute to software for ground software, or supporting development and test tools.

• Propose and iterate on software designs with guidance from the team.

• Participate in code reviews and document your work so other engineers can use and maintain it.

• Collaborate with software and hardware engineers and gain hands-on experience building reliable software for spacecraft.

jobs.title: Audit & Assurance Intern - AI and Data Science
Meritocracy Fellow
jobs.description:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.
 
The Program
 
We believe meritocracy is the operating system for execution: find ability wherever it exists, give people room to act, and judge them by the quality of what they do.

The American university once advanced this vision extraordinarily well. At its best, it found talented individuals from every background, exposed them to challenging ideas, and sent them into the world sharper, more capable, and imbued with purpose. When it worked, it was extraordinary.

Yet in recent decades, many of our finest institutions strayed from this calling. Admissions committees elevated other priorities. Classrooms rewarded conformity over honesty and rigor. Credentials replaced true capability. Cost became decoupled from value.

We launched the Meritocracy Fellowship to recover that highest purpose: find exceptionally talented individuals, forge them intellectually, give them responsibility, and judge them by their achievements alone. Based purely on merit and academic excellence, graduating high school students will be invited to interview, and select applicants will receive a Meritocracy Fellowship. Those that excel will obtain offers to join Palantir full time.

Skip the debt. Get the real education. Earn the Palantir degree.
 
The Curriculum
 
For five weeks, Fellows grapple with the ideas that shape our civilization. What is the West? Is it worth defending? In what ways is America exceptional within this broader context? And what is Palantir's mission in that context?

Fellows read great works, visit institutions at the frontiers of knowledge and public life, and work alongside one another to build something real. This is the education that universities were designed to deliver: rigorous, Socratic, grounded in the texts and ideas that actually matter. Not a lecture hall. Not a curriculum designed by committee. A room full of people who are smarter than you, expecting you to hold your own.

This initial period lays the intellectual foundation before Fellows join forward-deployed engineering or internal software teams. Fellows spend substantial time building in the first five weeks and learn from Palantirians working across engineering, product, security, deployment, and operations.

Our most vital technologies cannot be created by those indifferent to their purpose. Today's challenges demand builders who are guided by conviction and a clear sense of mission.
 
The Role
 
Once Fellows join Palantir's development or forward deployed engineering teams, they are treated like any other Palantir software engineer: joining a team and working alongside customers onsite.

Fellows are not given internship projects; they are given the responsibility of a full-time engineer. They learn the problem from the people who live it, build against real data, ship software, and iterate. The data is real. The stakes are real. The people depending on the outcome are real.

In this role, the challenges you'll seek will require a curious and analytical approach, a sharp intuition for product, and a strong degree of user insight. You will be matched to roles based on your skills, interests, and experience.

The only factor that determines whether you advance here is outcomes.

What We Value
• High degree of agency, autonomy, and maturity

• Extraordinary ability to confront open-ended and ambiguous problems

• Adaptive and introspective; willing to learn, guide, lead, and follow

• Ability to communicate and collaborate effectively with a variety of individuals, including engineers, users, and non-technical team members

• Willingness to learn proactively, make decisions independently, and ask questions when stuck

• Experience with programming, scripting, or statistical packages (e.g. Python, R, Matlab, SQL)
What We Require
• High school certificate of graduation at the start of the internship

• Candidates cannot be enrolled in an accredited U.S. university

• Candidates cannot have previously earned an undergraduate degree

• Spending fall 2027 (August - December) at Palantir exclusively; candidates cannot simultaneously be enrolled in university classes
Salary
 
The salary range for this position is estimated to be $5,400/month. Further note that total compensation for this position will be determined by each individual’s relevant qualifications, work experience, skills, and other factors. jobs.title: Strategic Finance & Analytics Intern (MBA)
jobs.description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join:

Airbnb is seeking MBA students to join the Finance organization as Strategic Finance & Analytics Interns for our 2027 Summer Intern Program from May 24, 2027 - August 13, 2027.

At Airbnb, we believe finance is about more than numbers. Our Strategic Finance & Analytics (SFA) team sits at the intersection of finance, strategy, and the business, partnering directly with leaders to decide where Airbnb invests, how we grow, and what we do next. We expect every member of the team to bring a CFO mindset to budget management, producing actionable insights, owning our performance story, and supporting day-to-day execution. 

We are looking for interns who are eager to learn, grow, and sharpen their strategic and analytical skills alongside leaders across Finance. While a return offer is never guaranteed, we have a track record of bringing exceptional summer interns back as full-time employees after graduation.

The Difference You Will Make:

You’ll be integrated into a team where you’ll contribute to challenging projects. Your manager, team, and our incredible employee community will strive to be superhosts to you during the summer. We provide the support, mentorship, fun, and real world experience needed to accelerate your learning and make a real impact on our product, as Airbnb revolutionizes connection, belonging, and travel. You can expect to:

• Analyze complex business problems and issues using data to provide insight to decision-makers

• Identify and interpret trends and patterns based on business data and market knowledge

• Construct and present forecasts, recommendations, and strategic/tactical plans to stakeholders and leaders

• Create specifications for reports and analysis based on business needs and required or available data elements.

The exact project you work on during your internship will be dependent on the team you are placed in. You’ll have the opportunity to learn more about the work during the interview process.

The Internship Experience

As an intern, you’ll get first-hand experience on what it is like to be a Strategic Finance & Analytics Partner at Airbnb. You’ll have the opportunity to: 

• Team up with colleagues from a wide variety of backgrounds and perspectives.

• Communicate with stakeholders, providing regular updates and insights.

• Seek and offer feedback in a supportive, growth-oriented environment.

• Participate in team meetings, learning sessions, and community events.

• Share your ideas—your unique perspective is valued and welcomed!

The exact project you work on during your internship will be dependent on the team you are placed in. You’ll have the opportunity to learn more about the work during the interview process.

Your Expertise:

We’re looking for first-year, full-time MBA students (expected graduation Spring 2028) at accredited U.S. business schools who bring the following skills and background:

• 3–5 years of professional experience in areas such as financial planning & analysis, corporate development, management consulting, private equity, investment banking, or business operations

• Excellent organizational and project management skills with the ability to define and execute projects independently

• Strong relationship-building skills with various internal and external stakeholders

• Clear, persuasive written and verbal communication, including presenting to senior leaders (e.g., the Chief Financial Officer or a VP of Finance)

• Robust quantitative skills and experience analyzing complex data to deliver actionable recommendations

• Experience with SQL, financial modeling, data analysis and visualization (Tableau or similar tools)

• AI fluency and sound AI judgment: you know how to apply AI effectively to the work and projects in front of you, and when not to

• Ability to manage your time and adapt to changing priorities

• Interest in high-growth, technology, or hospitality companies

• Authorization to work in the United States

Preferred but not required:

• Experience conducting industry research and due diligence

How to apply:

In addition to a resume, please submit a cover letter that addresses the following:

• why Airbnb,

• why you are interested in Strategic Finance & Analytics, 

• how this internship aligns with your long-term career goals, and

• how your background meets the expertise requirements listed above.

Deadline to apply: Sunday, November 1st at 11:45 pm PST

How We’ll Take Care of You:

Our job titles may span more than one career or degree level. This role may also be eligible for benefits and Employee Travel Credits. 

Currency: USD Pay Rate: $48 per hour

Your Location:

This position is US - Remote Eligible. The role may include occasional work at an Airbnb office or attendance at offsites, as agreed to with your manager. While the position is Remote Eligible, you must live in a state where Airbnb, Inc. has a registered entity. Click here for the up-to-date list of excluded states. This list is continuously evolving, so please check back with us if the state you live in is on the exclusion list. If your position is employed by another Airbnb entity, your recruiter will inform you what states you are eligible to work from. 

Equal Employment Opportunity:

Airbnb values diversity & belonging and is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. All individuals seeking employment at Airbnb are considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, gender, sex, marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, veteran status, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected characteristic. 

Reasonable Accommodations: We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process for applicants with disabilities. If you need assistance, or an accommodation, please let your recruiter know once you are contacted about a role.

A Note on Recruiting Scams: Scammers sometimes pose as Airbnb recruiters to get money or personal information from candidates. A few things that will always be true for Airbnb’s hiring process: our open roles are posted on Airbnb’s Career’s Page at careers.airbnb.com, and our recruiters correspond only from @airbnb.com or @ext.airbnb.com email addresses. Our recruiters will never ask for your Social Security number, bank account details, passport, or payment app information while you are interviewing. We’ll also never ask you to pay a fee, send money, deposit or cash a check, or purchase work-related equipment (such as a company laptop) during the interview process. We encourage candidates to remain vigilant of these recruiting scams and not share sensitive information if you do not believe an individual is actually affiliated with Airbnb.

About Tessera Labs

Tessera Labs is redefining how enterprises adop and operationalize Artificial Intelligence. Backed by Foundation and with a recent $60M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), we build multi-agent AI Systems that automate complex business workflows across platforms like SAP, Salesforce, Workday, Snowflake, Databricks and more.

Our mission: bring real AI automation to the enterprise - with speed and precision and measurable impact. We move fast, operate with extreme ownership, and build at the frontier of applied AI.

About the role

We're hiring a Full Stack Software Engineering Intern to help build Tessera Mosaic, where AI agents work alongside people to transform how enterprises operate. You'll help drive product problems end to end, from interfaces for understanding and controlling agents to the data and backend systems that power them.

You'll work closely with product and design, with real ownership over what we build and how we build it. If you enjoy turning ambiguous problems into polished products, you can have an outsized impact on a platform that's still early. You can lean toward frontend or backend depending on your preference, or do both.

What you'll do

 - Build product features in React and TypeScript on the frontend and/or Python on the backend, including APIs, data models, and services.

 - Take problems from a rough starting point to shipped: figure out what's actually being asked, dig into the data and code, propose an approach, and build it.

 - Build the tools that make AI agents understandable and controllable for the people using them: seeing what an agent is doing, reviewing its work, and stepping in when needed.

 - Work with data from systems like SAP, Salesforce, and Oracle, including their complex data models and real-world edge cases.

 - Partner with product and design to question assumptions, shape solutions, get feedback early, and iterate.

 - Strong product sense. You think about the people using what you build and have ideas about how to make it better, whether you're working on the frontend or the backend.

About Moment Energy

Independent energy is here. Help us deploy it.

Energy should be free. Free from aging grids, fragile supply chains, and unnecessary extraction. At Moment Energy, we’re building a world where clean power is abundant, affordable, and uninterrupted for everyone.

The world doesn’t need another promise about energy; it needs proof that a freer future is possible. Moment Energy is the pragmatic liberator of power, the only company certified to turn the largest untapped energy supply into independent energy.

Now is the moment. While the industry scraps millions of batteries with decades of life left, we put them to work by repurposing large-format batteries into advanced battery energy storage systems that deliver real-world impact.

We were told second-life batteries would never be safe enough or scalable enough. We didn’t argue, we engineered the solution. Today, Moment Energy delivers 5x the energy density and holds the certifications required to deploy energy independence at scale.

Now is the moment. Join us.

The Role

As an R&D Technician Co-op at Moment Energy, you will support the development of next-generation battery energy storage systems (BESS) by assisting with electronics prototyping, PCB assembly, wiring, and lab testing. Working closely with our electrical and mechanical engineering teams, you will help build, troubleshoot, and document hardware prototypes that bring new designs from concept to testing.

Responsibilities and Duties

• Perform surface mount and through-hole soldering, assembly, and rework for R&D printed circuit board (PCB) prototypes.

• Design, build, and troubleshoot custom electrical wiring harnesses and cable assemblies to support BESS, electronics, and lab testing setups.

• Assist the Electrical Engineering team in the creation of prototypes and test fixtures for new BESS and electronic designs.

• Create and maintain basic technical documentation, including detailed assembly instructions, and lab operating procedures (SOPs).

• Collaborate with electrical and mechanical engineers to ensure seamless integration of hardware during the prototyping phase.

The Student

We’re looking for individuals with the following traits, skills, and experiences:

• Currently enrolled in a college or university program in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering Technology, Mechatronics, or a related field.

• Basic understanding of electrical and electronic components, circuits, and wiring.

• Familiarity with soldering, PCB assembly, or electronics prototyping through coursework, personal projects, or previous experience.

• Comfortable using basic hand tools and electronic testing equipment, such as a multimeter.

• Strong attention to detail and a hands-on approach to troubleshooting and problem-solving.

• Willingness to learn, take direction, and collaborate with engineers in a fast-paced R&D environment.

• Able to follow technical instructions, maintain organized lab workspaces, and document work accurately.

Paid Time Off: Co-op’s receive three paid days off per term

Vibrant Culture & Perks: Open and collaborative office culture, frequent company socials and wellness programs (weekly yoga and fitness center), and free EV charging on-site.
Why join us?

• Be part of a mission-driven company focused on creating sustainable energy solutions and making a positive impact on the world.

• Collaborate closely with passionate co-founders and a team committed to innovation and excellence.

• Contribute to building and scaling a company from the ground up, where your work will have a direct and meaningful impact.

• Thrive in a workplace that values collaboration, wellness, and celebrating successes, with regular company socials, fitness sessions, and more.

We're a fast-paced and dynamic team.

Every day you'll be taking on a new challenge and learning something new. You'll take on a wide breadth of tasks and contribute to disrupting the battery industry. You'll be part of a tight-knit team that is working together to save the planet! Fun, health, and wellness are incorporated into our daily schedule and we encourage all our team members to bring innovative ideas to the table to create an interactive workplace. 

Moment Energy Benefits Highlights (full time, permanent employees only)

Financial Growth: Employee equity and a robust RRSP matching program.

Comprehensive Health Coverage: Extended health, dental, and vision benefits for you and your dependents through Manulife.

Generous Time Off & Flexibility: Paid time off plus a paid company closure between Christmas and New Year's, with a generous paid sick leave.

Moment Energy is an equal-opportunity employer. We are committed to inclusive, barrier-free recruitment and selection processes, including our work environment. We especially welcome applications from Indigenous peoples, members of racialized communities, persons with disabilities, women, and persons who identify as 2SLGBTQ+.

Our values are key to how we show up every day at Moment Energy! We keep them in the forefront of what we do, and they’re used everywhere. We refer to them when we have tough decisions to make, we give shoutouts based on living out these values, and we include them as part of our performance reviews.

We have 5 core values and 1 foundational pillar (Safety is our Foundation) which lays the groundwork for everything we do.

We prioritize the safety of our products, customers, employees, and the general public above all else. From the workshop to the field, we maintain the highest standards for our batteries in testing manufacturing and deployment, and daily operations. Safety is not only about procedures—it is about vigilance, responsibility, and speaking up when something does not feel right.

jobs.title: Software Engineer - Early Career - C++ & Systems
jobs.description:
About SirenOpt

SirenOpt helps manufacturers make better, safer, and more reliable micro- and nano-materials. These materials are the building blocks of critical sectors of the global economy such as batteries, computer chips, aircraft components, and power systems. But, surging material demand and growing complexity are pushing production to unprecedented scales and speeds, leaving manufacturers effectively flying blind. Small, undetected variations during production lead to wastage, lower performance, higher costs, and safety risks.

SirenOpt is changing this by developing a manufacturing intelligence platform that non-destructively probes materials during production, revealing critical internal information without damaging them. Using a novel combination of cold atmospheric plasma, physics-informed machine learning, and predictive analytics, SirenOpt generates unique, real-time material fingerprints that capture material signals not accessible through conventional measurement techniques. These insights give manufacturers unprecedented visibility into how materials behave as they are made.

We turn hidden data into actionable intelligence to help manufacturers reduce variability and thus increase yield and performance. The technology can be deployed as a standalone tool or integrated directly into factory production lines. SirenOpt is currently deploying early versions of its platform with some of the largest industrial manufacturers in the world across North America, Europe, and Asia.

About the job

Job Title: Software Engineer (Early Career) – C++ & Systems

Location: On-Site (San Leandro, CA)

Job Type: Full-Time

Role Overview

SirenOpt is seeking a Software Engineer to help build and maintain the real-time data pipeline behind our sensing platform: acquiring data from multiple sensors, processing and storing it on Linux-based systems, and delivering it to the applications our customers rely on. 

You will work primarily in modern C++ and Python, with mentorship from senior engineers, and you will be hands-on with real hardware in our lab to test and validate what you build. This is a role for someone who wants to grow into a well-rounded systems engineer by shipping production software end to end, from a first design discussion to a feature running at a customer site. 

What You'll Do

• Develop and maintain software components in modern C++ (C++17/20) for Linux-based systems, with guidance from senior engineers 

• Implement features, fix bugs, and write unit and integration tests across the data pipeline, from sensor acquisition through processing and storage to the services that deliver results to applications 

• Write and maintain Python scripts for automation, testing, and data analysis 

• Read, and where needed modify, existing code written in other languages across our codebase 

• Use AI coding tools (e.g., Claude Code, GitHub Copilot) to accelerate development, and verify their output through testing, profiling, and code review 

• Run the system on real hardware in the lab to test and validate your changes, including setting up sensors and collecting data 

• Participate in code reviews, both receiving and giving feedback, and follow team conventions for code quality 

• Help diagnose and debug issues across software and hardware boundaries, working with firmware and hardware engineers 

• Measure and improve performance of existing code under the direction of senior engineers

• Document your work so that others on the team can build on it

What We're Looking For

• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field (recent graduates welcome) 

• 0–2 years of professional software development experience; internships, co-ops, research, and substantial personal or open-source projects count 

• Solid foundation in C++, including memory management, references and pointers, the standard library, and basic object-oriented and generic programming 

• Strong ability to read, understand, and write Python, including working within existing Python codebases used for automation, testing, and data analysis 

• Ability to pick up new programming languages quickly; our codebase spans several languages and you will need to read, and occasionally modify, code outside of C++ and Python 

• Understanding of core computer science fundamentals: data structures, algorithms, operating systems, and concurrency basics 

• Comfortable with the everyday toolchain: Linux command line, build tools (CMake or similar), a debugger, and Git-based workflows (branches, pull requests, code review) 

• Hands-on experience using AI coding tools (e.g., Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Cursor) as part of a real development workflow, and the judgment to review and test what they produce 

• Comfortable working hands-on with lab and test equipment: setting up sensors, running the system on real hardware, and collecting data for testing and validation (we will train you on our specific equipment) 

• Clear written and verbal communication, and the ability to work well with teammates across disciplines

Nice to have:

• Experience with Qt, gRPC, or Protocol Buffers 

• Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines and automated testing 

• Experience with profiling and debugging tools such as perf, Valgrind, GDB, or sanitizers 

• Familiarity with hardware communication interfaces such as Ethernet, USB, or Serial 

• Contributions to open-source projects 

What You'll Learn

You will work on a real-time sensing platform that is already running at some of the largest manufacturers in the world, on a small team where your code reaches customers quickly.

• How a high-throughput, multi-sensor data pipeline is built end to end, from acquisition through processing and storage, and kept reliable in production

• Modern C++ and Linux systems engineering, with regular code review and mentorship from senior engineers

• How software, firmware, and hardware teams work together to ship a physical product

• How to use AI coding tools effectively and responsibly in a professional engineering workflow

• A clear path to grow into a mid-level engineer with ownership of your own components

Base Pay Range
$120,000—$160,000 USD

Benefits

• Equity and Salary compensation depends on experience 

• Health, Dental, Vision plans provided

• 401k matching provided

• Time off: 20 days of PTO per year, plus approximately 15 paid US holidays per year

jobs.title: Software Engineer - Firefox Desktop Integrations
jobs.description:
Why Mozilla?

Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser. Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people. 

About this team:

The Firefox team is a community of engineers who care deeply about delivering the fastest, friendliest, most usable browser possible. We are responsible for making the things you see in the browser work securely, quickly, and well! The Desktop integrations team is a cross-functional team that focuses on updates, installs and integrating Firefox with different OS platforms. As part of the Desktop Integrations team, you will be responsible for all things related to OS integration (particularly Windows and macOS) and helping us grow our user base. 

Our team is geographically distributed, and working in the open is the norm. We contribute to the code driving the Firefox browser on all desktop platforms.

About the role: 

A Software Engineer is an early-career individual contributor who is growing in their ability to take on more complex tasks. At Mozilla, this role involves working on engineering projects that typically span several weeks and require collaboration with peers. Software Engineers at this level contribute to implementation, ask thoughtful questions, and raise blockers early. They communicate clearly within their team, follow team processes, and steadily build expertise in their domain.

What you’ll do:

• Assist in the development and maintenance of Firefox features related to installs, updates, and OS integrations.

• Work on improvements to the Firefox installation and update process with guidance from senior engineers.

• Support efforts to solve platform-specific challenges on Windows and/or macOS, particularly where Firefox must interact directly with the operating system.

• Collaborate with your manager and teammates to define and scope tasks, with regular check-ins to share progress and ask for support when needed.

• Participate in code reviews to grow your understanding and contribute to a high-quality codebase.

jobs.title: Research Intern
jobs.description:
At Atom Computing, we build quantum computers using arrays of optically trapped neutral atoms that will empower customers to achieve unprecedented computational breakthroughs. Join a world-class team of scientists, engineers, and business professionals to advance the state-of-the-art in quantum computing.
We are seeking a research intern to contribute to the architecture and strategy of error correction on neutral atom quantum computers. Atomic qubit arrays provide a path to the large-scale quantum computers that will deliver fault-tolerant, error-corrected logical qubits.
You will work with our Quantum Error Correction team to tackle targeted research questions related to fault-tolerant quantum computing using neutral-atom hardware. We are specifically seeking candidates with expertise in the following areas:
Applications of machine learning/AI for quantum computing
QEC codes and fault-tolerant logic
Magic state production
Synthesis and compilation of fault-tolerant algorithms
Design, simulation, and execution of fault-tolerant protocols

Responsibilities
• 
Contribute to new and ongoing research projects at Atom Computing, particularly those related to quantum error correction and fault tolerance.

• Currently pursuing a PhD in Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related field.

• Willingness to translate concepts into demonstrations running on actual quantum computing hardware.

NVIDIA is hiring passionate, world-class computer science studetns to work in its Compute Developer Technology (Devtech) team. With highly competitive salaries and a comprehensive benefits package, NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology industry's most desirable employers. jobs.title: Seam Intern - Embodied AI
jobs.description:
Job Description
Work Arrangement: 
Hybrid: This internship is categorized as on-site. The selected intern is expected to report to the office 3 days a week. 

Location: 
Sunnyvale, CA 

About the Team
The State Estimation, Alignment, and Mapping (SEAM) team develops the sensing and spatial understanding capabilities that help autonomous vehicles know where they are, interpret their surroundings, and maintain reliable operation over time. The team works on sensor fusion, state estimation, real-time localization, static and dynamic sensor calibration, next-generation mapping, and capabilities that support primary and fallback driving systems.

SEAM combines robotics, computer vision, estimation theory, machine learning, geometry, and production software engineering. Our work supports both onboard, real-time autonomy and offboard, high-fidelity map and data-generation workflows.

About the Role
As a SEAM Intern, you will work on a well-scoped research or engineering project related to sensing, estimation, localization, mapping, or autonomy reliability. You will collaborate with experienced engineers and researchers to design algorithms, implement software, evaluate system performance, and understand how sensing capabilities operate in real-world autonomous driving systems.

Potential focus areas include:
• State Estimation and Sensor Fusion: Combine information from multiple sensors and vehicle signals to estimate position, orientation, motion, and other states robustly.
• Sensor Alignment and Calibration: Develop methods for static and dynamic calibration, sensor registration, and maintaining alignment as vehicle and environmental conditions change.
• Localization: Improve real-time localization and map-based positioning across diverse driving environments.
• Next-Generation Mapping: Build or evaluate high-fidelity, large-scale maps that provide useful spatial context beyond the immediate sensor range.
• Fallback and Secondary Capabilities: Develop reliable estimation, localization, or mapping functions that support safe operation when nominal system capabilities are unavailable or degraded.

What You’ll Do
• Develop, prototype, and evaluate algorithms for sensor fusion, state estimation, localization, calibration, mapping, or related autonomy capabilities.
• Work with camera, lidar, radar, inertial, vehicle, map, and other multimodal data sources.
• Implement software and tools for data processing, visualization, offline analysis, simulation, and system evaluation.
• Analyze accuracy, robustness, latency, and failure modes across diverse operating conditions.
• Apply software engineering best practices, including design reviews, code reviews, automated testing, continuous integration, and documentation.
• Collaborate with perception, planning, controls, robotics, systems engineering, and vehicle-program partners.
• Communicate technical findings and contribute to design discussions and project documentation.

Required Qualifications
• Currently enrolled in or pursuing a Master’s or Ph.D. degree in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related technical field.
• Demonstrated experience through coursework, research, academic projects, or professional work in robotics, state estimation, sensor fusion, computer vision, localization, mapping, controls, or a related area.
• Strong programming skills in C++ and/or Python.
• Strong foundation in linear algebra, probability, geometry, optimization, or estimation methods.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
• Ability to work collaboratively in a cross-functional, team-oriented environment.
• Strong written, verbal, and presentation skills.
• Availability to work full-time, 40 hours per week, during the internship period.

Preferred Qualifications
• Experience with Kalman filtering, factor graphs, SLAM, visual-inertial odometry, bundle adjustment, point clouds, geometric computer vision, or multi-sensor calibration.
• Familiarity with autonomous vehicles, advanced driver assistance systems, robotics, ROS, or safety-critical systems.
• Experience with large-scale sensor or map datasets, simulation, data association, or offline evaluation.
• Experience with machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or JAX.
• Familiarity with real-time systems, distributed systems, high-performance computing, or production software development
• Intent to return to a degree program after completion of the internship or co-op.
• Must be graduating between December 2027 and June 2028

Compensation: 
• The monthly salary range for this role is $11,800 – $14,600 per month  
• GM will provide a one-time lump sum taxable stipend payment to eligible students selected for the 2027 Student Program. 

What You’ll Get from Us
• Paid U.S. GM holidays.
• GM Family First Vehicle Discount Program.
• Potential for growth within GM based on performance and business needs.

• Mentorship and hands-on experience with the data and ML foundations behind autonomy

We believe we all must make a choice every day – individually and collectively – to drive meaningful change through our words, our deeds and our culture. Every day, we want every employee to feel they belong to one General Motors team.

Who We Are:
 
Every transaction matters. Every Canadian matters. At Interac, we protect both — driving trust, security, and inclusion, so our digital economy thrives. 
 
Founded in 1984, Interac connects Canadians through secure digital payments, advanced identity verification and industry-leading fraud protection. Connecting banks, businesses, and individuals, Interac enables millions to send, receive, and manage money safely and effortlessly every day — across both digital and physical environments.
 
As the backbone of Canada’s financial ecosystem, Interac facilitates over 20 million transactions daily, supported by trusted partnerships with government and financial institutions. Consistently ranked as Canada’s most reputable financial technology brand, Interac is deeply embedded in the daily lives of Canadians.

Who You Will Work With:
 
The intern will join Interac's Money Movement product team, working closely with product managers, engineers, designers, and business stakeholders. You will contribute to shaping product features, gathering insights, and driving key initiatives.
 
This is a hands-on role that will be responsible for supporting the Money Movement team in driving product evolution and supporting day-to-day product activities. You are someone who can quickly understand (or rapidly learn) the payments ecosystem, demonstrate strong strategic capability, and bring fresh, forward looking ideas to work.

• Provide general support to the product roadmap, defining requirements, conducting product research, and assisting in squads to deliver corporate objectives
• Conduct market research and analyze user feedback to identify opportunities for product improvements.
• Prepare documentation and conduct research as requested by the squad and/or product team
• Work with large, unclean data sources to visualize/democratize data and insights, assess emerging themes, and showcase how solutions could fit within the broader ecosystem

At Symbotic, Early Career talent plays a meaningful role in helping us reimagine the future of supply chain automation. Through our Internship and Co-op programs, students have the opportunity to contribute to real projects, collaborate with experienced engineers and business leaders, and gain hands-on exposure to the technologies powering our end-to-end robotics and automation solutions. We are looking for curious, motivated students who are excited to solve complex problems, bring new perspectives to cross-functional teams, and see their work make an impact in a fast-moving, innovative environment. 

Along the way, Interns and Co-ops are supported through mentorship, professional development, networking opportunities, and a robust calendar of events designed to help them build community and grow their careers. Symbotic offers transportation and housing benefits for students who meet our relocation requirements. 

Continue reading below to learn more about this exciting opportunity! 

What you'll do 
• Brainstorm with engineers on cross-functional teams to conceptualize and develop real-time high-performance software to manipulate real-world objects with high accuracy. 
• Apply best practices to the design of data structures and algorithms. Strive for both simplicity and performance. 
• Produce high-quality software contributing to projects that have a significant impact on the business. 
• Simulate robot motion using internal simulation tools during feature development. 
• Develop motion planning algorithms and state machines for robotic manipulators. 
• Design, develop, and implement control software for specialized end-of-arm tools and grippers. 
• Define metrics for pick and place quality in the field with different sensors and cameras. 
• Work broadly across teams to facilitate integration of specialized manipulation systems from hardware to software. 
• Optimize processes using data-driven and machine learning, with ownership from data curation and training to inference. 
• Support system testing of systems and subsystems. 
• Provide technical support for hardware design as needed. 
• Troubleshoot system problems in production or design by investigating issues related to product performance or production difficulties. 
• Evaluate and process engineering change requests 

What you’ll need 
• Pursuing a Bachelor's or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Engineering or related field. 
• Experience with general-purpose programming environments, languages and scripting systems, data analysis packages: Linux, C++, Python, Matlab. 
• Knowledge of Git, Jira, and Confluence or similar tools. 
• Familiarity with DevOps or CI/CD – GitHub automation and docker or Jenkins. 
• Experience with simulation tools such as MuJoCo, NVIDIA IsaacSim, PyBullet. 
• Familiarity with Forward Kinematics and Inverse Kinematics for custom kinematic chains. 
• Strong Linear Algebra and 3D Geometry fundamentals. 
• Familiarity with Machine Learning Fundamentals and Libraries 
• Experience with libraries such as OMPL, OpenRAVE, NVIDIA cuRobo, OpenCV, PCL, ROS, Boost, Eigen. 
• Hands on experience with embedded systems and platforms like Arduino, STM32, ESP32 or Raspberry Pi. Integrating sensors, motors and actuators using CAN, SPI, I2C. 
• Preferred experience with either of the following: motion planning algorithms, trajectory optimization and grasping. 
• You are interested in working in a dynamic Agile/Scrum based environment. 
• You possess strong computer science fundamentals: data structures and algorithms. 

Our Environment 
• Up to 10% of travel may be required. Employees must have a valid driver’s license and the ability to drive and/or fly to client and other customer locations. 
• The employee is responsible for owning a credit card and managing expenses personally to be reimbursed on a bi-weekly basis. 
About Symbotic
Symbotic is an automation technology leader reimagining the supply chain with its end-to-end, AI-powered robotic and software platform. Symbotic reinvents the warehouse as a strategic asset for the world’s largest retail, wholesale, and food & beverage companies. Applying next-gen technology, high-density storage and machine learning to solve today's complex distribution challenges, Symbotic enables companies to move goods with unmatched speed, agility, accuracy and efficiency. As the backbone of commerce the Symbotic platform transforms the flow of goods and the economics of supply chain for its customers. For more information, visit www.symbotic.com.
 
We are a community of innovators, collaborators and pioneers who embrace our differences, because we know unique perspectives make us stronger and smarter. Every perspective matters. We depend on the collective voices of our employees, customers and community to help guide us as we build a better place to work – for you and the world. That’s why we’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer. 
We do not discriminate based on race, color, ethnicity, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship status, marital status, disability, gender identity, gender expression, veteran status, or genetic information. 

The base range for this position in the posted location is $32.00 - $41.80 however, base pay offered may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. The compensation package includes medical, dental, vision, disability, 401K, PTO and/or other benefits.

jobs.title: Quant Analyst Intern
jobs.description:
This position is within the Quantitative Services team of the Post Trade Solutions division at LSEG based in Boston.
 
The Quantitative Services team is responsible for the development of ORE, its dependent services, and implementation of ORE in major financial institutions to deliver transparent, state-of-the-art risk management. 
 
To be eligible, you must be in your penultimate year of graduate study and due to complete your degree on or before summer 2027. You should have a predicted PhD or master’s degree in Math, Physics, Financial Engineering or other quantitative fields.
 
The successful candidate will work as part of a team of Quants to develop solutions for our risk analytics services. 

Role Summary:
 
• Contributing to the development of Open-Source Risk Engine (ORE). 
• Supporting the infrastructure for the IM Risk Generation (IMRG) service. 
• Pricing client portfolios and performing stress-testing and backtesting using ORE 
• Utilizing ORE to calculate risk (VaR, SIMM, etc.) on client portfolios 
• Translating client portfolios into the ORE XML format. 
• Collaborating with collateral management and risk teams to build financial applications 
 
What we are looking for:  
We are passionate about recruiting people who are interested in pursuing a career within Financial Engineering and would like to learn about the full breadth of our business – and are interested in playing a part of our development, as it grows and diversifies.  
• Interest in Quantitative Finance, demonstrated through studies, projects or independent work 
• A good understanding of at least Python or C++ 
• Familiarity with Git, LaTex, is ideal but not essential 
• Having functional knowledge on stochastic models/SDEs, e.g. Ornstein-Uhlenbeck/Hull-White model, Black-Scholes model, etc. 
• Someone who can collaborate with others, using their communication skills in the process. 
• A curiosity for data and an ability to analyse information to draw conclusions and propose solutions.  
• Knowledge of financial derivatives and pricing techniques, e.g. finite difference, Monte Carlo Simulation, etc.

jobs.title: PhD Researcher Intern - Agentic 3D Modeling in Immersive Environments
jobs.description:
Job Requisition ID #

26WD101374

Position Overview 
As a Research intern at Autodesk Research, you will explore and apply novel technologies and techniques to empower our customers in designing and building a better, safer, and more sustainable world. We are a team of researchers, engineers, and industry domain experts working on projects that range from learning-based design systems, computer vision, graphics, robotics, human-computer interaction, sustainability, simulation, manufacturing, architectural design and construction. 

Working with a multidisciplinary research team across AI, spatial computing, AEC, and human perception, you’ll develop and evaluate methods that interconnect different representations of the built environment within immersive, editable world models. Possible research directions may include exploring editing non-traditional 3d geometries such as gaussian splats, building multi-layered spatial representations of architectural spaces (simulations, physics, rendering, reality capture), and controlling 3d modeling and design environments and processes with agentic workflows. 

You’ll build research prototypes and explore how this work could inform future Autodesk design workflows. 

Responsibilities 

• Research multimodal AI approaches for the generation and editing of novel 3d representations of built environments. 
• Develop methods using foundation models, AI agents, and/or world models. 
• Work with multimodal datasets, including visual, spatial, behavioral, and physics simulations data. 
• Design experiments and benchmarks to evaluate AI predictions against human responses. 
• Build and evaluate research prototypes for real and simulated environments. 
• Document and communicate findings through papers, presentations, and demonstrations. 

Minimum Qualifications 

• Currently pursuing a PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Computer Graphics, Computational Design, or a related field - with a completion date in 2028 or later. 
• Research experience in AI/ML, computer vision, reality capture and 3d reconstruction, 3d modeling or geometry generation, or a related computational field. 
• Strong programming skills, ideally with Python and modern ML frameworks. 
• Experience designing computational experiments and working with complex datasets. 
• Strong collaboration and communication skills. 
• Track record of contributions to the field, demonstrated through related projects, open-source work, or publications. 

Preferred Qualifications 

Experience in one or more of the following: multimodal AI or vision-language models; world models, AI agents, or spatial intelligence; 3D, simulation, or virtual environments; human perception or human-centered AI; modern 3D modeling and reconstruction methods; AEC or computational design; Solid understanding of 3D modeling systems and data pipelines 

About the Research Intern Program (US) 

The 2027 Research Internship Program is a 16-week paid program running from May 24 to Sept 10, 2027. You’ll contribute to meaningful projects, learn from industry leaders, and take part in tech talks and development opportunities. Internships align with Autodesk’s Flexible Workplace approach, supporting office, remote, and hybrid work based on business and team needs. 

Learn More

About Autodesk
Welcome to Autodesk! Amazing things are created every day with our software – from the greenest buildings and cleanest cars to the smartest factories and biggest hit movies. We help innovators turn their ideas into reality, transforming not only how things are made, but what can be made.

We take great pride in our culture here at Autodesk – it’s at the core of everything we do. Our culture guides the way we work and treat each other, informs how we connect with customers and partners, and defines how we show up in the world.

When you’re an Autodesker, you can do meaningful work that helps build a better world designed and made for all. Ready to shape the world and your future? Join us!

Salary Transparency

Salary is one part of Autodesk’s competitive compensation package. Offers are based on the candidate’s experience, educational level, and geographic location, and can exceed this range.

For U.S.-based roles, we expect a starting annualized intern base salary to be between:
• $47,840 and $95,680 (undergraduate students)
• $72,800 and $118,500 (Masters/MBA students)
• $118,560 and $162,240 (PhD students)

Equal Employment Opportunity 
At Autodesk, we're building a diverse workplace and an inclusive culture to give more people the chance to imagine, design, and make a better world. Autodesk is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and considers all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status or any other legally protected characteristic. We also consider for employment all qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with applicable law.

Belonging
We take pride in cultivating a culture of belonging where everyone can thrive. Learn more here: https://www.autodesk.com/company/global-belonging

This role may require in-person onboarding and/or in-person ID verification.

jobs.description:
Data Science Intern

Company:
Boeing Vancouver

Calling all university students! Join our team of Student interns and embark on an extraordinary journey alongside seasoned professionals. Gain invaluable skills and knowledge as you dive into real-world tasks, tackle exciting challenges, and receive top-notch training. Plus, get the chance to contribute to special projects that will set you apart. Don't miss out on this thrilling opportunity – apply now and take your university experience to the next level!
 
Boeing Vancouver is seeking various Data Science Intern for our internship program. The Data Scientist intern will be reporting to the Manager of AI & Analytics. This is a full-time internship opportunity that is based at our office in Richmond, British Columbia and is up to 8 months in length, starting in early January 2027.
 
As a Data Scientist Intern, you will have to combine the skills of a developer and a detective, drawing on a wide palette of mathematics, statistics, machine learning, and programming techniques to unravel mysteries too subtle for the naked eye. You will get to work closely with our customers, building their trust, studying their problems and business needs, and you will blend artistry with science to visualize and explain your findings and stories.
 
Benefits of a Boeing Internship

• Have the opportunity to take part in impactful business projects.
• Network with experienced professionals.
• Engage in a strong student network.
• Gain valuable exposure in the Aerospace industry.
 
Position Responsibilities:
 
• Work directly with an assigned mentor or a buddy.
• Work closely with our customers/stakeholders to understand their business problems.
• Conduct exploratory analyses and data set characterizations.
• Research and propose (where applicable) appropriate technology/method to address business problem.
• Execute data science and analytics project tasks.
• Coordinate internal documentation and quality reviews.
• Effectively communicate technical approach, assumptions, help needed and business outcomes to project team, analytics leadership and customers.
 
This position is hybrid. This means that the selected candidate will be required to perform some work onsite at Richmond location. This is at the hiring team’s discretion and could potentially change in the future.

• Experience working with Python

• Must be legally able to work in Canada

jobs.title: Integrated Circuit Intern
jobs.description:
Overview:
Draper is an independent, nonprofit research and development company headquartered in Cambridge, MA. The 2,000+ employees of Draper tackle important national challenges with a promise of delivering successful and usable solutions. From military defense and space exploration to biomedical engineering, lives often depend on the solutions we provide. Our multidisciplinary teams of engineers and scientists work in a collaborative environment that inspires the cross-fertilization of ideas necessary for true innovation. For more information about Draper, visit www.draper.com.

Job Description Summary:
An ASIC Design Intern in the Silicon Architecture group contributes to the design of integrated circuits from conceptual phases through detailed design, implementation, verification, test and delivery to our customers. The Architect is responsible for developing initial architectural concepts and vetting them through modeling, analysis, and simulation. The Architect works with both Analog and Digital Circuit Designers to identify opportunities for trades across domains which enable the most efficient design solution. The Architect develops top level and circuit-level specifications, develops conceptual circuit designs, reviews detailed block-level designs during implementation, conducts chip level-planning with implementation team, and provides inputs to verification and test planning.
Job Description:
Duties/Responsibilities
• Design, develop, and enhancement engineering solutions for challenging problems. 

• Implement, test, perform analysis, and provide documentation support.

• Generate and present test reports including plots, tables, evaluation criteria, and conclusions from data collected and analyzed throughout the test process. 

• Complete assignments designed to develop a practical knowledge of processes, procedures, equipment, facilities, and systems as well as their interrelationships within engineering disciplines. 

• Performs other duties as assigned. 

Program Requirements 
• Enrolled in an accredited full-time undergraduate or graduate degree program required. 

• There is flexibility regarding hours and program duration based on applicant’s school schedule and availability. 

Skills/Abilities 
• Excellent written and oral communication skills. 

• Excellent work ethic with the ability to work independently or in a team environment. 

• Ability to adapt to ever-changing environments, risks, and vulnerabilities. 

• Strong computer skills including MS Word, PowerPoint and Excel.

Additional Job Description:
Duties/Responsibilities
• Contribute to integrated circuit-based solutions to complex customer problems.
• Contribute to integrated circuit requirements based on customer needs.
• Design and simulate circuits using functional modeling tools (e.g. MATLAB, Simulink, System Verilog)
• Design and simulate circuits at the transistor level to implement architecture
• Perform System-on-chip (SOC) design trades between analog, digital hardware, and software implementations to deliver optimized designs.
• Evaluate feasibility and costs/benefits of algorithm implementation in hardware vs software.
• Participate in top level verification planning with verification team.
• Thrive in multidisciplinary design teams, communicating effectively to peers and supervisors.
• Develop design documentation, e.g. architectural description, interface definition, and requirements.
• Contribute to test plans and conduct bench-level testing
Qualifications
• Proficiency with Cadence or equivalent integrated circuit design tools e.g. Virtuoso, Genus, Innovus, Tempus, Voltus
• Excellent verbal and written communication skills
• Excellent mathematical skills
• Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail
• Excellent time management skills with the proven ability to meet deadlines
Preferred Qualifications
• Proficiency or interest in learning high level mixed-signal modeling & verification tools such as System Verilog, SV-RNM, Verilog-AMS
• Proficient in scripting (e.g. Python, SKILL) for automating aspects of the design, implementation, verification, and test flows.

Applicants selected for this position may be required to obtain and maintain a government security clearance

jobs.title: Electronics Design Co-op
jobs.description:
Company Overview
At Motorola Solutions, we believe that everything starts with our people. We’re a global close-knit community, united by the relentless pursuit to help keep people safer everywhere. We build and connect technologies to help protect people, property and places. Our solutions foster the collaboration that’s critical for safer communities, safer schools, safer hospitals, safer businesses, and ultimately, safer nations. Connect with a career that matters, and help us build a safer future.

Aperçu de l’entreprise
Chez Motorola Solutions, nous pensons que tout commence par nos employés. Nous sommes une communauté mondiale soudée, unie par la volonté incessante de contribuer à la sécurité des personnes partout dans le monde. Nous concevons et connectons des technologies qui contribuent à protéger les personnes, les biens et les infrastructures. Nos solutions favorisent la collaboration essentielle pour améliorer la sécurité des populations, des écoles, des hôpitaux, des entreprises et, finalement, des nations. Connectez-vous à une carrière qui compte et aidez-nous à bâtir un avenir plus sûr.

Department Overview
At Motorola Solutions we are helping solve some of the biggest challenges around safety and physical security by developing advanced artificial intelligence (AI) technologies and products that are used to help keep people, businesses, and cities around the world safer. Avigilon, a Motorola Solutions company, designs, develops, and manufactures advanced AI, video analytics, network video management software and hardware, surveillance cameras, and access control solutions that help change the way people interact with their security systems.
Job Description

Our co-ops don’t wash cars or do coffee runs. They also don’t work on side projects. Our co-ops are treated like full team members and are given the opportunity to learn what being an electronics design engineer is like in the real world. You’ll have the opportunity to learn new technologies and best practices in design, layout, and testing of high speed circuits. You’ll also have a lot of fun and make a lot of friends. The State of Wisconsin Investment Board (SWIB), founded in 1951, is a premier global investment organization responsible for managing the more than $178 billion of assets of the fully funded Wisconsin Retirement System (WRS), the State Investment Fund and other state funds. Through SWIB’s effective and innovative investment management, WRS remains one of the only fully funded US public pensions. The WRS consistently ranks among the 10 largest public pension funds in the U.S. SWIB is recognized by the investment industry for our teamwork and innovation. SWIB pursues sophisticated global investment strategies across the asset and risk allocation spectrum. Providers across the investment ecosystem seek to partner with SWIB.
Serving more than 703,000 beneficiaries of the WRS, SWIB is a mission-driven organization focused on providing a strong financial future to those who committed their careers to public service. For public employees and the 1,607 Wisconsin employers who contribute on their behalf, we are a trusted partner. Our team innovates continuously to meet the challenges of an evolving investment landscape while growing and protecting the assets of the WRS.
SWIB provides a strong, steady economic pillar for the state of Wisconsin by growing the trust funds under its management, managing risk, and optimizing costs of the long term. We are a mission-driven organization and the participants we serve are our mission. By bringing a disciplined, prudent, and innovative approach to market opportunities, SWIB has been successful in generating required returns and maintaining the trust of the beneficiaries and stakeholders of the funds we oversee.

The Liquidity Management and Beta Implementation (LMBI) division of SWIB is tasked with managing the funds of the State’s money fund (State Investment Fund), centrally managing all our passive Beta allocations, arranging for all the leverage used as part of our asset allocation process, optimizing our use of collateral and trading in the public markets on behalf of all portfolios in SWIB.

Working at NLR
NLR is located at the foothills of the Rocky Mountains in Golden, Colorado is the nation's primary laboratory for energy systems research and development.
Join the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR), where world-class scientists, engineers, and experts are accelerating energy innovation through breakthrough research and systems integration. From our mission to our collaborative culture, NLR stands out in the research community for its commitment to an affordable and secure energy future. Spanning foundational science to applied systems engineering and analysis, we focus on solving complex challenges to deliver advanced, secure, reliable, and cost-effective energy solutions. Our work helps strengthen U.S. industries, support job creation, and promote national economic growth.

At NLR, you'll find a mission-driven environment supported by state-of-the-art facilities, multidisciplinary research teams, and strong collaborations with industry, academia, and other national laboratories. We offer robust professional development opportunities, and a competitive benefits package designed to support your career and well-being.

Job Description
The intern will conduct hands-on research at the intersection of machine learning, statistics, and critical energy infrastructure security. The position focuses on enhancing the reliability, transparency, and operator-readiness of AI-driven cybersecurity tools used to secure power grid substations and physical assets, with a primary focus on explainability and robust uncertainty bounds.

· Explainable AI (XAI): Design and implement XAI methods (e.g., attribution maps, rule extraction, root-cause analyses) to make complex ML models transparent and auditable for control-room operators and system administrators.
· Confidence & Uncertainty Quantification: Apply statistical techniques and frameworks (e.g., conformal prediction, Bayesian neural networks, or ensemble methods) to quantify model confidence and measure predictive uncertainty in real-time.
· Grid Dataset Analysis: Analyze cyber-physical power system security datasets (such as 9-Bus system baseline and cyber-physical anomaly runs) to extract feature patterns and validate anomaly detection model behavior.
· Model Safety & Robustness: Explore machine learning safety techniques, including model steering, to ensure grid security models behave predictably under distribution shifts or input corruptions.
· Visualization & Alert Design: Support research into visualization methods and alert design that present explainability and confidence metrics clearly to operators, assisting with alert prioritization.
· Collaboration & Reporting: Partner with cybersecurity researchers and AI development teams to integrate explainability modules, document results, and compile guidelines for deploying reliable AI models.
.

Working at NLR
NLR is located at the foothills of the Rocky Mountains in Golden, Colorado is the nation's primary laboratory for energy systems research and development.
Join the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR), where world-class scientists, engineers, and experts are accelerating energy innovation through breakthrough research and systems integration. From our mission to our collaborative culture, NLR stands out in the research community for its commitment to an affordable and secure energy future. Spanning foundational science to applied systems engineering and analysis, we focus on solving complex challenges to deliver advanced, secure, reliable, and cost-effective energy solutions. Our work helps strengthen U.S. industries, support job creation, and promote national economic growth.

At NLR, you'll find a mission-driven environment supported by state-of-the-art facilities, multidisciplinary research teams, and strong collaborations with industry, academia, and other national laboratories. We offer robust professional development opportunities, and a competitive benefits package designed to support your career and well-being.

Job Description
The Advanced Computing Solutions Group in the Computational Science Center at the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) has an opening for a graduate student researcher in connected and automated vehicle communications modeling, with an emphasis on data analysis and machine learning.

Vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication lets vehicles talk to each other and to roadside infrastructure, and it is the backbone of cooperative driving automation. Field-testing V2X at the scale needed to see its effect on traffic would take hundreds of roadside units and thousands of equipped vehicles, which is cost-prohibitive, so simulation is the practical path.
 
The intern will work with NLR colleagues to analyze field V2X data and develop new V2X models for simulation.
 
We are looking for a motivated researcher with strong data and programming skills and an interest in the mission of NLR. The successful candidate will collaborate with NLR researchers.
 
Responsibilities include:
• Clean, process, and analyze large-scale V2X field-test logs to characterize communication performance (e.g., packet delivery ratio, latency, and range) as a function of distance, device density, and environmental conditions.
• Help calibrate and validate microscopic LTE-V2X communication models against the field-test data.
• Develop and train machine-learning surrogate (approximate macroscopic) models of V2X behavior from large sets of simulation data, and evaluate their accuracy and computational efficiency.
• Write well-documented Python code and run workflows on NLR’s high-performance computing systems.
• Document results and contribute to technical reports, presentations, and publications.
.

• Experience applying machine learning to scientific or engineering data (e.g., scikit-learn, PyTorch, or TensorFlow).
• Coursework or project experience in at least one of: wireless communications or networking, transportation or traffic engineering, or data science.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work on a multi-laboratory team.

Preferred Qualifications
• Familiarity with V2X technologies (C-V2X/LTE-V2X, 5G NR sidelink, or DSRC), SAE J2735 messages, or wireless channel modeling.
• Experience with traffic simulation (Aimsun, SUMO, or VISSIM) or connected and automated vehicle modeling (e.g., car-following or cooperative adaptive cruise control).
• Experience with co-simulation frameworks (e.g., HELICS) or network simulators (e.g., ns-3, OMNeT++/Veins).
