jobs.description:
NORMAL COMPUTING | BUILD WITH US

Normal is an applied AI company solving the hardest problems in AI and silicon. We build foundational hardware and software for the semiconductor industry, critical AI infrastructure, and the broader systems that power our world, in partnership with the world's most advanced institutions. We work as one team across New York City, Silicon Valley (Mountain View), London, Copenhagen, and Seoul.


THE ROLE

As an early-career Product Manager, you'll work with the Product Lead and the engineering teams to help build the AI systems and autoresearch platform our ASIC team needs to tapeout unconventional, physics-based architecture. We are rethinking the chip design system from the ground up, automating the process of research: exploring the full design space, generating candidate architectures, evaluating them at appropriate levels of fidelity, and feeding learnings from experiments run in hardware labs and deployed silicon into the next generation chip. Domains of exploration include RTL optimization, design verification, and continual learning from experiment results. You'll help decide what we build, then be accountable for delivering on the incremental milestones to tapeout.

On any given day, you might sit with a chip architect benchmarking novel architectures, shadow a verification debug session and come back with a proposal for what to automate, scope out the requirements and success criteria for a custom EDA tool, or prototype an experiment dashboard. This is a building role. You'll write specs, run experiments, and use coding agents to prototype and land fixes yourself. When you have an idea, we would rather you spend an afternoon prototyping a rough version than a week describing it.

No semiconductor background is required to start. In your first few months the bar is understanding how the team works, asking the questions that move a design discussion forward, and earning trust by following through on deliverables.



WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - AI tooling scope: Investigate where the ASIC team's time actually goes, decide what we build, then be accountable for whether it gets used.

 - Specs and prototypes: Write the requirements docs and user journeys that engineering builds from. Where a working prototype communicates faster than a document, build the prototype instead.

 - Prototype to production: Work with engineers to turn a promising prototype into something the ASIC team can rely on.

 - Shipping small changes: Work in the codebase with coding agents, open PRs for bug fixes or UI changes, learn from code reviews from engineers, and develop judgment about which changes are yours to make.
   


WHAT MAKES YOU A GREAT FIT

 - A degree in CS, EE, physics, math, or similar, or the equivalent taught to yourself.

 - 1-3 years of experience in product management, engineering, research, technical program management, or a related technical role.

 - You can point to something that was your idea and that you made real.

 - Fluency with coding agents. You already use Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or something similar as a normal part of how you work.

 - Experience building or evaluating LLM-powered products.

 - Clarity of communication in both speaking and writing.

 - Comfort with ambiguity. Much of what you work on will be underspecified. You should be able to take a vague problem, frame it, and come back with a proposal.

 - Interest in how chips are designed.
   


BONUS POINTS

 - Coursework, research, or internship experience in chip architectures, digital design, verification, or hardware performance modeling.

 - Exposure to SystemVerilog.

 - Familiarity with the mechanisms underlying LLM inference

Normal Computing is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. jobs.description:
Come join one of America’s fastest-growing insurance companies. Since 1848, National Life Group has aimed to keep our promises, providing families with stability in good times and in bad. Throughout that history, we have provided peace of mind to those families as they plan their futures.

Our mission extends beyond the insurance and annuities policies that we offer. We strive to make the world a better place through our grants from our charitable foundation, paid volunteer time for our employees, environmentally sustainable and healthy workplaces, and events that promote the work of nonprofits in our own backyard.

We foster a collaborative environment with opportunities for growth and encourage our associates to live our values: Do good. Be good. Make good.

Please note that we do not offer visa sponsorship for this position.

POSITION SUMMARY:

At National Life Group, we are unlocking the power of data and AI to transform our business and enhance customer experience. Our AI Center of Excellence (AICoE) is leading this effort through innovations in machine learning, advanced analytics, and generative AI.

As a Data Science Intern, you will contribute to projects within our AI CoE. You’ll gain hands-on experience applying computer science and data science techniques to real business challenges. Projects may range from supporting the development of predictive models to testing and enhancing generative AI solutions.

This is a unique opportunity to explore both traditional data science methods and emerging AI technologies while working in a collaborative, mission-driven environment.

RESPONSIBILITIES: 

In this role, you will collaborate with AI and data science practitioners, technical experts, and business partners. You will work primarily in National Life’s Databricks environment to develop and evaluate data-driven solutions. Depending on project priorities, responsibilities may include:

• Prepare, explore, and validate datasets and features for life insurance and annuity use cases such as surrender propensity, premium persistency, and policyholder behavioral analysis.

• Support the development and evaluation of statistical and machine-learning models, comparing results with established baselines and investigating errors and limitations.

• Help design experiments and analyze business outcomes using appropriate comparisons, sound statistical methods, and clear measures of success.

• Develop reusable Python and SQL workflows, including validation checks and documentation that allow others to review and reproduce the work.

• Prototype and evaluate generative AI applications, assessing output quality, source support, failure modes, and practical business usefulness.

• Apply responsible AI and data-handling practices, including appropriate treatment of sensitive information and validation of AI-generated outputs.

• Communicate findings and recommendations to technical and business audiences.

QUALIFICATIONS: 

• Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, data science, mathematics, statistics, or a related field.

• Strong programming skills in Python, with experience using data analysis or machine-learning libraries such as pandas and scikit-learn. Exposure to Apache Spark, PyTorch, or TensorFlow is a plus.

• Working knowledge of SQL, including querying, joining, and aggregating data to prepare and validate datasets for analysis and modeling.

• Familiarity with foundational statistical and machine-learning concepts, including regression, classification, model evaluation, and hypothesis testing.

• Coursework or projects integrating generative AI APIs into software is a plus.

• Curiosity and eagerness to learn about the real-world application of both modern AI technologies and foundational statistical methods.

• Strong communication skills and ability to work collaboratively in a team environment.

AI Proficiency Expectations

At National Life Group, we view AI as an enabler of human potential. We use AI to help us work smarter, serve more clients, and keep our promises, while remaining a relationship-driven business where our people are our greatest strength.

All associates are expected to:

• Leverage approved AI tools, where appropriate, to improve the efficiency, quality, and impact of their work.

• Stay curious and open to new AI-enabled ways of working.

• Exercise sound judgment by reviewing and validating AI-generated content.

• Maintain accountability for the accuracy, quality, fairness, and integrity of work products by adhering to National Life's AI guiding principles.

• Use AI responsibly and in accordance with company policies related to confidentiality, data privacy, security, compliance, retention, and intellectual property.

Core Competencies

• Service Focus - Demonstrates a client centric focus for satisfying one’s external and/or internal customers; establishes and maintains effective relationships with customers and gains their trust and respect.

• Decision Making - Makes sense of complex information, critically evaluates, and creates solutions.

• Results Oriented - Sets performance and personal goals; Driven to meet or exceed goals and objectives.

• Plans and Aligns - Plans and prioritizes work to meet commitments aligned with organizational goals; Aligns people and skills to tasks and assignments; Evaluates results of work.

• Demonstrates Learning Agility - Enhances skills and knowledge through continuous learning; Focuses on personal results by establishing stretch goals; Seeks feedback and changes accordingly.

• Establishes Relationships - Builds partnerships with others to instill trust, collaborate, and meet shared objectives.

• Communicates Effectively - Actively listens, conveys messages to meet different audience needs, and remains open to new ideas and opinions.

• Fosters Diversity - Values diversity and difference in thought, experience, and perspective; Promotes an environment that embraces diversity, equity, and inclusion; Supports equal and fair treatment for all.

HOW YOU SHOW UP: 

• Highly reliable, engaged and possess a customer service attitude

• Demonstrate effective communication to various areas of the organization (technical and non-technical)

• Bring creativity, thought leadership, and curiosity to the table; actively participate in forums to contribute and learn

• Strong analytical and critical thinking skills, i.e. a problem solver’s mindset

• Eager to learn, ask relevant questions, seek new knowledge, and make connections

• Enjoy taking on challenges and working towards solutions both collaboratively and independently 

PROGRAM HIGHLIGHTS: 

• 10-week paid internship (June 1 - August 6) with formal orientation and onboarding

• Networking opportunities with peers and leaders throughout the summer

• Cross-Departmental group project focused on an enterprise-wide solution presented at company-wide event

• Presentation skills coaching sessions

• Learning opportunities throughout program

• Access to mentors (former program participants)

Base Pay Range. The base pay range for this position is the range National Life reasonably and in good faith expects to pay for the position taking into account the wide variety of factors, including: prior experience and job-related knowledge; education, training and certificates; current business needs; and market factors. The final salary or hourly wages offered may be outside of this range based on other reasons and individual circumstances.

Additional Compensation and Benefits. The total compensation package for this position may also include a full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits (including 401(k) eligibility and various paid time off benefits, such as vacation, sick time, and parental leave), dependent on the position offered. The successful candidate may also be eligible to participate in National Life’s discretionary annual incentive programs, subject to the rules governing such programs. I

jobs.title: Software Engineer Intern
jobs.description:
Who we are 

Atoms is building the machines that power the next era of progress.

Over the last decade, software has transformed the digital world. But the physical world, where food is made, minerals are mined, goods are moved, and industries are run, remains far less intelligent, far less efficient, and far more constrained. We’re changing that.

Atoms builds Physical AI— real-world robots for the industries that move civilization forward, starting with food, mining, and transport. Our systems are designed to understand, predict, and control the real world with precision, turning complex physical operations into something more reliable, more scalable, and more productive.

This work requires more than robotics. It requires deep integration across hardware, software, AI, operations, manufacturing, and real estate. We don’t just build machines in a lab. We deploy them into real environments, operate them, learn from them, and improve them until they work at scale.

We are roboticists, engineers, operators, and builders. We believe the next great technology companies will not only transform information, but the physical systems that shape everyday life.

If you want to work on hard problems with real-world impact, join us.

What we’re looking for

Actively pursuing a Bachelor/Master in Computer Science, Engineering or a related technical field

• Graduating in Summer/Fall/Winter 2027 or Spring/Summer 2028.

• 3.7 GPA Minimum 

• Must have completed an introductory Computer Science course

• Have advanced programming experience in one or more application or systems languages (Go, Python, Ruby, Java, Kotlin, C/C++, etc.)

• A problem-solver who thrives in tackling diverse technical challenges and demonstrates a clear track record of growth and learning

• A take-charge individual who exhibits ownership and takes pride in writing clean, maintainable, and fun code

• An engineer who can dive deep into open source software, find issues, and fix them.

What you’ll do

As an engineering intern at Atoms, you'll be an integral part of building out the state-of-the-art intelligent machine for the food industry. Your role will encompass a diverse range of responsibilities, including:

• You will build foundational software systems to enable globally scaled kitchen infrastructure and real estate innovations

• You test software development methodology in an agile environment

• You provide ongoing maintenance, support, and enhancements in existing systems and platforms

• You work alongside other engineers to elevate technology and improve systems overall

• You write, debug, maintain and test code

• You design scalable, fault tolerant architectural systems

• You develop information systems by designing, developing, and installing software solutions

• You drive innovation within the team and support Atoms’ technological advancements 

Why join us 

At Atoms, you’ll work on one of the defining challenges of our time—bringing automation into the physical world to drive real, lasting impact. We exist to uncover valuable unknown truths and turn them into progress, which means constantly pushing beyond what’s known and building what doesn’t yet exist. The work is ambitious and often challenging, but it’s grounded in a shared sense of purpose and a team committed to seeing it through together. Our work only matters if it serves others, and we know that meaningful progress depends on the trust of the people we serve and the strength of our team—so we invest in both, creating an environment where you can do your best work and grow.

What else you need to know

This role can be based in New York, Seattle, Los Angeles, Mountain View or San Francisco. Atoms is a company driven by invention and continuous change - we are constantly reimagining our industries, building new products, and refining how we operate. We do our best work together. Later is the world’s most intelligent influencer marketing company, built to give brands the confidence to create unforgettable campaigns. By combining real creator relationships, trusted intelligence, and expert guidance, Later removes fear and guesswork from one of marketing’s most visible investments.

Later is looking for a full-time co-op starting January 2027 to help support the product team; you will be working on new product features and having a meaningful impact on the company. Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

• 
No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

• Please always verify communications:

• Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.

• Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com. 

• 
Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

• 
What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.

Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

jobs.title: Software Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT CHECK

Payroll is broken. It's still running on decades-old infrastructure. We're rebuilding it.

We don't run payroll ourselves — we power the businesses that do. As the inventors of embedded payroll, we're redefining how people get paid and making it easier for those businesses to launch, grow, and thrive.

 

On our team, you'll use creative problem-solving, critical thinking, and grit to simplify the complexity of payroll for thousands of employers of every size, across all industries. We ignore conventional role boundaries in favor of the unique strengths and values each builder brings to our mission: make paying people simple. Check out our origin story! https://app.notion.com/p/checkhq/The-Generalist-Check-Solving-the-150-Billion-Payroll-Problem-3b24274a2e75804e9141cfac60476d25?source=copy_link

 

Check is far more than just API infrastructure. We’re a springboard for building and scaling payroll businesses. See how it works for our partners. https://www.checkhq.com/partners

 


ENGINEERING CULTURE AT CHECK

Engineering at Check works as one small team with a lot of ownership. We staff engineers on business priorities rather than fixed domains, and when something is stuck, people step in to move it forward instead of waiting on ownership boundaries. AI is central to how we build, and very little of our code is written by hand. That makes engineering judgment more important: deciding which problem to solve, defining what "done" means, and catching what the AI got wrong. A merged PR isn't the finish line. The work is done when it has had the intended impact.




ABOUT THIS ROLE

As a Software Engineer early in your career, you'll ship real work on the platform that moves money, calculates taxes and runs compliance for thousands of businesses. You'll learn a complex, regulated domain quickly and build the judgment to turn messy real-world problems into software that partners and operators rely on.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build and ship software that improves how partners, operators and internal teams run payroll on Check

 - Use AI to learn unfamiliar systems quickly, explore approaches, and write and test code

 - Own everything you ship, however it was written, so you can explain it, review it critically and debug it in production

 - Define the impact you're aiming for before you start, then release early, iterate and follow through until you reach it

 - Work directly with engineers, product and operations to understand problems from the people who have them

 - Share what you learn so the team gets better at building with AI

 - Take feedback and mentorship well, and keep raising your own quality bar




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - High agency and curiosity, with a habit of running at problems and picking up context quickly

 - Strong engineering fundamentals, so you can reason about systems and tradeoffs without an AI tool doing that thinking for you

 - Hands-on experience building with AI tools, and the judgment to tell plausible output from correct output

 - More interest in whether something worked than in how much code you wrote

 - Clear communication with both technical and non-technical teammates

 - Something you've built and are proud of, whether at work, in school or on your own

We don't require any particular programming language. You'll pick up our stack (Python/Django, React, TypeScript, AWS, Terraform, Postgres, Temporal, GitHub) as you go.




LOCATION

This role requires a minimum of 2 days/week in-office, based in either NYC or SF.




WHAT WE OFFER

For full-time employees, Check offers company-sponsored medical, dental, vision, short-term/long-term disability, and basic life insurance coverage, effective on their first day of work. We also provide stock options, flexible PTO and sick leave, up to 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave for new parents, flexible return-to-work, 9 annual holidays, a 401k retirement plan, and a $100 monthly stipend for home internet and mobile phone expenses.




TRAVEL & OFFICE POLICY

The Check team is distributed across the US. Roles can be remote, hybrid, or based in one of our offices in New York City or San Francisco. We offer ample opportunities and encourage employees to attend team offsites, events, and hackathons throughout year. All Checketeers gather in the spring for our annual 3-day company retreat. 

For our in-office and hybrid employees, our offices are open all week. We provide meals on Tuesdays and Thursdays and there are regular happy hours, game nights, and other in-person events.

Remote work at Check requires the ability to perform all responsibilities without distraction or disruption, while maintaining quality, effective communication, and productivity.

--

We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, transgender status, sexual stereotypes, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, provided they are consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws. Job Description:
Department
European Pricing and Structuring Desk
The desk is part of the Front Office with a direct reporting line to the CRO. It sits alongside the origination and trading teams providing wide structuring, valuation, and deal approval support for complex transactions and business development initiatives. 
We also support management and traders in live portfolio management including risk exposure representation and management.
The function covers market derivatives and asset-based structures on all commodities traded by EDFT and its affiliates in liquid and illiquid horizons. 
The function work closely with commercial and control functions to execute profitable deals that meet the company’s required rate of return, capital utilisation criteria, in compliance with EDF group risk policies.

Position
This is a Junior Pricing Analyst role in Pricing and Structuring Team with the main responsibility of valuing flow and structured commodity deals in the energy markets. This involves:
• understanding of commercial terms of deals including financial derivatives and real options contracts
• defining complete deal payoffs, formulating a problem, and proposing and developing an appropriate valuation approach
• carrying out data analysis and developing pricing models and valuation tools
• pricing and informing on the results of valuation in the context of a hedge strategy
• presenting and communicating own work in a structured manner to your manager or internal customers
Other duties and responsibilities as may arise and may be assigned by Management, this may include bespoke analysis, tool/model development for special projects, and development of library, user interfaces and data infrastructure.

Main Responsibilities
To support Origination team in structuring, valuation, approvals and execution of deals which maximise P&L and minimise non-market risk exposure.
To provide high standard analytics and valuation services in support of execution of EDFT’s business strategy and growth ambitions, in the areas of:
• Structured flexibility products
• Global gas and oil flow
• Renewable generation and Energy Storage
• Emissions and Green Fuels
• EDF risk management and market access service including facilitation of group hedging and optimisation of LNG, storages, power generation assets or liquidity products
To contribute to development and enhancement of mathematical pricing models and analytical tools to support data processing, valuation, risk management and trading, optimisation and cashflow modelling.

Candidate Profile
This role is a junior role within an existing team and may suit a recent graduate or someone at the early stages of their career looking to specialise in pricing and structuring or setting foundations for a future career in origination and trading. 

The role would be best suited for an individual with an analytical mindset and strong technical (programming / excel) skills.
The candidate would offer:
• Bachelors (or higher) degree in a STEM subject.
• Understanding of financial metrics
• Understanding of energy market fundamentals and physical constraints.
• Understanding of risk, both market and residual risks
• Understanding of derivative instruments and their pricing methods
• Practical modelling skills
• Enthusiasm for problem-solving and drive for detail and delivery
• Positive team player attitude
• Good communication and interpersonal skills

Personal skills
It is a multifaceted role, which requires a combination of commercial mindset and technical skills.
It is service based so communication and client facing skills are essential as you would be responsible for liaising with originators and traders as well as regularly collaborating with other pricing team members and other support functions.
The essential personal skills include:
• Curiosity and willingness to learn
• Determination and commitment to deliver high quality service
• Attention to detail and work ownership
• Integrity and accountability
• Efficiency - working to deadlines in a fast paced environment
• Excellent team player

Hours of work
40 hours a week

In this role, you will support the product development lifecycle for our data-driven marketing solutions, including the WPP Open platform. You'll be instrumental in translating user needs and data insights into clear product requirements, ensuring our solutions are innovative, valuable, and technically sound. Your strong understanding of data and SQL will be key to communicating effectively with engineering and data science teams and making informed product decisions.

You are:

• Data-curious, with a proven ability to analyze information and derive actionable insights.

• Analytical and detail-oriented, capable of breaking down complex problems and defining clear product needs.

• An excellent communicator, able to bridge the gap between technical and business stakeholders.

• A proactive learner, eager to deepen your understanding of AdTech, product management, and data-driven methodologies.

• Collaborative, thriving in a cross-functional team environment and contributing to a shared vision.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

• Support Product Development & Lifecycle Management

• Assist in defining, documenting, and prioritizing product requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria based on user needs, business goals, and data analysis.

• Work closely with Product Managers, Engineering Leads, Data Scientists, and UX Designers to ensure a shared understanding of product features and their underlying data implications.

• Help manage and refine product backlogs, participate in agile ceremonies (sprint planning, stand-ups, reviews), and support release cycles.

• Conduct competitive analysis and market research to identify opportunities and stay informed about industry trends in data and AI for marketing.

Leverage Data for Product Insights and Validation

• Utilize SQL and other data analysis tools to query datasets, analyze product performance, identify trends, and generate insights that inform product strategy and prioritization.

• Collaborate with data engineers and data scientists to understand data availability, schemas, quality, and potential for new product features or enhancements.

• Define and track key product performance indicators (KPIs) and metrics, helping to evaluate the success of new features post-launch.

• Help ensure data quality and integrity within product features, flagging discrepancies or potential issues.

Facilitate Stakeholder Communication & Feedback

• Communicate product updates, release notes, and progress to various internal stakeholders, effectively highlighting the data-driven rationale behind product decisions.

• Gather feedback from users, internal teams (e.g., commercial, operations), and clients to continuously iterate and improve our products.

• Support in preparing presentations and documentation to articulate product vision, strategy, and roadmap.

Continuous Learning & Contribution

• Actively seek to deepen your understanding of AdTech data, our internal platforms (including WPP Open), and user behaviors through self-study and mentorship.

• Contribute to the continuous improvement of product management processes and tools within the team.

WHAT YOU WILL NEED

• 0-2 years of experience in a product, business analyst, data analyst, or similar role with exposure to software development.

• Proficiency in SQL is essential, with the ability to write complex queries to extract, analyze, and manipulate data from various sources.

• Solid understanding of relational databases and data warehousing concepts.

• English fluency C2

• Experience with data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Looker, Power BI) is a strong plus.

• Familiarity with Agile methodologies (Scrum, Kanban) and the software development lifecycle.

• Ability to define and document clear product requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret complex data and translate it into actionable product insights.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, able to articulate technical concepts to non-technical audiences and vice-versa.

• Proven ability to work effectively in a cross-functional team environment.

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Business, Marketing, Economics, Statistics, or a related quantitative field.

If you are ready to be at the forefront of the AdTech industry, shaping its future, and driving success for both our clients, we encourage you to apply and join our team.

We believe the best work happens when we're together, fostering creativity, collaboration, and connection. That's why we’ve adopted a hybrid approach, with teams in the office around four days a week. jobs.title: Data Science Fellow
jobs.description:
WHY FACULTY? 


We established Faculty in 2014 because we thought that AI would be the most important technology of our time. Since then, we’ve worked with over 350 global customers to transform their performance through human-centric AI. You can read about our real-world impact here https://faculty.ai/impact.

 

We don’t chase hype cycles. We innovate, build and deploy responsible AI which moves the needle - and we know a thing or two about doing it well. We bring an unparalleled depth of technical, product and delivery expertise to our clients who span government, finance, retail, energy, life sciences and defence.

 

Our business, and reputation, is growing fast and we’re always on the lookout for individuals who share our intellectual curiosity and desire to build a positive legacy through technology.

 

AI is an epoch-defining technology, join a company where you’ll be empowered to envision its most powerful applications, and to make them happen.


WHY THE FACULTY FELLOWSHIP?

 

Artificial Intelligence is the defining technology of our age, but it is only valuable when applied to the real world. Since 2014, Faculty has helped over 500 PhDs, postdocs and engineers transition into high-impact careers in data science and machine learning.

 

How it works:

 - 2 Weeks of Intensive Training: Learn to apply your advanced technical knowledge to real-world data science problems.

 - 6 Week Paid Placement: Tackle a commercial data science project with a host company (paid at the London Living Wage).

 - Demo Day Finale: Present your work to 100+ guests and industry leaders from across the UK and Europe.
   
    

Where our alumni go: Our alumni have gone on to shape the future at companies like Google, Meta, Tesco, and AstraZeneca, as well as disruptive startups like PhysicsX and Orbital Witness. We are also incredibly proud that a high percentage of fellows choose to continue their journey internally, joining the Faculty team permanently.

 


ABOUT THE ROLE

 

As a Fellow at Faculty, you will join an elite cohort transforming industries through cutting-edge data science. This intensive, eight-week programme bridges academia and real-world impact, embedding you directly into high-stakes commercial environments. 

You will apply advanced machine learning techniques to solve complex, ambiguous problems for our clients, turning theoretical knowledge into high-value deployable solutions. It is a fast-paced launchpad designed to accelerate your technical growth, build exceptional commercial acumen, and empower you to shape the future of artificial intelligence in an ambitious, forward-thinking tech community.

 


WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR:

 - You hold a finished PhD or Master’s degree in a STEM subject, complemented by a strong foundation in data science or machine learning.

 - You possess a high level of mathematical competence alongside solid experience with theoretical concepts like hypothesis testing, Bayesian inference, and neural networks.

 - You demonstrate strong programming skills, particularly in Python, and feel comfortable navigating core data science coding libraries.

 - You bring an entrepreneurial mindset, showing the resilience and autonomy needed to structure your own project plans and hit critical deadlines.

 - You can communicate complex technical ideas clearly, adapting your language seamlessly for both technical peers and non-technical partners.

 - You thrive in fast-paced, ambitious environments, showing curiosity and a relentless drive to learn and deploy new technologies.

 


REQUIREMENTS

 - Right to Work: We are unfortunately unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role, so you will need to hold full-time UK right to work to apply. If your eligibility is based on a visa, just pop the details of your situation into your application so we can review it. To learn more about your options, check out  https://www.gov.ukwww.gov.uk http://www.gov.uk.

 - Location & Logistics: This is a fully in-person, eight-week programme based in London, so you will need to be able to commute daily for the entire duration. Please keep in mind that Faculty is unable to provide or reimburse accommodation and travel expenses.

 


OUR TIMELINES

 - 17th November 2026 (17:00 BST): Application Deadline.

 - Mid November: Coding tests sent via email.

 - End of November: Interviews held remotely online.

 - 18th December: Final notifications sent to all applicants.

 - Monday 25th January - Friday 19th March : Programme duration (Full-time, Monday–Friday).

*Please note that the program dates are tentative and may be adjusted or postponed entirely. We will notify all applicants immediately should any changes occur to the dates or the program schedule. We appreciate your flexibility and understanding.

 


WHAT THE FELLOWSHIP OFFERS

 

 - Fully Paid: Earn the London Living Wage for the full eight weeks.

 - Expert-Led Training: Two weeks of immersive lectures followed by weekly Friday masterclasses, bridging the gap between academic theory and commercial data science.

 - Dedicated Mentorship: Receive ongoing support and guidance from experienced Faculty practitioners, gaining insight into how AI and data science are applied to solve real-world business challenges while developing your technical, commercial and communication skills.

 - Real-World Value: A dedicated six-week placement embedded with a business, tackling a high-stakes data science challenge.

 - Career Launchpad: A proven pathway into industry, backed by more than a decade of helping technically exceptional individuals successfully transition into industry across tech, startups, and the FTSE 100.

 - Unrivalled Networking: Connect with a 500+ strong alumni community and pitch your project to 100+ industry guests at Demo Day.


OUR RECRUITMENT ETHOS




We aim to grow the best team - not the most similar one. We know that diversity of individuals fosters diversity of thought, and that strengthens our principle of seeking truth. And we know from experience that diverse teams deliver better work, relevant to the world in which we live. We’re united by a deep intellectual curiosity and desire to use our abilities for measurable positive impact. We strongly encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, ethnicities, genders, religions and sexual orientations.

jobs.description:
Job Details:

Job Description: 
The Role and Impact 

As a Development Tools Software Engineering Graduate Intern, you will contribute to the creation and improvement of software tools that empower developers and engineers within and outside Intel. You will be involved in hands-on coding, debugging, and optimizing solutions that enhance productivity and performance. Your contributions will play a key role in advancing Intel's data-centric technologies and solutions. 

Business Group 

You will be joining the Data Center Group (DCG), a dynamic organization focused on delivering innovative technologies that drive the future of computing and connectivity. The group works on cutting-edge solutions for data centers, cloud environments, and enterprise networks, supporting Intel's broader goal of enabling a world driven by data. 

Key Responsibilities 

- Work on the design, implementation, testing, or optimization of compiler and runtime technologies. 
- Develop and debug software using C or C++ within a large, collaborative codebase. 
- Create and enhance tests, reproduce and resolve defects, analyze failures, and deliver reliable solutions. 
- Evaluate functional correctness, compile-time behavior, runtime performance, or code quality relevant to the project. 
- Participate in technical discussions, code reviews, and project planning with team members and mentors. 
- Document designs, experiments, findings, and lessons learned while presenting project outcomes to the team. 
- Collaborate with open-source communities (where applicable) as part of your work.

Qualifications:
Minimum Qualifications
 
- Currently pursuing a Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related technical field (able to keep student status for at least 1 year).
- Graduate-level coursework or project experience in data structures and algorithms, plus at least one of: computer architecture, compiler construction, programming languages, or operating systems.
- Proficiency in programming with C or C++ within complex software systems
- Comfort with a Linux development environment: command-line tools, a debugger, Git, and build systems

Preferred Qualifications 

- Hands-on experience with LLVM or MLIR or with another compiler ecosystem such as Clang, SYCL/DPC++, Triton
- Working knowledge of Python - enough to read and extend test harnesses, build scripts, and benchmarking tools

jobs.title: AI Frameworks Engineer - Intern
jobs.description:
Job Details:

Job Description: 
The Role and Impact 

Intel is building the open software stack that makes large language models run fast on Intel GPUs. As an intern, you will join the engineering team that develops and optimizes LLM inference frameworks. You will work in vLLM and in the GPU kernel libraries beneath it with experienced engineers who will review your code and mentor you. This is a hands-on engineering internship, not a side project. You will write and test kernels, measure where performance goes, and see your changes land in open-source projects used across the AI industry.

Our internships usually last 12-24 months, and you will work with us part-time alongside your university degree. All applicants must be current university students and must remain students for the length of the internship. Candidates must be based in Poland on the internship start date and for its full duration.

Key Responsibilities 

- Develop and optimize AI framework software for LLM inference on Intel GPUs, under the guidance of senior engineers, with contributions going upstream to open-source projects such as vLLM.
- Implement, port, and tune compute kernels (e.g., Triton, SYCL) for core transformer building blocks such as attention, sampling, normalization, mixture-of-experts, and quantization.
- Run benchmarks and profile inference workloads to find performance bottlenecks, measure them, and report findings to the team.
- Write and extend unit tests, correctness checks, and performance regression tests so that framework and kernel code stays reliable as upstream moves.
- Investigate and debug failures across the stack, from Python framework code down to kernel behaviour on the hardware.
- Collaborate with framework, compiler, and kernel engineers across global teams, and take part in code review and technical discussion with the open-source community.

Qualifications:
Minimum Qualifications 

No professional experience is required.

- Currently pursuing a BS or MS degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, AI, Mathematics, Physics, or a related field. Student status is required for the whole internship, preferably for the next two years and for at least 12 months.
- Good Python programming skills.
- Understanding of deep learning and neural networks, including the basics of transformer architecture and LLM inference. 
- Familiarity with Linux environments from a user perspective.
- Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving skills.
- Eagerness to learn, an open mind, and the ability to work in a team.
- Ability to communicate clearly and concisely in English.

Preferred Qualifications 

- Hands-on experience with PyTorch.
- Exposure to GPU programming (Triton, CUDA, SYCL, OpenCL, or similar), for example through coursework or personal projects.
- Working knowledge of C or C++.
- Experience testing and debugging Python code, including unit testing.
- Familiarity with vLLM or another LLM inference serving framework.
- Contributions to open-source projects, or a public portfolio of code (e.g., GitHub).
- Coursework or interest in computer architecture, parallel programming, or numerical methods.
 
Bring your passion for AI, your curiosity, and your engineering drive to Intel, and help shape how the next generation of AI workloads runs on Intel hardware.

jobs.title: Commercial Graduate Program - Solution Engineering Path - Dutch Speaking Market
jobs.description:
To get the best candidate experience, please consider applying for a maximum of 3 roles within 12 months to ensure you are not duplicating efforts.

About Futureforce University Recruiting
Our Futureforce University Recruiting program is dedicated to attracting, retaining and cultivating talent. Our interns and new graduates work on real projects that affect how our business runs, giving them the opportunity to make a tangible impact on the future of our company. With offices all over the world, our recruits have the chance to collaborate and connect with fellow employees on a global scale. We offer job shadowing, mentorship programs, talent development courses, and much more.

Job Category

Sales
Job Details

About Salesforce
Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

Fixed-term contract
Duration: 12 months
Start Date: February 2027

We are thrilled to invite ambitious graduate candidates who would like to build a career in Salesforce to apply for the next cohort of our EMEA Graduate Rotation Program - Solution Engineering Path.

This exciting 12-month program is designed to give graduates exposure to both solution engineering and sales. Having built the foundational skills for both roles and met our eligibility criteria, top graduates on this path can begin their Salesforce Solution Engineering careers. The promotion window opens from month 7 onwards.

Our graduate program is a fully immersive experience, combining comprehensive learning paths with in-role experience. You will be assigned an experienced Solution Engineering Buddy who will provide hands-on coaching and involve you in some of their live deals. You will also be paired with experienced Sales Development Buddies during the Sales Rotation and you also get to call your first salesforce leads and find your first deals. Throughout the programme, you will gain exposure to senior solution engineering and sales professionals during our inspiration sessions.

By joining Salesforce, you will have the opportunity to lay the foundation for a fast-paced, successful career. We are a proud member of the Fortune 100 Best Places to Work list for the past 14 years and a consistent winner of Great Place to Work awards.

Who are we looking for?
• You are a 2025 or 2026 graduate (minimum bachelor’s degree)• For the Solution Engineering Path, we consider applicants from the following academic backgrounds:
Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Technology, Software Engineering, Data Science/Data Engineering, Information Systems, or other Adjacent disciplines.

• You are a creative problem-solver
• You are a relationship builder and possess a growth mindset
• You are curious, self-motivated, and focused on continuous learning
• You thrive in a team environment
• You have excellent interpersonal skills
• You are goal-oriented and comfortable in a fast-paced environment
• You are fluent in English and Dutch (essential)

What does our new EMEA Graduate Program look like?

The program is structured as follows:

Introduction Month

During your first month, you will receive extensive onboarding enablement through a Salesforce-style academy, where you will:
• Become immersed in the culture of Salesforce and gain a deep understanding of our values
• Develop an understanding of our solutions, technologies, and tools
• Learn critical professional skills for your career at Salesforce
• Follow a structured learning calendar with sessions and hands-on workshops led by experts and program alumni

Rotations

• During the Graduate Program, you will experience both the Solution Engineering Path and the Sales Path. The structure of each rotation is similar: you will spend 60% of your time immersed in the role with clear tasks, targets, and stakeholder alignment, while the remaining 40% will focus on role-specific learning. You will be paired with experienced buddies in each path.
• If your first rotation (months 2 through 4) is in Solution Engineering, you will then join the Sales Graduate Rotation from months 5 through 7, and vice versa. Over these six months, you will gain exposure to both roles. The time spent mastering the fundamentals of these complementary disciplines will enable you to be more productive and impactful upon promotion.
• Throughout the rotations, there will be self-paced certifications and skills assessments. You must meet all eligibility criteria before you can panel for promotion.

Examples of what you can expect during the rotations

Solution Engineering Graduate Rotation
• Learn our solutions at a deeper, more technical level
• Work closely with the Solution Engineering organisation, supporting the creation of cutting-edge customer demonstrations
• Learn the art of customer discovery and how to create a compelling customer point of view

Sales Graduate Rotation
• Learn Salesforce’s best-in-class prospecting and qualification methodologies
• Learn how to use social, digital, video, chat, and phone platforms to effectively engage Salesforce prospects
• Collaborate with Sales Development Specialists to run campaigns and help build sales pipeline for the EMEA Sales organisation

What’s in it for you?
• A clear and structured career path within our Solution Engineering organisation
• The opportunity to work in an international team within a nurturing environment
• Access to our diverse internal employee groups
• A comprehensive benefits package
• Relocation budget and guidance throughout your relocation process
• An additional seven days of paid time off for charitable causes – learn more about our 1-1-1 model

Map your future for the coming years

With the EMEA Graduate Program - Solution Engineering Path, you can continue to progress:
• After completing the Graduate Program rotations, you may progress to Associate Solution Engineer, with opportunities to work across ESB, SMB, and GRB customer segments, or join our Specialist SE team. In some instances, this path may vary or be subject to change.
• With our strong mentoring culture, we strive to develop industry-leading Solution Engineering leaders. This is a phenomenal opportunity to build international experience within an organisation that has transformed the enterprise software market through cloud computing.

Unleash Your Potential
When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best, and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best. Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for AI, and the world.

Accommodations

If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please submit a request via this Accommodations Request Form.

NVIDIA is at the forefront of the AI revolution, building the computing platforms that power the world’s most advanced AI systems. From GPUs and AI servers to high-speed networking infrastructure, we continue to push the boundaries of computing technology. As part of the PCB design team, you will work with industry-leading engineers and contribute to the automation implementation of hardware design for next-generation AI accelerated computing platforms.
Through structured training, mentorship, and hands-on project experience, you will grow into a hardware EDA and AI design expert with a system-level perspective and help shape the future of computing architecture.

What You’ll Be Doing:
• Contribute to the implementation and optimization of automation tools and processes for the hardware design for NVIDIA’s latest products.
• Participate in research and practical applications of AI in PCB design engineering.
• Support EDA research and development for the latest PCB design and manufacturing technologies.
• Communicate and collaborate closely with global EDA teams and hardware engineering teams on a daily basis.
• Work closely with PCB design, system circuit design, mechanical design, component library design, signal integrity design, system validation, and manufacturing teams to solve complex engineering automation challenges.
• Continuously optimize design methodologies and engineering workflows to improve product performance and design efficiency.

What We Need to See:
• Bachelor’s degree or above in Automation, Electrical and Electronic Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related engineering field.
• Familiarity with electronic circuits and PCB design.
• Familiarity with Cadence or similar EDA design software.
• Background with Python or EDA scripting development experience
• Familiarity with modern software tool flows such as GitLab and CI/CD.
• Basic understanding of AI Agent practices and related concepts.
• Proficient daily English communication skills.
• Strong logical analysis and engineering problem-solving abilities.
• Honesty, resilience, and strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively in a cross-functional team environment.
• Self-motivated, passionate about technological innovation, and willing to continuously learn and explore new technologies.

Ways to Stand Out from the Crowd:
• Experience with PCB, electronic hardware, or system design projects through coursework, competitions, research, internships, or personal projects.
• Excellent English communication skills.
• Hands-on engineering experience with AI Agents.
• Understanding of PCB manufacturing processes and design methodologies such as DFF, DFA, and DFT.
• Background of CUDA programming and the latest NVIDIA GPU architecture features, such as dedicated features of the Hopper and Blackwell architectures.

jobs.title: Partner Development Manager, International Bank Partnerships
jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Financial Partnerships team sits within the Global Partnerships organization and is a key component of our success. Our team is responsible for developing and managing relationships with the global and regional banks that enable the Stripe product strategy and deliver new capabilities to Stripe users. Our team executes on high-impact, cross-functional product partnership initiatives across existing products and early-stage "up the stack" financial products. These partnerships have a significant impact on Stripe and are essential for us to offer products used by millions of our users.

Note: This is not a commercial sales position - for those opportunities, see our Business Development roles

What you'll do

We're looking for a Partner Development Manager to help manage out portfolio of international banks. You'll be responsible for developing and executing the multi-year, global strategies for building our relationships across many of our most important banking partners. You'll focus on designing, scaling, and continuously improving mechanisms to deepen relationships with our partners, as well as highly impactful programs key to differentiating Stripe. As part of these efforts, you'll collaborate closely with cross-functional stakeholders (including Product, Engineering, Legal, Finance, Risk, etc.), and with the banking partners' executive teams.

The successful candidate will have a demonstrated ability to manage and develop partners, think strategically and apply diagnostic thinking to business, product, and technical challenges, and earn trust with and influence others. A high-agency attitude, the ability to raise expectations in changing environments, and a drive to create impact through ownership are all important in this role.

Responsibilities

• Develop the go-to-partner strategy and execute on our most ambitious company-bending, bank-network-driven projects that are global and cross-border in nature

• Own the banking partner plans, the overall economics, day-to-day operational excellence, and be responsible for driving the partnerships to successful outcomes for Stripe

• Leverage banking, treasury, and payments industry knowledge to craft thoughtful partnership and product strategies with transaction banks, lenders, capital markets, central banks, and schemes

• Navigate, in partnership with Product, to execute deals supporting that strategy and help ensure a proper execution plan is in place

• Leverage significant industry experience to educate and help internal teams compose our holistic bank-led strategy and to advance that strategy with banking partners

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

• 9+ years of relevant experience in banking or fintech, including direct ownership of banking partnerships supporting collections, payouts, stored value, or embedded financial products. This is a specialised banking-infrastructure partnerships role, rather than a general fintech business-development role. The strongest candidates will combine commercial bank-partner ownership with evidence that they have taken a payments capability into production.

• Advanced knowledge of the banking and clearing landscape across multiple geographies with specific focus on transaction banking, e-money, safeguarding, multi-currency, and cross-border payments

• Demonstrated experience building proprietary global collection and payout networks

• A proven track record of working in a product-centric environment with significant internal and external dependencies across product, engineering, legal, sales, risk, and compliance

• Broad and deep experience executing industry-wide partnership strategies to build innovative product experiences and go-to-market models

jobs.title: Systems Intern - Multiple Teams
jobs.description:
Tenstorrent is leading the industry on cutting-edge AI technology, revolutionizing performance expectations, ease of use, and cost efficiency. With AI redefining the computing paradigm, solutions must evolve to unify innovations in software models, compilers, platforms, networking, and semiconductors. Our diverse team of technologists have developed a high performance RISC-V CPU from scratch, and share a passion for AI and a deep desire to build the best AI platform possible. We value collaboration, curiosity, and a commitment to solving hard problems. We are growing our team and looking for contributors of all seniorities.

Overview: A chip isn't a product until it's a working system. These teams cover both ends of that: getting silicon to boot and validate correctly,building the board, power, mechanical, thermal, packaging and IO around it. You submit one application, you have one recruiter screen - then we match you to the specific team below and location that fits best.

• Systems & Silicon Validation: Post-silicon testing of physical chips and integrated systems to ensure they meet all functional, electrical, and performance specs.

• System Software: Development of foundational software, including firmware, drivers, and operating systems, that directly controls and interfaces with hardware.

• System Design: The process of defining, integrating, and mapping out hardware components such as PCBs, software modules, and interfaces into a complete product blueprint.

• System Architecture: Define the high-level structural framework, interfaces, and data-flow pathways between the CPU, memory, and peripherals.

• Packaging: A package is what is placed between the silicon and the board; and its design requires detailed electrical, electromagnetic, and mechanical simulations and analysis. 

This role is on-site based out of Toronto, Ontario or Vancouver, British Columbia.

Who You Are

• Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in EE, Computer Engineering, Computer Science or Mechanical Engineering

• Coursework or projects in embedded systems, microwave and signal integrity, board-level design, or thermal/mechanical engineering using low-level programming (C/C++, Python) or hardware design and/or simulation tools (e.g., CAD, FEA, Verilog).

• Problem solver with strong foundational knowledge in one of these areas: electrical engineering, digital logic, computer architecture, or thermal/mechanical.

• Curious learner who is passionate about the intersection of software, silicon architecture, and the physical constraints of chip packaging and printed circuit boards (PCBs).

What We Need

• Systems & Silicon Validation: Assist in post-silicon testing of physical microchips under real-world workloads to ensure they meet all functional, electrical, and performance specifications.

• System Software: Contribute to developing foundational software—including firmware, drivers, and operating systems—that directly controls and interfaces with the semiconductor hardware.

• System Design & Architecture: Help map out, define, and evaluate high-level structural frameworks, optimizing the power delivery and high-speed performance benchmarks of both the silicon components and the underlying PCBs.

• Semiconductor Packaging & Mechanical Design: Design and layout, Electromagnetic (signal integrity and power integrity), mechanical design, and stress analysis

What You Will Learn

• Hands-on silicon experience using industry-standard lab equipment to bridge the gap between theoretical hardware design, physical packaging layouts, and real-world chips.

• Low-level software development by writing production-grade firmware, device drivers, and diagnostic tools that run directly on bare metal.

jobs.description:
About Redwood Materials

Redwood Materials was founded in 2017 by JB Straubel, co-founder and former CTO of Tesla, on a simple but radical idea: the critical minerals powering the energy transition already exist. They just need to come back. Today Redwood is the largest lithium-ion battery recycler in North America — recovering, refining, and redeploying critical minerals from end-of-life batteries back into the supply chain. On the energy side, Redwood has deployed the largest second-life battery project in the world, delivering power to AI data centers in months rather than years using proprietary energy architecture engineered entirely in-house. The company is profitable, the market it operates in is projected to grow 20 to 50 times over the next decade, and Redwood is the only company with the supply chain, the technology, and the operational scale to lead it.

Position Summary: 

The Electrical Engineering Associate, Energy Storage supports Redwood's next-generation Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) program by performing hands-on technical tasks. This is a fully on-site role at 2800 Lockheed Way, Carson City. You will perform a broad variety of hands-on technical tasks in support of Redwood’s next-generation Battery Energy Storage System (BESS). In this role, you will primarily work with engineers to create sophisticated printed circuit board (PCB) designs using software tools and use your technical abilities to build, test, and fix PCB prototypes. Additional responsibilities include management of an electronics laboratory, installing and running tests on power equipment in the field, assisting mechanical engineers, and a variety of miscellaneous technical tasks. 

Essential Duties and Responsibilities 

• Create and manage a library of electronics component symbols and footprints for PCB designs using Altium CAD software. 

• Hand-soldering and rework of PCB components, including fine-pitch surface mount parts with rework station/hot air, and connectors; cable harness assembly. 

• Running functional/bring-up tests on new board revisions, flashing firmware, verifying power rails. Bench-level troubleshooting of prototype and production boards down to component level. 

• Managing an electronics lab, including lab equipment and tool purchasing, organization, maintenance, and cleaning. Keeping the lab organized, stocked with consumables and ESD/safety compliant. 

• Setting up electrical test equipment for field testing support at outdoor project sites. 

Skills, Knowledge, and Abilities 

• Degree in Electronics Engineering Technology, Electrical Engineering Technology, or related field (or equivalent military/technical training) 

• Relevant coursework or certification in electronics fundamentals, circuit theory, or digital/analog systems 

• Ability to read schematics, datasheets, and basic PCB layouts 

• Familiarity with hand soldering (THT and SMT) to IPC-A-610 or IPC J-STD-001 workmanship standards, or willingness to be certified 

• Basic proficiency with lab equipment: multimeter, oscilloscope, bench power supply, function generator 

• Comfortable with basic hand tools and ESD-safe handling practices, as well as machinery and power equipment 

• Exposure to CAD/EDA tools (Altium, KiCad, Eagle) a plus, even from coursework or personal projects 

The position is full-time. Compensation will be commensurate with experience.

If you have additional privacy-related questions, please contact us at privacy@redwoodmaterials.com.

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

• 
No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

• Please always verify communications:

• Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.

• Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com. 

• 
Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

• 
What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Astera Labs is a global leader in purpose-built connectivity solutions that unlock the full potential of cloud and AI infrastructure.

Our Intelligent Connectivity Platform integrates PCIe, CXL and Ethernet semiconductor-based solutions based on a software-defined architecture that is both scalable and customizable.

Inspired by trusted partnerships with hyperscalers and the data center ecosystem, we are an innovation leader of products that are flexible, interoperable, and reliable.

We are headquartered in the heart of California’s Silicon Valley, with R&D centers and offices in Taiwan, China, Vancouver and Toronto, Canada, and Haifa, Israel.

The mission of this role is to architect and develop firmware and microcontroller subsystems for Astera Labs’ SoC and systems products.

jobs.title: Finance Systems Co-op
jobs.description:
About Groma

Groma is blending real estate and technology to unlock a new real estate asset class while making it easier for everyone – from institutional investors to the residents in our buildings – to participate in ownership. Our property technology platform uses AI to bring new efficiencies to the small unit count multifamily sector, enabling us to efficiently acquire, upgrade, and operate these 2-20 unit multifamily buildings and bring institutional performance to this massive but historically overlooked sector. Our investor technology platform makes owning these assets accessible to a broad array of investors, with bespoke vehicles available to institutional and family office investors and our flagship vehicle, the blockchain-powered GromaREIT, available to everyone, with a special focus on enabling ownership for the residents in our buildings. Visit www.groma.com to learn more about us.

About the Role

This focused on helping our Finance team find practical ways to use AI to enable the department to work more efficiently and accurately. Over six months, you’ll learn how our finance and accounting processes work, identify opportunities to improve them, and help design and implement solutions using tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, Python, SQL, and our financial platforms. We're looking for someone who knows more about these tools than we do and wants to teach us. If you'd rather be the resident expert than the person fetching spreadsheets, this is the co-op.

Job Responsibilities:

• Automate recurring finance tasks with AI workflows (Claude, ChatGPT, and their APIs)

• Map how finance work gets done and prioritize what's worth automating

• Connect financial platforms, databases, APIs, and other systems to create more efficient workflows

• Build every automation with a human review step and audit trail

• Serve as the team's in-house AI expert and raise everyone's fluency

• Document every system so a non-technical teammate can run it

• Support AP and AR directly to learn the domain firsthand

• Analyze financial data for trends and exceptions; support reporting and auditing

• Take on special projects where a technical approach beats a manual one

Skills:

• Knows where AI output needs checking and where it can be trusted

• Can explain technical work clearly to people who don't code

• Strong spreadsheet skills (Google Suite); finance exposure a plus

• Diligent documentation and task management; excellent communication

• Works well independently and on a team

• Working knowledge of Python, SQL, and REST APIs

Experience

• Pursuing a degree in CS, Data Science, AI, Systems Engineering, MIS, Business Analytics, Fintech, or Finance with a focus on technical coursework

• Have built something real with LLM tools (share an example in your application if you have one!)

About our Culture

At Groma, we’re looking to build something big and are on a very fast growth trajectory. We strive to respect individuals and their needs, while also acknowledging the reality that we have a small team that is trying to accomplish some very ambitious goals in a short period of time. We are focused on maintaining our dynamic in-office culture at Groma’s headquarters in downtown Boston. We believe that in-person collaboration and spontaneous interpersonal interaction is critical to the company’s success at this stage. We understand that everyone will need to work from home or the road occasionally, but want to be transparent with this expectation.

We have an ever-evolving list of values and conventions that guide how we operate as a company, but here’s a high-level overview of how we think about doing what we do:

• We approach our work with pragmatic idealism that enables us to focus on our desire to make the world a better place in ways big and small while also being open to intelligent compromises that accelerate us on our path to serve our broader societal goals.

• Our whole team believes strongly that the challenges we are solving require effective teams, not individual heroes.

• We have complex conversations well. We sit at the intersection of housing and blockchain policy, both nuanced topics with real-world impacts. We pride ourselves on being thoughtful, seeking the best solutions to real-world challenges, and implementing them effectively in the real world.

Compensation

This is a 40 hour per week position and is paid at a rate of $20 per hour. 

Job Benefits

• Fully covered commuter passes for bus, subway, boat, or commuter rail

• Competitive paid time off policy, 4 company holidays within co-op cycle

• In-office gym and roofdeck

• Comprehensive catering, snack, and beverage program

Position Salary Range
$20—$20 USD

jobs.title: Research Scientist Intern - Robot Learning & Manipulation
jobs.description:
FieldAI is where embodied AI meets real robots, real sensors, and real field deployments. We build risk-aware, reliable, field-ready AI systems that tackle challenging robotics problems and unlock the potential of embodied intelligence. Our approach combines frontier research with rigorous engineering, connecting advances in robot learning with the demands of physical systems operating in unpredictable environments.
About the Internship
We are offering spring, summer, and fall 2027 research internships in the Irvine office for master’s and PhD students advancing robotic manipulation.
You will investigate how robots can perform useful physical tasks reliably across diverse objects, environments, and robot platforms. Working closely with researchers and engineers, you will own a focused research project and help translate promising ideas into capabilities that can be tested on hardware and improved through real deployment experience.
Research directions and methods will be shaped by your expertise and the problems we encounter in the field. The goal is to produce original research with measurable impact on what our robots can accomplish.
What We Offer
Real deployment problems: Work on manipulation challenges grounded in customer use cases and operational needs, with opportunities to evaluate beyond controlled laboratory settings.
Physical robots and hardware: Develop and validate your work on robotic systems, including humanoids, mobile manipulators, and arm-equipped quadrupeds.
Research ownership: Shape a focused project, propose your approach, and carry it through implementation, experimentation, and hardware validation.
Deployment feedback: Use observations and failure cases from real operation to guide research and improve reliability.
Close technical collaboration: Work with researchers and engineers across robot learning, perception, control, hardware, and deployment.
Research contributions: Pursue work suitable for leading conferences and journals, with opportunities to release code, datasets, or other research artifacts.
What You Will Get To Do
Develop manipulation capabilities that address meaningful physical tasks in real environments.
Investigate how skills transfer across objects, tasks, environments, and robot platforms.
Address practical challenges such as uncertainty, contact, changing conditions, and failure recovery.
Design experiments that measure task success, generalization, and reliability under realistic operating conditions.
Integrate and validate research on physical robots, collaborating with engineering teams to address system constraints.
Document findings, present results, and contribute to publications or reusable research tools.
What You Have
Current master’s or PhD enrollment in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, AI/ML, or a closely related field.
Research experience in robotic manipulation, robot learning, embodied AI, or a related area.
A strong research or open-source track record, demonstrated through substantive publications, research software, or technically rigorous projects.
Clear ownership of original research or technical development, including implementation and evaluation.
Strong foundations in robotics, machine learning, and experimental design.
Proficiency in Python and/or C++.
Ability to work independently, communicate findings clearly, and collaborate across research and engineering disciplines.
The Extras That Set You Apart
First-author publications at venues such as RSS, CoRL, ICRA, IROS, NeurIPS, ICLR, or ICML, or journals such as RA-L, T-RO, or IJRR.
Significant contributions to open-source robotics or machine learning projects with demonstrated adoption.
Hands-on experience taking research from an initial idea to reliable operation on physical robots.
Experience evaluating robotic systems outside controlled laboratory conditions.
Public research code, datasets, or robot demonstrations showing technical depth and measurable results.
Experience with robot integration, sensing, control, or data collection infrastructure.
