jobs.title: Salesforce & Data Coordinator
jobs.description:
About the Role:
This is an exciting opportunity for a technically curious, data-minded professional to join a global team supporting Investment Banking across the UK and US. With a primary focus on data quality, governance, reporting and automation, you’ll help ensure teams have access to trusted, actionable information while contributing to initiatives that simplify processes and support the expanding use of automation and AI. You’ll gain hands-on exposure to tools including Salesforce, Power BI, Power Automate and Snowflake while partnering with Operations and Technology colleagues across the organization. This developmental role offers the opportunity to build your technical expertise, take ownership of key processes and contribute to projects with global impact.
 
This position offers flexibility to work Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday in the London office and Monday and Friday remote.
 
The Impact You’ll Make:
• Support the development and ongoing maintenance of the Salesforce data dictionary, helping ensure definitions are documented, consistent and suitable for AI tools, integrations and downstream reporting
• Support the design, implementation and ongoing operation of GIB Data Compliance processes, reporting and audit cycles
• Help maintain Salesforce data integrity across EIB and GIB records by monitoring field usage and completeness and assisting with data clean-up and backfill activities
• Maintain Data Quality Dashboard items, track exceptions and follow up with bankers and support teams as directed
• Support the accuracy and timeliness of Hourglass data and other key data sets used for management reporting
• Assist with creating and modifying Salesforce reports and dashboards
• Support Salesforce user training and adoption by contributing to training materials and best-practice guidance
• Identify potential data integrity and consistency issues and contribute ideas to improve processes
• Support assigned Salesforce, data and technology workstreams through requirements gathering, completion of defined tasks and progress updates
• Assist with rebuilding and simplifying GIB and EIB reporting in Snowflake
• Build and maintain reporting and data visualizations using Power BI and Power Query, presenting information in a clear, decision-oriented format
• Help identify and deliver automation opportunities using Power Automate, Power Apps and potentially other tools such as FormAssembly
• Complete research and basic analysis in support of ad hoc data requests
• Support migration of deal files and precedent pitch materials, helping ensure content is accurately captured and accessible
• Contribute to the Salesforce team newsletter and other internal communications
• Support global GIB projects and system rollouts, including testing, implementation and user adoption
• Assist with administration of the weekly EIB staffing process, including maintaining and distributing the staffing tracker
• Support administration of protected time and the monthly PTO tracker for the EIB team
• Provide operational support to the EIB COO office and support teams on projects as required
 
What You’ll Bring to Baird:
• Interest in developing skills across Salesforce, data management, reporting, automation and business operations
• Strong attention to detail with a focus on data accuracy, completeness and consistency
• Ability to follow established data governance and compliance processes and identify potential data quality issues
• Ability to organize information and present data in a clear, decision-oriented manner
• Ability to balance assigned technology and data workstreams with ongoing operational responsibilities
• Strong organizational and follow-through skills when tracking exceptions, completing assigned tasks and providing progress updates
• Collaborative approach to working with Salesforce, technology, banking and support teams
• Curiosity and a continuous-improvement mindset, with an interest in simplifying processes and reducing manual work
• Ability to support changing priorities, global projects and system rollouts in a team-oriented environment
 
Compensation and Benefits:
• Compensation and bonus are commensurate with experience, performance and/or firm profitability
• You’ll have the opportunity to advance your career while enjoying our comprehensive benefits designed for your life, career and future

jobs.title: Data Analyst - Specialty
jobs.description:
Who are we?

Howden is a global insurance group with employee ownership at its heart. Together, we have pushed the boundaries of insurance. We are united by a shared passion and no-limits mindset, and our strength lies in our ability to collaborate as a powerful international team comprised of 24,000 employees spanning over 56 countries.

People join Howden for many different reasons, but they stay for the same one: our culture. It’s what sets us apart, and the reason our employees have been turning down headhunters for years. Whatever your priorities – work / life balance, career progression, sustainability, volunteering – you’ll find like-minded people driving change at Howden.

Role Overview
Role Overview
The role is dedicated to the Aviation team. Its primary focus is to support our Senior Data Analyst, Aviation and ultimately the wider Aviation team with data analysis, reporting and analytics; all of the role’s deliverables relate to the aviation portfolio.
 
For the first year, you will spend dedicated time each week embedded with the central Data & Analytics team. That team provides the formal training, tooling and access to the “back end” — the data lake, SQL and detailed data-analytical environment — that sits behind the Aviation team’s reporting, and the role applies that capability directly to Aviation work.
 
The Aviation team’s data function is currently led by deep domain knowledge — over 20 years of aviation insurance experience across claims, finance, broking and account management — together with a clear understanding of the data and the outputs the team needs. This role complements that domain expertise with formal analytical and technical depth (data-lake access, SQL and structured data analysis), developed and supported through the Data & Analytics team.

In summary:
• Focus: dedicated to Aviation team data, reporting and analytics.
• Working pattern: approximately 25% of each week embedded with the Data & Analytics team.
• Development model: technical training, tooling and back-end (data lake / SQL) access provided by the Data & Analytics team and applied directly to Aviation work.
What You’ll Do
• Work with brokers and business stakeholders to understand real-world problems and translate them into data and AI questions.
• Explore and prototype data ideas, helping to shape user stories and analytical approaches.
• Clean, analyse and validate data from multiple sources — including premium and placement data, claims experience and underwriter / portfolio performance — to ensure accuracy and reliability.
• Spot patterns, trends and anomalies, and help explain what they mean in practice.
• Use modern data and analytics tools to turn raw data into clear, actionable outputs — reports, dashboards and analytics that support broker lineslips / facilities and senior management, both regular and ad-hoc.
• Support the use of AI-enabled tools to automate repetitive data entry, cleansing and reconciliation, and to accelerate the production of reports and analytics.
• Collaborate with data, technology and analytics teams across the wider group.
• Apply appropriate human review, document your work and follow best-practice data and AI standards. Break problems into steps an agent can execute, and use good judgement about when to lean on AI and when to do the work yourself.

What You’ll Grow Into
As you build aviation domain knowledge and technical depth, the role broadens to include:
• Acting as a data and analytics point of contact for the team’s lineslip portfolio — building and maintaining reporting suites covering bordereaux, income, claims and utilisation.
• Producing consolidated, portfolio-level analytics to support renewal strategy and market presentations.
• Identifying data-quality issues in lineslip records and working with brokers to resolve them at source.
• Acting as a business-analyst liaison between the broking team and IT / AI development resources — defining requirements, mapping workflows and setting data-capture standards.
• Participating in testing (UAT) and supporting brokers using AI-enabled tools: troubleshooting, onboarding users and maintaining guides and training materials.

What We’re Looking For
Essential
• A degree (or equivalent) in a numerate or analytical subject — e.g. maths, statistics, data science, economics, engineering or sciences.
• Strong attention to detail and logical thinking.
• A genuine interest in how data can influence business decisions.
• Confidence explaining ideas to both technical and non-technical audiences.
• An inquisitive, problem-solving mindset — comfortable with modern AI tooling and keen to keep pace with a fast-moving landscape.
Technical skills (you don’t need all of these on day one)
• Experience using Excel for analysis.
• Exposure to Python, SQL and/or R through study, projects or internships.
• Familiarity with data-visualisation tools such as Power BI (or similar).
• Interest in learning modern data platforms (e.g. Databricks).
• Experience using GenAI / LLMs to support operational workflows and analytics.
• Any exposure to automation tools (e.g. Power Automate) and to producing presentation materials is an advantage.
Nice to have (but not required)
• University or personal projects involving real datasets.
• A basic understanding of data modelling or data pipelines.
• An interest in — or willingness to learn — insurance and aviation. Domain knowledge can be developed on the job.
Key Stakeholders
• Emma Roberts and the wider Aviation team.
• Aviation brokers and client executives.
• Markets / insurers (indirectly, through placement data and reporting).
• Central Data & Analytics team; IT / AI development teams.
• Operations teams.
How Success Will Be Measured
• Accuracy and timeliness of reporting.
• Quality and usefulness of data insights.
• Data quality and completeness across the aviation portfolio.
• Growing confidence and independence with the data platform and analytical tooling.
• Adoption and effectiveness of AI-enabled tools in day-to-day work.
• Progress against agreed learning and development goals.
Tools & Systems (Typical)
• Microsoft Excel.
• Power BI.
• SQL / data lake (e.g. Databricks).
• Power Automate / Power Platform.
• SharePoint / Dataverse
• GenAI tools (e.g. Copilot / Claude) for reporting and process support.
What You’ll Get 
• A structured early-career role with on-the-job learning and mentoring.
• Exposure to client and operations work across a specialist line of business.
• Training and professional qualifications (e.g. Chartered Insurance Institute).
• Competitive salary, generous pension and private medical cover.

What do we offer in return?

A career that you define. At Howden, we value diversity – there is no one Howden type. Instead, we’re looking for individuals who share the same values as us:
• Our successes have all come from someone brave enough to try something new

• We support each other in the small everyday moments and the bigger challenges

• We are determined to make a positive difference at work and beyond

Reasonable adjustments

We're committed to providing reasonable accommodations at Howden to ensure that our positions align well with your needs. Besides the usual adjustments such as software, IT, and office setups, we can also accommodate other changes such as flexible hours* or hybrid working*.

If you're excited by this role but have some doubts about whether it’s the right fit for you, send us your application – if your profile fits the role’s criteria, we will be in touch to assist in helping to get you set up with any reasonable adjustments you may require.

*Not all positions can accommodate changes to working hours or locations. Reach out to your Recruitment Partner if you want to know more.

Permanent

jobs.description:
APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS:
• CURRENT PENN STATE EMPLOYEE (faculty, staff, technical service, or student), please login to Workday to complete the internal application process. Please do not apply here, apply internally through Workday. 

• CURRENT PENN STATE STUDENT (not employed previously at the university) and seeking employment with Penn State, please login to Workday to complete the student application process. Please do not apply here, apply internally through Workday.

• If you are NOT a current employee or student, please click “Apply” and complete the application process for external applicants.

Approval of remote and hybrid work is not guaranteed regardless of work location. For additional information on remote work at Penn State, see Notice to Out of State Applicants. 

​

POSITION SPECIFICS​
Your working location will be 100% on-site, but options may exist for a hybrid work from office and work from home scenario dependent upon research requirements. Questions related to flexible work should be directed to the hiring manager during the interview process. 

We are searching for an entry-level Electrical Engineering Technologist to join the Mechanical – Electrical Design and Drafting Service Center of the Applied Research Laboratory (ARL) at Penn State University. In this role, you will assist in the design, analysis, manufacture, and procurement support of Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs) in support of ARL’s research offices. 
 
ARL is an authorized DoD SkillBridge partner and welcomes all transitioning military members to apply.
 
You will: 
• Support cutting-edge research utilizing PCB software to create schematics, PCBs, assemblies, library parts, bills of materials, and other documentation
• Collaborate with technical staff on conceptual design of electro-mechanical systems
• Assist with or facilitate material selection, packaging, tolerance analysis, manufacturing support, and cost projections efforts
• Provide work status updates and present in design review meetings with senior staff 
• Assist and support senior technical staff evolving design methods and techniques, including templates, as required for new and evolving research programs
• Assist and support the development or evaluation of new software tools and work processes to improve department capabilities in design, reporting, and efficiency of operation
 
Required skills/experience areas include: 
• Basic working knowledge of electronic circuits and components in analog and digital design
• Microsoft Office and Adobe products
• Previous success with collaborations in a diverse, multi-disciplinary, team-oriented culture
 
Preferred experience areas include: 
• PCB design software, including component creation, schematic layout, and design
• Altium software
• Electronics industry knowledge from PCB design through manufacturing
• Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) and Configuration Management (CM)
• Certification or familiarization with IPC standards

Bachelor's Degree
1+ years of relevant experience
Required Certifications:
None

Bachelor's Degree
No prior relevant work experience required

None
 
ARL’s purpose is to research and develop innovative solutions to challenging scientific, engineering, and technology problems in support of the Navy, the Intel Community (IC), and other federal government customers.

BACKGROUND CHECKS/CLEARANCES

Employees must be eligible to obtain a government security clearance, participate in the ARL drug testing program, and comply with electronic and physical monitoring requirements applicable to federal contractors. ARL operates in a secure information environment involving Unclassified, Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), and Classified information. Personal electronic devices brought onsite must be registered and may be restricted from certain areas. You must be a U.S. citizen to apply. 
SALARY & BENEFITS
The salary range for this position, including all possible grades, is $68,604.00 - $113,100.00.

jobs.description:
Company
Cox Automotive - USA
Job Family Group

Engineering / Product Development
Job Profile

Data Engineer I
Management Level

Individual Contributor
Flexible Work Option 

Can work remotely but need to live in the specified city, state, or region
Travel %

No
Work Shift

Day
Compensation
Compensation includes a base salary in the range of $67,100.00 - $100,700.00. The base salary may vary within the anticipated base pay range based on factors such as the ultimate location of the position and the selected candidate’s knowledge, skills, and abilities. Position may be eligible for additional compensation that may include an incentive program.
Job Description

Our Data & Analytics team partners closely with business stakeholders to deliver trusted data, analytics, and insights that support operational and strategic decision-making. We design, build, and maintain a modern data warehouse that serves as the foundation for reporting, analytics, and data-driven solutions across our line of business.

We are seeking a Data Engineer I to join our team and help develop scalable data solutions that transform raw data into actionable insights. This role is ideal for someone early in their data engineering career who wants hands-on experience with modern cloud technologies, AI-assisted development workflows, and data warehousing practices, working alongside experienced engineers, analysts, and business partners to build pipelines, enhance our Data Vault-based warehouse, and deliver high-quality data assets.

What You'll Do

• Build, test, and maintain data pipelines that ingest, transform, and deliver data from operational and third-party source systems.
• Contribute to the ongoing development of our Data Vault-based data warehouse.
• Develop and optimize ELT processes using modern cloud data platforms and transformation tools.
• Partner with analysts and business stakeholders to translate data requirements into scalable technical solutions.
• Monitor and improve data quality, reliability, and performance across warehouse and reporting solutions.
• Participate in code reviews, testing activities, and technical design discussions.
• Create and maintain technical documentation for data flows, transformations, and business rules.
• Support production processes and assist in troubleshooting data-related issues.
• Use AI-assisted development tools like Claude Code as part of daily engineering work — pipeline development, code review, testing, and documentation.
• Continuously learn and apply emerging technologies, tools, and engineering best practices.

Our Team
Our team delivers the data foundation that enables analytics, reporting, and data-driven decision-making across the business. We build and maintain a Data Vault-based warehouse that integrates data from numerous operational systems and provides trusted, analytics-ready data to stakeholders across the organization.

Our technology stack includes:

• Warehousing & Transformation: Snowflake, dbt Cloud, Data Vault 2.0
• Cloud Platforms: AWS, Microsoft Azure, Microsoft Fabric
• Source Systems: Microsoft SQL Server
• Engineering Practices: Git-based source control, CI/CD
• AI-Assisted Development: Claude Code

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science. The right candidate could also have a different combination, such as 4 years’ experience in a related field.
• Experience writing and troubleshooting SQL queries.
• Understanding of relational database concepts, including tables, joins, keys, and normalization.
• Foundational knowledge of data integration, ETL/ELT, or data warehousing concepts.
• Experience with a programming or scripting language such as Python, SQL, PowerShell, or similar.
• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and troubleshooting skills.
• Ability to work effectively in a collaborative team environment.
• Strong verbal and written communication skills.
• Demonstrated ability to learn new technologies and adapt to changing business and technical requirements.
• Availability for rotational on-call duties outside of standard business hours may be required.

Preferred Qualifications

• Internship, co-op, academic project, or professional experience related to data engineering, analytics, software engineering, or business intelligence.
• Experience working with cloud platforms such as AWS or Microsoft Azure.
• Familiarity with Snowflake, Microsoft Fabric, or other cloud-based data platforms.
• Experience using dbt or similar data transformation frameworks.
• Understanding of data warehousing methodologies, including Data Vault, dimensional modeling, or star schema design.
• Experience developing or supporting data pipelines and data integration processes.
• Familiarity with source control systems such as Git, GitHub, or Azure DevOps.
• Exposure to CI/CD concepts and modern software development practices.
• Experience with analytics and reporting tools such as Power BI.
• Relevant certifications in Microsoft Azure, AWS, Snowflake, Microsoft Fabric, or related technologies.

Who You Are

You're curious, analytical, and motivated to learn. You enjoy working with data, solving problems, and collaborating with others to deliver solutions that create business value. You're excited to build a strong foundation in modern data engineering while contributing to a team that shapes how data is leveraged across the business.

Drug Testing

To be employed in this role, you’ll need to clear a pre-employment drug test. Cox Automotive does not currently administer a pre-employment drug test for marijuana for this position. However, we are a drug-free workplace, so the possession, use or being under the influence of drugs illegal under federal or state law during work hours, on company property and/or in company vehicles is prohibited.
Benefits

The Company offers eligible employees the flexibility to take as much vacation with pay as they deem consistent with their duties, the company’s needs, and its obligations; seven paid holidays throughout the calendar year; and up to 160 hours of paid wellness annually for their own wellness or that of family members. Employees are also eligible for additional paid time off in the form of bereavement leave, time off to vote, jury duty leave, volunteer time off, military leave, and parental leave.
About Us

Through groundbreaking technology and a commitment to stellar experiences for drivers and dealers alike, Cox Automotive employees are transforming the way the world buys, owns, sells – or simply uses – cars. Cox Automotive employees get to work on iconic consumer brands like Autotrader and Kelley Blue Book and industry-leading dealer-facing companies like vAuto and Manheim, all while enjoying the people-centered atmosphere that is central to our life at Cox. Benefits of working at Cox may include health care insurance (medical, dental, vision), retirement planning (401(k)), and paid days off (sick leave, parental leave, flexible vacation/wellness days, and/or PTO). For more details on what benefits you may be offered, visit our benefits page. Cox is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer – All qualified applicants/employees will receive consideration for employment without regard to that individual’s age, race, color, religion or creed, national origin or ancestry, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, physical or mental disability, veteran status, genetic information, ethnicity, citizenship, or any other characteristic protected by law. Cox provides reasonable accommodations when requested by a qualified applicant or employee with disability, unless such accommodations would cause an undue hardship.

EOE, including disability/vets 
 
Applicants must currently be authorized to work in the United States for any employer without current or future sponsorship. No OPT, CPT, STEM/OPT or visa sponsorship now or in future.

jobs.title: Robotics Engineer 1
jobs.description:
Application close date:
Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.
At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!  

-

About the Role
The New Product Formulation team turns ideas and early concepts into credible products. This role combines robotics simulation, learned manipulation policies, and hands-on hardware to answer the questions that shape new robotic products.

You'll build simulation environments, train and evaluate robot manipulation policies, operate real hardware, and run the experiments that inform system-level trades on mobility, manipulation, power, and compute. The work spans the full stack — writing control software in ROS 2 one day, collecting teleoperation data the next, and presenting trade study results to stakeholders by end of the week. If you're energized by switching between a sim environment, a lab bench, and a design review, this is the role.

What You'll Do

• Develop, train, fine-tune, and evaluate robot manipulation policies (e.g., vision-language-action models, imitation learning, reinforcement learning) on multi-step tasks.
• Collect teleoperation demonstration data and build the data pipelines used for policy training and benchmarking.
• Build and maintain simulation environments in NVIDIA Omniverse, Isaac Sim, and Isaac Lab, including custom terrain, lighting, and physical conditions, and work to close the sim-to-real gap.
• Integrate, bring up, and operate robot hardware, including arms, dexterous hands and grippers, cameras, force/torque sensors, and commercial platforms.
• Write and maintain robot software in ROS 2, including control interfaces, perception pipelines, and safety limits on joints, forces, and workspace.
• Support system-level trade studies for mobility, power, thermal, compute, and communications by running analyses, simulations, and prototype tests that inform design decisions.
• Document results clearly and share findings with the broader team and stakeholders.

Minimum Qualifications• Minimum of a B.S. degree in Robotics, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Aerospace Engineering, or a related field.
• Hands-on experience with real robot hardware through coursework, research, internships, or project teams (e.g., competition robotics, rover teams, lab work).
• Proficiency in Python. Working knowledge of C++.
• Familiarity with robot kinematics, dynamics, and control fundamentals.
• Experience with at least one robotics simulation environment.
• Comfort working in a lab: assembling hardware, wiring, debugging sensors, and safely operating robots.
• Must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Preferred Qualifications• M.S. in a relevant field, or equivalent research experience.
• Experience training or fine-tuning learned robot policies (imitation learning, RL, VLA/foundation models) using frameworks such as PyTorch or JAX.
• Experience with ROS 2.
• Experience with NVIDIA Omniverse, Isaac Sim, or Isaac Lab.
• Experience with industrial or collaborative robot arms (e.g., Universal Robots).
• Experience with physics-based terrain, contact, or soil-interaction modeling.
• Exposure to computer vision and perception for manipulation (pose estimation, segmentation, depth sensing).
• Experience with teleoperation systems or data collection for robot learning.
• Familiarity with designing hardware for harsh or extreme operating environments.
• You've worked across software, simulation, and hardware, and you enjoy switching between them.

Base Pay Range for:
WA applicants is $110,623.00 - $154,871.85
Other site ranges may differ

Culture Statement
Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. jobs.description:
RELOCATION ASSISTANCE: Relocation assistance may be available

CLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: Yes

CLEARANCE TYPE: Secret

TRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the TimeDescription

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

Northrop Grumman Mission Systems is a trusted provider of mission-enabling solutions for global security. We have a wide portfolio of secure, affordable, integrated, and multi-domain systems and technologies. Our differentiated battle management and cyber solutions deliver timely, mission-enabling information and provide superior situational awareness and understanding to protect the U.S. and its global allies.
 
Entry Level opportunities at Northrop Grumman are unique. Are you interested in boosting your knowledge through experience and exposure, while supporting a mission that seeks to protect our nation and its allies? If so, then Northrop Grumman is the place you!
 
Our professionals live and breathe different perspectives; we are curious about the world, accepting each other, and aware that the more ideas, backgrounds, opinions and experiences we bring to our work, the stronger that work will be. Just as you would invest your time and hard work into our company, we focus on investing back into you through enriching professional experiences and high-quality learning and development opportunities. We want you to bring your whole self to work, and for you to have meaningful connections with your coworkers, customers and communities, while providing the best products, systems and technologies to protect our world.
 
Northrop Grumman is seeking Associate Digital Engineers. This position will be located at our Mission Systems sector in Baltimore, MD. This position will be in the Pathways rotational program.
 
The qualified candidate will become part of Northrop Grumman’s BaPS Division.
 
Basic Qualifications:
A candidate must meet ALL of the below criteria. The candidate must:
• Be completing or has completed their Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution
• Be majoring in or having majored in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a very closely related STEM field.
• Be able to obtain a U.S. Government security clearance (U.S. citizenship is a pre-requisite)
• The ability to obtain Special Access Program within a reasonable period of time, as determined by the company to meet its business needs
• A final DoD Secret Clearance is required to start
 
Preferred Qualifications: 
• Have an overall cumulative GPA of 3.00/4.0 or higher
• A current/active DoD secret clearance
 
Salary Range: 
$72,700 - 109,100

Primary Level Salary Range: $72,700.00 - $109,100.00

The above salary range represents a general guideline; however, Northrop Grumman considers a number of factors when determining base salary offers such as the scope and responsibilities of the position and the candidate's experience, education, skills and current market conditions.

Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay. Annual bonuses are designed to reward individual contributions as well as allow employees to share in company results. Employees in Vice President or Director positions may be eligible for Long Term Incentives. In addition, Northrop Grumman provides a variety of benefits including health insurance coverage, life and disability insurance, savings plan, Company paid holidays and paid time off (PTO) for vacation and/or personal business.

The application period for the job is estimated to be 20 days from the job posting date. However, this timeline may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates.

Northrop Grumman is an Equal Opportunity Employer, making decisions without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, national origin, age, veteran status, disability, or any other protected class. For our complete EEO and pay transparency statement, please visit http://www.northropgrumman.com/EEO. U.S. Citizenship is required for all positions with a government clearance and certain other restricted positions.

More than a career - a chance to make a difference in people's lives.

Build an exciting, rewarding career with us – help us make a difference for millions of people every day. Consider joining the Duke Energy team, where you'll find a friendly work environment, opportunities for growth and development, recognition for your work, and competitive pay and benefits.

Associate Software Engineer: iGrid – Duke Energy

More than a career - this is a chance to make a difference.

Build an exciting and rewarding career at Duke Energy, where your work helps power millions of people every day. iGrid develops modern, cloud-native applications on AWS that support grid planning, resiliency, and the transition to cleaner energy. Our products help teams anticipate future energy demand, identify grid upgrade needs, and make data-driven investment decisions that shape the future of the electric grid.
We’re looking for an Associate Software Engineer who is eager to learn, grow, and contribute to meaningful, real-world software used in production to support grid modernization.

Responsibilities 

As an Associate Software Engineer, you’ll work as part of a small, collaborative Agile team building and supporting cloud-based software solutions. Under the guidance of experienced engineers, you’ll contribute to the full software development lifecycle—learning modern engineering practices while delivering code that runs in production and makes a real impact.

You will:
• Assist in designing, developing, testing, and debugging software solutions and enhancements

• Write clean, efficient, well-tested code following established design patterns and team standards

• Help build and maintain backend services, APIs, and data pipelines

• Support system monitoring, troubleshooting, and continuous improvement of reliability and performance

• Participate in Agile ceremonies, code reviews, and test-driven development practices

• Collaborate closely with software engineers, product owners, designers, and data engineers

• Learn and apply modern cloud-native patterns, automation, and CI/CD practices

Our technology stack
• AWS services such as S3, DynamoDB, Glue, Athena, EC2, Lambda, and CloudWatch

• Backend development and API design

• SQL and NoSQL data stores

• Event-driven and microservices-based architectures

• Automated testing, CI/CD pipelines, and observability tools

Basic/Required qualifications
• Associates degree in Information, or Other Related Degree

• In lieu of Associates degree(s) listed above, High School/GED AND 2 year(s) related work experience

Desired qualifications:
• Recently graduated or preparing to graduate with a 2-year or 4-year IT-related degree, or equivalent experience

• Previous Duke Energy experience

• Foundational knowledge of programming concepts and software development principles

• Exposure to full-stack development

• Strong curiosity, problem-solving skills, and desire to learn

• Ability to work effectively in a collaborative Agile environment

• Familiarity with Java, JavaScript, Angular, or REST APIs

• Exposure to AWS or other cloud platforms

• Internship, academic, or project experience delivering software

• Interest in cloud computing and DevOps practices

Working Conditions
• Hybrid Mobility Classification – Work will be performed from both remote and onsite locations after the onboarding period. However, hybrid employees should live within a reasonable daily commute to a Duke Energy facility.

Why iGrid?
• Real impact supporting cleaner, more reliable energy

• Growth-focused culture with mentoring

• Modern engineering practices and cloud-native systems

• Clear career progression opportunities

Apply now to help build the future of clean, reliable energy with iGrid at Duke Energy.

Are you ready to explore the world of aerospace and defense? Do you want to learn from and collaborate with some of the greatest minds in the industry? At RTX, our internships, co-ops and full-time careers provide an exceptional foundation to work on complex problems, advance your skills and create a safer, more connected world. Discover opportunities to make a difference at RTX. 

At RTX, the world's largest aerospace and defense company, 185,000 great minds are united by purpose and inspired to make a difference solving the world’s most complex problems. With our three market leading businesses, world-class operations and investments in research and development, we offer capabilities and opportunity no one else can. Collins Aerospace is a leader in technologically advanced, intelligent solutions that help redefine the aerospace and defense industry. With a comprehensive portfolio and deep technical expertise, we help customers meet the demands of the global market. Join us and help shape the future of aerospace and defense.

The Digital Hardware Design Engineer will collaborate closely with cross-functional partners, including Systems, Software, Mechanical, Environmental Effects, and Manufacturing/Operations teams, to ensure all product requirements are successfully achieved. Competence in high-speed digital circuit board design, testability, and thermal management is essential. 

What You Will Do: 
As an entry level Digital Hardware Design Engineer 1 at Collins Aerospace,
• You will design, analyze, simulate and test Circuit Card Assemblies for Avionics Computers (Processors, FPGAs, Memory, high-speed interfaces).
• You will operate lab equipment to perform integration testing on hardware designs.
• You will do schematic capture of digital/analog mixed signal electrical circuit designs.

• A Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering or related Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics (STEM) degree obtained prior to start.
• Familiarity with the development and design of electronic circuit designs, and/or multi-assembly system/unit design.

• Experience with design tools (schematic capture) and PCB design process to analyze and simulate designs prior to hardware implementation.
• Experience using PCB electronic circuit design software: signal integrity, power integrity and analog simulation.

jobs.title: Associate Software Engineer
jobs.description:
The Company: 
Marigold is a fast-growing marketing technology company helping growing businesses build stronger customer relationships through its three core platforms: Emma, Campaign Monitor, and Vuture. We deliver powerful tools for email, SMS, and marketing automation that elevate engagement and drive real results. Marigold is headquartered in Nashville, Tennessee with offices in Sydney and London.

The Role: 
At Emma, we’re looking for a driven, curious software engineer to join our team. The Emma Engineering organization is made up of passionate engineers focused on building elegant, reliable tooling that helps our customers succeed in their email marketing efforts. Our teams operate with clear ownership boundaries, allowing engineers to specialize, deepen their expertise, and build sustainable software that’s easy to support and evolve over time. We take pride in crafting creative, scalable solutions for a wide range of customers—and we genuinely enjoy doing it together.

This is an entry-level, Software Engineer role. On the frontend, we work primarily with React and supporting libraries, including a proprietary UI toolkit. Our backend systems are Python-driven, Django, and AWS-based. Experience in any of these areas is a plus, but a strong desire to learn and grow across the full stack is essential. Within your first six months, you’ll also have opportunities to contribute to additional areas of development as you continue to build your skills and expand your technical foundation.
 
What You’ll Do: 
• Build and ship code that solves real problems for real customers. Engineering is central to what we do, and you’ll work closely with your team to plan, experiment, and deliver impactful solutions.
• Collaborate in code reviews, sharing ideas, learning from others, and helping raise the bar on quality and best practices.
• Get hands-on with how Emma builds intuitive, scalable tooling that helps marketing teams do their best work.
• Have fun while doing it! We care deeply about our customers, move with intention, and genuinely enjoy building great products together.
• Use AI-assisted tools thoughtfully to research, prototype, and build, while learning how to apply them responsibly in a production codebase.

About You:
You’re an early-career developer who’s excited to learn, grow, and contribute as part of a collaborative engineering team. While you may not be a master of React, Python, or AWS yet, you bring curiosity, strong potential, and a genuine desire to build your skills and learn best practices. You care deeply about technology, the products you help create, and the customers who rely on them. You enjoy variety in your work, are eager to take on new challenges, and are motivated by opportunities to expand your knowledge and grow alongside a supportive team. You're comfortable using AI tools as part of your everyday workflow, and you know that good engineering still means understanding, questioning, and owning the code you ship.

Ideal Qualifications: 
• Early-career developer or recent graduate with a strong interest in software engineering
• Foundational experience or exposure to modern technologies such as React, Python, AWS, or similar tools
• Demonstrated curiosity and willingness to learn new technologies, frameworks, and best practices
• Passion for building quality products with the end user in mind
• Comfortable working across different areas of the codebase and contributing where needed
• Strong collaboration skills and openness to feedback and continuous improvement
• Comfortable using AI-assisted development tools (e.g., Copilot, Claude) to speed up your work, and able to critically review, test, and own the code they help produce

Location Eligibility
This position is eligible for hire in the following US states: Arizona, Florida, Georgia, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Texas, and Virginia.

Compensation & Benefits

Compensation:
The base salary range for this role is $70,000 -$80,000 annually.
The compensation range represents the pay the Company reasonably expects to offer for this position. Actual compensation will be determined based on factors such as skills, experience, qualifications, internal equity, geographic location, and applicable law.

Benefits: 
• Competitive benefits including: medical/dental/vision insurance, life/accident/disabilities insurance, supplemental health benefits, FSA, EAP and pet insurance
• Generous time off (we call it Open Time Away) as well as paid holidays and a birthday benefit day off.
• Paid Volunteer Time
• 401k plan with a company match on your contributions.
• Employee-centric and supportive remote work environment with flexibility.
• Support for life events including paid parental leave.

jobs.title: Research Science Engineering
jobs.description:
Come join Analog Devices (ADI) – a place where Innovation meets Impact. For more than 55 years, Analog Devices has been inventing new breakthrough technologies that transform lives. At ADI you will work alongside the brightest minds to collaborate on solving complex problems that matter from autonomous vehicles, drones and factories to augmented reality and remote healthcare.

ADI fosters a culture that focuses on employees through beneficial programs, aligned goals, continuous learning opportunities, and practices that create a more sustainable future. 

About Analog Devices
Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI) is a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge. ADI combines analog, digital, AI, and software technologies into solutions that combat climate change, reliably connect humans and the world, and help drive advancements in automation and robotics, mobility, healthcare, energy and data centers. With revenue of more than $11 billion in FY25, ADI ensures today's innovators stay Ahead of What's Possible. Learn more at www.analog.com and on LinkedIn and X.
 
We are seeking a Research Science Engineer to develop advanced semiconductor technologies, including wide-band-gap materials like Gallium Nitride (GaN) for high-performance power applications. The role involves device design, simulation, characterization, and process optimization to enable next-generation solutions. 
 
Key Responsibilities: 
• Perform TCAD simulations, device testing, and data analysis. 
• Design and layout test structures using Cadence tools. 
• Conduct electrical characterization with analyzers (e.g., Keysight B1500). 
• Collaborate with cross-functional teams to support technology qualification and product integration.

Qualifications: 
• BS in Electrical Engineering, Physics, or Materials Science; MS/PhD preferred. 
• Strong knowledge of semiconductor device physics and fabrication processes. 
• Hands-on experience in lab measurements and data analysis. 
• Familiarity with TCAD, Cadence, and reliability testing.

jobs.title: AI/Machine Learning Researcher
jobs.description:
Job Description
The Role: 
Conduct original research and develop practical AI/ML methods that accelerate GM’s research, engineering, and product development capabilities. This role is intended for a recent or soon-to-be-completed Ph.D. who brings strong depth in one or more advanced AI areas and the ability to work across disciplines. The researcher will develop proof-of-concepts (POCs), evaluate them on meaningful engineering or scientific problems, communicate findings clearly, and collaborate with senior researchers and engineering partners to move promising ideas toward impact.

The Team:  
GM R&D is seeking an outstanding early-career researcher to contribute to advanced work in Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Large Language Models. The role is designed for a fresh Ph.D. It emphasizes research depth, originality, experimental rigor, and growth toward independent technical leadership. The successful candidate will work with senior researchers, technical fellows, and engineering collaborators to formulate important problems, develop new methods, build research prototypes, and validate results. The work may span causal reasoning, neurosymbolic AI, world models, multimodal and generative AI, engineering agents, or related areas. The researcher will be expected to connect theory and experimentation with real engineering needs while maintaining high standards for reproducibility, explainability, uncertainty awareness, and responsible AI.

What You’ll Do:    
• Conduct original research in one or more advanced AI areas such as causal AI, neurosymbolic AI, world models, multimodal or generative AI or engineering agents.
• Translate engineering and scientific challenges into well-defined research questions, hypotheses, algorithms, and experimental plans.
• Design, implement, and evaluate machine learning models and proof-of-concepts using real, simulated, experimental, or engineering data.
• Develop methods that can reason about physical systems, causal relationships, uncertainty, constraints, temporal evolution, or complex interactions among components.
• Establish meaningful baselines and evaluation protocols; analyze failure modes, robustness, generalization, interpretability, and uncertainty rather than relying only on headline accuracy.
• Build reproducible research code, data-processing workflows, and experiment pipelines using modern deep learning practices.
• Collaborate with GM R&D researchers and engineering partners to understand domain constraints, validate research results, and identify pathways from POCs to practical use.
• Communicate technical findings through research reports, presentations, publications, invention disclosures, demonstrations, and clear documentation.
• Contribute to technical discussions and research roadmaps by identifying promising approaches, important risks, and high-value experiments.
• Participate in a collaborative research culture that values intellectual curiosity, constructive peer review, responsible innovation, and continuous learning.

More About Who You Are
• A curious and intellectually rigorous researcher who enjoys working on difficult, open-ended problems.
• Deeply grounded in at least one technical area, while eager to learn and collaborate across adjacent AI, computational science, and engineering disciplines.
• Motivated by research that can create measurable value in real-world engineering workflows, not only benchmark performance.
• Comfortable moving between mathematical formulation, algorithm development, software implementation, and empirical validation.
• Able to explain complex ideas, assumptions, limitations, and results to both technical and general audiences.
• Independent in driving research tasks to completion while actively seeking feedback and working effectively with senior mentors and cross-functional teams.
• Committed to careful experimentation, reproducibility, safety, explainability, and responsible use of AI.

Required Qualifications:     
• Pursuit or Completion of a PhD in one of the following areas: Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Applied Mathematics, Statistics, Computational Science, Engineering, Physics, or a related field
• Able to work fulltime, 40 hours per week 
• Demonstrated research depth in at least one relevant area, supported by a dissertation, publications, patents, open-source work, research software, or comparable technical contributions.
• Strong foundations in machine learning and deep learning, with working knowledge of optimization, probability/statistics, numerical methods, or scientific computing as appropriate to the research area.
• Experience developing and evaluating models in Python and frameworks such as PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow, or comparable tools.
• Ability to formulate experiments, select appropriate metrics and baselines, analyze results, and communicate technical conclusions with appropriate caveats.
• Strong verbal and written communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively with researchers, engineers, and technical stakeholders.
• Ability to work on-site or in a hybrid research environment in accordance with GM work practices and project needs.
 
Preferred Qualifications): 
• Research experience in causal inference, counterfactual reasoning, neurosymbolic methods and world models for engineering applications.
• Experience with multimodal AI, large language models, agentic systems, retrieval and reasoning, or AI-assisted engineering and software development.
• Evidence of research impact through high-quality publications, patents, invention disclosures, open-source contributions, awards, or successful technology demonstrations.
• Research or internship experience in automotive, mobility, aerospace, industrial, energy, defense, national laboratory, or university-industry collaboration settings.

jobs.title: Semiconductors and Compute Platforms Researcher - Compute Platforms & SoC/MCU Semiconductor Systems Researcher
jobs.description:
Job Description
The Role: 
GM R&D invents, evaluates, optimizes, and matures next-generation in-vehicle architectures, compute platforms, and communication systems that enable GM’s vision of the Software Defined Vehicle. We focus on how SoCs, MCUs, memory, networks, and low-level software come together into robust, safe, and cost-effective automotive platforms, spanning deeply embedded ECUs as well as high-performance compute platforms for infotainment and automated driving.

Semiconductors and compute platforms, with a focus on SoCs, MCUs, memory subsystems, and associated board-level and platform software technologies for automotive ECUs, infotainment systems, and centralized/automated driving compute platforms. You are expected to define, propose, and develop research projects in alignment with GM R&D’s strategy and priorities, and to clearly define, communicate and demonstrate the value your work creates for GM and our customers.
 
What You’ll Do:    
• Lead semiconductor-focused research projects that influence GM’s electrical and software architecture roadmaps (central compute, zonal ECUs, domain controllers, edge nodes, infotainment, and automated driving compute platforms).
• Design and implement proof-of-concept prototypes on our R&D lab benches, using evaluation platforms and representative in-vehicle architecture benches to validate concepts before transfer to product teams.
• Evaluate and benchmark SoCs/MCUs and memory technologies (CPU cores, accelerators, interconnects, DDR/LPDDR, flash, NVM, cache hierarchies) for latency, throughput, power, cost, and safety/security trade-offs.
• Explore and prototype new compute and communication concepts using FPGAs, evaluation boards, and custom circuitry to de-risk new architectures and features (e.g., real-time safety-critical functions, mixed‑criticality workloads).
• Contribute to ECU and board-level design concepts, working with internal teams and suppliers on power, clocks, reset, high-speed interfaces (PCIe, Ethernet, DDR), and bring-up strategies.
• Drive low-level software concepts around boot flows, board support packages (BSPs), bare-metal or RTOS-based implementations, device drivers, and hardware abstraction needed for SDV architectures.
• Collaborate closely with GM engineering, purchasing, and suppliers to align semiconductor choices with GM’s long-term architecture, safety, cybersecurity, and cost objectives.
• Seek out and aggressively pursue technology insertion opportunities at GM, working with product engineering and program teams to move successful research outcomes into production programs, pilots, or platform roadmaps.
• Publish and protect IP through internal reports, patents, and external publications where appropriate, and represent GM R&D at key technical conferences and workshops.

Required Qualifications:     
• Pursuit/completion of an advanced degree (Masters or PhD) degree in one of the following areas: Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or related field
• Must be graduating between August 2026 - June 2027
• Able to work fulltime, 40 hours per week
• Relevant research experience in semiconductors, SoC/MCU architecture, or embedded compute platforms. 
• Understanding of modern SoCs/MCUs, including:• CPU cores (e.g., Arm, RISC‑V), memory hierarchies, interconnects, and on-chip peripherals.
• High-speed interfaces (e.g., PCIe, Ethernet, SerDes, DDR/LPDDR, GDDR, NVMe).· 

• Knowledge of automotive communication protocols (e.g., Ethernet, Time Sensitive Networking Standards, CAN, LIN, PCIe-based architectures, SOME/IP) and in-vehicle networks.
• Hands-on experience in the use of oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and JTAG for board bring-up and debug.
• Experience with ECU or embedded system design and low-level software, such as:• Board support packages, bootloaders, bare-metal or RTOS-based implementations, hardware drivers.
• Integration of low-level software with hardware in lab or bench environments.

• Strong communication skills, including:• Presenting complex technical content at multiple levels of detail (lab leadership, cross-functional partners).

Preferred Qualifications): 
• PhD

jobs.title: Deep Learning Software Engineer New Grad - TensorRT Performance
jobs.description:
We are now looking for a Deep Learning Software Engineer, TensorRT Performance! NVIDIA is seeking an experienced Deep Learning Engineer passionate about analyzing and improving the performance of NVIDIA’s inference ecosystem! NVIDIA is rapidly growing our research and development for Deep Learning Inference and is seeking excellent Software Engineers at all levels of expertise to join our team. Companies around the world are using NVIDIA GPUs to power a revolution in deep learning, enabling breakthroughs in areas like Generative AI, Recommenders and Vision that have put DL into every software solution. Join the team that builds the software to enable the performance optimization, deployment and serving of these DL inference solutions. We specialize in developing GPU-accelerated deep learning inference software like TensorRT, DL benchmarking software and performant solutions to deploy and serve these models.

Collaborate with the deep learning community to integrate TensorRT into OSS frameworks like TensorRT-EdgeLLM and PyTorch. Identify performance opportunities and optimize SoTA models across the spectrum of NVIDIA accelerators, from datacenter GPUs to edge SoCs. Implement graph compiler algorithms, frontend operators and code generators across NVIDIA’s inference ecosystem. Work and collaborate with a diverse set of teams involving workflow improvements, performance modeling, performance analysis, kernel development and inference software development.

What you'll be doing:
• Establish groundbreaking performance benchmarking methodologies and analysis workflows and identify performance issues and opportunities for NVIDIA’s inference ecosystem (e.g. TensorRT/TensorRT-EdgeLLM/Torch-TensorRT)

• Contribute features and code to NVIDIA/OSS inference frameworks including but not limited to TensorRT/TensorRT-EdgeLLM/Torch-TensorRT.

• Develop new model pipelines for NVIDIA’s inference ecosystem with optimized performance including but not limited to areas like quantization, scheduling, memory management, and distributed inference to set the gold standard for Gen AI performance.

• Work with cross-collaborative teams inside and outside of NVIDIA across generative AI, automotive, robotics, image understanding, and speech understanding to set directions and develop innovative inference solutions.

• Scale performance of deep learning models across different architectures and types of NVIDIA accelerators.

What we need to see:
• Bachelors, Masters, PhD, or equivalent experience in relevant fields (Computer Science, Computer Engineering, EECS, AI).

• 2 years of relevant software development experience.

• Strong C++, Python programming and software engineering skills 

• Experience with DL frameworks (e.g. PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow, ONNX) and inference libraries (e.g. TensorRT, TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, SGLang, FlashInfer).

• Experience with performance analysis and performance optimization

Ways to stand out from the crowd:
• Strong foundation and architectural knowledge of GPUs.

• Deep understanding of modern deep learning models and workloads (e.g. Transformers, Recommenders, ASR, TTS, Visual Understanding).

• Proficiency in one of the deep learning programming domain specific languages (e.g. CUDA/TileIR/CuTeDSL/cutlass/Triton).

• Prior contributions to major LLM inference frameworks (e.g. vLLM) or prior experience with graph compilers in deep learning inference (e.g. TorchDynamo/TorchInductor).

• Prior experience optimizing performance for low-latency, resource-constrained systems or embedded AI pipelines (e.g. Jetson systems or other edge AI accelerators).

GPU deep learning has provided the foundation for machines to learn, perceive, reason and solve problems posed using human language. The GPU started out as the engine for simulating human imagination, conjuring up the amazing virtual worlds of video games and Hollywood films. Now, NVIDIA's GPU runs deep learning algorithms, simulating human intelligence, and acts as the brain of computers, robots and self-driving cars that can perceive and understand the world. Just as human imagination and intelligence are linked, computer graphics and artificial intelligence come together in our architecture. Two modes of the human brain, two modes of the GPU. This may explain why NVIDIA GPUs are used broadly for deep learning, and NVIDIA is increasingly known as “the AI computing company.” Come, join our DL Architecture team, where you can help build a real-time, cost-effective computing platform driving our success in this exciting and quickly growing field.

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and the pay of employees in similar positions. The base salary range is 124,000 USD - 195,500 USD for Level 2, and 152,000 USD - 241,500 USD for Level 3.
You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

jobs.title: Hardware Engineer Intern
jobs.description:
Meter builds networking hardware that businesses depend on to stay connected. Building great hardware requires more than designing circuits and shipping products, it means thinking deeply about performance, reliability, manufacturability, supply chain, installation, sustainability, and how our products operate throughout their entire lifecycle.



We are hiring Hardware Engineering Interns to explore and solve technical problems across Meter’s hardware engineering and operations teams. During the 12-week internship, you will own a well-scoped project based on your interests, experience, and the problems that matter most to Meter.



Depending on your interests and background, you could tackle:

 - Next-generation power adapters: Evaluate and prototype compact, efficient power supplies for future Meter compact products such as Pets. This is an engineering-focused project including architecture selection, component evaluation, thermal performance, efficiency, reliability, product design, and cost. Ultimately, your work could help the company accomplish prototypes that will directly translate to a shippable product.

 - Hardware lifecycle and sustainability: Explore how Meter products can be reused, refurbished, donated, disassembled, or recycled at end of life, including the technical and economic feasibility of extending their useful life.

 - Installer hardware and tooling: Design and prototype custom hardware, tools, fixtures, or diagnostic devices that make Meter networks easier and faster to install, service, and troubleshoot in the field.

 - Acoustics and thermal systems: Develop and characterize custom fan or cooling solutions for future high-performance networking and data center products, optimizing airflow, acoustics, reliability, power consumption, and mechanical constraints.

 - Supply chain intelligence: Analyze Meter’s component and supply-chain data to identify material risks, long-lead components, concentration risks, and potential bottlenecks before they affect hardware builds. This is a data analysis focused project.

This is a hands-on engineering role with real-world outcomes. You will work alongside Meter engineers, operators, suppliers, and manufacturing partners to understand a problem, evaluate potential solutions, build and test where appropriate, analyze the results, and recommend a path forward.




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

You will take ownership of a meaningful hardware problem and move it from an open question to an evidence-backed recommendation. Success could mean building and validating a working prototype, characterizing the performance of a new technology, identifying and qualifying a supplier, developing a tool that improves how we install or manufacture hardware, uncovering supply chain risks through data, or creating a process that Meter can put into practice.



You will leave behind something the Hardware team can use: data, prototypes, test results, engineering requirements, supplier evaluations, tools, or technical recommendations that help us build better products.



By the end of the internship, you should be able to explain what you investigated, how you tested your assumptions, what you learned, the engineering tradeoffs involved, and what Meter should do next.



Your day-to-day will depend on the project you choose, but you may:

 - Design, build, and test electrical or mechanical prototypes for future Meter products

 - Evaluate components, technologies, architectures, materials, and suppliers

 - Develop test plans and characterize performance, reliability, thermals, acoustics, power, or other system-level behavior

 - Work directly with networking hardware, PCBAs, mechanical assemblies, test equipment, and manufacturing samples

 - Analyze manufacturing, component, or supply chain data to identify trends, risks, and opportunities

 - Work with overseas suppliers and manufacturing partners to understand technical capabilities, constraints, cost, and scalability

 - Explore sustainability, repairability, refurbishment, component reuse, recycling, and other hardware lifecycle opportunities

 - Work cross-functionally with hardware engineering, supply chain, operations, software, product, finance, and other teams

 - Present your findings and recommendations to the Hardware team at the end of the internship




WHO YOU ARE

We are searching for people who are curious, hands-on, and excited to learn by building. You are a good fit if:

 - You are pursuing a degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, mechanical engineering, manufacturing engineering, industrial engineering, supply chain, or another related technical field

 - You enjoy taking ambiguous technical problems and breaking them into questions you can answer through engineering and experimentation

 - You have experience building, testing, debugging, or taking apart hardware, or are eager to learn

 - You are comfortable getting hands-on with physical systems, whether that means PCBAs, mechanical assemblies, test equipment, prototypes, manufacturing data, or supplier samples

 - You can use data to make engineering decisions rather than relying solely on intuition

 - You are comfortable learning things you have never encountered before and asking questions when you don’t understand something

 - You can communicate technical findings clearly and turn your work into recommendations that others can act on



Experience with networking hardware, electronics, embedded systems, PCB design, CAD, manufacturing, thermal design, acoustics, data analysis, supply chain, or hardware lifecycle engineering is a plus, but none is required individually.



More than anything, we’re looking for people who want to understand how great hardware gets built.




WHY METER?

Meter is a vertically integrated networking company. Hardware, software, services, ISP, and autonomous networks—all built on a single data pipeline from the local network to the data center.



The internet runs the world. Every purchase you make, video call you join, it's all packets flowing through networks. But those networks haven’t changed for decades. They’re brittle, complex, and surprisingly hard to set up in an enterprise space.



We started Meter to build better networks. We had to build everything from the ground-up: designing and building our own enterprise hardware, intuitive software, and streamlined operations to deliver great outcomes for our customers. Today, we build and deploy these networks at scale. Ambitious companies and enduring institutions like Bridgewater, Lyft, Reddit, rely on Meter to keep their thousands of employees and locations online and productive.



Our bet with Meter is simple: we will all use the internet more than we do today. We believe we have the definitive networking stack in place to enable business to do so as seamlessly and reliably as any modern utility.




COMPENSATION

 - The estimated hourly rate for this role is $25-40/hr.

By applying to this job you acknowledge that you've read and understood Meter's Job Applicant Privacy Notice https://www.meter.com/careers/job-applicant-privacy.

jobs.title: Firmware Engineer Intern
jobs.description:
About the role 
 Zipline aircraft rely on embedded firmware to execute flight and safety functions across a network of microcontrollers. As a Firmware Engineer Intern, you will own C++ firmware and supporting tools critical to the operation of these systems. You will work alongside electrical, mechanical, and systems engineers to turn flight data and hardware behavior into maintainable software for aircraft deployed globally. 
 What you'll do 
 
 Design and build C++ firmware for a distributed system of aircraft microcontrollers. 
 Develop reliable communication interfaces including Ethernet and serial. 
 Define platform-level interfaces and reusable firmware components for various aircraft subsystems. 
 Ensure predictable performance of microcontroller systems and communication buses during startup, real-time operation, and fault recovery. 
 Optimize real-time behavior, including CPU utilization, memory usage, scheduling latency, timing jitter, and resource contention. 
 Create metrics, monitoring, and troubleshooting tools to prepare systems for field deployment at scale. 
 Build Rust-based tooling and software-in-the-loop simulations to test and validate firmware. 
 
 What you'll need 
 
 Prior experience through internships or design teams. 
 Proficiency in writing C or C++. 
 Excellent grades in embedded systems coursework. 
 Interest in firmware, real-time systems, and Zipline's mission. 
 Rising seniors are preferred for this role. 
 
 Location & details 
 
 This is a full-time, on-site internship based in South San Francisco, California. 
 The term is for Summer 2027. 
 Candidates must be available to work on-site five days per week.

jobs.description:
At Manulife John Hancock, we believe in investing in the future, starting with you! Our GRO program is a bold new approach to early talent development, designed to launch your career with the support, structure, and opportunities you need to thrive. GRO is Manulife John Hancock’s flagship early talent program. It’s more than just a job, it’s a launchpad for your career. GRO offers a consistent, high-quality experience for new graduates across the organization. 

Launch your tech career with the Data Engineering stream of the GRO Program. This is a two-year program designed to develop future data engineering professionals by contributing to the company’s ongoing initiatives in data architecture, data processing, and analytics enablement. As part of GRO Data Engineering, you’ll gain access to a supportive community and benefit from structured learning, core skills training, mentorship, and leadership exposure, empowering you to grow your skills while making a real impact. With a values-first culture, professional development at every step, and a focus on your well-being and accelerated career progression, GRO Data Engineering is your gateway to a meaningful and future-ready career. 

Position Responsibilities: 
• Design, build, and maintain reliable, scalable data pipelines and workflows. 
• Ingest, integrate, transform, and prepare data from multiple sources for reporting, analytics, and other business use cases. 
• Develop reusable processes that transform raw data into reliable, accessible, and actionable information. 
• Contribute to data models and structures that support business and technical requirements. 
• Work with databases, data warehouses, and enterprise data platforms to organize and move data across systems. 
• Monitor and validate data to support its accuracy, completeness, consistency, and reliability. 
• Develop and maintain data quality checks, testing practices, and operational controls. 
• Build reproducible code and data workflows using SQL, Python, and modern data engineering tools. 
• Collaborate with engineering teams to deploy data solutions into production environments. 
• Participate in code reviews, testing, debugging, documentation, and collaborative development practices. 
• Support the monitoring, maintenance, troubleshooting, and continuous improvement of data pipelines and systems. 
• Collaborate with data engineers, software engineers, analysts, and business partners to understand data requirements and develop solutions. 
• Contribute to data documentation, lineage, quality, and governance practices. 
• Ensure data solutions align with privacy, security, and data governance principles. 

Required Qualifications 
• This program is designed for students currently completing undergraduate or graduate degrees who are excited to apply data engineering skills in real-world settings. 
• Graduating in December 2026 or May 2027 with a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field. 
• Experience using SQL to query, manipulate, or transform data. 
• Experience with at least one programming language, such as Python or Java. 
• Understanding of foundational data engineering concepts, including data pipelines, data processing, databases, and data integration. 
• Understanding of version control systems such as Git and collaborative coding practices. 
• Exposure to cloud platforms such as Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud and data tools such as Databricks or Spark. 
• Familiarity with ETL or ELT processes, data modeling, or data warehousing. 

Preferred Qualifications 
• Internship, co-op, or academic project experience in data engineering, software development, databases, or analytics. 
• Understanding of large-scale or distributed data processing concepts. 
• Familiarity with software development practices, including testing, debugging, documentation, and code reviews. 
• Understanding of Agile, Scrum, DevOps, or CI/CD practices. 
• Strong problem-solving and communication skills, with the ability to work collaboratively in teams. 
• Aptitude to solve business problems with technology. 

When You Join Our Team 
• We’ll empower you to learn and grow the career you want. 
• We’ll recognize and support you in a flexible environment where well-being and inclusion are more than just words. 
• As part of our global team, we’ll support you in shaping the future you want to see.

jobs.title: Software Engineer - Multiple Teams
jobs.description:
The Role

Triumph ships a lot of cards. Behind that is a warehouse, a network of vendors, and hundreds of people running processes that should be automated. This team builds the software that makes all of it work, and we are hiring an engineer to help us scale it.

You will be on a team of five building the software behind Triumph's physical card business: the portal vendors sell to us through, the dashboard that tracks our inventory, computer vision that identifies cards, and the tools Ops uses to audit and ship from our warehouse. You'll work full stack across our Go backend, React frontend, and React Native mobile apps.

This team sits closer to the physical cards than any other engineering team at Triumph. Every card we buy, vault, and ship moves through software you'll build. A problem Ops flags in the morning often has a fix by the afternoon. You can walk to the Ops floor and watch it get used the same day. Please note this role is located in Mountain View, and will most likely be moving to Fremont, CA in the near future.



What You'll Do

 - Build and scale the tooling that runs logistics: vendor intake, validation, fulfillment, and third party logistics integrations.

 - Automate manual operations processes, working alongside mechanical engineering, to increase how much Triumph can ship.

 - Extend our computer vision system for identifying cards from a photograph, expanding it beyond its current scope to additional trading card games.

 - Build event and experiential tools, like the iPad pack rip we ran at Collect-A-Con, and help shape what comes next. This is an area where we want your ideas as much as your code.

 - Own and improve the internal dashboard and other internal tooling as the team's scope grows.

 - Work across the whole stack. We also maintain a few iOS apps, which the team built along the way.

What We're Looking For

 - 1-5 years of full stack web development experience.

 - Comfort with ambiguity and ownership. Projects here are defined loosely and you will shape them.

 - Fluency with AI as a tool, never as a substitute for understanding. You use it aggressively and can explain every line that ships under your name.

 - Willingness to work on site most days, where the operation actually happens.

Why Triumph?

 - High growth. Build the platform under a high-scale consumer product that touches gaming, finance, and social, with 16x year-over-year growth.

 - High agency. We let builders build. Blast radius is contained by modularity and feature flags, not by process and approval gates. Small team, real ownership, significant room for leadership.

 - High stakes. Real money moves through your systems every minute. The work is visible, and it matters.

 - Competitive salary and benefits. $400/mo lunch credit, healthcare, vision, dental, 401k, etc.

 - In person. Our team gathers 5 days a week.
