jobs.title: Product Applications Engineer
jobs.description:
Product Applications Engineer (Full-Time)

Job Description

As an Astera Labs Product Applications Engineer, you will tackle complex debugging challenges that span from low-level firmware configuration to PCB hardware design and full system-level integration. You will be responsible for root-causing issues that cut across multiple layers simultaneously—for example, determining whether an issue is caused by a firmware bug, a board design problem, or a system configuration mismatch—and then driving those issues to resolution.

You will work directly with cutting-edge PCIe Gen6 fabric switches and connectivity products deployed in real data center environments, collaborating with firmware, board design, and system architecture teams. This role is for candidates who want to understand how an entire system works from chip to rack and are motivated by problems that do not have obvious answers.

Basic Qualifications

• 
B.S. or M.S. in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field, completed or expected by the start date.

• 
Strong coursework or foundation in digital logic design, computer architecture, analog/mixed-signal circuits, or embedded systems.

• 
GPA of 3.5 or higher, or equivalent demonstrated excellence in technical coursework.

Strong Candidates Will Have One or More of the Following Technical Skills

Firmware and Embedded Programming

• 
Proficiency in C for bare-metal or embedded firmware development.

• 
Understanding of register-level hardware interaction, memory-mapped I/O, bit manipulation, and interrupt-driven programming.

Circuit Design and Analog Fundamentals

• 
Understanding of basic circuit analysis, op-amp circuits, power supply design, signal conditioning, or mixed-signal concepts.

• 
Ability to reason about voltage levels, impedance, noise, and how digital signals behave as analog waveforms at high speeds.

Scripting and Automation

• 
Strong Python skills.

• 
Experience writing test automation scripts, parsing hardware logs, processing data, and interfacing with hardware over serial, I2C, or SMBus protocols.

Lab and Measurement Skills

• 
Hands-on experience with oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, logic analyzers, multimeters, function generators, JTAG debuggers, or serial terminal interfaces.

• 
Comfort taking real measurements and correlating them with expected circuit and system behavior.

Digital Systems and Computer Architecture

• 
Understanding of bus protocols, state machines, link-layer concepts, clock domain crossings, and how hardware and firmware interact at the register level.

Technical Communication

• 
Ability to clearly document findings, write bug reports, and produce concise technical summaries for internal engineering teams and external customers.

Preferred Technical Experience

• 
PCIe or high-speed serial protocols: Coursework or project experience involving PCIe, USB, Ethernet, SPI, UART, or I2C. Understanding of how data moves between ICs and how link negotiation and training work.

• 
Signal integrity fundamentals: Exposure to transmission line theory, impedance matching, S-parameters, eye diagrams, or PCB stack-up design through coursework or projects in electromagnetics or high-speed digital design.

• 
Firmware development and debugging: Experience building or modifying embedded firmware, flashing and debugging via UART/JTAG, reading register dumps, and correlating firmware state with hardware behavior.

• 
PCB and schematic reading: Ability to read hardware schematics and board layouts, with an understanding of power delivery, decoupling, high-speed trace routing, and via structures.

• 
FPGA or HDL experience: Verilog/VHDL coursework or project experience, with an understanding of RTL design, simulation, and synthesis.

• 
Linux proficiency: Comfort working in Linux command-line environments, including SSH, shell scripting with Bash, remote system management, file systems, and basic system administration.

What Sets the Best Candidates Apart

• 
Prior internship, co-op, or significant project experience involving silicon bring-up, embedded systems debugging, FPGA-based prototyping, or hardware/firmware co-development.

• 
Demonstrated ability to independently diagnose complex problems where the root cause is unclear and could span multiple engineering domains.

• 
Evidence of being a fast, self-directed learner who is comfortable picking up proprietary tools, unfamiliar codebases, and new hardware platforms with minimal guidance.

• 
Passion for understanding how things work at every level of the stack.

Salary range is $140,000 to $150,000 depending on experience, level, and business need. This role may be eligible for discretionary bonus, incentives and benefits.

We know that creativity and innovation happen more often when teams include diverse ideas, backgrounds, and experiences, and we actively encourage everyone with relevant experience to apply, including people of color, LGBTQ+ and non-binary people, veterans, parents, and individuals with disabilities.

jobs.title: Packaging Engineer Intern
jobs.description:
Packaging Engineer Intern

Location: San Jose, California, United States
Employment type: Internship
Organization: Packaging / Engineering Operations

About Astera Labs

Astera Labs is a semiconductor company developing intelligent connectivity solutions for AI and cloud infrastructure. Our products depend on high-performance interconnects and advanced semiconductor packaging to move data reliably across compute, memory, and storage systems.

Role overview

As a Semiconductor Packaging Intern, you will be part of the packaging team developing Astera Labs’ portfolio of connectivity products for leading cloud service providers and server and networking OEMs. You will help enhance key areas of the package development cycle, including package design, modeling, automation flows, and documentation.

You will work cross-functionally to understand project requirements and develop solutions throughout the packaging development cycle. This is a hands-on engineering role for someone interested in the interaction between electrical performance, power delivery, thermal behavior, mechanical constraints, and manufacturability. You will contribute to package-design and modeling work, document your results, and help the team make well-supported engineering decisions.

Responsibilities

• 
Support package design, modeling, automation, and documentation for Astera Labs’ connectivity products.

• 
Collaborate cross-functionally to understand project requirements and develop solutions throughout the packaging development cycle.

• 
Support package definition by organizing inputs such as die files, pin-out details, signal- and power-integrity requirements, thermal requirements, board and footprint constraints, supplier design rules, cost considerations, and reliability needs.

• 
Help maintain package Plan of Record (POR) information, including package structure, substrate stackup and materials, package SI/PI requirements, thermal requirements, development schedule, and open risks.

• 
Generate or review package netlists from die files and package footprints, and support package layout work with internal or external design partners.

• 
Import and prepare package layout data for analysis; verify nets, stackups, materials, vias, bumps, and BGA or solder-ball geometries against available design and manufacturing information.

• 
Support package-level signal-integrity and power-integrity analysis using tools such as ANSYS Electronics Desktop, HFSS 3D Layout, SIwave, and Keysight ADS as appropriate to the project.

• 
Set up ports and target nets, extract S-parameters, analyze insertion loss, return loss, crosstalk, impedance, and related channel behavior, and compare results with design requirements.

• 
Support power-integrity studies such as DCIR, PDN impedance, and transient or frequency-domain analysis; help interpret voltage drop, current density, resonance, and impedance results.

• 
Assist with thermal and mechanical analyses by organizing material and structural inputs, reviewing results, and helping identify risks related to temperature, stress, warpage, or reliability.

• 
Review package layouts against substrate and OSAT design rules and support design-for-manufacturing activities such as density checks, degassing considerations, and design-rule checks.

• 
Contribute to package tape-out and NPI readiness reviews by checking documentation and tracking open actions.

• 
Help prepare and maintain package documentation, including bills of materials, netlists, package outline or lid information, substrate stackup drawings, and electrical, thermal, or mechanical models when applicable.

• 
Support communication with substrate suppliers and OSAT partners by organizing questions, requirements, feedback, and manufacturing-readiness information.

• 
Document assumptions, simulation setups, results, issues, and recommendations in a clear and reusable format; present project learnings at the end of the internship.

Basic qualifications

• 
Working towards an M.S. or PhD in Electrical Engineering or a related field.

• 
Cumulative GPA of 3.3/4.0 or higher.

• 
Entrepreneurial, open-minded behavior and a hands-on work ethic, with the ability to prioritize a dynamic list of multiple tasks.

• 
Ability to work with minimal supervision and deliver solutions in a fast-paced environment.

• 
Strong time-management skills and strong written and verbal communication skills.

Required experience

• 
Coursework in RF/microwave, communication systems and signal analysis, semiconductor manufacturing, or circuit design.

• 
Understanding of or coursework in signal and power integrity is a plus.

• 
Understanding of or coursework in semiconductor packaging is a plus.

• 
Scripting or software-development experience in Python, Visual Basic, or equivalent programming languages.

• 
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with careful attention to detail when working with geometry, models, data, and documentation.

• 
Ability to communicate clearly, collaborate across disciplines, and follow through on defined tasks.

Preferred experience

• 
Experience with physical-design or layout tools such as AutoCAD, Cadence Allegro, Cadence APD/SiP, or comparable tools.

• 
Experience using 3D electromagnetic-simulation tools such as ANSYS Electronics Desktop, HFSS, HFSS 3D Layout, or SIwave.

• 
Knowledge of semiconductor multilayer flip-chip packages, including FCBGA or FCCSP.

• 
Experience with package substrate stackups, copper pillars, solder bumps, BGA balls, package-to-board transitions, or high-density interconnects.

• 
Familiarity with S-parameter extraction and validation, including ports, Touchstone models, passivity, causality, de-embedding, or mixed-mode analysis.

• 
Exposure to power-integrity concepts such as IR drop, DCIR, PDN impedance, decoupling, or current-density analysis.

• 
Experience with thermal modeling, mechanical analysis, coefficient-of-thermal-expansion effects, warpage, reliability, or package materials.

• 
Familiarity with design-for-manufacturing, supplier design rules, package assembly, reflow, underfill, or OSAT workflows.

• 
Experience using Python, MATLAB, Visual Basic, spreadsheets, or similar tools to automate analysis, process engineering data, or communicate results.

• 
Prior semiconductor, package-design, hardware, supplier, or manufacturing experience through coursework, research, projects, or an internship.

What success looks like

• 
You learn the packaging development flow and the team’s analysis tools, then take ownership of a defined technical task with appropriate guidance.

• 
You produce accurate, traceable analysis or documentation; communicate assumptions and risks early; and follow open actions through to closure.

• 
By the end of the internship, you have contributed useful results to a package-design, SI/PI, thermal/mechanical, DFM, tape-out, or manufacturing-readiness workstream and can clearly explain your approach, findings, and impact.

Internship experience and compensation

This is a paid, hourly U.S. internship. The applicable hourly rate is determined as part of the offer process and specified in the offer letter, depending on education level ranges form $35/hour to $55/hour. U.S. interns currently receive a $500-per-week housing/relocation stipend for the duration of the internship. Interns participate in Early Career programming, including technical and professional-development sessions, community events, and an end-of-program project presentation.

Equal opportunity

Astera Labs is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. We encourage anyone with relevant experience to apply.

About Astera Labs

Astera Labs provides rack-scale AI infrastructure through purpose-built connectivity solutions. Our Intelligent Connectivity Platform brings together technologies including PCIe®, CXL®, Ethernet, NVLink, and UALink™ with the COSMOS software suite to help customers build cohesive, flexible AI systems.

This is an early-career role for an engineer who enjoys working close to hardware, learning quickly, and solving problems that cross traditional team boundaries. • 
Participate in design reviews, technical discussions, code or script reviews, and issue-tracking workflows.

• 
Maintain clear documentation of test setups, procedures, results, known issues, and recommendations.

• 
Take ownership of a defined workflow or project area, manage blockers with support, and progressively contribute reusable team output.

What You Bring

Required Qualifications

• 
Bachelor’s or master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field.

• 
Coursework, project, research, or laboratory experience in electrical engineering fundamentals, computer architecture, embedded systems, digital systems, signal integrity, or high-speed interfaces.

• 
Working knowledge of systematic debugging, measurement, data analysis, and technical documentation.

• 
Ability to read and interpret schematics, datasheets, specifications, and test results.

• 
Experience with Python, MATLAB, or another scripting language for automation, analysis, or engineering workflows.

• 
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical findings clearly.

• 
Collaborative mindset, learning agility, ownership potential, and the ability to execute with increasing independence.

Exposure to PCIe®, CXL®, Ethernet, SERDES, retimers, switches, NICs, or related connectivity technologies.

• 
Familiarity with signal-integrity concepts such as channel loss, jitter, equalization, eye diagrams, or link margin.

• 
Hands-on experience with oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, BERTs, power supplies, or similar laboratory equipment.

• 
Experience with embedded systems, register-level configuration, I2C or other control interfaces, firmware logs, or hardware/software integration.

• 
Experience building automated test flows, analyzing large data sets, or improving lab and validation processes.

• 
Prior internship, co-op, capstone, research, or project experience involving semiconductor, networking, computing, or AI-infrastructure systems.

Compensation

The base salary range for North Carolina NCG roles is $130,000–$150,000. Compensation details will be provided as part of the offer process and determined in accordance with applicable company guidelines.

Equal Opportunity

Astera Labs is committed to equal employment opportunity and to building an inclusive workplace. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, skills, experience, and business needs.

Platform Software Diagnostics Intern

Astera Labs · San Jose, CA · Internship · On-site

About Astera Labs

Astera Labs builds connectivity solutions and software that help power modern AI infrastructure. Our platform software connects low-level device behavior, diagnostics, telemetry, validation, and fleet-scale manageability so customers can identify issues quickly and keep critical systems running.

The opportunity

Join the Platform Software Diagnostics team within Hardware Engineering and work at the boundary of software and hardware. You’ll help create practical tools for board and chip bring-up, production testing, validation, and data-driven debugging across Astera Labs’ product lines.

This internship is designed for someone who enjoys learning by doing: reading a specification, writing code, connecting to real hardware, running a test, investigating the result, and improving the tool or workflow. You’ll work alongside experienced engineers and contribute to projects that turn low-level device behavior into reliable, understandable diagnostics.

What you’ll do

• 
Develop and improve diagnostic utilities in C for board and chip bring-up, including register access, initialization, device discovery, and device-health checks.

• 
Read schematics, specifications, register descriptions, and test output to understand expected hardware behavior and diagnose issues.

• 
Write Python utilities and test automation to make validation, data collection, and debugging more repeatable.

• 
Use Raspberry Pi-based lab systems and development tools to interact with boards, connectivity modules, and other hardware under test.

• 
Create or maintain tests for production and validation workflows, helping identify failures earlier and improve test coverage.

• 
Reproduce hardware/software issues, form hypotheses, run focused experiments, analyze evidence, and document findings.

• 
Collaborate with engineers across diagnostics, validation, production, and related hardware/software teams to communicate results and deliver practical fixes.

• 
Participate in code reviews, issue tracking, technical discussions, and documentation that make the team’s work easier to maintain and scale.

• 
Present your project, results, and key learnings at the end of the internship.

Additional opportunities

Depending on project needs and your interests, you may also:

• 
Investigate test results and failure logs, improving parsing, reporting, and data visualization so engineers can understand issues faster.

• 
Contribute to regression and infrastructure projects, such as unit-test or pytest enablement, Jenkins workflows, time-series test data, or software-release automation.

What you bring

• 
Hands-on experience with C, Python, or another programming language through coursework, projects, research, or prior experience.

• 
Curiosity about how software interacts with physical systems and a willingness to learn from schematics, specifications, registers, and test output.

• 
Comfort working in a Linux development environment and using Git-based workflows.

• 
A methodical approach to debugging: forming hypotheses, running focused tests, analyzing evidence, and documenting what you learn.

• 
Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to collaborate across software and hardware disciplines.

• 
Ownership, persistence, and a practical mindset in an environment where the first attempt may not work.

Helpful experience

Embedded software, device drivers, bare-metal development, or low-level debugging.

• 
I2C, SPI, PCIe, CXL, SerDes, signal-integrity concepts, or other hardware interfaces.

• 
Raspberry Pi, lab automation, test equipment, or semiconductor/networking hardware.

• 
Python test automation, pytest, log parsing, data analysis, or dashboard development.

• 
Jenkins or other continuous-integration and regression systems.

Internship experience and compensation

U.S. interns currently receive a $500-per-week housing/relocation stipend for the duration of the internship.

About Astera Labs

Astera Labs develops purpose-built connectivity solutions for rack-scale AI infrastructure. Our Intelligent Connectivity Platform brings together high-performance connectivity technologies for AI, cloud, server, and networking systems.

The role

As a Physical Design Engineer Intern in Toronto, you will gain hands-on experience taking a digital-design block through the physical-design flow, from RTL handoff and synthesis through floorplanning, placement, clock-tree synthesis, routing, timing closure, and signoff. You will read tool reports, debug flow issues, analyze power, performance, and area, and work with engineers across the ASIC implementation lifecycle.

This internship is an opportunity to build practical VLSI and backend-design skills while learning how physical implementation decisions affect timing, congestion, power integrity, reliability, and manufacturability.

What you’ll do

• 
Set up and run physical-design flow stages for a block using established methodologies and reproducible work areas.

• 
Review RTL and physical-design inputs, including netlists, constraints, technology files, libraries, and parasitic or extraction data.

• 
Support synthesis, floorplanning, power-grid planning, placement, clock-tree synthesis, routing, and implementation optimization.

• 
Analyze timing reports, slack, skew, transition, congestion, utilization, and other quality-of-results metrics.

• 
Help investigate setup and hold violations and evaluate fixes such as cell sizing, buffering, Vt swaps, useful skew, and routing optimization.

• 
Review physical-verification and power-integrity results, including DRC, LVS, antenna, electromigration, and IR-drop findings.

• 
Use Unix/Linux and Tcl or other scripting tools to automate runs, parse reports, compare experiments, and improve flow reproducibility.

• 
Debug tool errors, warnings, broken stages, and unexpected QoR changes by examining logs, configurations, and generated reports.

Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field.

• 
Coursework, project, research, or hands-on experience with digital logic, VLSI, ASIC design, computer architecture, or semiconductor engineering.

• 
Foundational understanding of timing, setup and hold, clocks, power, placement, routing, or physical verification concepts.

• 
Familiarity with Unix/Linux command-line environments and at least one scripting or programming language, such as Tcl, Python, shell, or C/C++.

• 
Strong analytical and debugging skills, attention to detail, and interest in understanding how designs become manufacturable silicon.

• 
Strong written and verbal communication, organization, and time-management skills.

• 
A hands-on work ethic, curiosity, learning agility, and ability to take ownership of assigned deliverables.

Experience with synthesis, floorplanning, placement, clock-tree synthesis, routing, static timing analysis, or physical-verification tools.

Familiarity with EDA tools such as Fusion or Genus, Innovus, PrimeTime, Calibre, Voltus, or equivalent tools.

Understanding of PVT corners, OCV/AOCV/LVF, timing closure, congestion, power planning, EMIR, DRC, LVS, or antenna checks.

Experience writing Tcl, Python, shell, or Make-based automation for design flows and report analysis.

jobs.description:
Hardware Test/Mechanical Engineer Intern

Astera Labs · San Jose, CA · Internship · On-site

About Astera Labs

Astera Labs builds connectivity solutions and software that help power modern AI infrastructure. Our Hardware Engineering teams develop and support the boards, modules, test platforms, and validation systems that enable high-performance connectivity products.

The opportunity

Join the Hardware Engineering team and work at the intersection of mechanical design, hardware testing, and product validation. You’ll help develop and evaluate the mechanical parts, fixtures, enclosures, and test setups that support board bring-up, engineering development, manufacturing, and validation across Astera Labs’ product lines.

This internship is designed for someone who enjoys learning by doing: understanding a product requirement, reviewing a board or mechanical design, building or modifying hardware, running a fit or airflow check, investigating the result, and improving the design or test setup. You’ll work alongside experienced engineers and collaborate across mechanical, electrical, validation, NPI, manufacturing test, and lab teams.

What you’ll do

• 
Support the design and documentation of mechanical parts for engineering boards, validation vehicles, cable modules, and test platforms.

• 
Review mechanical requirements from product specifications, board files, drawings, and related design inputs.

• 
Participate in layout placement and mechanical reviews covering board outlines and dimensions, mounting holes, cutouts, slots, keep-outs, component spacing, package and heatsink zones, and other mechanical interfaces.

• 
Create or update mechanical CAD models, drawings, and release files such as STEP and DXF files under engineering guidance.

• 
Help develop and improve backplates, baseplates, airboxes, chassis enclosures, mounting fixtures, and other hardware used to test and support Astera Labs products.

• 
Build or coordinate prototypes using 3D printing, sheet metal, machining, or other fabrication methods, and evaluate fabricated parts against design intent.

• 
Assemble test fixtures and lab hardware; verify mechanical fit, alignment, clearance, airflow, and usability with boards, sockets, heatsinks, connectors, cables, and other components.

• 
Support hardware test setups by documenting equipment, fixtures, cables, procedures, and required accessories.

• 
Investigate fit, interference, alignment, thermal, or airflow issues; propose design updates and verify corrective actions through focused testing.

• 
Contribute to design-for-manufacturability reviews, parts lists, bills of materials, supplier communications, and mechanical documentation and release workflows.

• 
Collaborate with engineers across Hardware Engineering, validation, NPI, manufacturing test, production, and lab teams to communicate findings and deliver practical solutions.

• 
Present your project, results, and key learnings at the end of the internship.

What you bring

• 
Coursework, project, research, or hands-on experience in mechanical engineering, manufacturing engineering, hardware engineering, or a related field.

• 
Familiarity with 3D CAD and the ability to interpret mechanical drawings, board files, specifications, or datasheets.

• 
Curiosity about how mechanical design affects electrical hardware, testability, manufacturability, thermal performance, and system integration.

• 
A methodical approach to problem-solving: understanding requirements, checking dimensions and interfaces, testing assumptions, analyzing evidence, and documenting what you learn.

• 
Comfort working hands-on with hardware, tools, prototypes, and lab equipment in a fast-paced engineering environment.

• 
Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to collaborate across mechanical, electrical, software, and manufacturing disciplines.

• 
Ownership, persistence, and a practical mindset in an environment where designs are iterated and the first attempt may not work.

Helpful experience

• 
Mechanical design, tolerance analysis, GD&T, design for manufacturability, or design for assembly.

• 
Sheet-metal, machined, or 3D-printed parts; rapid prototyping; or supplier/fabrication coordination.

• 
Test fixtures, mounting hardware, enclosures, backplates, baseplates, airboxes, or alignment features.

• 
Thermal management, heatsink or socket clearances, airflow, or thermal validation.

• 
PCB and PCBA mechanical integration, including mounting holes, component height limits, keep-outs, connectors, and cable interfaces.

• 
Familiarity with engineering documentation and collaboration tools such as Jira, Confluence, or Arena.

Internship experience and compensation

This is a paid, hourly U.S. internship. The applicable hourly rate is determined as part of the offer process and specified in the offer letter, depending on education level ranges form $35/hour to $55/hour. About the role

As a Product Engineering Intern, you will help support Astera Labs semiconductor products throughout the product lifecycle—from concept and engineering samples through characterization, qualification, production release, and continuous improvement. You will work alongside experienced product, test, hardware, validation, firmware/software, packaging, quality, and operations engineers to turn product requirements and test data into reliable, manufacturable products.

Learn Astera Labs products, architectures, datasheets, test requirements, and product-engineering processes.

• 
Support product development activities across characterization, qualification, engineering samples, manufacturing release, and post-release improvement.

Review product requirements, datasheets, test plans, test coverage, characterization plans, qualification plans, and related engineering documentation.

Analyze product-performance, yield, correlation, and test data across wafer sort, package test, burn-in, and other product-development stages.

jobs.title: Design-for-Test Engineer Intern
jobs.description:
DFT Engineer Intern

Astera Labs · San Jose, CA or Toronto, Ontario, Canada - Internship · On-site

About Astera Labs

Astera Labs builds connectivity solutions that help power modern AI infrastructure. Our products combine complex digital logic, high-speed interfaces, embedded control, and test infrastructure to deliver reliable connectivity across demanding systems.

The opportunity

Join the Design-for-Test (DFT) team and help make complex silicon easier to test, debug, and manufacture. You’ll learn how DFT structures and methodologies are designed, implemented, verified, and analyzed across the chip development flow.

This internship is designed for someone who enjoys connecting digital design fundamentals with practical silicon-quality challenges. You’ll work with experienced engineers on a meaningful project involving test structures, patterns, coverage, simulation, or debug, while collaborating with RTL design, physical design, verification, validation, and manufacturing-test teams.

What you’ll do

• 
Learn the product domain, DFT flow, project goals, development environment, and processes needed to contribute effectively.

• 
Support DFT architecture and implementation activities for digital designs, including scan, test compression, memory test, built-in self-test, boundary scan, JTAG, and design-for-debug structures.

• 
Work with RTL, netlists, constraints, test modes, clocking, resets, and power intent as needed to understand and implement test requirements.

• 
Generate, run, and analyze structural test or ATPG patterns and investigate coverage, fault, rule, or simulation results.

• 
Support scan insertion, test-logic validation, MBIST/BIST configuration, test-mode checks, or related DFT flow activities under engineering guidance.

• 
Run simulations and, where applicable, gate-level or X-propagation checks to debug DFT behavior and identify unexpected or uninitialized signals.

• 
Analyze logs, reports, waveforms, coverage results, and pattern failures to identify root causes and recommend next steps.

• 
Develop or improve scripts and automation for DFT setup, pattern generation, regression execution, report parsing, or result analysis.

• 
Collaborate with RTL, verification, physical design, silicon, validation, and manufacturing-test teams to communicate issues and track corrective actions.

• 
Participate in code and flow reviews, technical discussions, issue tracking, documentation, and project planning.

• 
Deliver assigned DFT work in a usable state and explain what was implemented, verified, or improved and how it supports the product flow.

• 
Present your project, results, and key learnings at the end of the internship.

What you bring

• 
Coursework, projects, research, or hands-on experience in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or a related field.

• 
Foundational understanding of digital logic, RTL, computer architecture, semiconductor design, or hardware verification.

• 
Programming or scripting experience in one or more of Verilog, SystemVerilog, Python, Tcl, Perl, C, C++, or a comparable language.

• 
Curiosity about how chips are tested and debugged and a methodical approach to analyzing technical evidence.

• 
Comfort learning in a Linux environment and working with command-line tools, source control, and technical documentation.

• 
Ability to organize priorities, ask focused questions, communicate progress and blockers, and follow through on commitments.

• 
Self-motivation, learning agility, professionalism, and a collaborative mindset.

Helpful experience

• 
Scan chains, scan compression, ATPG, fault models, fault coverage, pattern generation, or test-point insertion.

• 
MBIST, BIST, boundary scan, JTAG, IEEE 1149.1, design-for-debug, or manufacturing-test concepts.

• 
Verilog/SystemVerilog RTL simulation, gate-level simulation, assertions, lint, or X-propagation analysis.

• 
DFT or EDA tools, test-mode configuration, clock observation, reset architecture, or power-aware verification.

• 
Python, Tcl, Perl, or shell scripting for automation, report parsing, regressions, or data analysis.

• 
PCIe, CXL, Ethernet, SERDES, retimers, SoC design, or other high-speed connectivity technologies.

• 
Git, Jira, Confluence, or similar collaborative engineering workflows.

Internship experience and compensation

This is a paid, hourly U.S. internship. The applicable hourly rate is determined as part of the offer process and specified in the offer letter, depending on education level ranges from $35/hour to $55/hour. U.S. interns currently receive a $500-per-week housing/relocation stipend for the duration of the internship. Interns participate in Early Career programming, including technical and professional-development sessions, community events, and an end-of-program project presentation.

Astera Labs is seeking an Emulation Engineering Intern to help enable fast, repeatable pre-silicon validation of complex ASIC and system designs. Your work will support a scoped project that improves test coverage, reproducibility, debug turnaround, model performance, or resource utilization.

• Set up and operate emulation environments, including model selection, workspace configuration, resource allocation, run directories, and cleanup.

About the role

jobs.title: Electrical Validation Engineer Intern
jobs.description:
Electrical Validation Engineer Intern

Astera Labs · San Jose, CA · Internship · On-site

About Astera Labs

Astera Labs builds connectivity solutions that help power modern AI infrastructure. Our Electrical Validation teams measure, debug, and validate the electrical behavior of complex hardware platforms so products can move confidently through bring-up, validation, and release.

The opportunity

Join the Electrical Validation team and gain hands-on experience validating high-performance hardware. You’ll learn the team’s products, lab environment, measurement methods, firmware and update flows, and validation processes while contributing to a scoped project with a visible technical outcome.

This internship is designed for someone who enjoys working close to the hardware: setting up an experiment, selecting the right instrument, collecting trustworthy data, analyzing the result, investigating unexpected behavior, and documenting what the team should do next. You’ll collaborate with Electrical Validation, firmware, system validation, ATE, PApps, program-management, and other engineering teams.

What you’ll do

• 
Learn the Electrical Validation environment, assigned product area, lab equipment, scripts, specifications, and project success criteria.

• 
Run repeatable electrical measurements and validation workflows for hardware platforms, boards, links, interfaces, or subsystems.

• 
Set up and use lab equipment such as oscilloscopes, BERTs, VNAs, power supplies, electronic loads, temperature chambers, probes, and related fixtures under engineering guidance.

• 
Collect, organize, and analyze voltage, current, timing, signal-quality, link, power, temperature, or other electrical data as appropriate for the project.

• 
Compare results with specifications, expected behavior, previous runs, and validation criteria; identify trends, anomalies, margins, and failure conditions.

• 
Support hardware bring-up and debug by checking connections, configurations, firmware or update flows, test scripts, instrument settings, and environmental conditions.

• 
Develop or improve Python, shell, or other automation scripts for measurements, data collection, report generation, or repeatability.

• 
Create clear data packages, validation reports, plots, checklists, Confluence pages, and handoff documentation that others can trust and reuse.

• 
Investigate defined technical issues, form evidence-based hypotheses, run focused experiments, and communicate recommended next steps.

• 
Collaborate with firmware, system validation, ATE, PApps, design, and other cross-functional teams to unblock shared execution and close assigned tasks.

• 
Keep project trackers, action items, and technical documentation current while communicating progress, blockers, and risks.

• 
Own a scoped validation workflow or product slice with increasing independence and present your project, results, and key learnings at the end of the internship.

What you bring

• 
Coursework, projects, research, or hands-on experience in electrical engineering, computer engineering, physics, or a related field.

• 
Foundational understanding of circuits, electronics, digital systems, signal integrity, power, measurements, or hardware interfaces.

• 
Interest in learning how to use laboratory instruments and how to turn measurements into reliable engineering conclusions.

• 
Programming or scripting experience in Python, C/C++, MATLAB, shell, or another language used for automation and data analysis.

• 
Comfort learning in a Linux or technical lab environment and working with specifications, logs, plots, test procedures, and source control.

• 
A methodical approach to troubleshooting: verify the setup, isolate variables, collect evidence, compare against expectations, and document what changed.

• 
Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain results and uncertainty to cross-functional partners.

• 
Ownership, curiosity, humility, and persistence in an environment where experiments may need to be repeated and refined.

Oscilloscopes, BERTs, VNAs, logic analyzers, spectrum analyzers, power supplies, electronic loads, or temperature chambers.

High-speed serial links, PCIe, CXL, Ethernet, SERDES, clocking, jitter, eye diagrams, or signal-quality measurements.

• 
Board bring-up, firmware update flows, test fixtures, lab automation, or hardware debugging.

• 
Python data analysis, instrument control, report generation, or automated regression.

• 
Validation plans, test coverage, failure triage, data packages, or technical report writing.

• 
Jira, Confluence, Excel, Git, or other collaborative engineering workflows.

Internship experience and compensation

The applicable hourly rate is determined as part of the offer process and specified in the offer letter, depending on education level ranges from $35/hour to $55/hour. U.S. interns currently receive a $500-per-week housing/relocation stipend for the duration of the internship. You’ll work at the intersection of architecture, RTL, simulation, synthesis, verification, physical design, DFT, and firmware to help turn product requirements into robust, implementable hardware.

This internship is designed for someone who enjoys understanding how a system should work, expressing that behavior in RTL, and debugging the difference between intended and observed results. Learn the product architecture, microarchitecture, design methodology, development environment, tools, and project workflow needed to contribute effectively.

Read architecture, interface, microarchitecture, and product-requirement documentation and translate requirements into clear design behavior.

SystemVerilog interfaces, parameterized modules, FIFOs, arbiters, pipelines, state machines, register maps, or bus protocols.

Location: San Jose, California
Employment type: Full-time
Organization: Business Intelligence

About Astera Labs

Astera Labs (NASDAQ: ALAB) is a pioneering fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Silicon Valley, driving the evolution of AI and cloud infrastructure through purpose-built connectivity solutions. As a leader in rack-scale architecture, Astera Labs is enabling the shift to AI Infrastructure 2.0, where compute is optimized at the rack level to support next-generation workloads. Our portfolio spans high-performance silicon, software, and system-level solutions that address critical bottlenecks in data movement across compute, memory, and networking domains. We are committed to open standards, continuous innovation, and building a collaborative environment to solve complex challenges at scale.

Role Overview

Astera Labs is seeking a Data Analytics Engineer NCG to support reporting, automation, and data pipeline initiatives across the business. This role will help turn business data into actionable insights, scalable datasets, and automated workflows that improve decision-making and operational efficiency.

The ideal candidate brings a strong analytical mindset, curiosity about business systems and data flows, and hands-on experience or coursework in tools such as Excel, Power BI, SQL, and Azure-based data platforms. This person should be comfortable working across both analytics and engineering tasks, partnering with business stakeholders and technical team members to build practical, high-impact solutions.

A Workday at Astera Labs

In this role, you will work primarily with the Business Intelligence team to support reporting, analysis, and automation initiatives in a structured learning environment. Your day may include working with sample or curated datasets, building Excel-based models or trackers, developing Power BI dashboards, writing SQL queries, and assisting with data pipeline and workflow automation tasks. You may also support recurring reporting processes, help document business rules and reporting logic, investigate data quality patterns in non-production datasets, and contribute to lightweight Azure-based integrations and process improvements.

This is a hands-on internship where you will gain exposure to both business intelligence and data engineering work. You will learn how data moves across systems, how dashboards and reports are built for business users, and how automation can improve speed, accuracy, and scalability across core processes.

• Support lightweight integrations and automation using Azure Functions where applicable

• Support documentation of report definitions, data sources, data models, business logic, and workflow steps

• Azure SQL Database skills, such as writing queries, working with tables and views, joins, aggregations, stored procedures, triggers, and query optimization

• Azure Data Factory skills, such as linked services, datasets, copy activities, pipeline development, triggers, parameterization, monitoring, and error handling

• Azure Functions skills, such as Function Apps, triggers, bindings, service integrations, logging, troubleshooting, and serverless design

• Comfortable working with structured and imperfect data, with the ability to identify inconsistencies, improve data quality, learn new tools quickly, and operate effectively in a fast-paced environment

• Interest in building scalable, reliable data solutions that support better business decisions

• Gain hands-on experience across analytics, BI, automation, and cloud data tooling at a company at the forefront of AI infrastructure

• Work on meaningful projects that directly improve reporting, process efficiency, and decision-making

• Partner closely with stakeholders across business and technical functions

• Build practical experience with modern Microsoft and Azure data platforms in a fast-paced, high-growth environment

• Competitive compensation and the opportunity to learn from experienced cross-functional teams

Compensation

Astera Labs is seeking an ATE Engineer Intern to support the development, validation, and improvement of automated test solutions for advanced semiconductor products. Design Architecture Engineer Intern

About the role

Astera Labs is seeking a Design Architecture Engineer Intern to help define complex ASIC and system designs from product requirements through implementation. You will work with architects and cross-functional engineering teams to develop clear architectural and microarchitectural specifications, evaluate design tradeoffs, and create the technical foundation for RTL, verification, physical design, DFT, and firmware.

You will gain hands-on experience turning system goals into block definitions, interfaces, dataflows, state machines, registers, clocking and reset behavior, performance budgets, and software-programming guidance. You will own a scoped architecture project with mentorship and present the resulting analysis, specification, and recommendations.

What you will do

• Review product requirements, system use cases, protocol specifications, and technical constraints to identify architecture needs and open questions.

• Develop or update architectural specifications describing major blocks, functions, interfaces, clocking, resets, software interactions, and system behavior.

• Create or refine microarchitecture specifications for blocks and subsystems, including logical implementation, data structures, programmable registers, state machines, datapaths, and dataflow diagrams.

• Define and analyze interface behavior, ownership, ordering, buffering, flow control, error handling, interrupts, and recovery sequences.

• Evaluate architecture tradeoffs involving latency, bandwidth, throughput, buffering, area, power, timing, scalability, complexity, and software impact.

• Build lightweight performance, capacity, traffic, or resource models using Python, spreadsheets, or comparable tools to support design decisions.

• Review address maps, CSR/register definitions, configuration options, clock and reset relationships, and programming requirements for consistency and completeness.

• Trace requirements into implementation and verification considerations; identify assumptions, corner cases, and measurable acceptance criteria.

• Participate in architecture, design, DV, physical-design, DFT, firmware, and program reviews; capture decisions, actions, risks, and unresolved items.

• Work with RTL, DV, PD, DFT, firmware, and systems engineers to clarify interfaces and improve the quality of handoff specifications.

• Support architecture-to-RTL and architecture-to-DV handoff by organizing specifications, diagrams, register collateral, review evidence, and verification guidance.

• Document the completed project, technical rationale, tradeoffs, open questions, and recommendations; present the results to engineering stakeholders.

What you bring

• Coursework, research, or project experience in computer architecture, digital systems, ASIC/FPGA design, embedded systems, high-speed interfaces, or hardware/software integration.

• Understanding of digital design concepts such as datapaths, state machines, registers, memory systems, interrupts, clocks, resets, and interfaces.

• Programming, scripting, or modeling experience with Python, C, C++, SystemVerilog, spreadsheets, or a comparable toolset.

• Ability to read technical specifications, organize complex information, reason about tradeoffs, and communicate precise technical decisions.

• Experience with performance modeling, bandwidth/latency analysis, traffic modeling, queue or buffer sizing, or resource budgeting.

• Exposure to RTL, design verification, formal methods, physical design, DFT, firmware, or system bring-up workflows.

jobs.title: Advanced Design Verification Engineer Intern
jobs.description:
Advanced DV Engineering Intern

About the role

Astera Labs is seeking an Advanced Design Verification Engineering Intern to help validate complex ASIC and system designs before silicon is available. You will work with design verification engineers to develop tests, improve verification environments, analyze coverage, debug failures, and apply simulation and formal methods to assess whether designs meet their specifications.

This internship is intended for a student who is ready to go beyond running existing tests and contribute to verification strategy, reusable infrastructure, and difficult debug problems. You will own a scoped project with guidance from experienced engineers and deliver verification work in a usable state.

What you will do

• Translate architectural, microarchitectural, interface, and product requirements into verification scenarios, test plans, coverage goals, and checkers.

• Develop and maintain SystemVerilog and UVM testbench components, sequences, tests, monitors, scoreboards, functional coverage, and end-of-test checks.

• Add directed, constrained-random, error-injection, compliance, stress, and corner-case tests for blocks, subsystems, or top-level functionality.

• Configure and run simulations and regressions using project submission flows, manifests, plusargs, firmware images, and test definitions.

• Debug failures by correlating logs, UVM messages, assertions, register reports, firmware output, and Verdi or DVE waveforms.

• Triage regression failures, distinguish design issues from testbench or environment issues, reproduce failures, and communicate actionable root-cause analysis.

• Analyze functional and code coverage, identify untested scenarios or coverage gaps, and propose targeted tests or verification improvements.

• Write, review, and debug SystemVerilog assertions and coverage properties that capture design intent and interface behavior.

• Support formal verification flows such as design compile, reset analysis, automatic property extraction, dead-code analysis, and formal property verification.

• Create or improve Python, Tcl, or other automation that simplifies test generation, regression execution, result parsing, coverage analysis, or failure triage.

• Collaborate with RTL design, firmware, emulation, physical design, and systems engineers to clarify assumptions and close verification issues.

• Document test intent, debug findings, coverage status, known limitations, and handoff information; present the completed project and recommendations.

What you bring

• Enrollment in a bachelor’s, master’s, or Ph.D. program in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or a related field.

• Coursework, research, or project experience in digital logic, computer architecture, ASIC/FPGA design, verification, embedded systems, or hardware/software integration.

• Programming or verification experience with SystemVerilog, Verilog, C, C++, Python, or a comparable language.

• Familiarity with digital design concepts, simulation, testbenches, interfaces, clocks, resets, registers, and debugging from waveforms or logs.

• Familiarity with Linux development environments, Git, command-line tools, and technical documentation.

• Ability to reason from a specification, investigate failures systematically, and communicate clear technical conclusions.

• Strong ownership, curiosity, practical judgment, and willingness to collaborate across engineering functions.

Preferred qualifications

• Experience with UVM components, sequences, virtual sequences, agents, monitors, scoreboards, reference models, or functional coverage.

• Familiarity with SystemVerilog Assertions, constrained-random testing, coverage-driven verification, error injection, or compliance testing.

• Exposure to verification IP and protocols such as PCIe, CXL, AXI, or other high-speed and control interfaces.

• Experience with Verdi, DVE, VCS, Questa, Xcelium, VC Formal, or comparable simulation and formal tools.

• Familiarity with formal concepts such as assumptions, assertions, covers, counterexamples, reset analysis, dead-code analysis, or automatic property extraction.

• Experience managing regressions, parsing results, debugging intermittent failures, or running jobs on a compute cluster or CI system.

Internship experience and compensation

The applicable hourly rate is determined as part of the offer process and specified in the offer letter, depending on education level ranges from $35/hour to $55/hour. U.S. interns currently receive a $500-per-week housing/relocation stipend for the duration of the internship. Interns participate in Early Career programming, including technical and professional-development sessions, community events, and an end-of-program project presentation.

Equal opportunity

jobs.title: Electrical Engineer Intern
jobs.description:
Who we are 

Atoms is building the machines that power the next era of progress.

Over the last decade, software has transformed the digital world. But the physical world, where food is made, minerals are mined, goods are moved, and industries are run, remains far less intelligent, far less efficient, and far more constrained. We’re changing that.

Atoms builds Physical AI— real-world robots for the industries that move civilization forward, starting with food, mining, and transport. Our systems are designed to understand, predict, and control the real world with precision, turning complex physical operations into something more reliable, more scalable, and more productive.

This work requires more than robotics. It requires deep integration across hardware, software, AI, operations, manufacturing, and real estate. We don’t just build machines in a lab. We deploy them into real environments, operate them, learn from them, and improve them until they work at scale.

We are roboticists, engineers, operators, and builders. We believe the next great technology companies will not only transform information, but the physical systems that shape everyday life.

If you want to work on hard problems with real-world impact, join us.

What you’ll do

As an Electrical Engineering Intern, you will work alongside senior hardware engineers to help expand our autonomous transport platforms. You will get hands-on experience designing, testing, and integrating real-world hardware solutions for next-generation, on-road autonomous vehicles.

• PCB & Carrier Board Design: Support the design and revision of custom circuit boards and carrier boards for vehicle compute, sensors (camera, radar, lidar), GPS, and actuation systems.

• Vehicle & Protocol Integration: Assist with analyzing and debugging automotive communication protocols (CAN, CAN FD, Ethernet) on real vehicle test platforms.

• Hardware Validation & Testing: Help design, assemble, and execute test procedures and hardware test fixtures to validate board designs and troubleshoot edge cases.

• Fleet Support: Work directly with hardware and software engineers on vehicle bring-up, fleet installations, and physical hardware troubleshooting on-site.

What we’re looking for

• Education: Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Robotics, or a related technical field.

• Core Technical Knowledge: Solid foundation in circuit design, analog/digital fundamentals, and basic embedded systems logic.

• Hands-on Experience: Practical experience with PCB design tools (e.g., Altium, KiCad, Eagle) and bench equipment (oscilloscopes, multimeters, logic analyzers) through lab work, student design teams (e.g., Formula SAE, Robotics Club), or personal projects.

• Protocols & Hardware: Familiarity or coursework covering common hardware communication protocols (CAN, SPI, I2C, UART).

• Mindset: Proactive problem solver who thrives in a fast-paced, highly collaborative startup environment and is excited to work with physical hardware.

Why join us

At Atoms, you’ll work on one of the defining challenges of our time—bringing automation into the physical world to drive real, lasting impact. We exist to uncover valuable unknown truths and turn them into progress, which means constantly pushing beyond what’s known and building what doesn’t yet exist. The work is ambitious and often challenging, but it’s grounded in a shared sense of purpose and a team committed to seeing it through together. Our work only matters if it serves others, and we know that meaningful progress depends on the trust of the people we serve and the strength of our team—so we invest in both, creating an environment where you can do your best work and grow.

What else you need to know

This role is based in our San Francisco office. Atoms is a company driven by invention and continuous change - we are constantly reimagining our industries, building new products, and refining how we operate. We do our best work together. That’s why all of our office-based teams work onsite, five days a week.

Program Dates: Our internship is a 12-weeks program. Cohort sessions run as follows:

• Winter 2027: January – April

• Summer 2027: Late May – September

The base salary range for this role is $50.00 per hour.

Actual compensation will be determined on an individual basis and may vary depending on experience, skills, and qualifications.

Ready to join us as we serve those who serve others?

About Us

Fanatics is building a leading global digital sports platform. We ignite the passions of global sports fans and maximize the presence and reach for our hundreds of sports partners globally by offering products and services across Fanatics Commerce, Fanatics Collectibles, and Fanatics Betting & Gaming, allowing sports fans to Buy, Collect, and Bet. Through the Fanatics platform, sports fans can buy licensed fan gear, jerseys, lifestyle and streetwear products, headwear, and hardgoods; collect physical and digital trading cards, sports memorabilia, and other digital assets; and bet as the company builds its Sportsbook and iGaming platform. Fanatics has an established database of over 100 million global sports fans; a global partner network with approximately 900 sports properties, including major national and international professional sports leagues, players associations, teams, colleges, college conferences and retail partners, 2,500 athletes and celebrities, and 200 exclusive athletes; and over 2,000 retail locations, including its Lids retail stores. Our more than 22,000 employees are committed to relentlessly enhancing the fan experience and delighting sports fans globally. 

Quantitative Analyst: 

As a Quantitative Analyst, you’ll operate at the intersection of sports trading, mathematics, and data science. Your primary focus will be on analyzing sport & betting data, developing predictive models, and assisting with trading decisions. You’ll collaborate with senior quants, traders, engineers and product managers to continuously improve pricing efficiency and expand the range of betting odds generated by our proprietary trading platform and continuously improve our risk models & management strategy. Internships or coursework related to quantitative finance or numerical modeling are a plus.

• Assist in the development, implementation, training and testing of mathematical models for pricing & managing the risk of sport betting events.

• Data Sourcing & Analysis 

• Collect and clean sports-related data,

• Analyze large datasets of play by play (simulated or historical) and betting data to identify patterns, trends, and correlations that can inform trading strategies.

• Programming 

• Use programming languages such as C# or Python to develop quantitative models, code and automate analytical processes, and perform data analysis tasks.

• Collaboration 

• Collaborate with senior quantitative analysts, traders & product managers to understand business requirements, implement solutions, and communicate findings effectively

• Document and maintain clear and concise documentation of quantitative models, methodologies and analysis procedures for internal reference

• Continuous Learning 

• Stay abreast of developments in quantitative analysis & betting markets, and related fields through self-study & training

• Detail-oriented mindset with a commitment to producing high-quality work and adhering to best practices in quantitative analysis and research.

Join us on our mission to empower confident, fraud-free commerce by helping online retailers provide superior customer experiences and eliminate fraud. Learn about our company values here!

Signifyd is one of the world’s leading tech start-ups! They develop best-in-class AI fraud prevention software; which helps make the world a better place. As an intern, you'll be given a masterclass into the software development lifecycle. You'll get to work with amazing colleagues on complex challenges. jobs.title: Software Engineer 2 New Grad - Developer Portal
jobs.description:
Company Overview

ID.me is the next-generation digital identity wallet that simplifies how individuals securely prove their identity online. Consumers can verify their identity with ID.me once and seamlessly login across websites without having to create a new login and verify their identity again. Over 152 million users experience streamlined login and identity verification with ID.me at 20 federal agencies, 45 state government agencies, and 70+ healthcare organizations. More than 600+ consumer brands use ID.me to verify communities and user segments to honor service and build more authentic relationships. ID.me’s technology meets the federal standards for consumer authentication set by the Commerce Department and is approved as a NIST 800-63-3 IAL2 / AAL2 credential service provider by the Kantara Initiative. ID.me is committed to “No Identity Left Behind” to enable all people to have a secure digital identity. To learn more, visit https://network.id.me/.

ID.me is a full-time, in-office culture. Unless a specific job description explicitly states otherwise, all roles are on-site five days per week at one of our offices in McLean, VA; Mountain View, CA; New York City, NY; or Tampa, FL. Certain roles — such as field-based sales or other remote-by-design positions — may have different work arrangements as noted in their individual postings.

At ID.me, we embrace the thoughtful use of AI tools in our daily work and there are even occasions where we leverage AI in our hiring process. However, during the interview process, we want to understand your individual skills and experiences. Therefore, we have guidelines on how AI can be appropriately used during your application and interviews which can be found here.

Location: Mountain View, CA (Onsite 5 days per week)

Role Overview

ID.me is seeking a Software Engineer II to join the Developer Portal team, where we're building the self-service platform that enables organizations to rapidly integrate ID.me.

Identity proofing is fundamentally complex. Integrating an identity proofing flow requires many steps while meeting standards-body assurance requirements. The Developer Portal is the product that brings those pieces together for the external developer.

Today, much of that onboarding is still performed manually by in-house Solutions Consultants who have many other responsibilities. Our mission is to enable customers and their developers to register their application, configure their identity needs, test in a production-like sandbox, and launch to production, all through a modern self-service experience.

This is an early-career role for engineers who are 0 to 2 years into their career and write excellent code. You don't need years of industry experience. You need strong fundamentals, a track record of building real things, and an AI-native way of working: you already use AI coding tools as a core part of how you design, build, test, and debug, and you have the judgment to know when their output is right and when it isn't.

This is a backend-leaning full-stack role. You'll work on the services, APIs, and data models behind the portal (application registration, authorization, and the developer-facing APIs our customers integrate against), and you'll ship the user-facing surfaces those services power in our Next.js and React frontend. You'll start with well-scoped features alongside senior engineers and grow quickly into owning features end-to-end, from API contract to production.

Our backend services are primarily Java (Spring Boot) alongside legacy Ruby services. The frontend is a micro-frontend platform built with Next.js, React, and TypeScript. You don't need to know all of these on day one. If your fundamentals are strong, we're confident you'll pick up whatever the problem requires.

What You'll Do

Build and Ship Developer Features

Design, implement, test, and deploy Developer Portal capabilities across the stack: backend APIs, database changes, and the frontend experiences customers use. Start with well-defined features and bugs, then take on progressively larger and more ambiguous work as you grow.

Write High-Quality, Well-Tested Code

Write clean, readable, maintainable code with strong test coverage. Participate actively in code review, both getting feedback and giving thoughtful feedback to teammates, including senior engineers.

Build AI-First

Use AI-assisted development tools (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor) every day to move faster on implementation, testing, debugging, and understanding unfamiliar code. Help the team find better ways to use these tools, and hold AI-generated code to the same bar as code you wrote by hand.

Learn the Identity Stack

Build hands-on depth in authentication and authorization, including OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, enterprise SSO, multi-tenant access control, and credential management, working with our Wallet, Organizations, and Platform Engineering teams.

Operate What You Ship

Help keep the systems our team owns healthy in production: monitoring, alerting, debugging live issues, and participating in on-call once you're ramped up.

Collaborate and Grow

Work closely with Product, Design, and engineers across teams. Learn to break down problems, write short technical designs, and communicate clearly about tradeoffs and progress. You'll have a dedicated mentor and a clear path toward end-to-end feature ownership.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

• 0 to 2 years of professional software engineering experience.

• Excellent coding skills and strong computer science fundamentals: data structures, algorithms, complexity, and debugging.

• Fluency in at least one modern programming language (e.g., Java, TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Go, Kotlin, C#, Ruby).

• Evidence that you build real software: internships, substantial class or team projects, open-source contributions, hackathons, or side projects that other people use.

• AI-native development workflow: daily, hands-on use of AI coding tools (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot) to build and ship software, paired with the ability to critically evaluate AI-generated code for correctness, security, performance, and maintainability, and to explain every line you submit.

• Experience building with LLMs or agentic workflows (e.g., using the Claude or OpenAI APIs, MCP, or agent frameworks) in projects or coursework.

• Understanding of how web applications work, including HTTP, REST APIs, and relational databases/SQL.

• Ability to learn unfamiliar systems quickly through independent research and by working with mentors and subject-matter experts.

• Clear written and verbal communication. You can explain what you built, why, and what tradeoffs you made.

Preferred Qualifications

• Internship experience building backend services or full-stack web applications.

• Experience with Java and Spring Boot, or another backend framework (Rails, Node.js/Express, Django, Go).

• Experience with React, TypeScript, or Next.js.

• Experience with PostgreSQL or another relational database, including schema design.

• Exposure to authentication and authorization concepts such as OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, JWTs, SSO, or access control models.

• Experience building developer tools, APIs, SDKs, or documentation that other developers use.

• Experience writing automated tests (unit, integration, or end-to-end with tools like Jest, JUnit, or Playwright).

• Familiarity with cloud platforms (GCP, AWS, Azure), containers, or CI/CD pipelines.

• Interest in security, identity, fraud prevention, or regulated systems.

What Success Looks Like

• First 30 days: Your dev environment is set up, you've shipped your first production change, and you understand how the Developer Portal fits into ID.me's identity platform.

• First 90 days: You're independently delivering well-scoped features across backend and frontend, contrib

jobs.title: Firmware Engineering Co-op
jobs.description:
About Moment Energy

Independent energy is here. Help us deploy it.

Energy should be free. Free from aging grids, fragile supply chains, and unnecessary extraction. At Moment Energy, we’re building a world where clean power is abundant, affordable, and uninterrupted for everyone.

The world doesn’t need another promise about energy; it needs proof that a freer future is possible. Moment Energy is the pragmatic liberator of power, the only company certified to turn the largest untapped energy supply into independent energy.

Now is the moment. While the industry scraps millions of batteries with decades of life left, we put them to work by repurposing large-format batteries into advanced battery energy storage systems that deliver real-world impact.

We were told second-life batteries would never be safe enough or scalable enough. We didn’t argue, we engineered the solution. Today, Moment Energy delivers 5x the energy density and holds the certifications required to deploy energy independence at scale.

Now is the moment. Join us.

The Opportunity

We are seeking a motivated Firmware Engineering Co-op to join our Engineering team starting in January 2027. In this role, you will support the development of our battery management system (BMS), which optimizes the performance, safety, and longevity of second-life batteries.

You will work closely with firmware and electrical engineers to develop, test, and improve embedded software that powers our energy storage systems. This is a great opportunity for a student interested in embedded systems and hardware-software integration within the clean energy industry.

Responsibilities and Duties

• Assist in the development of embedded firmware for the battery management system (BMS)

• Support firmware testing and validation to ensure system reliability and performance

• Work with engineers to integrate firmware with battery monitoring hardware and system controls

• Debug and troubleshoot firmware and hardware interactions

• Develop and execute test plans and document test results

• Maintain clear and organized firmware documentation

• Assist with improving system performance, stability, and safety features

• Collaborate with electrical, mechanical, and software engineers on system integration

The Student we’re looking for:

• Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related discipline

• Career Interest in embedded systems and firmware development

• Familiarity with C/C++ or other embedded programming languages

• Basic understanding of microcontrollers and hardware interfaces

• Experience with debugging tools and version control (e.g., Git) is an asset

• Strong problem-solving and analytical skills

• Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced engineering environment

The Experience You’ll Gain:

• Hands-on experience developing embedded firmware for energy storage systems

• Exposure to battery management systems and hardware-software integration

• Mentorship from experienced firmware and electrical engineers

• The opportunity to contribute to technology supporting the clean energy transition

Moment Energy Co-op Benefits Highlights

Paid Time Off: Co-op’s receive three paid days off per term

Vibrant Culture & Perks: Open and collaborative office culture, frequent company socials and wellness programs (weekly yoga and fitness center), and free EV charging on-site.

Why join us?

• Today, we’re delivering 5x the energy density and have all the certifications needed to ship energy independence to the world.

• Be part of a mission-driven company focused on creating sustainable energy solutions and making a positive impact on the world.

• Collaborate closely with passionate co-founders and a team committed to innovation and excellence.

• Contribute to building and scaling a company from the ground up, where your work will have a direct and meaningful impact.

• Thrive in a workplace that values collaboration, wellness, and celebrating successes, with regular company socials, fitness sessions, and more.

We're a fast-paced and dynamic team.

Every day you'll be taking on a new challenge and learning something new. You'll take on a wide breadth of tasks and contribute to disrupting the battery industry. You'll be part of a tight-knit team that is working together to save the planet! Fun, health, and wellness are incorporated into our daily schedule and we encourage all our team members to bring innovative ideas to the table to create an interactive workplace. 

Moment Energy Benefits Highlights (full time, permanent employees only)

Financial Growth: Employee equity and a robust RRSP matching program.

Comprehensive Health Coverage: Extended health, dental, and vision benefits for you and your dependents through Manulife.

Generous Time Off & Flexibility: Paid time off plus a paid company closure between Christmas and New Year's, with a generous paid sick leave.

Vibrant Culture & Perks: Open and collaborative office culture, frequent company socials and wellness programs (weekly yoga/fitness), and free EV charging on-site.

Company Dinner: Weekly Tuesday dinner provided by Moment Energy. We also have a generous supply of coffee and snacks for the office! 

Our Commitments

Moment Energy is an equal-opportunity employer. We are committed to inclusive, barrier-free recruitment and selection processes, including our work environment. We especially welcome applications from Indigenous peoples, members of racialized communities, persons with disabilities, women, and persons who identify as 2SLGBTQ+.

—---

Our Values

Our values are key to how we show up every day at Moment Energy! We keep them in the forefront of what we do, and they’re used everywhere. We refer to them when we have tough decisions to make, we give shoutouts based on living out these values, and we include them as part of our performance reviews.

We have 5 core values and 1 foundational pillar (Safety is our Foundation) which lays the groundwork for everything we do.

Safety is our Foundation

We prioritize the safety of our products, customers, employees, and the general public above all else. From the workshop to the field, we maintain the highest standards for our batteries in testing manufacturing and deployment, and daily operations. Safety is not only about procedures—it is about vigilance, responsibility, and speaking up when something does not feel right.

Safety is everyone's responsibility. We follow safety protocols, use proper equipment, and continuously improve our systems to prevent risks before they occur. If something is unsafe, we stop work and address it.

Safety also means protecting our colleagues, customers, and communities by designing reliable products, maintaining safe workspaces, and ensuring our work is done carefully and responsibly.

We’re Building a Greener Future Together: 

We infuse passion for our cleantech mission into every aspect of our work and incorporate fun into the workplace. We motivate one another, celebrate our successes and embrace eco-friendly practices to reduce our carbon footprint.

We Prioritize our Customer’s Needs: 

We place our customers at the core of everything we do, ensuring that every decision considers their needs and aims to provide increased value to them. We provide reliable support for our customers, every step of the way. 

We’re Open, Honest and Accountable:

We prioritize open and honest communication to foster mutual understanding, strengthen knowledge sharing, and reduce miscommunication within the team. We admit when we’ve made a mistake, and remedy our actions. We transparently communicate outcomes whether good, bad, or unexpected. 

We Think and Act like Owners:

We’re self-starters that proactively embrace new challenges along with personal and collective ownership of responsibilities in the organization. We focus on growth, not titles, and we do what needs to be done.
