Company Overview

ID.me is the next-generation digital identity wallet that simplifies how individuals securely prove their identity online. Consumers can verify their identity with ID.me once and seamlessly login across websites without having to create a new login and verify their identity again. Over 152 million users experience streamlined login and identity verification with ID.me at 20 federal agencies, 45 state government agencies, and 70+ healthcare organizations. More than 600+ consumer brands use ID.me to verify communities and user segments to honor service and build more authentic relationships. ID.me’s technology meets the federal standards for consumer authentication set by the Commerce Department and is approved as a NIST 800-63-3 IAL2 / AAL2 credential service provider by the Kantara Initiative. ID.me is committed to “No Identity Left Behind” to enable all people to have a secure digital identity. To learn more, visit https://network.id.me/.

ID.me is a full-time, in-office culture. Unless a specific job description explicitly states otherwise, all roles are on-site five days per week at one of our offices in McLean, VA; Mountain View, CA; New York City, NY; or Tampa, FL. Certain roles — such as field-based sales or other remote-by-design positions — may have different work arrangements as noted in their individual postings.

At ID.me, we embrace the thoughtful use of AI tools in our daily work and there are even occasions where we leverage AI in our hiring process. However, during the interview process, we want to understand your individual skills and experiences. Therefore, we have guidelines on how AI can be appropriately used during your application and interviews which can be found here.

Engagement Type: Full-Time Location: Mountain View, CA (Onsite 5 days per week)

Role Overview

ID.me is seeking a Software Development Engineer II to join the Life Hub team, building the SuperApp's life-events experience — the surface that helps members discover and access the government, healthcare, and commercial benefits they are eligible for based on major life moments (turning 65, leaving the military, becoming disabled, and similar events).

This role is full stack: you will help build the data model and application logic that connects a member's self-asserted and verified attributes to eligible life events, use cases, and application resources, working across both backend services (Java, REST APIs) and the React/Next.js experiences members interact with. You will work closely with the team's senior engineers, Product, and Design to turn eligibility rules and use-case definitions into working software, starting with the team's Medicare pilot and expanding into additional life events such as retirement and disability.

This position will work from our Mountain View, CA office five days per week.

Key Responsibilities

• Build Life Hub Eligibility Logic: Build and maintain application logic that turns eligibility attributes (self-asserted, or read from the Persons and Profiles APIs) into ranked, eligible life events and use cases for a member.

• Implement Use-Case & Eligibility Models: Implement use-case and eligibility JSON models, in partnership with senior engineers and the Developer Portal team, that map application resources, use cases, and eligibility conditions for pilot programs such as Medicare.

• Support Discovery & Access Flows: Contribute to discovery and access flows, ensuring discovery remains lenient (showing ineligible life events, sorted appropriately) while access enforcement remains a hard gate tied to resource-level policy.

• Integrate with Platform APIs: Integrate with Persons, Profiles, and Developer Portal control-plane APIs for eligibility and access data rather than hardcoding business logic client-side.

• Build Member-Facing UI: Build and maintain React/Next.js web experiences for Life Hub, turning discovery and eligibility concepts into working, member-centered UI.

• Track Attribute Gaps: Support tracking and documentation of attribute gaps (e.g., residency, disability status, entitlement data) in partnership with the Profile and Persons API teams.

• Collaborate with Design and Product: Work closely with Design and Product, and ask insightful questions during planning and refinement, to help shape Life Hub's ontology and roadmap.

• Performance, Accessibility & Reliability: Ensure shipped features meet ID.me's standards for performance, accessibility, and cross-browser reliability.

• Production Support: Provide production support and maintenance for shipped features, including triaging and resolving incidents and bugs.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

• 0–2 years of professional software engineering experience (or equivalent internship/academic project experience).

• Working proficiency in at least one modern backend language (Java preferred) and comfort with REST APIs.

• Working experience with a modern frontend framework (React and/or Next.js).

• Solid fundamentals in data structures, debugging, and automated testing.

• Comfortable working on well-defined tickets with pair programming and consultation from more senior engineers.

• Clear written and verbal communication — this role requires close collaboration with Product, Design, and adjacent platform teams (Developer Portal, Persons/Profile API).

• AI-native engineering practices — comfortable using AI tooling (e.g., code generation, test coverage, documentation) to accelerate development.

We'd Love to See

• Exposure to eligibility, entitlements, or identity/benefits-adjacent domains.

• Experience with JSON-based data modeling or rules/policy engines.

• Familiarity with ID.me's Wallet, OAuth/OIDC concepts, or the Nova/Fragno design system.

• Prior full-stack project experience spanning a UI, an API layer, and a database.

• Familiarity with accessibility standards and cross-browser behavior.

The annual base salary listed does not include a company bonus, incentive for sales roles, equity and benefits which will be determined based on experience, skills, education, relevant training, geographic location and role. 

ID.me offers comprehensive medical, dental, vision, health savings account, flexible spending accounts (medical, limited purpose, dependent care, commuter benefit accounts), basic and voluntary life and AD&D insurance, 401(k) with company match, parental leave, ability to participate in unlimited paid time off subject to the terms and conditions of the PTO policy, including 8 company wide holidays, short and long-term disability insurance, accident and critical illness insurance, referral bonus policy, employee assistance program, pet insurance, travel assistant program, wellbeing and childcare discounts, benefit advocates, and a learning and development benefit.

Final offers may vary from the amount listed based on qualifications, professional experiences, skills, education, relevant training, geographic location, and other job related factors.

 As a Data Engineer Co-op, you will build and maintain the data infrastructure needed to analyze and improve our pilot systems. ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

SPACE SYSTEMS

At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets — we're building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, and more.

Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. The team has built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help them get to space — our world class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

ELECTRICAL ENGINEER I

We are currently seeking an Electrical Engineer I for our avionics design engineering team based out of Long Beach, CA. You will participate in the development and test of avionics hardware for our spacecraft programs. You will work collaboratively with engineers of various disciplines and participate in all aspects of electrical hardware development, from requirements definition through design, prototyping, fabrication, testing, and production. As an engineer on the spacecraft development team, you will have frequent opportunities to test and operate your systems on orbit. We're looking for people who are passionate about spacecraft electrical hardware design, with a willingness to learn in a fast-paced environment.

• Experience with FPGA design and embedded software development for ARM core processors

• Demonstrated success working in a dynamic environment and ability to manage competing priorities

We see the world differently at Capstone Investment Advisors. You will, too. 

Capstone is a global, alternative investment management firm operating across a broad range of derivatives-based strategies with a deep understanding of volatility. With approximately $14.6 billion of AUM and 315 employees (as of September 1, 2026, Capstone was formed in 2007 and is headquartered in New York with offices in London, Amsterdam, Tokyo, California, Stamford, Boston, and Milan. 

At Capstone, we constantly aim to expand our view of how WE SEE THE WORLD DIFFERENTLY® in order to create opportunity. Our commitment to provoking the evolution of asset management provides us with a perpetual hunger for knowledge that we believe drives the improvement of our particular approach to investment. We seek to harness the complexities of global derivatives markets with disciplined strategic insight, an experienced, accomplished team and advanced technology to create sustainable value. We’ve created a particular approach to investment that we believe drives continuous improvement and opportunities for our clients, team and industry. 

Overview: 

Capstone’s 2027 Summer Risk Tech Internship is a ten-week program designed to provide interns with practical exposure to the firm’s Risk Tech team and broader working environment. Interns will support the team’s day-to-day activities while completing a defined project designed to provide a meaningful learning experience and address a relevant business need. 

We are seeking intellectually curious, analytical, and motivated candidates with a demonstrated interest in financial markets and investment management. During the program, interns may gain exposure to how risk is measured and managed across multiple asset classes and strategies. This includes analysing live trades and seeing how they perform across hundreds of thousands of historical and hypothetical scenarios, breaking down traders’ PnL to understand what drives it, and calculating the firm’s exposure to key risk factors to understand how market moves will affect our PnL and how best to manage that. 

Our future colleague has these skills: 

• Studying towards or holding a degree in a quantitative subject (Comp Sci, Maths, Engineering, Physics or similar), or equivalent experience 

• Strong programming ability in Python, Java or C, demonstrated through projects or work experience 

• Able to explain technical ideas clearly to both technical and non-technical colleagues 

• Takes ownership of problems, from research to design and implementation

• To thrive at Capstone, a keen curiosity about technology and artificial intelligence is essential, as we continually drive innovation and enhance our strategic capabilities.

jobs.description:
Job Details:

Job Description: 
The Role and Impact

As a Module Engineering PhD Intern, you will play a key role in developing and optimizing semiconductor manufacturing processes for a specific module. You will gain hands-on experience by sustaining and improving manufacturing equipment, troubleshooting issues, and supporting qualification activities. This internship offers a unique opportunity to apply your academic knowledge, build practical skills, and contribute to real-world projects in a dynamic environment that fosters growth and innovation. 

Business Group

Intel Foundry is focused on advancing semiconductor manufacturing technologies and delivering innovative solutions to meet customer needs worldwide. As part of this organization, you will join a group dedicated to sustaining high-performance manufacturing processes and driving process optimization to support Intel's broader mission of technological excellence. 

Key Responsibilities

• Support the development and implementation of manufacturing processes for a specific module in semiconductor production. 
• Sustain and enhance manufacturing equipment performance to ensure operational reliability and efficiency. 
• Assist in troubleshooting equipment issues and performing qualification activities to achieve production standards. 
• Collaborate with engineering teams to optimize process control methodologies and enhance process efficiency. 
• Apply statistical analysis and experimental design to improve process reliability and throughput. 
• Gain hands-on experience with materials and device characterization techniques, such as SEM and TEM. 
• Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives for process control systems and methodologies.

Qualifications:
Minimum Qualifications

• Currently pursuing a Ph.D. degree in Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Physics, Electrical Engineering, or another STEM-related field. 
• Knowledge of semiconductor processing fundamentals, including lithography, etching, polishing, and deposition techniques. 
• Familiarity with statistical data analysis and experimental design methodologies. 
• Experience in materials and physical device characterization techniques like SEM or TEM, gained through coursework, academic research, or hands-on training. 

Preferred Qualifications

• Expertise in advanced semiconductor device structures, fabrication techniques, and process integration. 
• Proficiency in statistical analysis tools and programming languages such as JMP, Python, MATLAB, or C++. 
• Hands-on research experience in device fabrication, physical characterization, or materials testing. 
• Strong foundational knowledge in process control systems and semiconductor device physics. 

Explore the opportunity to grow your expertise in cutting-edge semiconductor manufacturing while contributing to innovative solutions in a collaborative environment. Apply today and take the first step toward shaping the future of technology.

Figma is growing our team of passionate creatives and builders on a mission to make design accessible to all. Figma’s platform helps teams bring ideas to life—whether you're brainstorming, creating a prototype, translating designs into code, or iterating with AI. From idea to product, Figma empowers teams to streamline workflows, move faster, and work together in real time from anywhere in the world. If you're excited to shape the future of design and collaboration, join us!

The AI Research team at Figma is working on the cutting edge of AI and Design. We work on optimizing agentic systems for design quality and end user experience. We build robust evaluators for Design and post-train models. We are a very collaborative, close-knit and impact-focused team of researchers and research engineers working on some of the most challenging technical problems at the intersection of AI and creativity.

We are seeking PhD interns with expertise in machine learning and artificial intelligence to develop innovative AI solutions for design and creative products. Through both fundamental and applied research, your work will contribute to new AI-driven features in Figma products.

• Explore the boundaries of what is possible with the current technology set and experiment with novel ideas

jobs.description:
Location: London, in office
Reports to: Head of Commercial and Audiovisual, Works in Progress
Salary: £30k-35k 

About Works in Progress

Works in Progress is Stripe’s magazine of new and underrated ideas to improve the world. We publish an eclectic mix of articles on policy, economics, business, technology, science, history, arts and culture.

Our audience is growing quickly and includes people making things happen, particularly in technology and politics. We are expanding the commercial side of the magazine—including advertising, subscriptions, events and partnerships—and are looking for an ambitious graduate to help us build it.

The role

This is an entry-level commercial role for a recent graduate who is ambitious, organised and excited to learn quickly in a small, entrepreneurial team.

You will work closely with the Director of Commercial and Audiovisual across the magazine’s commercial activity: advertising, subscriptions, events, marketing and partnerships. You will help keep commercial projects moving by conducting research, supporting outreach, maintaining pipelines and trackers, following up with prospective partners, and contributing to growth experiments.

You will learn by doing: writing outbound emails, building target lists, preparing materials, tracking results, joining calls and following up consistently. It is a strong opportunity for someone who wants early exposure to senior commercial work and meaningful responsibility from the start of their career.

What you’ll do

• Support the advertising sales process, including preparing rate cards, pitch decks, outreach and pipeline materials.

• Research and build target lists of potential advertisers, sponsors, agencies, founders, investors and partners.

• Draft clear, thoughtful outbound emails and follow-ups.

• Maintain accurate CRM records, commercial trackers and reporting.

• Support subscription growth through acquisition and retention ideas, and help measure their effectiveness.

• Help develop the events business, including sponsor research, partnership outreach and event planning support.

• Assist with early marketing and growth experiments across paid acquisition, referrals, partnerships, direct mail and audience development.

• Prepare decks, reports and briefing materials that help commercial conversations move forward.

• Join meetings and calls with clients, partners and agencies, taking notes and supporting follow-up.

• Help turn commercial ideas into clear proposals with pricing, positioning and next steps.

• Work across sales, marketing, events and subscriptions, adapting quickly as priorities evolve.

• Take on the practical, sometimes unglamorous work needed to help a small business grow.

We’re looking for someone who

• Is a recent graduate, or has equivalent early-career experience.

• Is excited by commercial work and motivated by helping ideas turn into revenue.

• Is interested in sales, marketing, partnerships, media, events or business development.

• Is highly organised and comfortable managing lists, trackers and multiple follow-ups.

• Is numerate and confident using spreadsheets.

• Is a sharp, clear writer who can communicate professionally over email and in presentations.

• Is proactive, resilient and comfortable reaching out to people they do not know.

• Is curious, resourceful and willing to learn quickly.

• Enjoys working in a small team where everyone pitches in.

• Is comfortable with both high-profile opportunities and repetitive operational work, such as researching prospects and following up on outreach.

• Has an interest in media, publishing, technology, economics, policy or culture. Previous media or publishing experience is helpful but not required.

Working at Works in Progress

This role is based in London and requires working from the office every day. You will be part of a small, ambitious team that cares deeply about the magazine and its growth. In return, you will get a steep learning curve, close mentorship and the chance to contribute directly to building the commercial future of Works in Progress.

jobs.title: Analog Design Intern
jobs.description:
About Marvell 
Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities. 

At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead. 

Your Team, Your Impact

Every time a hyperscaler trains a frontier AI model, streams a zettabyte of data across a data center fabric, or pushes a coherent optical signal across a transoceanic link, analog and mixed-signal circuits are doing the work that makes it possible. At Marvell, our analog design team is the reason those circuits exist. The custom XPUs, the 224G and 448G SerDes IP, the Silicon Photonics light engines, the co-packaged optics platforms powering the world's largest AI infrastructure — none of it ships without the analog IP this team designs from scratch. This is one of the few places in the industry where analog engineers work at the true physical limit of what silicon can do, on problems at and beyond 448G that have no established design playbook and no known solutions — open research questions that require exactly the kind of rigorous, first-principles thinking a Ph.D. program is built to develop.

Our Ph.D. Intern Program embeds doctoral candidates directly inside active design teams, working alongside staff and distinguished engineers on production IP and research-stage silicon. Projects are selected because they sit at the intersection of Marvell's most pressing engineering challenges and the circuit theory, device physics, and signal processing that define doctoral research in electrical engineering. Interns work through the complete design flow and participate in a structured analog design curriculum alongside their peers. What you will take away from this program is something no coursework can replicate: the experience of seeing your own research become real, working silicon, deployed at scale inside the world's most advanced AI infrastructure.
What You Can Expect
As our Ph.D. Analog Design Intern, every day you will work on circuit design problems tied directly to your doctoral research focus. Specifically, you can expect to:
• Design, simulate, and verify analog and mixed-signal circuit blocks across the full design flow — from architecture and schematic through simulation, layout coordination, and silicon bring-up

• Work on production-grade IP including high-speed SerDes building blocks, Silicon Photonics driver and receiver circuits, ADC/DAC architectures, PLLs, clock distribution networks, LDOs, and other precision analog circuits in advanced CMOS FinFET processes

• Use industry-standard tools including Cadence and MATLAB throughout your project

• Collaborate directly with layout engineers to implement your designs and iterate based on simulation and silicon feedback

• Attend and contribute to design reviews alongside the full engineering team

• Present your work — both the research framing and the design results — to the engineers around you

• Participate in a structured analog design curriculum alongside your Ph.D. intern peers

What We're Looking For
To thrive in this role, you must have experience designing analog and mixed-signal circuits at the transistor level. Specifically:
• Currently enrolled in a Ph.D. program in Electrical Engineering or a related field, with a research focus in analog, mixed-signal, or RF circuit design

• Demonstrate hands-on experience designing and simulating analog circuit blocks such as PLLs, SerDes building blocks, ADCs, DACs, LDOs, amplifiers, or high-speed I/O — not just theoretical familiarity

• Apply strong fundamentals in transistor-level circuit design, including device physics, noise analysis, linearity, stability, and low-power techniques in advanced CMOS processes

• Simulate and verify designs independently using industry-standard tools such as Cadence Virtuoso and Spectre; experience with MATLAB or Python for system-level modeling is a plus

• Communicate design decisions and tradeoffs clearly — you will be expected to present your work to the engineering team and defend your approach

Preferred Qualifications
• Experience designing in FinFET process nodes (7nm, 5nm, 3nm, or equivalent)

• Familiarity with high-speed serial link architectures, optical transceiver circuits, or Die-to-Die interconnect design

• Exposure to layout-aware design, parasitic extraction, or post-layout simulation

• Experience with behavioral modeling in Verilog-A or similar

Expected Base Pay Range (USD)
38 - 76, $ per hour.
The successful candidate’s starting base pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location and market conditions. The expected base pay range for this role may be modified based on market conditions.

This role is eligible to participate in Marvell's bonus and equity plans, including a new hire equity grant and annual equity refreshers, ensuring you are rewarded for your contributions and remain invested in the company's long-term success.
Additional Compensation and Benefit Elements 
Marvell is committed to providing exceptional, comprehensive benefits that support our employees at every stage - from internship to retirement and through life’s most important moments. Our offerings are built around four key pillars: financial well-being, family support, mental and physical health, and recognition. Highlights for our interns: medical, dental, and vision coverage, perks and discounts, robust mental health resources to prioritize emotional well-being, and paid holidays. Additional compensation may be available for intern PhD candidates. We look forward to sharing more with you during the interview process.
All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status.

Any applicant who requires a reasonable accommodation during the selection process should contact Marvell HR Helpdesk at TAOps@marvell.com.

Interview Integrity 
To support fair and authentic hiring practices, candidates are not permitted to use AI tools (such as transcription apps, real-time answer generators like ChatGPT or Copilot, or automated note-taking bots) during interviews.

These tools must not be used to record, assist with, or enhance responses in any way. Our interviews are designed to evaluate your individual experience, thought process, and communication skills in real time. Use of AI tools without prior instruction from the interviewer will result in disqualification from the hiring process.

This position may require access to technology and/or software subject to U.S. export control laws and regulations, including the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). As such, applicants must be eligible to access export-controlled information as defined under applicable law. Marvell may be required to obtain export licensing approval from the U.S. Department of Commerce and/or the U.S. Department of State. Except for U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, or protected individuals as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), all applicants may be subject to an export license review process prior to employment.

jobs.title: Digital and Technology Solutions Degree Engineer Apprentice
jobs.description:
Job Description:
Start date: September 2027
Location: Filton, Bristol
Duration: 4 years and 3 months
University: Weston College (UCW), degree accredited by the University of the West of England
Degree: BSc (Hons) Digital and Technology Solutions
Apprenticeship standard: ST0119 Digital and Technology Solutions Professional Level 6

Application closing date: Applications will be open until 26 October 2026. After this date, the advert will close once sufficient applications are received. Early submission is recommended.

We love your interest in joining Airbus! There is no limit on the number of positions you can apply for. However, please be aware that you can only progress in the selection process for one position at a time. We recommend reviewing all available opportunities and applying to those that best match your experience and aspirations.

Benefits:

Salary: £23,245

35 hours per week // Half day Fridays! // 25 days holiday plus bank holidays // Pension // Success share // Plus many more flexible benefits! 

About Us: 

This is an ideal role for someone with a keen interest in learning and applying digital solutions to real engineering problems.

Alongside your degree, you’ll be joining our experts at Filton, immediately being able to apply your skills to the world of Commercial Aircraft. You'll be assigned to a department with incredible career potential:
• Flight Physics;

• Fuel (incl Hydrogen) & Landing Gear Testing;

• Digital Airframe.

We empower our apprentices with significant placement flexibility. You'll not only gain deep technical expertise within your core area but also develop a diverse skill set through rotations in various engineering departments. This unique blend of academic study, on-the-job experience, and training ensures you're well-equipped for a successful and impactful career.

What you will be doing:

Our Digital Degree Apprenticeship offers a full degree with no fees, plus vocational training with a regular salary. Airbus is leading the way with this unique 4 year programme through which you will achieve a BSc (Hons) Digital and Technology Solutions. You will be studying via our training partner, Weston College (UCW), and your degree will be accredited by the University of the West of England. Your industry based work takes place at our world leading aircraft manufacturer site in Filton, Bristol.

Key activities of the industry based work of this apprenticeship include:
• Contributing to new and innovative software which is used in the overall aircraft design, testing or optimization processes;

• Working on software solutions to support design & manufacturing of physical aircraft as well as in-service aircraft;

• Participate in all phases of the application development life cycle including research and design, development, testing, implementation and support;

• Interface with engineers and IT specialists to provide solutions to business needs.

Requirements:

In order to be eligible for this apprenticeship you must have a minimum:
• 3 A-Levels as grade C/4 or above, preferably in Maths, Sciences and IT;

OR
• T Level in an IT/Digital subject at Merit or above;

OR
• BTEC L3 Extended Diploma in an IT/Digital subject, at minimum MMM grade;

OR
• Equivalent qualifications/Experience subject to validation;

AND
• Minimum of 4 GCSEs including English Language and Maths – Grade 4/C or above.

**Please note that, due to the funded nature of this programme, applicants with undergraduate degrees in computing/IT are not eligible.

The successful candidate will also be able to demonstrate the following:
• Submit your CV stating your grades and if they are predicted or achieved; 

• Submit a Cover Letter highlighting your passion and suitability for this apprenticeship;

• Enjoys solving mathematical or science problems through coding;

• Some previous experience of coding and/or Linux/cloud;

• The ability to work well in a team;

• Not afraid to get “stuck-in” and learn;

• Proactive, love to learn and be able to focus on your own self development;

• Ability to manage problems, communicating effectively to resolve them in a fast-paced environment.

BOOST YOUR APPLICATION:

We want to get to know you—not just your grades or school background so, tell us on your cover letter:
• Why Airbus and this apprenticeship?
What is it about Airbus that makes you excited to start a career with us? What is it about our company, our values, or the future of aerospace that excites you? We want to hear about what motivates you to pursue this unique path and how you see yourself growing with us.

• What skills and experience do you bring? 
Think about projects, hobbies, or academic subjects that have given you practical experience. This could include personal projects, academic work and extracurricular activities. 

Important Information:

GRADES: If you are on predicted grades, your offer will be conditional to achieving the position’s requirements before the apprenticeship start date.

SECURITY CLEARANCE: You will be subject to a BPSS (Baseline Personnel Security Standard) check. You may also need to gain UK SC-level Security Clearance or Export Control, depending on the role.

RIGHT TO WORK IN THE UK: Candidates must have current legal authorisation to work in the United Kingdom for the full duration of the programme. For more information, please check the Government Website.

LEVY FUNDING: Successful candidates must be eligible for the levy funding. 

Our apprenticeship roles do not meet the minimum requirements set by UK Visas & Immigration to enable sponsorship of migrant workers.

AI Guidance: We know you might be thinking about using AI to help you in your application - before you do, please read our guidelines on the use of AI for recruitment at Airbus Use of AI Guidance.

Contact:

Please let us know if you need us to make any adjustments to allow you to access and participate fully in the recruitment process. If you wish to discuss this further please contact via email apprentices@airbus.com​. ​ ​Any information disclosed will be treated in the strictest confidence.

Degree Apprenticeship Programme
 
You will study towards an AI and Data Science Graduate Level Apprenticeship qualification with Glasgow Caledonian University, developing the knowledge, skills and behaviours required to build and apply artificial intelligence responsibly in an engineering environment.
 
The programme is delivered through a blended learning approach, combining:
 
• On campus study
• Live virtual lectures
• Online learning resources
• Self-directed study
 
Programme structure:
 
The BSc (Hons) AI and Data Science (Graduate Apprenticeship) will equip you with the knowledge and skills required to succeed in your role within Thales. Providing a strong foundation across data and AI, this programme will help you to learn how to manage, explore, analyse, understand and visualise data, alongside technical skills such as software development and machine learning.
 
Delivered over 4 years, you will achieve:
Year 1: Certificate of Higher Education in Computing
Year 2: Diploma of Higher Education in Computing
Year 4: BSc (Hons) AI and Data Science (Graduate Apprenticeship)
 
Entry Requirements
 
To apply, you will need:
 
Highers
• 96 UCAS points
• Four Highers (BBCC) including Maths or Computing
• A foundation apprenticeship will be equal to one Higher at B
• A modern apprenticeship SCQF Level 6 in a relevant discipline will be equal to two Highers at B
 
Benefits
• Competitive salary of £24,000 per annum
• Performance-related pay uplifts
• Holiday entitlement of 201 hours a year (plus a company day and bank holidays)
• Contributory Company Pension
• Health Care Cash Plan
• Hybrid/flexible working options
• Employee assistance programme
• Learning and development support
• Employee discounts and wellbeing initiatives
• Life Cover
• 80 Hours Volunteering per year (first two years)

Thales Apprentice Recruitment Process
 
1. Apply Online - submit your application online to register your interest. You only need to register for one role as you will have the opportunity to apply for additional roles at the full application stage.
 
2. Upload Your CV
 
3. Check your emails for the invitation to apply – this will come from recruiting@jobalerts.thalesgroup.com
 
4. Complete Your Application – follow the link provided in the email to complete your application. You can apply for one primary role and up to 3 additional roles.

5. Complete Online Tests - undertake the online assessments designed to evaluate your suitability for the role.
 
6. Virtual Assessment Centre - candidates who progress from the online assessment stage will attend a virtual assessment centre, which will include group exercises, and competency-based interviews.

7. Job Offer – successful candidates who perform well throughout the recruitment process will receive a job offer from Thales.

For further information about our Future Talent recruitment process, including hints and tips, or to connect with a member of the Future Talent Team, a Graduate, or an Apprentice, please visit Thales Future Talent - Connectr.

Please note, assessment centres for shortlisted candidates will be held between February - May 2027. Induction week for all Graduate and Apprentices will take place from Monday 6 September - Friday 10 September 2027.
 
Closing date: Our applications will close at 11.59pm on Wednesday 17 February 2027, this is the only time we will be accepting applications this year. Please note, we will be in contact by the end of February 2027 with details of next steps.

PLEASE NOTE THAT ROLES MAY CLOSE EARLIER THAN THE ADVERTISED DEADLINE IF WE RECEIVE A HIGH NUMER OF APPLICATIONS. WE ENCOURAGE YOU TO APPLY AS SOON AS POSSIBLE TO AVOID MISSING OUT ON THIS OPPORTUNITY.
 
Because of the work we do at Thales, all roles are subject to security requirements.
 
To be considered for this position, you must have the permanent right to work in the UK and be able to successfully complete and maintain UK Government security checks, including Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) screening and Security Clearance (SC), which is a government background check, before starting employment.
 
To be eligible for SC clearance, you will typically need to have lived in the UK continuously for the last five years. As part of the vetting process, you will be asked to provide evidence of your identity, right to work in the UK, any time spent overseas during the last five years, and your employment and/or education history.
 
For further details of the evidence required to apply for security clearance please follow this link - https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/united-kingdom-security-vetting-clearance-levels/national-security-vetting-clearance-levels.

37 hours per week // Half day Fridays!* // 25 days holiday plus bank holidays // Pension // Success share // Plus many more flexible benefits! 

*subject to completing full hours prior to this

About us:

Airbus is a global leader in aeronautics, space and related services. In 2016, it generated revenues of € 67 billion and employed a workforce of around 134,000. Airbus offers the most comprehensive range of passenger airliners from 100 to more than 600 seats. Airbus is also a European leader providing tanker, combat, transport and mission aircraft, as well as Europe's number one space enterprise and the world's second largest space business. In helicopters, Airbus provides the most efficient civil and military rotorcraft solutions worldwide.

Our people work with passion and determination to make the world a more connected, safer and smarter place. Taking pride in our work, we draw on each other's expertise and experience to achieve excellence. Our diversity and teamwork culture propel us to accomplish the extraordinary – on the ground, in the sky and in space.

Would you like to work on advanced high grade crypto systems and key management systems to protect Governments, Military, Enterprise Organizations and essential National Infrastructure from cyber threats? Airbus Defence & Space have exciting apprenticeships starting in our Cyber Security Division at our base in Newport, South Wales.

As an apprentice you will be trained in high grade cryptographic development, you will learn about our existing Ectocryp and CertSecure suite of products. You will join a team of highly skilled team of engineers working to deliver the next generation of encryption devices. You will receive on the job training and a formal degree qualification all while being paid and accruing no course fees.

As part of this degree apprenticeship, you will be studying towards achieving a BSc (Hons) Electrical and Electronic Engineering Degree Apprenticeship which will be provided by University of South Wales.

What you will be doing:

Our UK Apprenticeship Programme provides exceptional candidates the opportunity to master managerial and technical skills. Over the four year period it combines rotational placements with focused training and the possibility of European assignments as well as further personal development and the chance to build your professional network.

From day one, you will be assigned to a particular department and will be guided through the various placement opportunities that exist within your function, the wider business and even with customers and suppliers. This, along with training provided works to ensure you are ready and experienced enough to take the next step of your career following the programme's conclusion.

There are several departments that require electronic engineers; these include Production, Test & verification, and New Product Development. You will move around the different departments throughout your apprenticeship learning the key skills that each department requires, giving you a broad range of technical skills. These skills will include: how to specify, perform, build, test, and document electronics hardware design for electronic system architecture. 
Skills you will be taught will include:

• Construction of complex low volume communication products;
• Maintenance of product assembly and test capabilities;
• Repair and test products;
• Design and repair PCB's to IPC standards;
• Requirements capture skills;
• Soldering to approved standards;
• Schematic capture;
• Computer Aided Design for simulation and design;
• Performing in-house electronics design;
• Documenting the design.

The successful candidate will be subject to security clearance in order to undertake related work in accordance with business needs.

Requirements:

In order to be eligible to this apprenticeship, you must have a minimum of:

• 120–160 UCAS points made up of A levels which must include Maths and an additional numerate subject (such as Physics, Chemistry, Biology or Geography)

Or

• BTEC National Diploma at PP or BTEC Extended Diploma at PPP

And

• 3 GCSEs at Grade 4/C or above including Maths and English Language or equivalent subject to validation

Successful candidates will be able to demonstrate the following:

• Genuine interest in electronic design and development;
• Must be highly self-motivated, articulate, with good verbal and written communications skills;
• Submit your CV stating your grades and if they are predicted or achieved;
• Submit a Cover Letter highlighting your passion and suitability for this apprenticeship.

BOOST YOUR APPLICATION:

We want to get to know you—not just your grades or school background so, tell us on your cover letter:

• Why Airbus and this apprenticeship?
What is it about Airbus that makes you excited to start a career with us? What is it about our company, our values, or the future of aerospace that excites you? We want to hear about what motivates you to pursue this unique path and how you see yourself growing with us.

• What skills and experience do you bring? 
Think about projects, hobbies, or academic subjects that have given you practical experience. This could include personal projects, academic work and extracurricular activities. 

Important Information:

GRADES: If you are on predicted grades, your offer will be conditional to achieving the position’s requirements before the apprenticeship start date.

SECURITY CLEARANCE: You will be subject to a BPSS (Baseline Personnel Security Standard) check. You may also need to gain UK SC-level Security Clearance or Export Control, depending on the role.

RIGHT TO WORK IN THE UK: Candidates must have current legal authorisation to work in the United Kingdom for the full duration of the programme. For more information, please check the Government Website.

Our apprenticeship roles do not meet the minimum requirements set by UK Visas & Immigration to enable sponsorship of migrant workers.

Please let us know if you need us to make any adjustments to allow you to access and participate fully in the recruitment process. If you wish to discuss this further please contact via email apprentices@airbus.com​. Any information disclosed will be treated in the strictest confidence.

35 hours per week // Half day Fridays! // 25 days holiday plus bank holidays // Pension // Success share // Plus many more flexible benefits! 

About us: 

Our Digital and Technology Solutions Degree Apprenticeship at Airbus offers a truly unique launchpad for your career. You'll gain a full "university experience" combined with three years of invaluable, real-world industry expertise, all while earning a full-time salary and paying ZERO fees. During this exciting program, you'll dive into diverse digital solutions and platforms and apply industry-leading project management methodologies to deliver critical business projects, directly contributing to our success and your degree.

The apprenticeship gives you the unique opportunity to work in a wide variety of disciplines including:

• Cyber Security; 
• IT Service Delivery Management; 
• Operations Digitalisation & Automation;
• Software Development;
• Information Management. 

Over the 3 years, alongside your workplace commitments, you will achieve a fully funded BSc (Hons) in Applied Data Science. The completion of this degree will be intertwined with your work based experiences, part of which will directly contribute to your degree. 

You will be studying via our partner Bangor University and local colleges. Your industry based work takes place at our world leading aircraft manufacturer site in Broughton (near Chester), North Wales. Please note, this will require some travel on day release study to a college in North Wales.

We are also believers in experiential learning too, and there are many events that take place that offer exciting opportunities to grow and develop whilst also having fun!

This apprenticeship is delivered through a combination of on the job training at Airbus, and university based learning on day release over the duration of the 3 year programme. 

You will learn and apply cutting-edge Applied Data Science principles to real-world business challenges. You'll gain invaluable hands-on experience that not only contributes to your degree but also directly adds significant value to our operations.

• End-to-End Project Management: Managing projects from inception, including gathering requirements, defining technical specifications, architecting solutions, maintaining comprehensive documentation, and overseeing project timelines.

During this time, you will also get to work with various teams in our engineering, design, quality, operations, cyber security, IT solutions and help desk teams, whilst also having the opportunity to pick placements outside of your area of study, including HR, facilities management, recruitment, finance and much more.

12-Month IT Developer Analyst Student Placement offering hands-on experience in software development, business analysis, AI technologies, and Agile delivery within a global healthcare environment.

Are you a university student eager to innovate at the heart of a global healthcare leader? Join our dynamic IT team as a placement student and play a pivotal role in developing and maintaining cutting-edge IT systems that drive productivity and innovation. Collaborate with international teams, leverage AI technologies, and enhance your technical and analytical skills in an Agile environment. We're looking for passionate individuals with excellent communication, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to diversity and inclusion. Apply now to kickstart your career and contribute to our mission of creating the greatest value for human health.
 
This role will be based in our modern state-of-the-art co-working facilities in Moorgate, London. This site, at the heart of London provides fantastic amenities, support services and collaborative workspaces with convenient transport links.
 
We are a global biopharmaceutical leader committed to enhancing the lives of individuals through a diverse portfolio of prescription medicines, oncology treatments, life-saving vaccines, and animal health products. Our unwavering dedication to delivering innovative solutions is the driving force behind everything we do.

jobs.title: Electronics Engineer Apprentice - Level 6 Electrical and Electronic Engineering Degree Apprenticeship
jobs.description:
Location: Templecombe, United Kingdom

Thales is a global technology leader with more than 83,000 employees on five continents. With over 7,500 people in the UK, operating across defence, space, aerospace, and digital security, we help build a future we can all trust. Thales supports the security and stability of our nation by providing extraordinary technology to our customers, as well as delivering social value to the UK with our products and services.

2027 Electronics Engineer Apprentice - Level 6 Electrical and Electronic Engineering Degree Apprenticeship
 
Start Date: 06 September 2027
Salary: £24,000 per annum
Employee type: Permanent
Location: Templecombe
Working Schedule: Monday – Friday, 37 hours a week (8 hours Monday – Thursday, 5 hours Friday)
 
Turn your curiosity into a career. If you're passionate about engineering, eager to learn, and looking for a degree apprenticeship that combines academic study with exciting on-the-job experience, we'd love to hear from you.
 
Benefits of the programme:
• Earn a salary while studying
• Gain hands-on experience in a real engineering environment
• Receive job-specific training and development
• Achieve a recognised qualification
• Secure a permanent role from the start of your apprenticeship
• Have your university tuition fees fully paid
 
About the Role
 
An Electronics Engineering Apprenticeship at Thales is a hands-on entry route into engineering, where you learn electronics design, integration, testing, and troubleshooting while working alongside qualified engineers on real programmes. The exact scope can vary by team, the role centres on building and validating electronic solutions.
 
What You Will Do
 
• Support electronics design and development
Assisting with circuit design activities, component selection, schematic/layout reviews, or adapting existing designs.
• Build and integrate hardware
Working with breadboards/prototypes and progressing to production-relevant hardware (e.g., assembling modules, wiring, integrating sub-systems).
• Test and verify equipment
Using test equipment (e.g., oscilloscopes, mustimeters, signal generators) to validate functionality against requirements, debug faults, and document results.
• Troubleshoot and problem-solve
Investigating issues found during lab testing, system integration, or trials, then helping implement fixes or process improvements.
• Document engineering work
Writing test reports, maintaining records, updating documentation, and contributing to engineering reviews.
• Work in a safety/quality-focused environment
Following procedures, configuration control practices, and quality standards relevant to Thales and its programmes.
 
What You Will Learn
 
• Core electronics fundamentals (analogue/digital concepts, power, signal integrity basics, interfaces)
• Engineering processes (requirements, verification/validation, configuration management)
• Practical test methods and interpretation of measurement results
• Teamworking and professional engineering behaviours (reviews, clear reporting, traceability)
 
Typical environment & day-to-day
 
You’ll usually split time between:
• On-the-job training with engineers in labs/engineering teams (practical hardware/test work)
• Structured apprenticeship learning (college/college-equivalent coursework leading toward a qualification in engineering or electronics)
 
Skills and qualities that help
• A strong interest in electronics and how systems work
• Ability to follow technical instructions and procedures
• Curiosity and persistence when debugging
• Clear communication and attention to detail (especially for test data and documentation)
• Basic competence with tools (e.g., soldering/assembly, spreadsheets/measurement logs) is beneficial

Degree Apprenticeship Programme
 
You will study towards a Level 6 BEng Electrical and Electronic Engineering Degree Apprenticeship with Exeter University.
 
In your first year you will be given a broad theoretical and practical knowledge across all core engineering disciplines, before progressing onto increasingly advanced topics later in the course.
 
Years one and two provide core fundamental knowledge of engineering principles, as well as applying mathematics to engineering problems. Years three and four are spent applying your knowledge to engineering problems.
 
You will complete a Technical Report and Presentation in the final year: an opportunity to apply your knowledge and skills to devise an engineering solution at a professional level in an area of engineering study that aligns to your role at Thales.
 
By the end of the programme, you will have achieved a BEng in Electrical and Electronic Engineering as well as a Level 6 Electrical and Electronic Engineering Degree Apprenticeship.
 
Programme structure:
 
Throughout the four-year programme, you will combine university study with practical workplace experience, developing both academic knowledge and professional engineering skills.
• Lectures and workshops are delivered through a series of 2-week blocks spaced throughout your degree apprenticeship
• Alongside campus taught lecturers, you will have access to digital resources and discipline experts to support your studies.
 
Entry Requirements
 
To apply, you will need:
 
A Levels
 
• Three A Levels at ABB, including a Grade B in Maths and a Science subject.
 
Or BTEC Extended Diploma (DDM)
 
• Applicants studying one of the following BTEC Extended Diplomas will be considered: Applied Science; Aeronautical Engineering; Building Services; Engineering Construction and the Built Environment; Civil Engineering; Operations and Maintenance Engineering; Computer Engineering; Electrical/Electronic Engineering; Engineering; Manufacturing Engineering; Mechanical Engineering; Environmental Sustainability.
 
Or T Level (Distinction)
 
• Required Subjects: Design and Development for Engineering and Manufacturing; Engineering; Manufacturing; Processing and Control; Maintenance, Installation and Repair for Engineering: Manufacturing only, Surveying and Planning for Construction. 
 
GCSEs
• Minimum of five GCSEs at Grade 4-9 (A-C)
• Must include:• English
• Maths

Please note that applicants who already hold a relevant degree will not be eligible for this programme.
 
Benefits
· Competitive salary of £24,000 per annum
· Performance-related pay uplifts
· Holiday entitlement of 201 hours a year (plus a company day and bank holidays)
· Contributory Company Pension
· Health Care Cash Plan
· Hybrid/flexible working options
· Employee assistance programme
· Learning and development support
· Employee discounts and wellbeing initiatives
· Life Cover
· 80 Hours Volunteering per year (first two years)
 
Thales Apprentice Recruitment Process
 
1. Apply Online - submit your application online to register your interest. You only need to register for one role as you will have the opportunity to apply for additional roles at the full application stage.
 
2. Upload Your CV
 
3. Check your emails for the invitation to apply – this will come from recruiting@jobalerts.thalesgroup.com
 
4. Complete Your Application – follow the link provided in the email to complete your application. You can apply for one primary role and up to 3 additional roles.

5. Complete Online Tests - undertake the online assessments designed to evaluate your suitability for the role.
 
6. Virtual Assessment Centre - candidates who progress from the online assessment stage will attend a virtual assessment centre, which will include group exercises, and competency-based interviews.

7. Job Offer – successful candidates who perform well throughout the recruitment process will receive a job offer from Thales.

For further information about our Future Talent recruitment process, including hints and tips, or to connect with a member of the Future Talent Team, a Graduate, or an Apprentice, please visit Thales Future Talent - Connectr.
 
Please note, assessment centres for shortlisted candidates will be held between February - May

jobs.title: Hardware Engineering Intern
jobs.description:
By submitting your resume, you acknowledge that your Hardware Engineering internship application will be processed in accordance with NVIDIA’s Applicant Privacy Policy and you agree to our Terms of Service. We’ll review resumes on an ongoing basis, and a recruiter may reach out if your experience fits one of our many internship opportunities.

NVIDIA pioneered accelerated computing to tackle challenges no one else can solve. Our work in AI and digital twins is transforming the world's largest industries and profoundly impacting society — from gaming to robotics, self-driving cars to life-saving healthcare, climate change to virtual worlds where we can all connect and create. Our internships offer an excellent opportunity to expand your career and get hands on experience with one of our industry leading Hardware teams. We’re seeking strategic, ambitious, hard-working, and creative individuals who are passionate about helping us tackle challenges no one else can solve. 
 
Throughout the 12-week full-time internship, students will work on projects that have a measurable impact on our business. We’re looking for students pursuing a B.S., M.S., or Ph.D. degree within a relevant or related field. 
 
Potential Internships in this field include: 
System Validation 
• These teams are responsible for system validation and post-production activities for datacenter server products, such as HGX baseboards, DGX Servers or DGX Workstations. You will need to maintain a close relationship with all members of the Architecture, Hardware and Software Design teams to ensure rigorous testing and debugging of all new features and changes made during product development. 

Hardware Design 
• With strong backgrounds in electrical engineering and a curiosity about hardware product design, Hardware Design Interns work with a close-knit, multi-disciplinary team, enjoying hands-on work, with cutting-edge visual computing platforms. Primary responsibilities may include Hardware Testing, Debugging, and Validation of new products to ensure they meet performance, functional, and quality objectives. 

Mechanical Engineering 
• This team helps craft and test new NVIDIA products. You will be part of a multi-functional team researching and developing new concepts and materials for our next generation of products. You must demonstrate excellent interpersonal skills and a strong academic background in Mechanical Engineering. 

Silicon Solutions 
• As a part of the Silicon Solutions Engineering Team, you will be responsible for productizing NVIDIA’s chips into groundbreaking consumer, professional, server, mobile, and automotive solutions.

jobs.title: PhD Researcher Intern - Machine Learning for Construction
jobs.description:
Job Requisition ID #

26WD101430

Position Overview
Autodesk Research is looking for a PhD Researcher Intern in machine learning to help advance AI for the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry.
AEC projects generate large amounts of data across design, planning, and construction. Our team studies how machine learning and AI can connect this data and learn from them to understand, predict, and reason about how projects unfold.

As a Researcher intern, you will own a research problem in this area, scoped to fit your expertise and the team's current direction. You'll collaborate with researchers and industry domain experts, and your work will help shape how Autodesk brings AI to AEC workflows.

Responsibilities

• Research: Define and investigate an open research question in machine learning and AI for AEC data, from problem framing through experiments and results
• Model development: Design and train AI and machine learning models, including graph-based and temporal models, on large, heterogeneous real-world project data
• Uncertainty and evaluation: Build predictive models with reliable uncertainty estimates, and evaluate them rigorously against strong baselines
• Data preparation: Prepare, integrate, and validate data from multiple sources, including knowledge graph representations
• Communication: Document methods and results, present findings, and potentially contribute to research publications
• You will work as an individual contributor within a research team

Minimum Qualifications

• Currently pursuing a PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Data Science, Civil Engineering, Construction Informatics, or a related field with a graduation date no sooner than April 2027.
• Research experience in graph machine learning on heterogeneous knowledge graphs, including graph neural networks, graph transformers, link prediction, node classification, and graph self-supervised learning (e.g., masked graph autoencoders, joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPA))
• Experience with temporal or time-varying data, through temporal graph models or time-series forecasting
• Experience with uncertainty-aware prediction, including calibrated probability estimates and learning from small or imbalanced labeled data
• Rigorous experimental practice: baselines, ablations, leakage-safe train/test splits, and label quality checks
• Proficiency in Python and PyTorch (PyTorch Geometric or DGL a plus), and graph query languages
• Self-directed, with the ability to explain technical results clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences

Preferred Qualifications

• Time-series, state-space, or multimodal modeling, including combining time-varying signals from multiple sources and modalities
• Bayesian or probabilistic modeling
• Natural language processing or large language models for classifying or extracting information from technical text and AEC data
• Experience with AEC data or workflows, such as building models, drawings, project schedules, project records, or design review, etc.
• Knowledge graph engineering: Neo4j/Cypher, ontologies, entity linking, and data integration
• Publications at top machine learning venues (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, KDD) or construction computing venues (e.g., Automation in Construction, ASCE computing journals, ISARC, CIB W78)

jobs.title: Strategy Intern
jobs.description:
*****THIS POSITION IS NOT ELIGIBLE FOR VISA SPONSORSHIP*****

To be considered for this position, applications and resumes are accepted only through our careers site by directly applying to the posted job. We do not accept unsolicited resumes or sales solicitations from staffing agencies. Any OCC employee wishing to submit a referral must do so through their Workday account. Any resume submitted outside of an active job posting will not be considered for employment.

*****INTERNS AND SEASONAL INTERNS ARE ELIGIBLE ONLY FOR PAID SICK LEAVE ACCRUED BASED ON HOURS WORKED. NO OTHER BENEFIT INCLUDING TECHNOLOGY STIPEND APPLY TO INTERNS OR SEASONAL INTERNS*****
Hybrid Work Program
OCC operates under a Hybrid Work Program which, absent an approved exception, requires employees to work from an OCC office at least 3 days per week . To maximize in–person collaboration, Tuesday and Wednesday are considered anchor days, and all employees are expected to work in the office both days. Employees meeting performance expectations are generally permitted to select 2 other days per week to work remotely if desired. When working remotely, employees are generally expected to work from the state in which they reside, absent an exception approved by Human Resources. Additionally, OCC generally does not permit employees to work while traveling internationally.
About OCC:
A World Class Clearing Organization
The Options Clearing Corporation (OCC) is the world's largest equity derivatives clearing organization. Founded in 1973, OCC is dedicated to promoting stability and market integrity by delivering clearing and settlement services for options, futures and securities lending transactions. As a Systemically Important Financial Market Utility (SIFMU), OCC operates under the jurisdiction of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), and the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. OCC has more than 100 clearing members and provides central counterparty (CCP) clearing and settlement services to 21 exchanges and trading platforms.
OCC also provides free and engaging educational resources about the benefits and risks of options through its Options Industry Council (OIC). 
OCC is building a culture that empowers continued learning, authentic innovation, and constant creativity.
About the Intern Program:
OCC is looking for interns who are eager to learn, humble enough to ask questions, and ready to think critically about complex problems. The OCC Internship Program equips students with the real-world skills needed to transition successfully into a career in financial services. As an intern, you will contribute to meaningful projects, applying your skills and knowledge to real challenges facing the business. Your time with us is a real opportunity to make a genuine impact on the future of OCC!
OCC's Summer Internship Program is a 12-week opportunity running either May through August or June through September, and is open to undergraduate and graduate students who are actively enrolled at a college or university. Interns work up to 40 hours per week in a hybrid work environment, and overtime is not permitted.
About the Team & Role
The Strategy team sits within OCC's Product Management organization and is responsible for defining, prioritizing, and delivering enhancements to OCC's clearing platforms. We operate as an Agile Scrum team, managing our backlog and sprint execution in Jira and maintaining our documentation, roadmaps, and requirements in Confluence. The team partners closely with Engineering, Risk, Operations, and QA to translate business needs into well-defined user stories and to ensure what we build aligns with both regulatory requirements and market participant needs.
Beyond day-to-day delivery, the team also contributes to longer-term product strategy — evaluating industry trends, competitive positioning, and emerging needs in the derivatives clearing space to inform our roadmap.
The intern would contribute directly to both tracks of this work: supporting active sprint execution (backlog grooming, story writing, ceremony participation) alongside our Product Owners, while also assisting with research and analysis that feeds into product strategy discussions. This gives the intern visibility into both the tactical "how we build" and the strategic "why we build it" sides of product ownership.
Job Summary & Responsibilities
• Support the creation and refinement of user stories, acceptance criteria, and backlog items in Jira
• Assist in maintaining product documentation, roadmaps, and meeting notes in Confluence
• Participate in Agile ceremonies (sprint planning, daily stand-ups, backlog refinement, sprint reviews, retrospectives)
• Help prioritize the product backlog in partnership with Product Owners based on business value and stakeholder input
• Conduct research and gather requirements from internal stakeholders (Operations, Risk, Technology)
• Support competitive analysis, market research, and other inputs to product strategy initiatives
• Track sprint progress, help identify blockers, and support reporting on team velocity and delivery metrics
• Collaborate with cross-functional teams (engineering, QA, design) to ensure alignment on product goals
• Assist in creating presentations or summaries for leadership on product updates and strategic recommendations
Candidate Qualifications
Rising senior or second-year graduate student, graduating December 2027 or May/August 2028.
Desired Majors
• Business, Finance, Information Systems, Information Systems, Computer Science
Technical Skills/Experience Desired
• Strong interest in product management, financial technology, or capital markets
• Familiarity with Agile/Scrum methodology (coursework, certification, or prior experience acceptable)
• Basic understanding of or willingness to quickly learn Jira and Confluence
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills
• Detail-oriented with an ability to manage multiple priorities
Additional Qualifications
• Prior internship or coursework experience in product management, business analysis, or software development
• Exposure to financial markets, derivatives, clearing, or post-trade processing (a plus, not required)
• Experience with data analysis tools (Excel, SQL, Tableau) is a plus
• Interest in product strategy, market research, or competitive analysis

About Us
The Options Clearing Corporation (OCC) is the world's largest equity derivatives clearing organization. Founded in 1973, OCC is dedicated to promoting stability and market integrity by delivering clearing and settlement services for options, futures and securities lending transactions. As a Systemically Important Financial Market Utility (SIFMU), OCC operates under the jurisdiction of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), and the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. OCC has more than 100 clearing members and provides central counterparty (CCP) clearing and settlement services to 19 exchanges and trading platforms. Join us and assimilate cutting edge tech knowledge at SOTI: Next Gen!

Job Title: Data Scientist (Intern)
Position Type: Co-op 
Location:  Mississauga, ON (Hybrid)
Temporary, Internship

What You’ll Do

As a Data Scientist Intern at SOTI, you’ll have the opportunity to work alongside experienced Data Scientists and Engineers on real-world AI and Machine Learning initiatives that support SOTI’s enterprise products. You’ll contribute to projects involving Generative AI, Natural Language Processing (NLP), Machine Learning, and data-driven solutions, while gaining hands-on experience with technologies such as Large Language Models (LLMs), Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), embeddings, and vector databases.

This internship offers hands-on experience working on real-world Data Science and AI projects within SOTI’s products. You’ll have the opportunity to explore emerging AI technologies, contribute to meaningful projects, and learn from experienced team members in a collaborative and innovative environment.
 
What you will learn: 

• Enhance your programming skills by working in a team alongside experienced team members 
• Learn how cutting-edge Generative AI technologies (e.g., OpenAI, LangChain, vector databases) are evaluated, selected, and integrated into large-scale enterprise products
• Get hands-on experience applying Gen AI to solve real-world business problems in SOTI’s core products (e.g., intelligent automation, conversational interfaces, AI-powered analytics)
• Gain an understanding of how various roles work together to deliver software products: Developers, Architects, Quality Assurance, User Experience, Product Management, Software Development, Marketing, etc. 
• Gain an understanding of how user requirements are gathered, and the various processes used to translate real-world problems into software solutions 
• Understand the tools and processes used to develop professional software products e.g. Jira, Git 
• Understand the testing processes and frameworks used to deliver high quality software products 

Required skills:  

• Knowledge of algorithms, data structures and database fundamentals 
• Strong Data Science and ML Basics, foundational knowledge of NLP, AI
• Awareness about NLP fundamentals, vector spaces, Embeddings, Regression, Classification, Non supervised learning.
• Awareness about GenAI concepts like RAG, Classification, Evaluation metrices
• Basic knowledge of Software Development Life Cycle concepts 
• Strong math, analytic and problem-solving skills 
• Basic knowledge of programming in one or more of the following programming languages: C, C++, Java, JavaScript, SQL, Ruby, Rust, Lua, Haskell 
• Most importantly curiosity, a desire to learn and be a part of a team 

About SOTI

It all started with a classic story about one developer’s vision. While Carl Rodrigues, President and CEO of SOTI, was an IT consultant, he developed solutions for managing mobile device screens from a desktop. SOTI’s two decades of success has built strong partnerships with leading mobile platform providers and device manufacturers. At SOTI, we have demonstrated commitment to staying at the forefront of mobility management and security. We are deeply committed to researching and developing solutions that address today’s toughest mobility challenges. We strive to go where nobody has gone before.

If you want to bring your ideas to life, apply at SOTI today. 

Use of Artificial Intelligence in Hiring 

SOTI uses AI tools to support parts of our recruitment process, such as reviewing resumes, screening qualifications, and creating interview questions. Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities. 

At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead. 

Your Team, Your Impact

As a part of the Multimarket Business Group, the System Engineering Hardware team is responsible for developing silicon validation board (EVB) and customer reference design board (CRB) for products ranging from compute processors, CXL accelerators, Security controllers as well as custom SoCs. Engineers on the team lead board design from concept through silicon validation by collaborating with internal cross-functional teams and external partners.

It's fun to work in a company where people truly BELIEVE in what they're doing!
We're committed to bringing passion and customer focus to the business.

If you like wild growth and working with happy, enthusiastic over-achievers, you'll enjoy your career with us!

Lumentum Canada was awarded the 2022 National Capital Region’s Top Employers for the 6th consecutive year and the 2022 Career Directory Canada’s Best Employers for Recent Graduates for the 5th consecutive year. 
 
Position Title: Optical Characterization Engineer Co-op/Intern
Employment Type: Student – Co-op/Intern, Existing vacancy
Location: Ottawa ON, Onsite

Lumentum is seeking an enthusiastic and innovative Optical Verification Engineer (Co-op/Intern) to join the R&D Design Verification and Characterization (DVaC) team in the Applied Photonics Solutions Department based in Ottawa, Ontario.

At Lumentum, we’re building the tech behind the world’s fastest networks and most advanced systems. Our optical and photonic solutions power everything from AI and cloud computing to data centers, telecom, and advanced manufacturing.

We’re a global team of innovators working where light meets technology, solving big challenges that keep the world connected and moving forward. If shaping the future of connectivity excites you, you’ll fit right in.

The Opportunity...
• 8-month term (preferred): Jan 2027 to September 2027 
• 12-month term: Jan 2027 to December 2027 
• Pay range: $24-35/hr

What You’ll Be Doing
Do you enjoy having autonomy and independence in tasks, while also collaboratively contributing to novel, cutting-edge products in the photonics and optical communications industries?

If so, consider joining our team of talented optical engineers and software designers.

You will have a positive impact on our success by:
• Employing theoretical concepts and principles from optics & photonics in practice, to improve the robustness of our test & measurement techniques.
• Sharing your advanced knowledge of optical technologies with the team to further team growth.
• Developing automated test software and scripts
• Analyzing optical, hardware, and software failures
• Designing and conducting test cases to properly validate the operation of critical product features.
• Implementing and expanding upon automated test software and scripts that improve our test coverage as well as the quality of our results.
• Analyzing and characterizing optical, hardware and software failures and reporting them to relevant designers using our internal process and tools

What We’re Looking For
• Data analysis using Python (NumPy, Pandas, SciPy) or similar tools.
• Experience with machine learning or statistical modeling applied to real-world datasets is an asset.
• Demonstrated technical expertise in active optical & electromagnetic components.
• Ability to take initiative in your tasks and ask meaningful questions.
• Team guidance skills.
• Strong, persistent troubleshooting and debugging skills.
• Good understanding of test plans, test execution, and bug reporting.
• Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
• Familiarity with optical lab practices is an asset.
• 2+ years towards a degree in Computer/Electrical Engineering, Engineering Physics or equivalent.
