jobs.title: MCP & Memory Intern
jobs.description:
Job Description:

DataRobot delivers AI that maximizes impact and minimizes business risk. Our platform and applications integrate into core business processes so teams can develop, deliver, and govern AI at scale. DataRobot empowers practitioners to deliver predictive and generative AI, and enables leaders to secure their AI assets. Organizations worldwide rely on DataRobot for AI that makes sense for their business — today and in the future. 

This effort is about making AI agents more useful in real work: giving them the right tools, the right context, and a memory that holds up across a conversation and across sessions. The focus is Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agent memory, how an agent discovers tools, calls them safely, keeps track of what it has learned, and stays helpful without someone watching every step. The goal is practical value for people using agents day to day, with clean implementations that others can build on.

Summary:

This is a hands-on internship for someone curious about AI agents who wants to learn by building. You do not need to already be an expert. What matters is that you like figuring things out, you move without waiting to be told every next step, and you care about unblocking the people around you. Most of the work sits on MCP and memory: connecting agents to tools, shaping how context is passed in, and designing how an agent remembers what is useful and forgets what is not. You will write code, try ideas, see what breaks, and ship improvements in a fast-moving environment. A good attitude and the willingness to learn matter more than a perfect resume.

Required Skills:

• Comfort writing and reading Python, and a willingness to get better at it quickly.
• Curiosity about how AI agents work: tools, prompts, context windows, and why an agent succeeds or fails on a real task.
• Interest in MCP — how servers expose tools, how clients call them, and how that contract stays simple and reliable.
• Interest in memory for agents: what to store, what to retrieve, and how that changes what the agent can do next.
• Ability to take a vague problem, try a small version, and show what you learned.
• Clear communication: you say when you are stuck, you share what you tried, and you help other people move faster.
• Good engineering habits you are willing to practice: readable code, small tests, and notes so the next person is not lost.
• You take feedback on board. When someone points out a better approach, a mistake, or a simpler path, use it and adjust.

Strong Plus:

• You have built or used an MCP server or client, even a small one.
• You have played with agent frameworks or tool calling.
• You have thought about memory, caching, or conversation state in any product, not only in AI.
• You enjoy fast environments and would rather try something today than wait for a perfect plan.
• You like helping teammates get unblocked, even when the task is not yours.

What You Can Expect To Work On:

• Building and improving MCP servers and clients: tool definitions, inputs and outputs, error handling, and examples other people can run.
• Experimenting with agent memory: what gets saved, how it is retrieved, and how that changes task quality.
• Wiring tools and memory into an agent loop and watching where it gets confused, slow, or wrong.
• Making small, clear changes that unblock teammates - docs, fixtures, smoke tests, and fixes that remove friction.
• Turning a rough idea into something that runs, then tightening it based on what you see.
• Pairing with people who know the system well, then owning the next slice yourself.

What You Should Expect:

• Work close to how agents actually get used, with MCP and memory at the center.
• A fast pace: short loops, quick feedback, and room to try things without a long approval chain.
• Trust to drive your own tasks once the goal is clear. You will not be micro-managed.
• A team that likes curiosity, a steady attitude, and people who make others faster.
• Room to learn in public: questions are welcome, and “I don’t know yet” is a fine starting point if you go find out.
• A role for someone who wants to grow into agentic systems by shipping, not by waiting until they feel fully ready.

Job Details:

Job Description: 
The Role and Impact
Are you interested in GPUs, computer hardware, and understanding how complex systems work? As a Graphics Hardware Validation Undergraduate Engineering Intern you will gain hands-on experience validating Intel's discrete graphics platforms and helping ensure their functionality, performance, quality, and product readiness.

You will work alongside experienced engineers to develop and execute validation tests, analyze results, investigate hardware and software issues, and support system-level debugging. You'll gain practical exposure to GPU and PC architecture, discrete graphics, laboratory equipment, Python automation, power and thermal validation, PCIe, operating systems, and system-level troubleshooting.

This is an opportunity to apply what you've learned through coursework, labs, research, personal projects, or prior internship experience to real-world engineering challenges.

Business group
The Data Center Group (DCG) drives Intel's innovative solutions to meet the complex demands of data-centric environments. Focused on developing high-performance platforms, DCG plays a vital role in advancing Intel's leadership in cloud computing, enterprise, and AI workloads. As part of this group, you will help ensure the quality and reliability of Intel's offerings, supporting our mission to enable businesses to harness the power of data.

What You’ll Do
Key responsibilities will include but not limited to:
• Execute platform and board validation tasks, including developing and implementing test plans to assess functionality and performance.
• Analyze test results to identify anomalies and assist in debugging functional and performance issues.
• Collaborate with hardware and software teams to ensure full platform readiness and high-quality deliverables.
• Support configuration testing and manufacturability assessments for data center platforms.
• Participate in benchmarking execution and validation of power and thermal characteristics.
• Contribute to hands-on projects while learning and applying knowledge relevant to Intel's business goals.
 
Behavioral traits that we are looking for:
 
• Curiosity and learning agility: Eager to learn new hardware, tools, and validation techniques.
• Problem-solving: Approaches technical issues logically and uses data to troubleshoot problems.
• Attention to detail: Carefully executes tests, analyzes results, and documents findings.
• Collaboration: Works effectively with teammates and cross-functional engineering partners.
• Communication: Clearly explains technical observations, results, and questions.
• Initiative: Takes ownership of assigned work and seeks guidance when needed.
 Intel invests in our people and offers a complete and competitive package of benefits employees and their families through every stage of life.

Build what's next in graphics technology. Job Description
About the role:

As a Simulation AI/ML Engineer intern, you’ll partner with senior engineers to deliver key components of the evaluation strategy for GM’s autonomous vehicle programs. In this role, you will scale the testing and evaluation of our self-driving stack by applying AI/ML techniques to software solutions. You will design, perform experiments, and deploy these solutions as production-ready code. The work you do will be directly applied to the iteration and validation of the self-driving stack. 

About the team:

The GM AV Simulation team builds world-class testing and analysis related products and technologies to enable GM to accelerate the development of autonomous vehicles as well as general vehicle software development. Our customers range from AV developers understanding the effects of their code on vehicle behavior, data engineers using our data pipelines to generate meaningful insights for various evaluation needs, to the release team tracking top-line performance metrics on releases. AV Simulation aims to deliver intuitive user experiences for robotics and AI engineers that accelerate GM towards a driverless future. 

What you’ll do:
• Leverage AI/ML techniques to scale testing, classify autonomy performance, and mine critical scenarios, integrating human-in-the-loop where appropriate.
• Collaborate with engineers to integrate ML models into simulation tests and evaluation pipelines.
• Ramp up quickly on the codebase and domain; deliver assigned tasks efficiently with few iterations.
• Develop, test, and deploy production-ready code across components of our simulation infrastructure.
• Define problem statements and implement optimal, tradeoff-aware solutions that cover edge cases.
• Collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders, contribute to design and code reviews, and ensure seamless integration through clear communication.

Required Qualifications:
• Currently pursuing a Bachelor's Degree in computer science, artificial intelligence, machine learning, robotics, engineering, or a related STEM field.
• Must have at least one additional quarter/semester of school remaining following the completion of the internship
• Solid understanding of modern machine learning techniques
• Demonstrated coursework, research, or projects in AI/ML.
• Strong programming skills in Python.
• Able to work full-time, 40 hours per week.

As a PhD AI/ML Engineering Intern within General Motors’ Autonomous Vehicles organization, you will advance reliable AI/ML capabilities by translating deep research into validated, production-oriented systems. Your work may support perception, prediction, planning, decision-making, embodied AI, simulation, sensor understanding, mapping, or large-scale model development. You will work with real-world driving and sensor data, modern machine learning methods, and autonomous vehicle evaluation environments. You will collaborate with researchers and engineers to design experiments, build and assess models, investigate failure cases, and integrate promising approaches into broader AV systems.

What you’ll do
• Research and prototype advanced machine learning methods for perception, prediction, planning, or decision-making.
• Design, train, evaluate, and improve models using large-scale multimodal driving and sensor data.
• Build data pipelines, experimentation workflows, and evaluation tools for rapid model iteration.
• Validate models through simulation, testing, performance analysis, and failure-case investigation.
• Optimize models and systems for scalability, latency, reliability, and deployment constraints.
• Collaborate with engineering and research partners to integrate prototypes into autonomous vehicle systems.
• Document findings, present technical insights, and contribute to publications or other research outputs.

Required qualifications
• Currently enrolled full-time in a PhD program in computer science, machine learning, artificial intelligence, robotics, engineering, or a related STEM field.
• Must have at least one additional quarter/semester of school remaining following the completion of the internship
• Demonstrated depth of AI/ML research through publications, research projects, advanced coursework, or equivalent technical work.
• Strong understanding of modern machine learning and deep learning methods.
• Proficiency in Python and hands-on experience with an ML framework such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or JAX.
• Experience designing experiments, analyzing results, and applying quantitative problem-solving methods.
• Strong programming, debugging, and software development fundamentals.
• Strong communication skills and the ability to collaborate across research and engineering disciplines.
• Availability to work full-time, 40 hours per week, during the internship period.

Preferred qualifications
• Candidates are not expected to meet every qualification listed below. Depending on the needs of a specific Autonomous Vehicles team, a combination of these skills and areas of knowledge may be relevant.
• Conduct research in autonomous vehicles, ADAS, robotics, computer vision, or embodied AI.
• Demonstrate knowledge of foundation models, transformers, generative and diffusion models, or vision-language architectures.
• Apply multimodal learning techniques to camera, lidar, radar, or other sensor data.
• Use self-supervised, imitation, reinforcement, or deep reinforcement learning methods.
• Train models on large-scale datasets using distributed, parallel, or high-performance computing environments.
• Develop ML systems, data pipelines, experimentation frameworks, or production-oriented model infrastructure.
• Validate models through simulation, closed-loop environments, or real-world driving scenarios.
• Apply expertise in trajectory prediction, behavior planning, motion planning, perception, mapping, or structured scene understanding.
• Program in C++ or other systems programming languages.
• Optimize models and systems using GPU programming, CUDA, accelerator frameworks, or performance profiling.
• Apply numerical optimization, statistical estimation, probabilistic modeling, and systems-level tradeoff analysis.
• Demonstrate a strong research record through first-authored publications, grants, fellowships, patents, or open-source contributions.

The compensation information is a good faith estimate only. It is based on what a successful applicant might be paid in accordance with applicable state laws. The compensation may not be representative for positions located outside of New York, Colorado, California, or Washington.

• GM Family First Vehicle Discount Program

• Intern events to network with company leaders and peers

jobs.description:
Associate Software Engineer - San Diego, CA

Job Description

Associate Software Engineer – San Diego, CA 

Company Overview: 

CoStar Group (NASDAQ: CSGP) is a leading global provider of commercial and residential real estate information, analytics, and online marketplaces. Included in the S&P 500 Index, CoStar Group is on a mission to digitize the world’s real estate, empowering all people to discover properties, insights and connections that improve their businesses and lives. 

We have been living and breathing the world of real estate information and online marketplaces for over 35 years, giving us the perspective to create truly unique and valuable offerings to our customers. We’ve continually refined, transformed, and perfected our approach to our business, creating a language that has become standard in our industry, for our customers, and even our competitors. We continue that effort today and are always working to improve and drive innovation. This is how we deliver for our customers, our employees, and investors. By equipping the brightest minds with the best resources available, we provide an invaluable edge in real estate. 

Learn more about CoStar.   

Role Description: 

We’re looking for an Associate Software Engineer with a passion for designing and building modern web applications. This role develops tools that power CoStar Group’s proprietary platform, supporting sales and research teams across our portfolio of brands - including Homes.com, CoStar.com, Apartments.com, and LoopNet.com. 

At CoStar Group, we invest in early-career talent by providing hands-on learning opportunities, meaningful responsibilities, and clear pathways for professional growth. You'll be empowered to contribute ideas, solve complex challenges, and develop both the technical and collaborative skills needed to thrive in a fast-paced, innovative environment. CoStar Group offers competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, performance-based career advancement, and the opportunity to help shape products that serve millions of users. 

This position is located in San Diego, CA and offers a schedule of Monday to Thursday in office and the option to work from home on Friday. 

What You’ll do: 

At CoStar Group, our engineering teams build innovative, scalable solutions while following industry best practices for software development. You'll collaborate with experienced engineers to write clean, maintainable code, develop automated tests, participate in code reviews, and contribute to cross-functional design and planning discussions. 

Working alongside talented teammates, you'll gain hands-on experience with modern technologies including but not limited to leading JavaScript programming language and frameworks such as React, Vue, and Angular, Typescript, backend development language .NET, .NETCore, SQL, NoSQL, Postgres, AWS, Kafka, Databricks, and emerging AI-powered development tools like GitHub Copilot and Claude Code. 

We're looking for curious, adaptable students who are eager to learn, embrace new technologies, and apply strong software engineering fundamentals to solve meaningful business challenges. This role provides the building blocks for a strong and rewarding technical career, offering mentorship, real-world experience, and continuous opportunities for professional growth. 

Basic Qualifications: 

• Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree from an accredited, not-for-profit university or college in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a comparable major. 

• Must have an expected graduation date of December 2026 - June 2027. 

• Minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA. 

• At least 2 months of previous relevant internship or co-op experience. 

• Experience applying software engineering fundamentals through coursework, projects, internships, or work experience. 

• Ability to discuss prior internship, project, or academic work, including the problem solved, technical approach, collaboration, and outcomes. 

Preferred Qualifications and Experiences: 

• Experience writing understandable, maintainable, and well-documented code. 

• Interest in learning new technologies and building high-quality software. 

• Demonstrated initiative and collaboration through academic, internship, extracurricular, or team-based experiences. 

• Familiarity with Agile development practices, the Software Development Lifecycle, APIs, web services, or application design concepts. 

• Exposure to programming languages, databases, cloud concepts, AI/machine learning, frameworks, or other technical tools through coursework, projects, internships, or personal learning. 

What’s in it for you?   

When you join CoStar Group, you’ll experience a collaborative and innovative culture working alongside the best and brightest to empower our people and customers to succeed. 

We offer you generous compensation and performance-based incentives. CoStar Group also invests in your professional and academic growth with internal training and tuition reimbursement. 

Our benefits package includes (but is not limited to): 

• Comprehensive healthcare coverage: Medical / Vision / Dental / Prescription Drug 

• Life, legal, and supplementary insurance 

• Virtual and in person mental health counseling services for individuals and family 

• Commuter and parking benefits 

• 401(K) retirement plan with matching contributions 

• Employee stock purchase plan 

• Paid time off 

• Tuition reimbursement 

• On-site fitness center and/or reimbursed fitness center membership costs (location dependent) 

• Access to CoStar Group’s Employee Resource Groups 

• Complimentary gourmet coffee, tea, hot chocolate, fresh fruit, and other healthy snacks 

The final salary or hourly rate offered for this role will fall within the range set forth below based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to, geographic location, skills, and competencies. 

Base Compensation: $100,000 - $105,000 annually 

We welcome all qualified candidates who are currently eligible to work full-time in the United States to apply. However, please note that CoStar Group is not able to provide visa sponsorship for this position. 

CoStar Group is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer; we maintain a drug-free workplace and perform pre-employment substance abuse testing

jobs.description:
Company
Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland

The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland is part of the nation’s central bank. We’ve provided many opportunities for professional growth during our history. 
 
For twenty-seven years in a row, we’ve been named “One of Northeast Ohio’s Best Places to Work” by North Coast 99. This prestigious award honors organizations with outstanding employment practices, including compensation, benefits, training, recruitment, retention, community services, and employee communications. 
 
Our People Make the Difference! The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland is seeking innovative thinkers with vision to build the framework that will carry the Bank into the future. 
 
Follow us on LinkedIn, Twitter, Instagram, and our YouTube channel – Cleveland Fed

To be considered for this role, candidates must be a U.S. citizen, permanent resident, or green card holder. 
 
Take your skills to the next level and gain valuable experience contributing to work within Research. 
 
Intern Duties: 
The Research department produces academically respected economic research, monitors and reports on regional and national economic trends, and helps to craft public communications on economic issues. The department also models complex economic systems, analyzes data, and evaluates economic information to support the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland’s monetary policy responsibilities.  
  
During their time at the Bank, research interns will develop their data analysis and programming skills, and work with the Bank’s economists and research analysts to conduct research in various areas of economics. 

Requirements for Research Internship: 
• Currently pursuing an undergraduate degree in Economics or a closely related field, such as Finance, Statistics, Mathematics, or Computer Science with a minimum GPA of 3.0. Should have at least one semester left to complete in school 
• Working knowledge of econometrics and/or statistics packages such as Stata, MATLAB, R, or Python.  
• Prior research experience in economics strongly preferred. 
• Excellent oral and written communication skills. 

Application Requirements: 
• Resume 
• Transcript  
• Cover Letter  

What We Offer: 
• Hands-On Experience: Gain practical experience and insights into the operations field through real-world projects and challenges. 
• Mentorship: Receive guidance and mentorship from experienced professionals who are committed to your development. 
• Networking Opportunities: Build connections within the industry and with fellow interns and employees. 
• Professional Development: Participate in workshops, training sessions, and seminars designed to enhance your skills and knowledge. 

Our interns will work onsite at our Cleveland, Ohio location. We’re looking for collaborative and innovative full-time students entering their sophomore year or beyond. Our student interns work 40 hours per week for the duration of a 10- to 12-week internship that starts as early as June and ends as late as September, depending on student schedules and business needs. The expected starting salary range for this position is between ​$20.50 and $26.00 hourly. Final salary and offer will be determined by the applicant’s background, experience, skills, internal equity, and market data.

To be considered for the position, please apply before October 31st, 2026. 

Physical Demands and General Working Conditions 
This is not necessarily an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, performance standards or requirements, efforts, skills or working conditions associated with the job. While this is intended to be an accurate reflection of the current job, the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland reserves the right to revise this or any job description at any time.  

Bank’s Ethics Rules and Drug Testing:  
As a condition of employment, Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland employees must comply with the Bank’s ethics rules which generally prohibit employees, their spouses/domestic partners, and minor children from owning or controlling, directly or indirectly, any debt or equity interest in a depository institution or an affiliate of a depository institution. A "depository institution" means a bank, a trust company, or any institution that accepts deposits, including a bank chartered under the laws of a foreign country. In addition, employees (and their spouses/domestic partners, and minor children) may not own shares of mutual funds, unit investment trusts or ETFs that have a policy, as stated in the prospectus, of concentrating in the financial services industry and that have underlying investments in banks or other depository institutions.  If you or your spouse/domestic partner or minor child own such securities and would not be willing or able to divest them if you accepted an offer of Bank employment, you should raise this issue with the recruiter for this posting. 

In addition, as a condition of employment, candidates must undergo a background check and will be tested for all controlled substances prohibited by federal law, to include marijuana, prior to hire and for certain safety sensitive positions during employment. 

Reasonable Accommodation Statement - The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland is committed to ensuring that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, perform essential job functions, and receive other benefits and privileges of employment. To request a reasonable accommodation for any part of the employment process, please send an email to clev.4d.benefits.specialist@clev.frb.org

jobs.title: Consumer Analytics & Insights Intern
jobs.description:
Job Location
BROOKLANDS GO
Job Description
Ready to help shape the success of globally renowned brands such as Gillette, Pampers, Head & Shoulders and Oral-B? Do you want to understand what consumers need, identify the trends shaping markets and turn data into recommendations that influence real business decisions? Want to work for a company consistently recognised as one of the UK’s leading graduate employers?

Then apply for our Consumer Analytics & Insights Summer Internship 2027 at P&G. This is a role for people who are curious about human behaviour and excited by the power of data. You will explore what consumers want and why, analyse market and retailer information, spot patterns and opportunities, and translate your findings into clear recommendations for our commercial teams.

You will work in multi-functional teams and use market research, consumer understanding and analytics to solve live business challenges. This could include identifying fast-growing consumer groups, improving the shopping experience, evaluating new media or retail trends, or using complex datasets to uncover growth opportunities. You will communicate your recommendations to internal stakeholders and also help shape the story we take externally to our retail partners.

What To Expect: 

During your 12-week summer internship, you will take ownership of live business projects. This could involve understanding consumers and markets, exploring data to identify opportunities, or turning insights into recommendations for P&G teams and retail partners. The exact focus will depend on the business need, giving you the opportunity to build a broad mix of analytical and communication skills with tailored coaching and support throughout.

This internship is available in our UK Head Office in Weybridge (an easy commute from Central London with regular trains from Waterloo & Clapham Junction and a free shuttle bus from the station to the office).

What You Will Gain: 
• Responsibilities and Real Work from Day 1: You will be given specific projects and responsibilities working on real and live business challenges, just like a true P&Ger. 
• Continuous training & coaching: You will work with passionate people and receive both formal training as well as day-to-day mentoring from your manager. 
• Competitive Compensation & Benefits: The monthly salary for this summer internship is £2,625. On top of this you’ll enjoy lots of benefits like the option to enrol in our pension, flexible working arrangements, and your very own ‘Flex4Me’ Fund which enables you to allocate a portion of your benefits package to the areas that matter most to you. 
• Full Time Role: Successful interns have the potential to secure a full-time position with P&G after graduation. As a 'build from within' company, our people start at entry level and progress through the organization. When we make a job offer, it’s with the expectation that you will grow into one of our future leaders, and to help you get there, you will work closely with skilled P&G veterans for mentoring and coaching at every step.

Job Qualifications

What We Look For:
• University students graduating in 2027 or 2028.
• We welcome students from Business, Psychology, Economics, Anthropology, Sociology, Data Analytics, Statistics, Mathematics or other related fields. Your degree matters less than your ability to combine curiosity and be confident working with data.
• A researcher mindset: you are curious about the true “why” behind behaviour, enjoy forming and testing hypotheses, and are motivated to uncover new insights rather than accept the obvious answer.
• Evidence of passion and achievements in academic and/or non-academic activities. Tell us what you’re proud of – be it playing a musical instrument or holding down a job alongside your studies. We want to get to know you during your application!
• Demonstrated leadership skills with strong observational and analytical capability.
• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
• Strong verbal and written English language skills.

Start Date: 

The summer internship is available from 5th July 2027 until 24th September 2027. We expect you to be available for the full duration.

Right to Work: 

For our internship roles, you will need to provide your own right to work in the UK for the full duration of your internship without requiring sponsorship from P&G. Note, this will require your right to work permission to be valid between 5th July 2027 until 24th September 2027 for a minimum of 37.5 hours per week. 

P&G is legally required to ensure all candidates have the right to work in the UK from Day 1 of their employment. All applicants will therefore be asked to provide evidence of their right to work at the conclusion of the recruitment process as a condition of employment. 

Application Deadline: 

1pm (GMT) October 30th, 2026. You must apply by the deadline. We encourage you to apply and complete our online assessments as soon as possible, as we may close early if positions are filled. 

Application Process: 

• Complete your Application (Deadline 1pm GMT 30th October 2026) 
• Complete our Online Assessments (Deadline 1pm GMT 9th November 2026) 
• Virtual Interviews (will run across October - December 2026) 
• Internship Offers Extended (End of December 2026) 

As part of our application process, your virtual interviews will be conducted by managers working in the business you have applied for who are committed to finding the next generation of talent here at P&G!

Secure a Role before 2027! In order to fairly assess all candidates, our internship offers will only be extended at the end of our recruitment process, once all candidates have been processed. Finalist candidates can therefore expect to have an outcome before the end of the year!

At P&G #weseeequal 

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. At P&G we strive to build a culture where everyone feels welcome, included, and able to bring their full selves to work. 

We champion social mobility and believe socio-economic status should not be a barrier to accessing job opportunities. That’s why in addition to this internship being paid, we offer provision of all the necessary technology and electronic equipment, access to a range of benefits, and financial support if you need to relocate for your internship - such as covering the cost of travel to your internship location. 

We ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process. Please click here if you require an accommodation during the application process. Please make sure to wait to hear back from us regarding your accommodation before proceeding with the online assessment, we thank you in advance for your patience.

Company Overview
At Motorola Solutions, we believe that everything starts with our people. We’re a global close-knit community, united by the relentless pursuit to help keep people safer everywhere. We build and connect technologies to help protect people, property and places. Our solutions foster the collaboration that’s critical for safer communities, safer schools, safer hospitals, safer businesses, and ultimately, safer nations. Connect with a career that matters, and help us build a safer future.

Department Overview
We’re looking for talented, hard working Computing Science graduates to join us at our Glasgow office and help us develop our cutting edge mobile application.

We offer full training and support, so new graduates are encouraged to apply. 

Our ‘Pronto’ team is the largest supplier of mobile police apps in the UK, providing software to half of the UK’s 45 police forces - used by around 70,000 police officers on a daily basis.

Based in the West End of Glasgow, we currently have around 100 employees. Our team started as Kelvin Connect in 2002, a spin-out company from the University of Glasgow. Now, as part of Motorola Solutions, we continue to expand with future opportunities in the UK and beyond.

We have a relaxed but hardworking environment where jeans and t-shirts are the norm and good ideas and debate are encouraged. You’ll work as part of an agile team, taking part in sprint planning sessions, daily scrums and sprint reviews and retrospectives.
Job Description
PLEASE NOTE - THIS ROLE IS TO START JANUARY 2027

Key responsibilities of Jr Software Developer:
You’ll be responsible for writing Java, XSLT and using our in-house tools to produce Android applications. You don’t need any previous experience other than a strong Computing Science or Software Engineering degree as you’ll be trained by experienced staff throughout the role and work alongside our highly skilled team.

While a large part of the Jr Software Developer role is development work, the role is designed as a graduate position where you’ll be exposed to the full life cycle of a project, including requirements capture, design, implementation and testing. After you have a few years of experience under your belt, there are opportunities to progress into Senior Developer, Business Analyst and Project Management roles depending on your preference and abilities. 

This is a hybrid role with time split between our Glasgow Office and your home.

Basic Requirements
As Jr Software Developer you will require:
• 3 years UK residency is required for security check

• A minimum of a 2:1 degree in BSc Computing Science, BSc Software Engineering, MSc Software Engineering, or similar.

• Some experience with Java, but more importantly, an excellent general understanding of programming concepts

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills

​
We believe that to develop great software, we need to clearly understand the requirements of our end users, so we encourage the team to get out and about and meet our customers. Once you’ve been here for a while, the role may involve occasional customer site visits, so you should be willing to undertake some travel as required (accompanied by a more experienced member of the team).

jobs.description:
AIG is reimagining the way we help customers manage risk. Join us as an Analyst in the Data Office department to play your part in that transformation with opportunities to learn and grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.
 
About Us
At AIG, helping organizations and people discover new potential is our purpose. As a global risk leader, we do this for our clients every day. Through our deep expertise in their industries and our innovative solutions that help them smartly manage risk, we enable their growth in ways they never thought possible.
 
But we also do the same thing for our colleagues, because we know our people are our greatest strength – the source of every insight, every idea and every innovation. When we're working as one team to do what's right for our colleagues and our communities, we can achieve excellence together. We encourage colleagues to give back to the causes they care most about, supporting these efforts through our Volunteer Time Off and Matching Grants Programs.
 
Make your mark in Data Engineering
Data Engineering plays a critical role in enabling data-driven decision-making across the organization by delivering scalable, reliable, and secure data solutions. This function partners closely with business and technology teams to ensure data is accessible, trustworthy, and positioned to drive innovation, analytics, and operational excellence.
 
How you will make an impact
When you join AIG, you will be part of a connected cohort community of early career talent participating in a program that equips you with learning experiences and skills needed to launch your career. From day one, you will develop your knowledge and understanding of AIG and the insurance industry and learn new skills through meaningful on-the-job experiences and instructor-led masterclasses. Through exposure to senior leaders, mentoring circles, networking and volunteering, you will build connections with colleagues across the organization. Collectively, these different experiences are designed to enable you to make an impact and build a rewarding and successful career. 
 
Data Engineering Rotation Overview
 
Data Engineering & Data Architecture: Leverage modern, cloud-based technologies to develop data pipelines that collect, manage, and transform raw data into usable information for business analysis, data science and other analytic use cases. Build modern software systems with Blue/Green Deployment, chaos testing, A/B testing, API and Agents to support the data needs of the customers with adherence to all code/data quality, security, and compliance standards. Familiarity with AWS environment including EMR, Glue, Step Functions; languages like python/pyspark, coding environments like Git and coding assistants like Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, etc. are desirable; but not mandatory.
 
Minimum Qualifications
Our Early Careers programs are designed for students and recent graduates who are beginning their professional careers, generally within one year of completing their degree.

• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree to be received no later than June 2027 (unofficial transcript required upon application) in a STEM major or with STEM coursework learned in associated majors. Examples of considered majors include, but are not limited to, Computer Science, Data Engineering, Data Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, Mathematics, Applied Mathematics, Statistics, Finance, Economics, Library Science, Geography, or Psychology.

• Analyst positions are in-person opportunities, requiring employees to work in the office at least four days per week.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively in a professional environment.
• Demonstrated analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills, with strong attention to detail.
• Ability to collaborate effectively, manage multiple priorities, and adapt in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment.
 
What you’ll need to succeed
AIG seeks candidates who have excelled in previous work experience, demonstrated outstanding academic and extracurricular achievement, possess strong analytical, quantitative and interpersonal skills, and are enthusiastic about learning more about the insurance industry. We also look for a diverse background of experience, culture and thought. Successful candidates typically have a global perspective and a team-oriented track record.
 
Application Deadline
Applications will be accepted through November 15, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and we encourage candidates to apply early. We reserve the right to close this posting prior to the application deadline based on application volume.

Salary for this role is between $86,200 and $103,500

At AIG, we value in-person collaboration as a vital part of our culture, which is why we ask our team members to be primarily in the office. This approach helps us work together effectively and create a supportive, connected environment for our team and clients alike.

Enjoy benefits that take care of what matters
At AIG, our people are our greatest asset. We know how important it is to protect and invest in what’s most important to you. That is why we created our Total Rewards Program, a comprehensive benefits package that extends beyond time spent at work to offer benefits focused on your health, wellbeing and financial security—as well as your professional development—to bring peace of mind to you and your family.

Reimagining insurance to make a bigger difference to the world
American International Group, Inc. (AIG) is a global leader in commercial and personal insurance solutions; we are one of the world’s most far-reaching property casualty networks. It is an exciting time to join us — across our operations, we are thinking in new and innovative ways to deliver ever-better solutions to our customers. At AIG, you can go further to support individuals, businesses, and communities, helping them to manage risk, respond to times of uncertainty and discover new potential. We invest in our largest asset, our people, through continuous learning and development, in a culture that celebrates everyone for who they are and what they want to become.

Welcome to a culture of inclusion

With global chapters, ERGs are a cornerstone for our culture of inclusion. Overview:
Serves as a member of the Management Development Program (MDP) and participates in ten weeks of Core Training and one year of On-the-Job training (OJT). Core Training responsibilities include participation in classroom training, observations of departmental presentations, interaction with senior management, peer networking, and working in teams on group project assignments. OJT responsibilities vary by department and are assigned by the department manager. The position may be responsible for additional projects assigned by the department manager or Leadership Development Manager.

Department Description:
The Wilmington Trust Institutional Services (IS) division is experiencing rapid business growth and has initiated a strategic digital transformation program. The goals of the program are to grow revenue through new and transformed digital-first trust and agency service products, to move from a product-centric to client-centric operating model, to move from market-specific to global solutions, and to dramatically lower the cost to serve.
Wilmington Trust is seeking a Forward Deployed Digital Product Analyst to join its Management Development Program and help accelerate digital transformation across core operations. This early-career role is designed for candidates interested in developing digital products, AI products, business transformation, or client-facing technology leaders.
This role is a hybrid between a junior product manager, business analyst, AI-enabled process analyst, and workflow designer. The role focuses on identifying operational problems, defining user needs, documenting requirements, testing solutions, and using agentic AI tools to rapidly analyze, prototype, and improve business workflows.
Ideal candidates are curious, analytical, hands-on, and comfortable working across business and technology teams. They should have exposure to digital product management concepts such as writing user stories or specifications, mapping process flows, creating simple UI designs or wireframes, testing software or workflows, or using AI tools to improve productivity and solution design.
 
Department Responsibilities:
• Help discover, design, test, and launch digital workflow solutions across Wilmington Trust Institutional Services.
• Sit down with business product owners, operations teams, technology partners, and senior product leaders to learn what is not working today and where automation could help.
• Turn what you hear into clear write-ups: user stories (short descriptions of what a user needs), acceptance criteria (the checklist that says when the work is done), process flows, and wireframes (simple screen sketches).
• Use agentic AI tools (AI that can carry out multi-step tasks for you) to analyze processes, draft documentation, generate test cases, and prototype workflows faster.
• Think through big, unclear problems in a structured way: break them into smaller pieces, get to the root cause, weigh the options, and recommend practical next steps.
• Join working sessions where the team maps how a process runs today versus how it should run, and shape early MVP ideas (a first, simple version of a solution).
• Build quick prototypes using enterprise tools, agentic AI tools, low-code or no-code platforms (build with little or no programming), and design collaboration tools.
• Partner with product owners and delivery teams to keep the backlog (the prioritized list of work) clear, current, and tied to business goals.
• Support QA, UAT (user acceptance testing, where real users confirm a solution works), and production checks by writing test scenarios, logging defects, and confirming fixes.
• Help define and track the numbers that show whether a solution is working, such as user adoption, cycle time, exception rates, and business impact.
• Work with technology partners to understand how systems connect and where data, system limits, or operational risks could get in the way.
• Learn and apply agile, lean, design thinking, process engineering, and product management practices on real transformation work.
• Keep up with new agentic AI capabilities, digital product tools, workflow automation practices, and responsible ways to use AI.
• Share what you find, including requirements, risks, test results, and recommendations, in language that business, product, and technology partners can act on.
• Understand and adhere to the Company’s risk and regulatory standards, policies and controls in accordance with the Company’s Risk Appetite. Identify risk-related issues needing escalation to management.
• Promote an environment that supports belonging and reflects the M&T Bank brand.
• Maintain M&T internal control standards, including timely implementation of internal and external audit points together with any issues raised by external regulators as applicable.
• Complete other related duties as assigned.
 
Department Experience Required:
This role is built for junior candidates and anyone interested in a Management Development Program, and recent college graduates are encouraged to apply. Experience from internships, co-ops, capstones, campus consulting projects, fintech labs, digital product projects, or AI projects is welcome, but none of it is required to apply.

• A real interest in digital product management, business transformation, financial technology, AI-enabled operations, or workflow automation.
• Some exposure, through coursework, an internship, a class project, or a job, to product work such as writing user stories, documenting requirements, mapping processes, or sketching wireframes.
• Some hands-on time with agentic AI or AI-assisted tools, such as Open Claw, Hermes, Claude Code, or Codex, used to help plan, build, test, analyze, or automate work.
• Comfort taking an open-ended problem apart, working through the information, spotting patterns, and explaining what you’ve found.
• Some exposure to testing software: QA, UAT (having real users confirm a solution works), writing test cases, logging defects, or checking data.
• The ability to explain things clearly in writing and out loud, from requirements and processes flows to feedback, test results, and recommendations.
• A collaborative style that works well with business, products, operations, design, and technology partners.
• Curiosity about how AI, automation, and digital products can improve business processes, client experiences, and day-to-day operations.
• Attention to detail, good organization, strong follow-through, and a willingness to learn quickly in a fast-paced environment.
 
Department Experience Preferred:
 
• An internship, co-op, project, or first job touching financial services, fintech, banking, wealth management, trust services, capital markets, payments, operations, risk, or compliance.
• Exposure to low-code or no-code workflow tools (platforms that let you build with little or no programming) such as Appian, Power Platform, ServiceNow, Salesforce, Pega, Airtable, Retool, or Mendix.
• Coursework or hands-on work in process mapping, workflow or service design, user journey mapping, or operational improvement.
• Any time spent building, configuring, testing, or documenting workflows and screens in Appian Designer - Appian Level 1 certification or similar exposure is a plus, not a must.
• A general sense of what Appian can do, such as process models, interfaces, records, reports, dashboards, case management, AI features, or RPA (software robots that handle repetitive tasks).
• Using AI tools to help with requirements, prototypes, test generation, documentation, code review, workflow design, or data analysis.
• Exposure to product management methods and agile delivery, including sprint planning, backlog management (keeping the work list prioritized), and retrospectives (short team check-ins on what to improve).
• Practice writing user stories and acceptance criteria that are detailed enough for a team to act on.

jobs.description:
Overview:
Participates in the Bank’s Technology Development Program (TDP), a 2-year program, designed to develop in-depth technical skills within a specific discipline, prior to completing a series of rotations within multiple Technology departments to gain a wider understanding of all technical disciplines and continue to grow within the specific discipline.

Scope of Responsibilities:
The Bank’s Technology Development Program is a rotational training program for Bachelor degreed individuals in a technical discipline. The Program is designed with flexibility to shape the jobholder’s career and expand their career objectives. The Program offers a combination of career planning, technical and competency-based training mentorship with challenging assessments designed to accelerate one’s career with the Bank.

Primary Responsibilities:

Associate Embedded Software Engineer

Job Description

Associate Embedded Software Engineer – Sunnyvale, CA
 
Company Overview: 
CoStar Group (NASDAQ: CSGP) is a leading global provider of commercial and residential real estate information, analytics, and online marketplaces. Included in the S&P 500 Index, CoStar Group is on a mission to digitize the world’s real estate, empowering all people to discover properties, insights and connections that improve their businesses and lives. 
 
We have been living and breathing the world of real estate information and online marketplaces for over 35 years, giving us the perspective to create truly unique and valuable offerings to our customers. We’ve continually refined, transformed, and perfected our approach to our business, creating a language that has become standard in our industry, for our customers, and even our competitors. We continue that effort today and are always working to improve and drive innovation. This is how we deliver for our customers, our employees, and investors. By equipping the brightest minds with the best resources available, we provide an invaluable edge in real estate. 
 
Learn more about CoStar. 
 
Role Description: 
We’re looking for an Associate Software Engineer with a passion for designing and building modern web applications. This role develops tools that power CoStar Group’s proprietary platform, supporting sales and research teams across our portfolio of brands - including Homes.com, CoStar.com, Apartments.com, and LoopNet.com. 
 
At CoStar Group, we invest in early-career talent by providing hands-on learning opportunities, meaningful responsibilities, and clear pathways for professional growth. You'll be empowered to contribute ideas, solve complex challenges, and develop both the technical and collaborative skills needed to thrive in a fast-paced, innovative environment. CoStar Group offers competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, performance-based career advancement, and the opportunity to help shape products that serve millions of users. 
 
This position is located in Sunnyvale, CA.
 
What You’ll do: 
At CoStar Group, our engineering teams build innovative, scalable solutions while following industry best practices. 
• Work with real sensor data (imaging, depth/LiDAR, or test-bench measurements) to build models, tools, or analysis pipelines that help the team make faster, better-informed engineering decisions 
• Help develop or improve methods for analyzing optical, calibration, or reliability test data 
• Prototype approaches to problems like anomaly detection, signal/data processing, calibration modeling, or automated data quality checks 
• Collaborate with hardware, test, and software engineers to understand the problem before jumping to a solution 
• Document your approach and present findings to the team 
 
We're looking for curious, adaptable students who are eager to learn, embrace new technologies, and apply strong software engineering fundamentals to solve meaningful business challenges. This role provides the building blocks for a strong and rewarding technical career, offering mentorship, real-world experience, and continuous opportunities for professional growth. 

Basic Qualifications: 
• Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree or higher from an accredited, not-for-profit, in-person university or college in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Data Science, Statistics, Robotics, or a comparable major. 
• Must have an expected graduation date of December 2026 - June 2027. 
• Minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA. 
• At least 2 months of previous relevant internship or co-op experience.
• Proficiency in at least one programming language commonly used for ML/data work (e.g., Python, C++, and/or MATLAB)
• Experience applying software engineering fundamentals through coursework, projects, internships, or work experience. 
• Ability to discuss prior internship, project, or academic work, including the problem solved, technical approach, collaboration, and outcomes. 
• Comfortable working with real-world, imperfect data.
 
Preferred Qualifications and Experiences: 
• Exposure to any of the following (no specific combination required): PyTorch, TensorFlow, OpenCV, signal processing, computer vision, sensor fusion, or robotics 
• Experience with hardware, embedded systems, or physical test data (academic, personal projects, or professional) 
• Personal, academic, or capstone projects applying ML to a real dataset or physical system 
• Comfort moving between exploratory analysis and more rigorous engineering documentation 
• Curiosity about how hardware and ML intersect 
• Experience writing understandable, maintainable, and well-documented code. 
• Interest in learning new technologies and building high-quality software. 
• Demonstrated initiative and collaboration through academic, internship, extracurricular, or team-based experiences. 
• Familiarity with Agile development practices, the Software Development Lifecycle, APIs, web services, or application design concepts. 
• Exposure to programming languages, databases, cloud concepts, AI/machine learning, frameworks, or other technical tools through coursework, projects, internships, or personal learning. 
 
What’s in it for you? 
When you join CoStar Group, you’ll experience a collaborative and innovative culture working alongside the best and brightest to empower our people and customers to succeed. 
We offer you generous compensation and performance-based incentives. CoStar Group also invests in your professional and academic growth with internal training and tuition reimbursement. 
 
Our benefits package includes (but is not limited to): 
• Comprehensive healthcare coverage: Medical / Vision / Dental / Prescription Drug 
• Life, legal, and supplementary insurance 
• Virtual and in person mental health counseling services for individuals and family 
• Commuter and parking benefits 
• 401(K) retirement plan with matching contributions 
• Employee stock purchase plan 
• Paid time off 
• Tuition reimbursement 
• On-site fitness center and/or reimbursed fitness center membership costs (location dependent) 
• Access to CoStar Group’s Employee Resource Groups 
• Complimentary gourmet coffee, tea, hot chocolate, fresh fruit, and other healthy snacks 
 
The final salary or hourly rate offered for this role will fall within the range set forth below based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to, geographic location, skills, and competencies. 
 
Base Compensation: $100,000 - $120,000 annually 
 
We welcome all qualified candidates who are currently eligible to work full-time in the United States to apply. However, please note that CoStar Group is not able to provide visa sponsorship for this position. 

CoStar Group is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer; we maintain a drug-free workplace and perform pre-employment substance abuse testing

jobs.title: Test Engineer 1
jobs.description:
Torch Technologies
Thank you for your interest in employment with Torch Technologies. We are a 100% employee-owned, Certified Great Place To Work and named Best Places to Work in Huntsville/Madison County, headquartered in Huntsville, AL. Our team provides superior research, development, and engineering services to the Federal Government and Department of War. As one of the nation’s top 100 defense companies, the services we provide directly support the men and women who serve our country. Our corporate mission sums up the pride our employee-owners take in the work we do: “Lighting the Pathway of Freedom”. And, as a Certified Evergreen ESOP, we have made the commitment to grow and sustain our company for the next 100 years! Come grow with us!

Torch Technologies is seeking an Entry Level Test Analyst to join our team and provide in-depth system performance and interoperability analysis supporting Missile Defense System (MDS) flight testing, ground testing, and simulation-based test events. This position supports the Missile Defense Agency (MDA) Test Analysis and Reporting activity across all phases of system-level test execution, including pre-mission predictive analysis, on-site quick-look assessments, and post-mission detailed analysis.

As an Entry Level Test Analyst, your duties will include the following, but are not limited to:

• Conduct system-level performance and interoperability analyses for flight test, ground test, and simulation-based Missile Defense System (MDS) events.
• Support pre-mission predictive analysis activities to assess expected system performance and mission outcomes.
• Perform on-site quick-look analysis during test execution to provide timely insights and preliminary results.
• Conduct post-mission detailed analysis using multiple data sources to evaluate system performance and interoperability.
• Utilize existing and off-the-shelf tools, including data processing and visualization software, to analyze MDS test data.
• Develop data visualizations and reports using tools such as Tableau, SQL, and Python to support analysis and decision-making.
• Prepare test analysis documentation, test readiness briefs, quick-look reports, and detailed post-test analysis products.
• Collaborate with engineers, analysts, government stakeholders, and test teams to support integrated test planning and execution activities.
• Support reporting and briefing activities for senior leadership, ensuring clarity and accuracy of technical findings.
• Participate in a multi-disciplinary team environment supporting mission-critical test and evaluation efforts.

Qualifications

• U.S. Citizenship.
• Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering, Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, or another technical discipline. Accepting applications for candidates with projected graduation on December 2026
• Active Secret security clearance.
• Knowledge of or experience with Tableau workbook development.
• Familiarity with SQL and Python for data analysis and visualization.
• Strong curiosity, self-initiative, leadership potential, and customer interface skills.
• Ability to clearly communicate ideas and concepts both verbally and in writing.
• Ability to work effectively in a team environment and manage multiple tasks simultaneously.
• Interest in systems analysis, test and evaluation, and data-driven performance assessment.

Preferred Qualifications

• Exposure to DoW test and evaluation environments.
• Experience supporting data analysis, systems engineering, or simulation-based testing.
• Familiarity with missile defense or aerospace systems.

Schedule: M-F; 8-5
Work Location: Onsite, Redstone Arsenal
Travel: Some travel may be required
Relocation Assistance Available: No
Position Contingent Upon Award of Contract: No

Are you ready to explore the world of aerospace and defense? Do you want to learn from and collaborate with some of the greatest minds in the industry? At RTX, our internships, co-ops and full-time careers provide an exceptional foundation to work on complex problems, advance your skills and create a safer, more connected world. Discover opportunities to make a difference at RTX.

What You Will Do 
Join the Test Solutions Engineering team within the Hardware Discipline Center at Raytheon, where we architect and build sophisticated software applications and automated test environments for mission-critical defense systems. In this role, you will develop cutting-edge software solutions that interface directly with state-of-the-art engineering hardware, supporting products across the entire lifecycle—from early lab demonstrations and design verification to high-rate production testing and long-term sustainment. Working alongside a collaborative, multi-disciplinary engineering team, you will design robust tools that ensure our nation's defense technologies perform flawlessly. 

Key Responsibilities
• Design, code, and integrate object-oriented software applications and test software targeting Windows operating platforms. 
• Develop and derive system-level software requirements, operational specifications, and architectural designs. 
• Troubleshoot, debug, and optimize software applications to ensure rigorous test accuracy, repeatability, and reliability. 
• Collaborate closely with systems, electrical, and mechanical engineers to integrate software test tools with specialized hardware instrumentation. 
• Participate actively in formal design reviews, code peer reviews, and technical defect resolution. 
• Work within structured engineering frameworks applying both Agile and Waterfall development lifecycles. 

Qualifications You Must Have 
• Bachelor’s degree in Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics (STEM) discipline. Degree must be obtained by start date. 
• Experience developing, testing, or integrating software applications using one or more programming languages, such as C, C++, C#, Python, or Visual Basic (VB/VBA/.NET). 
• Experience developing, building, and debugging software applications targeting Windows operating systems using the Microsoft Visual Studio integrated development environment (IDE). 
• Experience may be obtained through on-the-job experience, research, coursework, or projects. 

Qualifications We Prefer 
• Demonstrated foundation in software development principles and Object-Oriented Design (OOD/OOP), including encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, and modular class structure. 
• Experience or coursework utilizing C# or modern C++ in an engineering or laboratory test setting. 
• Familiarity with hardware/software interfacing, test automation frameworks, or instrumentation control (e.g., via GPIB, Ethernet, or serial interfaces). 
• Hands-on exposure to version control tools (such as Git) and Agile software development practices. 
• Strong diagnostic and analytical problem-solving skills applied to complex software/hardware integration issues. 
 
What We Offer  
• Our values drive our actions, behaviors, and performance with a vision for a safer, more connected world. At RTX we value: Trust, Respect, Accountability, Collaboration, and Innovation.  
• Relocation Eligibility 

Learn More & Apply Now!

• Onsite: Employees who are working in Onsite roles will work 100% onsite. This includes all production and maintenance employees, as they are essential to the development of our products 
• Please upload a copy of your most recent transcripts with your resume when applying to this requisition. Include your cumulative GPA and projected graduation date on your resume. 
• This position requires a security clearance. DCSA Consolidated Adjudication Services (DCSA CAS), an agency of the Department of Defense, handles and adjudicates the security clearance process. jobs.title: Remote Monitoring Analyst
jobs.description:
Sandvik Mining is looking for a Remote Monitoring Analyst, White Pine, TN
 
Sandvik has a strong platform based on our world-class R&D capabilities, and premium, high-tech products. We are at the forefront of automation, digitalization and electrification, and sustainability is an integral part of how we do business. We seek bright, curious, and forward-thinking multi-cultural team members who are motivated by serving customers and employees, in future proofing business and thrive in an inclusive learning culture. We offer competitive wages and benefits, strong support for learning and professional development, and opportunities to grow a successful, rewarding career in a diverse, collaborative, and globally connected organization that values innovation, fairness, and long‑term impact.
 
Business area Mining is a global leading supplier of equipment and tools, parts, service, digital solutions and sustainability-driving technologies for the mining and construction industries. Applications include rock drilling, rock cutting, loading and hauling, tunneling and quarrying.
 
The Remote Monitoring Analyst is responsible for monitoring equipment health and performance through Sandvik’s digital solutions, identifying potential issues and improvement opportunities, and delivering timely recommendations to customers. The role supports proactive maintenance, maximizes equipment availability, and creates customer value through data-driven analysis, reporting, and technical support.
 
The analyst serves as a key customer contact, providing insights on equipment condition, managing critical alerts, conducting operational performance reviews, and supporting customer adoption of digital services platforms. Working closely with Remote Monitoring Specialists and internal stakeholders, the role contributes to continuous improvement initiatives, root cause investigations, and the delivery of a high-quality Remote Monitoring Service.
 
Key Focus Areas:
 
Equipment health monitoring and analysis.
Proactive maintenance recommendations.
Customer reporting and engagement.
Critical alarm management.
Digital services support and training.
Data analysis and continuous improvement.
Service delivery and customer value creation.
 
This role Remote Monitoring Analyst will be a hybrid role requiring 3 days in office in White Pine, TN.
 
Key Responsibilities:
 
Equipment Monitoring and Analysis
• Monitor equipment condition, performance, and utilization using Digital services tools.
• Analyze machine data to identify developing failures, operational inefficiencies, and improvement opportunities.
• Prioritize and investigate abnormal events, alarms, and performance trends.
Recommendations and Case Management
• Develop and communicate actionable maintenance and operational recommendations.
• Track recommendations through closure and document outcomes.
• Support investigations related to equipment failures, recurring events, and critical alarms.
Customer Relationship Management
• Serve as the primary contact for assigned Remote Monitoring Service customers.
• Conduct regular service reviews and communicate monitoring findings and opportunities.
• Support customers in understanding equipment performance and data-driven recommendations.
Reporting and Documentation
• Prepare monitoring reports, performance summaries, and technical documentation.
• Maintain accurate records of recommendations, investigations, and customer interactions.
• Ensure data quality and consistency across monitoring systems.
Digital Services Support
• Support onboarding and training activities for Sandvik digital solutions.
• Promote customer adoption and utilization of monitoring platforms and reporting tools.
• Assist in resolving customer questions regarding digital services and escalate issues when required.
Continuous Improvement
• Contribute to the improvement of monitoring processes, reporting standards, and alarm effectiveness.
• Share operational insights and recurring trends with internal stakeholders.
• Support validation and implementation of new monitoring methodologies and digital capabilities.
 
Minimum Qualifications:
• High School diploma, or GED
• Technical background with full equipment systems (mining equipment for example)
• Self Motivated Individual
 
Preferred Qualifications:
• University degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrica Engineering or Technical Certification in equipment maintenance
• Technical experience with engines, transmission, hydraulics, brakes
 
Location: White Pine, TN
 
Travel Requirements / shift / hours: Regular office hours
 
Compensation Range: $75,000 to $85,000
 
Work authorization
Must have the legal right to work in the United States on an indefinite basis without employer sponsorship.

jobs.description:
Dandy is transforming the massive and antiquated dental industry—an industry worth over $400B. Backed by some of the world’s leading venture capital firms, we’re on an ambitious mission to simplify and modernize every function of the dental practice through technology. As we expand our reach globally, Dandy is building the operating system for dental offices around the world—empowering clinicians and their teams with technology, innovation, and world-class support to achieve more for their practices, their people, and their patients.

We’ve built the largest ML and CAD engineering teams in dentistry, drawing exceptional talent from leading organizations such as Google DeepMind, Amazon, and Waymo. Our full-stack engineering teams tackle complex challenges across platform architecture, supply chain optimization, and SaaS product development. Research is core to our culture, and our team includes authors of award-winning work, including ICML Best Paper. We are looking for motivated PhD Research Interns to join our team. We are looking for motivated interns to join us in exploring how bleeding edge machine learning can reshape the future of digital dentistry and advance the state-of-the-art for generative AI.

What You’ll Do

 - Work with large, complex datasets (3D scans, sensor data, and beyond) to build and evaluate ML models.

 - Explore and implement state-of-the-art machine learning methods, including generative modeling, deep learning, and applied optimization.

 - Tackle frontier problems in 3D dental prosthetic design by consuming and refining the outputs of generative AI models and perception layers.

 - Collaborate with researchers and engineers to improve existing ML pipelines and identify opportunities for innovation.

 - Contribute to experiments, prototypes, and production-ready solutions in real-world applications.

 - Learn best practices in MLOps, model evaluation, and applied research.

What We’re Looking For

 - Current PhD student in Computer Science, Electrical/Computer Engineering, Applied Math, Physics, Mechanical Engineering, or related field.

 - Strong programming skills in Python and familiarity with PyTorch or TensorFlow.

 - Coursework or research experience in machine learning, deep learning, or applied AI.
