Claude Corps
jobs.description:
About Claude Corps

Claude Corps — a partnership between CodePath and Anthropic — places early-career fellows inside nonprofits, government agencies, and public-interest organizations for a year to put AI to work on problems that matter. Fellows embed full-time at a host organization — building real solutions with Claude, teaching the people around them to do the same, and leaving behind something that keeps running after they're gone.

We are currently searching for fellows to join our third cohort which will start August 2027. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, with a deadline of January 31, 2027 for consideration.

About the Role

Over a year, embedded at a single organization, you'll do whatever moves the needle for your host — and that will look different month to month. We're looking for utility players: people who can build, teach, scope, and translate — and who don't treat any of that work as beneath them. The hard part is doing excellent work inside an organization that has stakeholders who have difficult constraints and less experience working with Claude.

For more information, please check out our FAQ for interested fellows

Responsibilities

Discover and scope. Spend real time understanding what your host organization actually needs. Pull usage data, talk to the people doing the work, and define projects in sprints with clear outcomes.

Build with Claude. Ship working solutions — agents, automations, internal tools, evaluation harnesses, integrations — that make a process faster, cheaper, or possible for the first time. Some of this will be ambitious; some will be as simple as building a dashboard.

Enable the organization. Run training for mixed technical and non-technical audiences. Turn three or four colleagues into the people others go to with AI questions. Your job isn't done when the tool works — it's done when someone else can own it.

Hand off well. Sit with the person who'll own your work after you leave. Watch them break it. Write the runbook. Make sure it survives you.

Exercise judgment. Catch your own wrong answers. Tell a stakeholder "we shouldn't build that" when it's true. Cut the part of the demo that isn't landing.

Prerequisites

To apply, you need all three of the following:

• Completion of AI Fluency and Claude 101. Proof of completion must be submitted with your application.

• You have built something. A website, app, or script others used; an automation, bot, or workflow that saved someone time; a dashboard or tracker; a project built with Claude or another AI model; a training or how-to guide with a technical component; or something else you built end-to-end. It does not need to be big, polished, or from a job.

• Demonstrated experience in community, nonprofit, or public-interest work. This could be working, interning, or volunteering at a nonprofit, public sector, or community-serving organization; completing a service program (AmeriCorps, City Year, Peace Corps, Teach For America, etc.); community organizing, mutual aid, or advocacy work; or founding or leading a student or community service organization. 

Who Should Apply

Claude Corps is a launchpad for people at the very start of their careers. It's a fit if you're:

• finishing or have just finished a degree or trade program and are looking for your first full-time role

• transitioning out of military service into your first civilian career

• in your first full-time job and looking to move into mission-driven work

This fellowship is designed as a first step into professional work, so it's best suited to people who don't yet have several years of experience behind them. Not sure which side you're on? Apply anyway.

You May Be a Good Fit If You

We care about what you've done and how you think, not your degree. You may be a good fit if you:

• Can talk honestly about something you built and shipped — what you scoped, what worked, and what you'd do differently. Doing it on a small team where you wore several hats is a plus.

• Can say why social-impact work pulls you, and what you learned from the time you've spent in or around nonprofits, public service, education, public health, workforce, civic tech, or community organizations.

• Can explain something technical to a non-technical room and read whether it's landing — whether that's teaching, mentoring, or running a workshop.

• Take initiative without someone tracking you, and stay coachable while doing it.

• Are energized — not deflated — by ambiguity, resource constraints, and problems that turn out to be different than advertised.

• Have hands-on time with agent frameworks, evals, or production LLM deployments — not required, but it helps.

• Are 18 or older, authorized to work in the United States (we are not able to sponsor visas for this program), and open to relocating within the US to work in person at a host organization.

What You'll Get

• A full-time salary of $85,000 and benefits for the fellowship year, plus Claude API and tooling access

• Relocation support for Fellows placed more than 100 miles from their current residence

• An onboarding bootcamp with Anthropic before you start at your host

• Dedicated support, regular cohort sessions with other Fellows, and direct access to Anthropic engineers through office hours

• A portfolio entry that's still running six months after you leave, and incredible references to go with it

Application & Interview Process

A short application with a couple of written questions, including what you've built and your community or nonprofit experience → a practical take-home assessment → a first round interview → a final-round interview.

Claude Corps is a partnership between CodePath and Anthropic. CodePath is the employer of record for this fellowship.

jobs.title: Junior Machine Learning Engineer - ML - Developer
jobs.description:
Machines learned to understand language. We’re teaching them to understand matter.
Forty percent of global manufacturing happens through physical and chemical processes inside pipes, tanks, and reactors. Despite decades of industrial automation, much of what happens inside them remains remarkably invisible. Manufacturing is the most ubiquitous and foundational sector in global economy, yet the way factories are fundamentally run have used the same control philosophies, manual operations, and legacy software for the past 60 years.
Laminar deploys state-of-the-art patented sensors and edge hardware directly into live production environments, generating data that didn’t previously exist to build foundation models deployed in factory floors that understand chemistry, composition, quality, and material state in real time. We use that understanding to run autonomy and rethink how things are made.
The last generation of industrial automation taught machines to execute instructions reliably. The next will teach them to understand the processes they control and run autonomously, adaptively, and agentically: higher quality, safety, more efficiently, sustainably, and productively. 
That future is already taking shape. Today, Laminar works with 7 of the world’s 10 largest food and beverage manufacturers and operates across hundreds of factories globally across six continents. Our systems have materially reduced waste, cut manufacturing downtime, saved water, chemicals, energy, and helped prevent safety and quality failures. Our technology has gained international recognition, from being selected as a 2026 World Economic Forum Technology Pioneer, Gold 2026 Edison Award, Unilever Startup of the Year, to Innovator Awards by both Coca-Cola and AB InBev, and more.
We are backed by tier-one investors in physical AI to make intelligent, self-improving production the new standard for industry.
Join us to build what makes matter intelligible, and the intelligible controllable.

The Role
As our company grows and scales, we are excited for a ML Developer to join the team! We are looking for ambitious, hard-working recent graduates who want to be at the forefront of bringing AI to fluid & process manufacturing. As a ML Developer, you will own the development and refinement of Laminar’s machine learning models – the heart of our process optimization technology. Your work will affect all of Laminar’s key process optimization models across domains including (but not limited to): CIP (clean-in-place), product changeovers, material identification, and emerging use-cases.

You’ll work closely with ML/Data Scientists to bring cutting-edge models all the way from prototype to production. This entails scaling up model training methodologies, crafting experiments, and running ablation studies across a wide and diverse range of domains, all with the goals of increasing model accuracy and reliability. Your work will be instrumental to hyper-scaling Laminar’s solutions and unlocking key markets through enabling new use-cases.
What You Will Do
• Build machine learning models that usher in the next generation of data-driven, fluid-based industrial processes powered by Laminar's proprietary spectral sensors and software platform

• Design and run experiments to evaluate and select machine learning models that are generalizable, accurate, and robust to day-to-day process variability

• Work with spectral and multi-modal sensor data, building preprocessing and feature extraction pipelines that can derive insights from noisy, real-world sensors

• Support model reliability by developing monitoring (and correction systems, when applicable) for model drift, sensor drift, and process anomalies

• Develop performant ML infrastructure and tooling in collaboration with ML/Data Scientists and software team members

• Work across problem domains including chemometrics, hybrid modeling, and self-supervised learning. Modeling tasks include distribution modeling, drift and anomaly detections, similarity analyses, and continuous calibration
About You
• Proficient in at least one Python ML framework (PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow)

• Fluent with Python packages for numeric computing and data workflows (e.g. NumPy, Polars, Pandas, scikit-learn)

• An engineer who favors clean, testable code and has a proven track record of delivering high-quality work on a timeline

• An executor who thrives with direction and can independently complete technical project objectives

• Someone detail-oriented who has a natural curiosity about data. You are enthusiastic to test out hypotheses, understand in detail how our models work, and run physical experiments to improve our modeling capabilities.

Preferred:

• Chemical engineering, process engineering, or manufacturing domain knowledge (highly valued)

• Experience with cloud environments (AWS, GCP) and/or Databricks

• Familiarity with spectral data, time-series modeling, or sensor-driven ML

• Familiarity with Bayesian modeling and probabilistic reasoning

• Experience building real products (ideally utilizing machine learning) and practicing user-centric design
Benefits
• Direct impact on product and culture.

• Comprehensive benefits package including Medical, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, Disability, Transportation benefit, Health and Wellness benefit, and more.

• 401k plan with employer matching

• Equity

• Competitive salary and bonus opportunities.

• Dynamic and inclusive work environment.

• Opportunities for growth and professional development.

• Access to Greentown Labs' extensive network of cleantech startups.

• Transportation benefit for your commute

• A team that celebrates together from rooftop lunches, ping pong matches, Lunch & Learns, and regular team events
Learn How We Think
• Learn about our startup journey: Our Journey

• How we're combating climate change: AI-Powered Climate Tech

• A customer story: Unilever uses Laminar precision automation to cut time & water usage
There are many easier places to work on AI. Laminar is for people who want the hardest version of their discipline. Models here must survive contact with physics. Hardware must survive years of continuous industrial operation. Software must integrate with machinery built decades ago. Everything we build ultimately has to work on a factory floor.
 
We believe exceptional people should be given exceptional amounts of ownership. At Laminar, you will have the context to form your own view, the permission to challenge ours, and the resources to pursue the right answers, whatever technical or organizational boundaries stand in the way. There are few layers between identifying something important and changing it.
 
We’re fortunate to work with a small polymathic team of hardware and software engineers, chemists, AI researchers, factory operators, and go-to-market wizards who are unusually capable, curious, rigorous, ambitious, and low-ego. If that sounds like you, we’d love to meet you.
 

Our Interview Process
1. Phone screen with Laminar HR/Recruiter (15-20 minutes)
2. Intro call with Hiring Manager (30 minutes)
3. On-site interview, overview of tech, and interview/presentation with the Hiring Manager and a few team members. Depending on the role, a skills exercise that should take no longer than an hour to prep, would be sent ahead of time. We record your skills exercise to share with any team members who could not join the interview and/or with Founder's ahead of their Founder's Interview. If you are not local, we can conduct this virtually. 
4. Finalists for Full-Time positions will have a Founder’s Interview in-person
 
Final steps:
Two professional references are requested, ideally one from your current organization and one who served as your Manager
If an Offer Letter is extended, a Background check is conducted

jobs.title: Electrical Engineering Internship - Summer 2027
jobs.description:
There was a time when all of America believed that the future of the physical world could be radically different. The engineers of the mid-1900s put a man on the moon in eight years, designed and built planes and submarines from scratch in under three, and conceived of building things we wouldn’t even be able to dream up today.

Today, the last of the engineers who imagined and built these systems are retiring. As they go, we lose not only the engineering knowledge gained from their decades of imagination and trial-and-error, but also the spirit that made that imagination possible.

Amca is working day-in and day-out to restore America’s ability to engineer anything that our critical systems depend on, and reinvigorate the cycle of creation that allows imagination to shape physical reality. We rapidly develop and manufacture new critical components and subsystems required to build and sustain the planes, military vehicles, and core infrastructure America needs. By restoring the capability of our antiquated supply chains, we increase the country’s capacity to imagine and realize new systems, and make a physical world that looks very different from today.

Overview

The Electrical Design Engineering Intern works alongside our electrical team to take aerospace hardware from concept toward flight qualification. You will own a scoped electrical design project for the summer, with a dedicated mentor and direct access to the build and test engineers who will bring your work to life.

This is not a shadowing program. Interns at Amca design, build, and debug real hardware. You should expect your schematics and boards to be reviewed with the same rigor as a full-time engineer's, and to have something on the bench before you leave.

Responsibilities

• Design electronics from concept to functional prototype, including hardware selection, PCB design, and system-level integration

• Contribute to the design and prototyping of new electrical hardware

• Support electrical design for flight hardware, including schematic capture, electrical analysis, component selection, and PCBA layout

• Build up early hardware, then iterate quickly based on results

• Run bench testing and basic functional and development tests on the hardware you build

• Debug failures down to root cause and carry the fix back into the design

• Troubleshoot issues that span the system, using lab equipment such as oscilloscopes and digital multimeters

• Select components with attention to de-rating, tolerance, and availability, and defend those choices in design review

• Work closely with other electrical, mechanical, software,, and test engineers to deliver fully functional products

• Work with test engineering to help define and execute functional and environmental and EMI test plans

• Incorporate manufacturability and testability feedback from build engineers into your systems

• Help evaluate existing Amca designs for opportunities to improve reliability and reduce cost

• Work in a fast-paced environment supporting new developments, active deployments, and customer-operated hardware

• Concurrently manage involvement in multiple projects at various stages

• Present your project and results to the engineering team at the end of the internship

Basic Qualifications

• Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD program in electrical engineering, computer engineering, engineering physics, or a related field

• Returning to school in Fall 2027, or graduating in Spring 2027 and interested in a full-time role. Must be returning to school at the end of the internship to continue academic studies for at least one quarter or semester

• Ability to commit to a full-time, in-person 10-week internship in one of our offices in Summer 2027

• Completed coursework in circuits, electronics, or signals, and a working understanding of first principles across power, filtering, and logic

• Hands-on electrical design experience through coursework, a student project team, personal projects, or a prior internship

• Familiarity with test equipment such as oscilloscopes, multimeters, logic analyzers, debuggers, and current probes, and test automation

Preferred Skills and Experience

• Experience with Altium Designer or equivalent electronic design automation tools

• Experience with circuit simulation, component selection, and de-rating

• Experience on a student project team building electronics for physical hardware, such as rocketry, Formula SAE, CubeSat, or robotics

• Familiarity with DO-160, MIL-STD-810 or other qualification and certification frameworks

• Exceptionally curious and a fast learner, able to contribute across diverse part categories and manufacturing processes

• Demonstrated ability to use engineering first principles to challenge and simplify requirements

• Hands-on and practical, comfortable building, testing, and troubleshooting in real-world environments

• Thrives with ownership and takes initiative without waiting to be directed

Additional Requirements

• This internship is on-site in El Segundo, California.

• Occasional travel to vendors or other Amca sites may be required

Hourly Pay Range
$30—$50 USD

Plot is building the next generation of social intelligence — an AI-native platform that helps some of the world's most influential brands understand culture, find emerging trends, and activate their communities at scale. We're a high-growth, venture-backed startup supported by the co-founders of Reddit and Plaid, with customers like Tory Burch, Lululemon, La Roche-Posay, and other household names.

We operate at the frontier of applied AI and agentic systems, ingesting and reasoning over millions of short-form videos to uncover consumer insights no one else can see. Our work impacts real product decisions, global marketing campaigns, and how brands engage their fans.

You'll join a small experienced team where engineers ship product — not tickets. You'll work hand-in-hand with our product designer from day one, shaping features before specs exist and turning rough ideas into shipped experiences. You'll work directly with founders, hop on customer calls, and own company-defining features end-to-end. If you want real responsibility, fast learning loops, and the ability to shape both product and company, Plot is the place. It's also a perfect fit if you aspire to build your own startup one day — we operate with a deep founder's mindset.

 


WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

 - Build agentic, reasoning-driven systems on top of cutting-edge LLMs to power consumer intelligence, marketing automation, and influencer activation.

 - Collaborate closely with founders, design, marketing, and customers to ensure our AI deliver real customer value

 - Stay at the front of the curve: research, prototype, and integrate emerging methods in agentic reasoning, context engineering, and LLM-driven automation.

Since 2006, we've been the industry's trailblazer, launching the first AI-powered measurement platform for publishers and the first AI-driven DSP. Our AI doesn't just optimize—it delivers the measurable outcomes that matter most to our clients, giving them the competitive edge they need in a crowded marketplace. Ready to join the team that's defining the future of digital advertising?

The Modeling team is responsible for Machine Learning (ML) systems at Quantcast. We build and maintain high-frequency ML infrastructure that prices millions of advertising opportunities per second in a real-time auction environment to maximise advertiser outcomes. In less than 100 milliseconds, our models predict age, gender, viewability, fraud, advertiser relevance and many more characteristics of internet users. Using NLP, clustering and LLMs we build topics in multiple languages to help our advertisers target customers interested in their products.



As a Machine Learning Engineer you care about the health and maintainability of our systems and the velocity of the engineering teams. You explore data, research new algorithms, experiment with proof of concepts, and build out scalable real-time production systems to tackle challenges the company faces.



What you'll do:

 - Design, code, test, and debug ML applications and constantly improve large-scale global systems that respond to millions of real-time requests per second, efficiently.

 - Run Machine Learning experiments to test new modeling ideas.

 - Collaborate with senior scientists and engineers to iterate on ML models and learn industry best practices for high-quality ML products and large-scale systems.

 - Write clean, efficient, and maintainable code using industry best practices.

 - Participate in code reviews and provide constructive feedback to team members.

 - Identify performance bottlenecks and optimise system components for enhanced scalability.

 - Keep up to date with developments in machine learning outside the company.

 - Receive hands-on mentorship from senior scientists and engineers to help bridge academic concepts with industrial scale.



Who you are:

 - Experience: 0-2 years of experience (including internships or significant academic projects) in machine learning or applied statistics.

 - Academic Background: A degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, or an adjacent field.

 - Technical Foundation: Fluency in Python, Java, or similar programming languages.

 - Analytical Rigor: Strong foundation in mathematics, specifically: probability, statistics, hypothesis testing.

 - ML Knowledge: Practical understanding of machine learning fundamentals (classification, regression, clustering, ranking, NLP, or LLMs).

 - Data & ML Ecosystem: Familiarity with data processing libraries (e.g. Pandas, NumPy) and ML frameworks (e.g. PyTorch, Scikit-learn or XGBoost).

 - Growth Mindset: A genuine interest in distributed system and software design, concurrent algorithms, data structures, and software engineering.


At Quantcast, we craft offers that reflect your unique skills, expertise, and geographic location. On top of a competitive salary, this position includes a performance bonus, equity, and a comprehensive benefits package. For more details, visit our Careers Page https://www.quantcast.com/careers/ and see how we support our team. We are headquartered in San Francisco with offices around the world. Quantcast is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Please see the Applicant Privacy Notice https://legal.quantcast.com/#applicant-privacy-notice for details on our applicant privacy policy. Join the team that unlocks potential.

jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE

Perchwell is the modern real estate listings platform built for agents to search smarter, collaborate better, and close deals faster. We are building the future of residential real estateʼs critical listings infrastructure: a platform where market  research and client collaboration converge. Our modern architecture enables continuous innovation at a pace legacy systems cannot match, with AI-powered features and mobile-first capabilities designed for how agents actually work. As consumer expectations and technology evolve, Perchwell remains focused on our core vision:  empowering real estate professionals with the most intelligent, data-driven, and connected platform in the industry.

Backed by leading venture capital firms including Lux Capital and Founders Fund, along with strategic partnerships with some of the country's top Multiple Listing Services (MLSs), Perchwell represents the first major new platform to enter the listings technology market in decades. This unique combination of institutional investment and deep industry alignment provides both the resources and market validation needed to transform the multi-trillion dollar residential real estate industry.




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Rising seniors enrolled in a CS or STEM degree program who are looking to intern at a fast paced, SaaS company this summer.

 - Passionate problem solvers who thrive in fast moving environments.

 - Strong communicators and team players who can work cross functionally.

 - Eager learners who want to gain real world engineering experience.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Build and Ship: Work in a fast paced startup environment to build high quality SaaS products that real estate professionals rely on.

 - Own a Project: Take ownership of a summer project, making key product, architecture, and implementation decisions.

 - Collaborate and Learn: Partner with engineers, product managers, and designers to bring ideas to life.

 - Deliver Impact: Work on scalable solutions from broadly defined problems and see your work in production.




WHY THIS INTERNSHIP? 

 - Dedicated Mentor: You’ll work 1:1 with an experienced engineer who will provide mentorship and support your growth.

 - Real Ownership: Over 10 weeks, early June to mid August, you will choose and lead your own project, making key decisions along the way.

 - Fully In Person Experience: This is a full time, in office internship based at our beautiful New York City HQ in Soho. You’ll work on site five days a week and collaborate closely with our team, gaining hands-on experience in a fast paced, learning oriented environment.

 - Showcase Your Work: At the end of the summer, present your project to our executive and engineering teams.

 - Work on Real Features: Beyond your project, you’ll contribute to real features and bug fixes with a structured software development lifecycle.

 - NYC Perks and Fun: From team dinners to museum trips, immerse yourself in the greatest city in the world while working with an awesome team




REQUIRED FOR THE ROLE

 - Passion for web applications, from the data layer to the front end

 - Working familiarity with RDBMS storage systems and SQL

 - Experience with a web application framework such as Ruby on Rails, TypeScript, and React

 - Strong communication and problem solving abilities

 - Excitement to learn, grow, and build




BONUS POINTS FOR THE FOLLOWING

 - Ruby on Rails experience

 - React experience

 - Demonstrated leadership skills developed during your college experience







INTERNSHIP INFORMATION

Internship Dates: June 7 - August 13, 2027

Application Deadline: Applications for this internship close on October 18, 2026, at 11 PM ET. Be sure to apply by the deadline to be considered! We will be reviewing all applications, so please take the time to submit a thoughtful application.

Offers: Internship offers will be extended by November 25, 2026.

$12,000 for 10 weeks (minus applicable taxes and withholdings)

 - 401K with a company match

 - HSA and FSA options

Perchwell is expanding rapidly across the US, and every new MLS client brings a data source we haven't worked with before. Our Data Analytics Engineering team owns what happens next: understanding what is actually in that data, transforming it into our warehouse, and building the intelligence layer that sits on top of it. This summer, you'll work on that alongside our analytics engineers and data engineers, supporting both the MLS customers we serve today and the ones we're onboarding next.




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Rising seniors enrolled in a CS, data science, statistics, or other STEM degree program who are looking to intern at a fast paced SaaS company this summer.

 - Passionate problem solvers who thrive in fast moving environments.

 - Strong communicators and team players who can work cross functionally.

 - Careful thinkers who chase down a number that looks wrong instead of passing it along.

 - Eager learners who want to gain real world analytics engineering experience.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Build and Ship: Extend the dbt models that transform raw MLS data into our warehouse, adding the tests and documentation the rest of the team depends on.

 - Build Intelligence: Strengthen the layer that sits on top of the warehouse, including metric definitions, semantic models, and the dashboards internal teams and customers rely on.

jobs.title: Data Engineer
jobs.description:
Who are we? 

Zeta Global is seeking a talented and versatile Data Engineer to join our Data Exchange team within our highly skilled development office in Copenhagen. This team plays a critical role in developing and deploying Zeta’s next-generation data science and engineering technology, collaborating closely with our global teams in the US, Europe, India and Philippines. The Copenhagen office boasts a dynamic and focused environment, comprising a core group of start-up veterans and approximately 30 highly skilled professionals. 

As a member of the Data Exchange team, you will contribute to the analysis, development, and maintenance of our complex data infrastructure, a sophisticated ecosystem of interconnected systems. This team tackles a continuous stream of challenging projects originating from across the organization, demanding a high degree of expertise and innovation. We are seeking candidates with a strong foundation in data engineering, data analysis, and software development principles, and a demonstrated interest in exploring the intersections between these disciplines. 

The Company 

Zeta Global is a data and AI-powered marketing technology company built on the foundation of a robust consumer data platform. With billions of proprietary data points and sophisticated machine learning algorithms, Zeta helps marketers unlock actionable insights into consumer behavior and preferences. The company's Zeta Marketing Platform harnesses this powerful combination of data and AI to create personalized customer experiences across the entire customer journey, ultimately driving significant growth for its clients. Through a commitment to innovation in data science, Zeta Global provides enterprises with the tools they need to build meaningful and profitable customer relationships. 

The position 

The ideal candidate for the Data Engineer position at Zeta Global Copenhagen is a highly motivated and analytical individual with a passion for understanding complex (software) systems. You are adept at using data to identify issues, formulate solutions, and develop robust data pipelines and software. You thrive in an environment that offers significant autonomy in planning and executing your work, yet you are also a strong collaborator, readily engaging with fellow developers and international product stakeholders. 

You will be involved in every stage of the development process, from initial brainstorming to ongoing maintenance, with a primary emphasis on analysis, prototyping, and development. Our development process is a dynamic blend of agile and rapid prototyping methodologies, designed to foster a culture of "flexibility under responsibility." We prioritize focused development time and believe in the power of collaborative problem-solving, encouraging team members to both seek and offer assistance readily. 

Your profile 

We welcome candidates with a solid background in data analysis or software development, seeking professionals with proven experience or recent graduates. Regardless of your background, a crucial element is your intellectual curiosity, self-motivation, and a demonstrable ability to translate real-world challenges into data models, ETL processes, algorithms, and ultimately, functional code. A strong interest in data engineering and/or the AdTech domain, along with its associated technologies, is highly desirable, as well as knowledge of object-oriented programming languages, particularly Scala. 

Minimum Qualifications: 

• 
A strong academic background in a quantitative field (Computer Science, Mathematics, Physics, or related disciplines). 

• 
Hands-on experience in designing, building, and maintaining scalable and reliable data pipelines. 

• 
Proficiency in Python, Scala or other OOP languages for data engineering and processing tasks. 

• 
Strong data analysis skills, including working with large datasets. 

• 
Knowledge of distributed data processing for batch workloads. 

• 
Solid understanding of database technologies. 

Desired Qualifications: 

• 
2-3 years of experience with Scala for data processing. 

• 
Strong software engineering skills, including experience with CI/CD pipelines and best coding practices. 

• 
Familiarity with data integrations and efficient data transfers. 

• 
Knowledge of data modeling, data warehousing concepts, and query optimization techniques. 

• 
Experience with distributed data processing using Apache Spark. 

• 
Experience with Airflow for workflow orchestration, scheduling, and monitoring data pipelines. 

• 
Cloud expertise, particularly AWS, including services such as S3, Glue, Athena and EMR. 

You approach problems with an analytical mindset and a pragmatic approach to solution development. You are a creative thinker, capable of identifying opportunities and weaknesses in proposed solutions, and constructively contributing with your own ideas. You thrive in a dynamic environment, adept at juggling multiple projects and connecting them with underlying data. You recognize that exploring new facets of data often yields greater insights than fine-tuning algorithmic parameters. You are equally comfortable implementing and optimizing solutions, and you are eager to tackle new challenges. 

You are a proactive and independent worker, eager to understand and engage with the company's core problem space. You possess excellent English communication skills, enabling effective collaboration with management and colleagues across our international offices. You are adaptable and comfortable navigating a dynamic environment where priorities may shift, taking ownership of tasks and seeing them through to completion. 

What we offer 

Join our dynamic team, largely comprised of Masters and PhDs in fields like Physics, Math, and Computer Science, and play a key role in shaping the future of our technology. You will collaborate with highly skilled professionals in a stimulating environment that fosters both learning and individual initiative. While we are passionate about exploring cutting-edge technologies and algorithms, we maintain a practical approach to implementing solutions. 

We believe in empowering our employees with autonomy and flexibility. We offer flexible work arrangements, including adjustable office hours and the possibility of occasional remote work, provided commitments are consistently fulfilled. You will have the freedom to select your preferred operating system (Mac, Windows) and development tools, with the expectation of independent maintenance and troubleshooting. We encourage the introduction of new technologies, contingent upon demonstrating their value and gaining team buy-in. 

Our international presence provides ample opportunities for cross-departmental collaboration and potential career advancement in locations like Berlin, San Francisco or New York. 

Interested candidates are encouraged to apply via LinkedIn, submitting a cover letter along with their application. Interviews will be scheduled on a continuous basis.

jobs.description:
About Us:
DailyPay is the leader in On-Demand Pay, helping employers modernize how people get their pay. DailyPay serves more than 1,900 employers and over 6 million employees, including many of the world's most recognized brands. By providing real-time access to earned pay and financial wellness tools, DailyPay helps employees manage their finances and helps employers attract and retain talent. DailyPay is helping define the future of pay, where money moves at the speed of work. Learn more at DailyPay's Press Center. http://www.dailypay.com/press


THE ROLE:

As a Placement Engineering Student, you will join the leader in the on-demand pay industry during a 9–12 month placement. You will be part of a mission-driven team hyper-focused on designing technology that builds a better, more equitable financial system. This role is designed for students who are passionate about reimagining how money moves and are willing to define new rules to change systems and lives. You will have the opportunity to learn how to build an unrivaled technology platform that enables workers to access their earned pay when they need it, ensuring money moves faster and smoother between employers and employees.

 


RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Support Scalable Technology: Contribute to the development of an unrivaled technology platform that serves an unmatched list of blue-chip clients.

 - Master New Systems: Help rewrite the invisible rules of finance by assisting in the creation of a more equitable and inclusive financial system.

 - Develop Technical Proficiency: Apply your knowledge of data structures and algorithms to real-world software design challenges within a fast-paced environment.

 - Adopt Best Practices: Gain hands-on experience and a deep willingness to learn and apply Test-Driven Development (TDD) to ensure high-quality code.

 - Collaborate Cross-Functionally: Use your strong communication skills to work effectively with experienced engineers and cross-functional teams.

 - Drive Innovation: Participate in the continuous improvement of technology that allows money to move faster and smoother across the financial ecosystem.

 - Learn and Grow: Actively engage in a culture of continuous learning, developing your technical career under the mentorship of industry experts.
   
    


WHAT YOU BRING TO THE TEAM:

 - Academic Foundation: Currently registered in a Bachelor's or Master’s degree in Computer Science or a related technical field that supports a 9–12 month placement.

 - Core Fundamentals: Strong understanding of data structures, algorithms, and the basic principles of software design.

 - Coding Experience: Practical coding experience in at least one modern programming language, such as Java, JavaScript, Python, or Go.

 - Eagerness to Learn: A proactive mindset and a strong desire to develop your career in technology and master new methodologies like TDD.

 - Communication Skills: The ability to articulate technical ideas clearly and collaborate effectively within a team setting.

 - Mission Alignment: A passion for reimagining financial systems and a drive to contribute to a company growing at an extraordinary pace.
   
   


WHAT WE OFFER:

 - Competitive compensation

 - Employee Resource Groups

 - Fun company outings and events

 - Generous PTO Allowance

 - Pension contribution

 



 

High-performing cultures aren't built in silos, they thrive on partnership. At DailyPay, we Commit Together to an inclusive, professional environment where multifaceted perspectives are our greatest competitive advantage. We recognize that our team members don’t live “single-issue lives,” and we lean into the wide-ranging backgrounds and life stages that sharpen our collective decision-making.



In our high-trust environment, we empower you to Challenge Norms. We’ve created a space where it is safe to ask difficult questions, disrupt the status quo, and share bold perspectives without fear of professional fallout. We believe that by checking our own assumptions and staying curious about the experiences of others, we arrive at better, more innovative results.

We provide the space for you to do your best work through peer advocacy and transparent career development. If you are looking for a culture that values intellectual honesty, celebrates the unique lived experiences of its people, and thrives on collective success, you’ll find it here.



If you require reasonable accommodation for any aspect of the recruitment process, please send a request to peopleops@dailypay.com. All requests for accommodation will be addressed as confidentially as practicable.



DailyPay is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion or creed, alienage or citizenship status, political affiliation, marital or partnership status, age, national origin, ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition, veteran status, gender, gender identity, pregnancy, childbirth (or related medical conditions), sex, sexual orientation, sexual and other reproductive health decisions, genetic disorder, genetic predisposition, carrier status, military status, familial status, or domestic violence victim status and any other basis protected under federal, state, or local laws.

At Rhoda AI, we’re building the next generation of generalist intelligent robots. We own the full robotics stack from high-performance hardware and robot systems to the infrastructure and state-of-the-art foundation world models that control our robots. Our robots are designed to be generalists capable of operating in complex, real-world environments and handling long-tail edge cases, made possible by our cutting edge research and end-to-end system design. We've raised over $450M and are investing aggressively in model research, infrastructure, hardware development, and manufacturing scale-up to make generalist robotics a reality.


ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Robot Software Engineer Intern, you'll work on the software foundation that keeps our robots running. You'll own real projects on the software platform stack: ranging from on-robot software, networking and communication infrastructure, data collection pipelines, telemetry, teleoperation, inference infra, developer tooling etc., and see your impact run on physical robots by the end of your internship. You'll sit with the engineers who build our robots and ship code that the team depends on every day.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Contribute to the networking and communication infrastructure connecting onboard robot systems to each other, to the cloud, and to teleoperation and monitoring systems

 - Help build data collection pipelines that capture sensor, telemetry, and behavioral data from the robot and upload it reliably to cloud storage for model training

 - Work on telemetry and observability systems that give the team real-time visibility into robot health and field performance

 - Build internal tooling that accelerates robot software development: deployment pipelines, logging, debugging tools, and field testing utilities

 - Support bring-up and field testing on live hardware, debugging issues across the onboard software stack

 - Collaborate with ML, perception, and control engineers to keep onboard systems reliable and training data high quality

 - Automate internal workflows to improve execution efficiency of the Rhoda teams


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Currently pursuing an undergraduate or graduate degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, or a related field — or a recent graduate

 - Solid computer science foundation: data structures, algorithms, operating systems, and networking

 - Genuine passion for working on robots — coursework, research, personal projects, competition teams, or internships all count

 - Strong programming skills in C++, Python, Golang, or Rust

 - Curiosity and comfort working with physical hardware in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment

 - Ability to debug across layers, from driver-level issues up to application behavior

 - Open to learn new things and grow from knowing nothing to an expert on arbitrary technical topics


NICE TO HAVE (BUT NOT REQUIRED)

 - Experience with bringing up & manipulating robots

 - Familiarity with networking, IPC, or communication protocols (e.g. gRPC, DDS, QUIC, WebSockets)

 - Exposure to cloud storage and data pipelines (AWS, GCP, S3, GCS)

 - Experience with perception pipelines, control systems, or learned models running on real-time robot stacks

 - Prior work on prototype or pre-production hardware


WHY THIS ROLE

 - Your work is the connective tissue of the robot — the networking, data, and tooling infrastructure that determines how fast the team can develop and improve our humanoids in the field

 - Work across the full onboard stack alongside perception, control, and ML engineers & researchers on a platform pushing the frontier of humanoid robotics

 - Real ownership on a small team, with your code running on real robots — not a side project on the shelf

jobs.title: Associate Data Engineer
jobs.description:
Radiology is the second most used healthcare service, used by over 51% of the workforce annually. Despite the critical role of radiology in healthcare, the process for undergoing a medical imaging exam has remained unchanged for decades. OneImaging is solving this with a concierge approach and a premium-quality radiology network of over 5,000 vetted providers across 48 states, which also reduces imaging costs by 60-80%. Our solution helps patients and families access essential radiology services at fair prices and without surprise bills, all while delivering immediate savings and ROI for employers and payers on every exam.

We’re hiring Data Engineers graduating between December 2026 and June 2027 to join our data team in Miami, starting May or June 2027. This is not a rotational program and it isn’t a shadowing role. You’ll work on the pipelines and integrations that make OneImaging’s data the source of truth for the business - from the raw feed coming out of a payer, a provider, or our own platform, through the transformation logic, to the dashboard or automation that someone in operations, finance, or care navigation actually relies on every day.

It also means you’ll be building alongside a team that has moved unusually early on AI-assisted engineering. We run a shared AI harness that every engineer’s agent builds on, and we’re explicit internally that writing code is no longer the slow part of the job - the slow parts are deciding what to build and verifying what comes out. We’ll expect you to use these tools heavily and to own everything they produce for you.

What you'll do:

• Build and maintain data pipelines in Databricks (SparkSQL/PySpark) that ingest, transform, and validate data from sources like our platform databases, payer eligibility files, provider and claims systems, and third-party APIs - with a senior engineer as your mentor and reviewer

• Work across the full path a dataset takes - ingestion, transformation, modeling, and the Looker dashboard or downstream workflow it feeds - with guidance at first and increasing independence as you go

• Help build and maintain automated inbound/outbound file exchanges (eligibility, claims status, reporting) that other teams depend on to run their day-to-day operations

• Work with AI coding agents as a normal part of your workflow, and take full accountability for the output: you should be able to explain every file in your diff

• Write tests and validation checks for your pipelines, and treat data quality as part of shipping rather than a phase afterwards

• Participate in design reviews and code reviews from your first weeks - including reviewing other engineers’ work, because a bare approval with no comment isn’t a completed review here

• Ask why. We reason from first principles and we have an explicit norm that engineers are not implementation machines - if a requirement doesn’t make sense, we want you to say so

• Handle protected health information correctly, with data governance, access controls, and audit logging as first-class requirements rather than afterthoughts

About you:

• Graduating with a B.S. or M.S. in Computer Science, Data Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical discipline between December 2026 and June 2027

• You’ve built things nobody assigned you - side projects, coursework you took further than required, hackathon work, something with real data, however small

• Strong SQL skills and working knowledge of Python for data processing

• Some exposure to Databricks, Spark, or a similar distributed data processing tool - coursework, an internship, or a personal project is enough; we don’t expect production experience

• A basic mental model of how data moves from a source system into a warehouse or lakehouse and out to a report

• You use AI coding tools and you’ve formed opinions about them - including where they mislead you and how you catch it

• You can explain a technical decision you made and what you’d do differently, which matters more to us than the sophistication of the project

• Comfortable with ambiguity and with being told “we haven’t figured that out yet”

• Intellectually honest: you can change your mind when the evidence changes, and you’d rather delete your own work than defend it

• Clear written and verbal communication - you’ll be writing documentation and PR descriptions that other teams depend on

• Authorized to work in the United States, and able to be based in Miami

Nice to have, and genuinely not required:

• An internship or co-op where you shipped a data pipeline or report to production

• Experience with a BI tool (Looker, Tableau, Power BI) or building a dashboard someone other than you used

• Exposure to AWS or another cloud provider

• Familiarity with relational or document databases (PostgreSQL, MongoDB)

• Anything you’ve built on top of LLM or agent APIs - tools, harnesses, evals, agents

• Curiosity about healthcare data standards (HL7, FHIR, DICOM) or claims/eligibility data - we’ll teach you these, and we’d rather you question how things are done in healthcare than arrive already knowing

• Coursework or projects involving statistics, data modeling, or data warehousing concepts

What we'll give you

A published career framework with written promotion criteria, so you can see the path from Associate Software Engineer through Senior, Staff and Principal, and know exactly what's expected at each step. A mentor from among our senior engineers, for whom mentorship is a written part of their job. Real ownership, quickly. And a mission that's easy to get behind with real life impact.

The base salary range for this position is $85,000 - $115,000. Individual compensation will depend on various factors, including qualifications, skills, experience, location, and applicable laws. In addition to base salary, this role is eligible to participate in our equity incentive and competitive benefits plans.

If you have been contacted by someone claiming to be a OneImaging recruiter or a hiring manager from a different domain about a potential job, please report it to law enforcement here and to candidateprotection@oneimaging.com.

jobs.title: Software Engineer Intern
jobs.description:
Who We Are

GITAI is a vertically integrated space and defense company building the next generation of hardware for low-Earth-orbit missions.

At our core is the space robotics technology that has defined GITAI from the beginning. A small, highly capable engineering team applies that foundation across satellite buses, in-orbit servicing robotics, and mission hardware for applications such as Earth observation. Today, a major focus of our work is supporting U.S. national security missions, particularly through proliferated LEO satellite constellations and other next-generation space systems.

We design, build, integrate, and test much of our hardware in-house. Electrical, mechanical, software, manufacturing, integration, and test teams work closely together, allowing a small team to own complete systems rather than isolated components. This vertical integration helps us move quickly, learn directly from hardware, and shorten the path from architecture to a working system.

We are still early. The systems, the company, and the market are all being built at the same time. Requirements change, technical problems are often ambiguous, and many answers do not yet exist. We are looking for exceptional engineers and operators who want broad ownership, can work across disciplines, and are willing to stay close to the hardware until the mission succeeds.

Your Mission

As a Field-Deployed Software Engineering Intern, you will support the development, integration, and testing of GITAI’s robotic and space systems. A major part of this role happens on real hardware. You will regularly deploy to our outdoor test site to support data acquisition, system bring-up, troubleshooting, and test execution. You will also contribute to software development in at least one technical area such as robotics, computer vision, or guidance, navigation, and control (GNC). You should be comfortable moving between code, sensors, computers, networks, actuators, and test equipment to understand why a system is or is not working.

What You’ll Drive

• Support weekly field testing, including system setup, bring-up, data acquisition, logging, monitoring, and troubleshooting.

• Develop and debug software for robotics, computer vision, GNC, or related systems.

• Diagnose problems across software and hardware, including sensors, actuators, communications, timing, configuration, and computing systems.

• Build scripts and lightweight tools for data collection, visualization, system health monitoring, and test automation.

• Review test data and logs, reproduce failures, and work with engineers to identify root causes and fixes.

• Support hardware/software integration and test preparation at our Torrance facility between field deployments.

• Document test configurations, issues, findings, and software changes so the engineering team can act on them quickly.

What We’re Looking For

• Start Date: Fall 2026 / Spring 2027. Earlier availability is preferred, and candidates who can start immediately are welcome.

• Currently pursuing or recently completed a BS or MS in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related technical field.

• At least 1 year of sustained, hands-on contribution to a robotics team, rocketry team, Formula SAE, research lab, or a similar environment where software was developed, integrated, and debugged on physical hardware.

• Available to work at least three days per week.

• Able to spend Wednesdays and Thursdays at GITAI’s outdoor test site in the desert region near Los Angeles on a regular basis.

• Hands-on experience getting software to work with real hardware through internships, research, student teams, competitions, or personal projects.

• Experience in at least one of the following areas: robotics, computer vision, controls, GNC, autonomy, or embedded systems.

• Experience programming in Python or C++.

• Comfortable working in Linux.

• Strong debugging skills and the ability to work through problems that cross software and hardware boundaries.

• Comfortable working outdoors around active engineering test operations.

• U.S. citizenship required, as this role may support U.S. Government programs that require eligibility for a U.S. Secret security clearance.

Strong Plus:

• Experience with ROS or ROS 2.

• Experience integrating sensors, cameras, actuators, embedded computers, or robotic systems.

• Experience with OpenCV, PyTorch, state estimation, motion planning, control systems, or related robotics software.

• Experience with hardware communication interfaces such as CAN, Ethernet, serial, EtherCAT, or similar protocols.

• Experience with data acquisition, telemetry, time synchronization, or analysis of experimental test data.

Location & Employment Details

• Location: Torrance, CA (onsite). Frequent overnight travel to desert test sites, including Barstow, Mojave, and other locations throughout Southern California, is expected based on program needs.

• Employment Type: Part-time, temporary, non-exempt

• Compensation: $28 - $40 per hour. Final compensation will be determined based on academic level, relevant technical experience, and demonstrated hands-on engineering capability.

• Typical Work Hours: Monday to Friday, approximately 9:00am – 6:00pm (onsite). Flexibility is expected based on mission schedules and program needs.

GITAI does not accept unsolicited resumes from staffing or recruiting agencies. We work only with recruiting partners that have been specifically engaged by GITAI. No fees will be paid for resumes submitted without a prior agreement.

Important Notice

• Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the U.S. This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

• To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), GITAI Employees must be a U.S. citizen, lawful U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State and/or the U.S. Department of Commerce, as applicable. 

• GITAI USA is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment with GITAI USA is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

jobs.title: Software Engineer New Grad - Software - Starfall
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

NEW GRADUATE ENGINEER, SOFTWARE (STARFALL)

As a Software Engineer on the Starfall Engineering organization, you will design and implement software and firmware for the next generation of avionics systems at SpaceX. You will be responsible for ensuring your system behaves as expected and troubleshoot when necessary. You will have a direct impact on our ability to launch SpaceX systems frequently, safely, and reliably.

Aerospace experience is not required to be successful here - we want our engineers to bring fresh ideas from all areas. We look for engineers who love solving problems and seek to make an impact on an inspiring mission. As we expand this team, we're looking for versatile, motivated, and collaborative engineers. Our team is involved in designing the vehicle systems at every phase of development. Our software engineers are responsible for the life cycle of the software they create, including development, testing, and operational support.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Design and deliver high-quality software and firmware for common processors and micro-controllers

• Support launch operations

• Collaborate with peers and customers

• Bring up and validate devices that communicate-to and fly-in space

• Analyze test results and bugs which require in-depth investigations

• Hands-on integration and troubleshooting of flight hardware/software systems

• Work in a dynamic environment with changing needs, requirements, and challenges

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor’s degree in computer science, data science, engineering, math, physics, or other STEM discipline

• Professional development experience in C++ or C languages (internship experience is applicable)

• Graduating in the class of 2026 or 2027

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Development experience with microcontrollers

• Strong software engineering fundamentals in C++

• Solid fundamental knowledge of computer architecture and networks

• Familiarity with NXP microcontrollers

• Commitment to high standard of software development, including adherence to software process and best practices

• Linux and bash shell scripting

• Understanding of verification methodologies

• Excellent communication & documentation skills, and ability to collaborate in multidisciplinary environments

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Must be available to work extended hours and weekends when needed to meet critical deadlines

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Pay Range:

Level 1: $125,000.00 - $160,000.00
Level 2: $145,000.00 - $195,000.00

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees accrue paid sick leave pursuant to Company policy which satisfies or exceeds the accrual, carryover, and use requirements of the law.
ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

jobs.title: Cross-border E-commerce Product Operations Intern - TikTok Shop - User & Promotion Growth Product
Data Scientist Intern - Current PhD
jobs.description:
At Neighbor, we’re building the largest hyperlocal marketplace the world has ever seen. We’ve raised over $75 million from top-tier investors such as Andreessen Horowitz and the CEOs of DoorDash, StockX, and Uber. Our marketplace is already flourishing in all 50 states and we’re just getting started!
We're excited to add a Data Scientist Intern to our Data & Analytics team. You'll work on the machine learning models we already run in production, including lifetime value, unit economics, and forecasting, making them more accurate and showing with evidence that they've improved. You'll also help Product, Marketing, and Sales divisions design A/B tests and interpret the results. Your work feeds directly into decisions across a marketplace that operates in nearly every U.S. city. This is a great fit for a PhD student who wants to apply their research skills to live business problems. You'll report to our Data & Analytics manager, with regular code review and hands-on mentorship.
Our stack: Python, dbt, and Dagster on Redshift and Athena, with a Cube semantic layer and Superset for BI.

The Problems You'll Solve
• Improve our lifetime value and unit economics models. Retrain them, re-engineer their features, and validate their predictions against realized outcomes.

• Audit inherited models: find the leakage, the stale hardcoded assumption, the segment where performance quietly falls apart, and the feature that's doing less work than everyone believes.

• Build forecasts our operators actually plan against: demand and supply by market, revenue, and the levers that move them.

• Partner with Product, Marketing, and Sales to design tests before they launch. Catching an underpowered test in the design review is worth more than any analysis you can do afterward.

• Analyze results and make a call and be candid about what each design can and can't identify

• Become a subject matter expert on Neighbor's product, users, and marketing life cycle. The modeling is the easy part; knowing which features mean something is the hard part.
Qualifications
• PhD-level candidate currently enrolled in a quantitative field (Computer Science, Statistics, Math, Physics, Data Science, etc.) completing your PhD by May of 2028; transcript required

• Demonstrated research, coursework, or project experience applying statistics and machine learning to real-world or complex datasets

• Strong SQL and fluent Python for modeling are required; experience with dbt or semantic layers like Cube is a big plus, but we're happy to train you on our specific transformation stack

• Academic or project-based experience with A/B testing design or statistical hypothesis testing

• Real grounding in inference, not just fitting: you can explain what your confidence interval means, why the p-value moved when you added a second metric, how leakage sneaks into a validation split, and when you don't have the data to answer the question

• Strong problem-solving mindset and eagerness to diagnose and improve existing code and statistical models

• Intellectual stubbornness in a productive direction: you keep pulling on a thread when the numbers don't reconcile, and you don't ship an explanation you don't believe

• Clear communication with non-technical stakeholders: you can explain a result and its uncertainty without either overclaiming or hiding behind jargon

Neighbor is the largest and most comprehensive marketplace for self storage and parking, with listings in almost every U.S. city. From storage facilities to neighborhood garages, driveways, and RV spots, Neighbor brings every option together in one simple search. Come help us disrupt the $500 billion storage and parking industry! This is a unique opportunity to join a fast-growing, VC-backed tech startup. You will be part of a an extremely talented, hardworking and passionate team committed to changing the world one neighbor at a time.
 
Neighbor is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to providing a positive interview experience for every candidate. If accommodations due to a disability or medical condition are needed, connect with us via email at hr@neighbor.com. Our top-rated summer internship program is designed to give college students meaningful work experience in specific functions, providing a deeper understanding of the processes of a Fortune 500 financial services organization. The program offers interesting challenges, valuable experience, and an opportunity to get to know Thrivent. This 12-week internship is a key piece of Thrivent’s entry-level talent program to ensure a strong talent pipeline to meet the needs of the organization now and into the future. The internship program offers assignments to optimize your skills and experience while giving you exposure to multiple business areas. 

Job Description
As an Investments IT Application Engineer Intern, you will have the opportunity to expand your IT understanding beyond the classroom in a dynamic environment where technology and business come together to deliver software and data solutions that support Thrivent's Investments and Asset Management business. You will collaborate daily with Agile Scrum teams and work alongside Application Engineers, analysts, and business partners to develop, test, support, and enhance technology solutions.

Through this internship, you will gain hands-on experience designing and maintaining applications, supporting data pipelines and integrations, solving technical challenges, and learning how technology enables investment operations. You will participate in a collaborative environment that helps refine the skills gained through your academic experiences while learning how technology professionals work at Thrivent.

Responsibilities
• Assist with the design, development, enhancement, testing, and maintenance of software applications and data solutions
• Support development efforts using technologies such as Python, R, Java, SQL, or similar tools
• Participate in Agile Scrum ceremonies including planning, standups, sprint reviews, and retrospectives
• Analyze and troubleshoot application, data, and system issues
• Assist with testing software applications, APIs, system integrations, and data workflows
• Support data ingestion, transformation, validation, and reporting processes
• Contribute to the development of data pipelines, integrations, and automation solutions
• Work with business partners, analysts, architects, and engineers to support business-driven technology solutions
• Maintain technical documentation for applications, processes, and operational procedures
• Become knowledgeable about and apply Thrivent's development standards, processes, and best practices

Position Requirements 
• Current Junior pursuing an undergraduate degree in: Computer Science, Software Engineering, Management Information Systems (MIS), Mathematics, Data Science, or a related technical field
• Expected graduation date between December 2027 and May 2028
• Proven history of strong academic performance (GPA 3.0+ preferred)
• Exposure to one or more programming languages such as Python, Java, R, SQL, or similar technologies
• Foundational knowledge of software development concepts and database design
• Strong problem-solving and analytical skills
• Well-developed written and verbal communication skills
• Strong organizational and time-management skills
• Ability to work effectively in a team-oriented environment
• Ability to work in the United States for an indefinite period without sponsorship

Additional Program Information 
• Competitive compensation: $27.00 - $30.00 per hour
• Full intern event program including professional development, networking, and social activities
• Exposure to Thrivent leaders, technology teams, and business partners
• Opportunity to work on impactful projects that support the Investments business
 
Location 
Minneapolis, MN (Hybrid)

Thrivent’s long-term growth depends on attracting, rewarding, and retaining people who are committed to helping others thrive with purpose. We accomplish this by offering a wide variety of market competitive compensation programs to attract, reward, and retain top talent. The applicable hourly wage range for this full-time role is $27.00-$30.00 per hour, which factors in various geographic regions. The base pay actually offered will be determined by a variety of factors including, but not limited to, location, relevant experience, skills, and knowledge, business needs, market demand, and other factors Thrivent deems important. ​
 
Pay Transparency

The following benefits may be offered for roles working 20 or more hours per week: medical insurance; Sick and Safe Time; paid company holidays, and other employee benefits. Eligibility for receipt of these benefits is subject to the applicable plan/policy documents. Thrivent’s plans/policies are subject to change at any time at Thrivent’s discretion.
 
Thrivent provides Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) without regard to race, religion, color, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, pregnancy, national origin, age, disability, marital status, citizenship status, military or veteran status, genetic information, or any other status protected by applicable local, state, or federal law. jobs.title: Early Career Intern - Technology
jobs.description:
About Invesco

As one of the world’s leading independent global investment firms, Invesco is dedicated to rethinking possibilities for our clients. By delivering the combined power of our distinctive investment management capabilities, we provide a wide range of investment strategies and vehicles to our clients around the world. If you're looking for challenging work, intelligent colleagues, and exposure across a global footprint, come explore your potential at Invesco.

What’s in it for you?

Our people are at the very core of our success. Invesco employees get more out of life through our benefit and perk offerings including: 
• Company networking events with other interns

• Peer Sponsor Program 

• Leadership Connection series

• Virtual Lunch and Learns

• Invesco Cares volunteer events

• Complimentary coffee and snacks

• 401(K) matching of 100% up to the first 6% with a discretionary supplemental contribution 

Job Description

Early Career Intern – Distribution Technology Overview 
Ready to make your mark in the world of investments? Spend an unforgettable summer at Invesco alongside a select group of driven students. Our 9-week Summer Internship Program kicks off in June 2027 and offers you the chance to dive into the fast-paced world of investments, learn from industry pros, and build connections that will last a lifetime. 
 
In this internship, you’ll get hands-on experience, one-on-one mentorship, and the inside scoop on what it’s really like to work at a global investment firm. As part of a Summer Internship Program cohort, you will have a variety of initiatives to keep you engaged throughout the summer including orientation, networking events, development workshops, and volunteer activities. You’ll work side-by-side with talented teams to learn about the business. 
 
Here’s the best part: crush your internship, and you could be eligible for a full-time offer to join our Early Career Program after graduation! 

Overview of Department/Team
The Distribution Technology team enables data-driven decision-making by building and managing platforms that help business teams understand clients, products, sales, and market trends. The team also designs and operates scalable, cloud-based data pipelines that integrate and transform data from multiple sources for reporting, analytics, and business applications.

Using technologies such as Snowflake, AWS, Python, and Airflow, we deliver secure, scalable, high-performing data solutions across the organization. We also apply AI, automation, and modern data engineering practices to improve efficiency, accelerate insights, and create new business capabilities.

What you’ll do
• Learn the Invesco business model and growth strategy (product, investment, sales, operations and corporate services) 
• Develop professional skills and networking across the organization as well as the industry
• Participate in cultural, technology, and management training 
• Shadow end-to-end technology solutions
• Build one or more of the following core capabilities (business analysis, project management, application development, web development, enterprise architecture, quality assurance, infrastructure engineering) 
• Participate in meetings with Early Careers technology team and contribute to the influence of positive change and ideas 
• Develop your technical aptitude, business insight, and collaborative abilities through a variety of project work. 
 
What you get
• A Launchpad for Your Career – Get ready to build real skills and set yourself up for a future at Invesco (and beyond).
• Your Own Mentor – You’ll be paired with a mentor who’s got your back, answers your questions, and helps you navigate your summer.
• Intern Community – Join a crew of fellow interns to collaborate, share ideas, and get to know—both in and out of the office.
• Pathway to Future Opportunities – Nail your internship, and you could be eligible for a full-time offer to join our Early Career Program after graduation!
• Real Experience, Real Impact – Work on meaningful projects, learn from our team, and see what it’s like to work at a global investment firm.
 
Minimum Qualifications
• Currently enrolled in a bachelor’s degree program and be a Junior graduating by summer of 2028
• Minimum GPA of 3.2 on a 4.0 scale
• Proficiency in Microsoft Office, especially Excel
• All majors are welcome with an emphasis on Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology.
• Strong leadership, initiative, and interpersonal skills; ambitious and creative demeanor
• Strong analytical/quantitative and technical abilities, organizational skills, and attention to detail
• Technical course work 
• Ability to adapt to ambiguous situations 
• Ability to work well with others across teams with varied strengths 
• Must be able to work in the Invesco office where the position is available
• Must be authorized to work in the U.S. on a permanent basis. We do not offer any type of employment-based immigration sponsorship for this program. Invesco will not provide any assistance or sign any documentation in support of any other form of immigration sponsorship or benefit including optional practical training (OPT) or curricular practical training (CPT).
• Relocation and housing will not be included if an offer is extended.

Preferred Qualifications
• Ability to adapt to ambiguous situations 
• Ability to work well with others across teams with varied strengths 
• Ability to communicate and work with both technical and non-technical partners 
• Intermediate proficiency with Python, SQL, Power BI, or Excel preferred

$37/hr

Full Time / Part Time

Full time
Worker Type

Student/Intern (Fixed Term)
Job Exempt (Yes / No)

No
Workplace Model

Pursuant to Invesco’s Workplace Policy, employees are expected to comply with the firm’s most current workplace model, which as of October 1, 2025, includes spending at least four full days each week working in an Invesco office. This reflects our belief that spending time together in the office helps us build stronger relationships, collaborate more easily, and support each other’s growth and development.

It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities and qualifications required of employees assigned to this job. The job holder may be required to perform other duties as deemed appropriate by their manager from time to time.

Invesco's culture of inclusivity and its commitment to diversity in the workplace are demonstrated through our people practices. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, creed, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, citizenship status, disability, age, or veteran status. Our equal opportunity employment efforts comply with all applicable U.S. state and federal laws governing non-discrimination in employment.
