jobs.title: Simulation Engineer Intern - Neural Rendering
jobs.description:
JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING ADVANCED AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD

At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and into the real world. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. Today, we're deploying autonomous systems on heavy construction equipment across the country, improving safety on job sites and accelerating schedules on critical infrastructure projects.

We're not here debating the future of AI. We're deploying it in the real world. In just two years, we've raised $350M and achieved the first fully autonomous excavator deployments in construction.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.




ABOUT THE ROLE & TEAM

Before an autonomous excavator digs its first trench on a new site, it's already dug thousands in simulation. The Simulation team builds the virtual environments our autonomy stack trains and tests against — and the closer sim looks and behaves like the real world, the faster we move. Neural rendering is the next step: replacing hand-authored assets and approximations with learned representations that capture the visual complexity of real jobsites — dust, lighting, deformable terrain, heavy equipment in motion. As our Simulation intern, you'll push neural rendering techniques into our sim pipeline and measure whether they actually close the visual gap that matters for downstream autonomy performance.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Research, implement, and benchmark neural rendering methods (NeRF, 3D Gaussian splatting, or related techniques) for generating realistic construction-site imagery within our simulation stack

 - Train models on real-world site data captured by our fleet and evaluate visual fidelity, temporal consistency, and render speed

 - Integrate neural rendering outputs into the simulation pipeline so perception and planning teams can train and test against them

 - Build evaluation metrics and tooling that quantify how well rendered scenes match real fleet data — and whether that improvement transfers to autonomy performance

 - Identify and address failure modes: dynamic objects, deformable terrain, dust, harsh lighting, and other construction-specific challenges

 - Document findings, limitations, and a recommendation on where neural rendering should (and shouldn't) replace traditional sim assets


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR


REQUIRED

 - Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in computer science, computer graphics, robotics, or a related field — or bringing equivalent research or industry experience

 - Strong Python and hands-on experience with PyTorch (or equivalent)

 - Solid understanding of 3D graphics fundamentals: rendering pipelines, scene representations, camera models, and coordinate systems

 - Familiarity with neural scene representations (NeRF, Gaussian splatting, neural radiance fields, or related methods)

 - Comfort with real-world data — construction sites are messy, dusty, and nothing like an indoor dataset


PREFERRED

 - Published work or substantial project experience in neural rendering, novel view synthesis, or differentiable rendering

 - Experience with simulation engines (Unreal, Unity, NVIDIA Isaac Sim, or similar)

 - Background in autonomous vehicle simulation or synthetic data generation

 - Familiarity with C++ and GPU programming (CUDA, OpenGL, Vulkan)

This is a fixed-term, project-based internship designed strictly for students (undergraduate or graduate) seeking resume-building experience, hands-on skill development, or industry exposure rather than a direct career launchpad. Candidates will own discrete, short-term projects that can be fully completed within the internship timeframe. Please note that while exceptional interns may occasionally be considered if business needs align, opportunities for full-time conversion are highly limited."

jobs.title: AI Tutor – Polish
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars. 

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to understand the universe and help expand humanity’s knowledge and capabilities. We work across the full Super Intelligence stack: compute (Colossus supercomputers), models (Grok), and applications (Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X). We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

As an AI Tutor specialized in multilingual audio capabilities, you will contribute to SpaceXSI's mission by training and refining Grok to excel in voice interactions, speech recognition, and auditory experiences across diverse languages, accents, and cultural contexts. Your work will focus on curating and annotating high-quality audio data to enhance Grok's global accessibility, enabling natural spoken interactions for users worldwide, bridging language barriers through accurate speech processing, and improving the AI's handling of multilingual audio nuances.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Use proprietary software to provide labels, annotations, recordings, and inputs on projects involving multilingual audio clips, voice recordings, speech samples, and auditory elements in various languages.

• Support the delivery of high-quality curated audio data that ensures clear, natural spoken output, accurate representation of linguistic and prosodic details (such as intonation, rhythm, and accent), and professional audio standards.

• Collaborate with technical staff to develop tasks that improve AI's ability to handle speech modulation, accent variation, noise in real-world recordings, and multilingual audio processing.

• Work with technical staff to improve annotation tools for efficient audio workflows.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Native proficiency in Polish with exposure to diverse accents, dialects, or regional variations.

• Proficiency in English (minimum B2 level) with clear, natural vocal delivery and pronunciation suitable for audio recording purposes.

• Strong auditory perception to identify nuances in speech, accents, pronunciation, intonation, and audio quality across languages.

• Demonstrated ability to handle multilingual audio content, including evaluating speech accuracy, cultural vocal expressions, and contextual interpretation in spoken form.

• Demonstrated ability to transcribe audio with high accuracy across accents and varying audio quality.

• Comfort providing high-quality voice recordings and feedback on audio samples in multiple languages.

• Strong comprehension skills and the ability to make independent judgments on ambiguous or varied audio material, including noisy or accented speech.

• Strong communication, interpersonal, analytical, detail-oriented, and organizational skills, with the ability to articulate audio-related feedback effectively.

• Commitment to developing AI that masters sophisticated multilingual audio capabilities.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Demonstration of exceptional attention to linguistic nuance, auditory detail, and data quality beyond standard transcription work.

• Deep understanding and taste of what good/useful Audio data is.

• Strong command of advanced transcription and annotation practices, including handling disfluencies, accents, and prosodic features (intonation, stress, rhythm, emotion, etc) with high consistency and accuracy.

• Background in linguistics (e.g., phonetics, phonology, sociolinguistics), speech sciences, cognitive science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience, with demonstrated ability to analyze accent variation, pronunciation differences, and multilingual speech patterns.

• Experience working with speech/audio datasets, annotation workflows, or AI training data, including knowledge/experience with training voice models, and an understanding of how data quality impacts model performance.

• Professional experience in voice work, including voice acting, voice recording, podcasting with a measurable audience (e.g., X following), or similar audio production demonstrating attention to clarity and recording quality.

• Demonstrated ability to exercise independent judgment in ambiguous audio scenarios and make consistent, defensible annotation decisions.

• Portfolio (strongly preferred for advanced candidates): Voice samples, annotated transcripts, or audio-related work demonstrating quality, methodology, and attention to detail.

jobs.description:
What The Role Is

Reporting to the Senior Manager, Energy Management, the Analyst, Market Optimization & Trading, will support the development and execution of trading, hedging, and optimization strategies for Clearway’s ERCOT and PJM assets. The Analyst will work in close coordination with the Market Optimization & Trading, Market Fundamentals, Business Development, Origination, Asset Management, Credit and Energy Risk, and Operations groups to help manage Clearway’s market exposure while building deep expertise in nodal power market analytics within a rapidly growing organization.

If you do not meet 100% of the below qualifications but see yourself contributing, please submit your resume.

What You'll Be Doing

• Support the development and execution of day-ahead, real-time, and term trading and hedging strategies for Clearway’s ERCOT and PJM assets, including energy, ancillary services, and basis positions.

• Assist in identifying and analyzing congestion market risk, including congestion.

• Support participation in CRR/FTR auctions and virtual bidding strategies.

• Work with Credit and Energy Risk to support the internal approval process for trading counterparties and transactions.

• Communicate with project stakeholders on market conditions, trading risks, and optimization opportunities.

• Work with the Market Analytics and Credit and Energy Risk teams to develop and enhance tools for position management, reporting, trade capture, and the eventual implementation of an enterprise risk management system.

• Develop, operate, and maintain production cost and price forecasting models (e.g., using tools such as UPLAN, PROMOD, or Dayzer) to support nodal price and congestion forecasting for ERCOT and PJM.

• Leverage data to create tools and automate workflows.

• Mark and maintain forward price curves for ERCOT and PJM power products, and support stochastic risk modeling and correlation assumptions.

• Prepare recurring and ad-hoc market recaps, outlooks, and presentation materials summarizing ERCOT and PJM fundamentals, price drivers, and trading performance for internal stakeholders.

• Support day-to-day position management and P&L reporting for ERCOT and PJM trading portfolios.

• Oversee the Energy Management documentation process, leveraging Clearway’s internal and external subject matter experts to bring trading, ISO, QSE, and enabling agreements to execution.

• Participate in energy working groups, professional organizations, trade shows & conferences.

• Track and report on ERCOT and PJM policy and regulatory developments, including ISO market rule changes, that may impact trading strategy, leveraging Clearway’s internal and external subject matter experts.

• Ability to travel up to 25% of the time.

• Maintain confidentiality and sensitivity with respect to all functions of Clearway.

What You'll Bring

• Bachelor’s degree in finance, business administration, engineering, economics, mathematics, meteorology, or a related quantitative field.

• 0-2 years of relevant experience

• Strong analytical and quantitative skills with a curious, inquisitive mindset and a genuine drive to understand how power markets work. Prior trading experience is not required – relevant coursework, internship, or academic research in a quantitative field will also be considered.

• Interest in or exposure to ERCOT and/or PJM market structure, including day-ahead and real-time markets, CRR/FTRs, and ancillary services, is a plus but not required.

• Solid understanding of power markets, including forwards, futures, swaps, and options.

• Ability to extract, manipulate, and analyze large datasets relevant to energy markets to support trading and risk decisions.

• Proficiency with Python, SQL, or other coding/statistical tools is a plus.

• Highly motivated, self-starter, friendly personality, and good team player.

• Attention to detail and inclination towards structure, organization, and process – as well as the ability to examine, question, and improve on the inputs and recommendations of others.

• Strong organizational skills with the ability to oversee multiple projects simultaneously, track progress and needs of each, and provide high-quality deliverables accurately and on time.

• Able to work well with geographically dispersed, cross-functional teams in a fast-paced environment.

• Highly proficient in Microsoft Excel; proficient in Word and PowerPoint.

The Lyft Rider Science team is seeking an Applied Scientist intern to develop next-generation user simulation methods using state of the art AI methods. The goal of this project is to develop and validate LLM-based Rider Agents that can serve as behavioral proxies for real riders, and study when agent simulations can provide reliable signal about rider responses to product interventions before online experimentation.

You will build agent-based simulation systems grounded in real rider context and behavioral data, evaluate their fidelity against observed rider behavior and historical experiments, and study where these simulations can accelerate product iteration and experimentation.

This role combines LLM engineering, agent-based modeling, machine learning, and causal inference with direct applications to real-world rider products. • Build evaluation pipelines to assess realism, robustness, and mechanism plausibility of simulated behavior against human data or established theory

Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities. 

At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead. 

Your Team, Your Impact

Marvell’s Compute and Custom Solutions organization (CCS) is looking for a talented ASIC architect/engineering intern to join our architecture team. This team acts as the central technical interface to our datacenter clients. It is responsible for the overall technology choice, silicon partitioning strategy, IP definition and selection and architectural guidance of datacenter products (SmartNIC, servers, AI accelerators and switches, mainly) for the main hyperscalers and companies worldwide. We actively participate in the definition of next generation datacenter products with our clients and respond to their ASIC RFQs. Role spans engagement with both customers and internal technology teams to define the best solution to the custom product needs and includes all functions required to build, test and manufacture an advanced custom silicon System in a Package.

• Engaging with customers, engineering, and marketing to help define chip architectures of innovative and complex datacenter products
• Identifying the best silicon partitioning, IP selection, packaging technology
• Mapping Marvell solutions into highly effective presentations and sharing with customers
• Communicating and coordinating with other business units in Marvell on internal IP and sharing/leveraging capabilities and knowledge

• Currently pursuing a Master’s Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field with an expected graduation date between Fall 2027 – Summer 2028
• Experience with or knowledge of system architectures for datacenter products strongly appreciated

• Passion for learning and working in a fast-paced, collaborative environment.

jobs.title: Measurement Services Intern
jobs.description:
At TC Energy, we are proud to connect the world to the energy it needs. Guided by our values of safety in every step, personal accountability, one team and active learning, we deliver the critical energy that North America and the world rely on while balancing reliability, affordability and sustainability.

Join us. Connect to what matters.

Work Term: May 2027 - August 2027

To be considered, applications must include a resume and unofficial academic transcript. Incomplete submissions may not be reviewed. We appreciate your attention to detail and look forward to learning more about you!

The Opportunity

We are seeking a Student Intern to support gas quality and measurement operations through data analysis, reporting, laboratory coordination, and asset management activities. This opportunity will provide hands-on experience working with operational data, maintaining performance dashboards, supporting inventory management processes, and contributing to laboratory sample coordination activities. The Student Intern will collaborate with cross-functional teams while gaining exposure to operational efficiency initiatives, asset optimization efforts, and measurement systems that support the safe and reliable operation of energy infrastructure.

At TC Energy, connection is at the heart of everything we do. As a Student Intern, you will contribute to meaningful work that helps connect people, communities and industries to the energy they rely on every day. You will gain hands-on experience working alongside experienced professionals, applying your academic knowledge to real-world projects and helping support the safe and reliable delivery of energy across North America.

As a valued member of our team, you will take on challenging and rewarding work, build lasting professional relationships and develop skills that will help shape your future career. Through collaboration, mentorship and practical experience, you'll gain insight into our business while contributing to work that matters. Every day presents an opportunity to learn, grow and make an impact while helping power progress for the communities we serve.

What you'll do

• Support gas quality and measurement operations through data analysis and reporting activities
• Maintain operational dashboards and performance reporting tools
• Assist with analyzer and chromatograph inventory management processes
• Coordinate laboratory sample tracking and related administrative activities
• Analyze meter station data to identify opportunities for operational efficiency and asset optimization
• Collaborate with cross-functional teams to support measurement and operational initiatives
• Contribute to data collection, validation, and reporting processes that support business decision-making

Minimum Qualifications

• Currently enrolled in an accredited Chemistry or Data Analysis degree program
• Completion of at least one academic term prior to the start of the work term in May 2027
• Returning to full-time studies immediately following the work term
• Availability to work full-time (40 hours per week) for the duration of the work term

Preferred Qualifications

• Knowledge of Microsoft tools that support data analysis and visualization
• Experience with data analysis and reporting
• Exposure to dashboard development and maintenance
• Knowledge of asset management processes
• Experience working with operational or laboratory data
• Demonstrate a safety mindset, in a professional and personal setting
• Exhibit the TC Energy corporate values and incorporate them into work activities and initiatives
• Strong interpersonal and communicative skills to work efficiently in a collaborative team environment
• Commitment to building and maintaining relationships with internal and external stakeholders
• Ability to accurately analyze information and deal with ambiguity
• Experience working in a dynamic and challenging environment, and adaptable to changing priorities
• Ability to multi-task effectively, with strong organizational and time management skills
• Reflective and committed to continuous improvement and personal development

To remain competitive, support our high-performance culture and allow for more flexibility in the way we work, we offer a hybrid work model and flexible dress code for our eligible office-based workforce in Canada, the U.S. and Mexico. #LI-Hybrid

Relocation Eligibility

This position is eligible for our student relocation assistance program.

About our business

We are a leader in North American energy infrastructure, spanning Canada, the U.S. and Mexico. For over 75 years, we have proudly connected the world to the energy it needs. Every day, we move more than 30 per cent of the natural gas used across the continent and connect LNG exports to global markets, powering communities and industries. Complemented by strategic ownership and low-risk investments in power generation, our infrastructure delivers affordable, reliable and sustainable energy across North America. Our field operations span seven Canadian provinces, 34 U.S. states and seven Mexican states. Together, we strengthen the connections that deliver the energy the world relies on-every day.

We welcome applications from all qualified individuals regardless of race, religion, age, sex, color, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, or disability. We are also committed to providing accommodations throughout the recruitment process. Applicants requiring accommodations or accessible formats are encouraged to contact us at careers@tcenergy.com for support.

All applicants must have legal authorization to work in the country where the position is based, without restrictions. Background screening is required for all positions, which may include criminal and/or credit checks. Offers may be extended at a different level or job title that best aligns with the successful candidate's qualifications.

Learn more

Visit us at TCEnergy.com and connect with us on our social media channels for our latest news, employee stories, community activities, and other updates.

Thank you for considering TC Energy in your career journey.

As the operator of a federally funded research and development center (FFRDC), we are broadly engaged across all aspects of space— delivering innovative solutions that span satellite, launch, ground, and cyber systems for defense, civil and commercial customers. When you join our team, you’ll be part of a special collection of problem solvers, thought leaders, and innovators. Join us and take your place in space.

Aerospace Corporation is hiring Software Engineering Grad Interns for the Software Implementation and Integration Department within the Information Systems and Cyber Division (ISCD). Position will be full-time and 100% onsite at our office in El Segundo, CA or Chantilly, VA.

Job Summary
Information Systems and Cyber Division (ISCD) staff couple the latest in information system technologies, such as elastic compute clouds, containerization, microservices, real-time operating systems, and visualization frameworks, with expertise in cyber security, software architecture, software engineering, data science, Artificial Intelligence, process improvement, and software development to deliver responsive, resilient, high-performance software intensive systems to our Intelligence Community, DoD, and civilian customers. 

What You’ll Be Doing 
• Participates in the software design & implementation of a simulated space system.
• Develops prototype software in Python, Java & C to operate on the simulated space element and the simulated ground element.
• Participates with an interdisciplinary team in ongoing research or technical programs with academic collaboration partners.
• Applies standard techniques and procedures to carry out a series of prescribed scientific and/or engineering tasks.
• Training and mentorship will be provided.

What Corporate Skills You Will Bring
• Strong written and oral communication skills
• Must work well in a team environment.
• Must possess strong organizational, time management and project management skills.
• Demonstrate flexibility and ability to adapt to changing organizational need.
• Interpersonal skills to coordinate efforts and work with other internal and external organizations.
• Demonstrate behavior that is consistent with the company’s values of Dedication to Mission Success, Technical Excellence, Commitment to Our People, Objectivity and Integrity, and Innovation

What You Need to Be Successful

• Currently enrolled full-time at an accredited college/university degree program pursuing a Master's or PhD Degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or related technical field(s)
• Availability to work full-time for a minimum of 10 weeks outside of university term and ability to return to a degree program full- time after completion of the internship.
• Experience with Microsoft Office applications (Word, PowerPoint and Excel)
• Advanced level programming experience in Python, C/C++, or JAVA
• Experience working with common cloud computing services such as Amazon Web Services or Microsoft Azure.
• This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government security clearance. U.S. citizenship is required to obtain a security clearance.

In this role, you will collaborate with experienced data scientists, software engineers, and business stakeholders to support solutions that improve grid optimization, asset management, distributed energy resource (DER) integration, and customer engagement.

We welcome candidates from diverse backgrounds who are excited to learn, contribute, and grow in a collaborative, customer-centric environment.
Internship Details

Duration: 
• 40 hours per week for 10 weeks during Summer 2027

Target Start Date: 
• May/June 2027

• Support the development, maintenance, and enhancement of data and machine learning pipelines used in production environments.

• Experience using AI agent-driven tools to support software development, testing, code review, or related technical activities.
• Intermediate proficiency in Python and SQL.
• Knowledge of statistical methods, data analysis techniques, and data-driven problem solving.
• Exposure to machine learning through academic coursework, independent projects, research, internships, or professional experience.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to share ideas clearly and respectfully.
• Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively in team environments while maintaining accountability for assigned work.

• Previous internship, research, or professional experience related to data science, analytics, software engineering, or machine learning.
• Experience using AI agent-supported tools for interactive data analysis and technical problem solving.
• Familiarity with cloud platforms such as AWS or Microsoft Azure.
• Experience with version control systems such as GitHub.
• Enrollment in a master's degree program in a STEM-related discipline, including Statistics, Data Science, Software Engineering, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, or a similar field.

jobs.title: Data Engineer Intern
jobs.description:
ABOUT POET
At POET, it is our mission to be good stewards of the Earth by converting renewable resources to energy and other valuable goods as effectively as humanly possible. For over thirty-five years, our drive and passion to change the world has enabled us to become the largest producer and marketer of bioethanol and a leader in sustainable products in the world.

CULTURE IS KING AT POET
We’re all on the same team. We always communicate. And we park our egos at the door. These aren’t just slogans on our walls. It’s the way we do things at POET. We provide an environment for team members to maintain a healthy work-life balance. It’s the best way to optimize health, wellness, and productivity in a sustainable way. We work hard. We play hard. We have frequent team events, volunteer efforts, and we know how to celebrate wins!

JOB SUMMARY & RESPONSIBILITIES
POET is a fast-paced, data-driven biotech company which operates a complex business affected by hundreds of variables, and data is used every day to help drive decisions and improve outcomes. Our data comes from many areas of the business, including sensors in our bioethanol plants, commodity markets, financial systems, logistics, and other business applications.
The Data Engineering Intern will work alongside the Data Engineering team to gain hands-on experience with the systems and processes used to collect, organize, transform, and deliver data throughout the organization. This internship is intended to provide meaningful project experience while introducing the intern to enterprise data systems, tools, and development practices.
 
This is an on-site role located in Sioux Falls, SD. Responsibilities include:

• Assist with building and maintaining data pipelines used to collect, clean, transform, and deliver data.
• Write and troubleshoot SQL queries to retrieve, validate, and analyze data.
• Help identify and resolve data quality issues.
• Assist with automating manual or repetitive data processes.
• Participate in testing and validating new or updated data solutions.
• Work with Data Engineers, analysts, and business stakeholders to better understand how data is used throughout POET.
• Create and maintain documentation for data processes, pipelines, and systems.
• Gain exposure to databases, orchestration tools, APIs, industrial data systems, and other enterprise technologies.
• Contribute to one or more projects that provide measurable value to the Data Engineering team or the business.
• Since we’re all about teamwork and getting the job done, your skills may be put to a lot of other uses!
• 
The POET Never Satisfied Internship openings are for Summer 2027. We post Internships in early September with the intention of having interns selected by November 1st.

QUALIFICATIONS & SKILLS

• Currently pursuing an Associate’s or Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Data Science, Engineering, or a related field.
• Basic understanding of relational databases and SQL.
• Some programming or scripting experience with languages or tools such as Python, SQL, PowerShell, C#, Java, or similar technologies is preferred.
• Interest in learning about data engineering, automation, databases, and enterprise technology.
• Strong problem-solving and critical-thinking skills.
• Ability to learn new technologies and concepts quickly.
• Good written and verbal communication skills.
• Attention to detail and a willingness to ask questions.
• Ability to work both independently and as part of a team.
• Working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications and the ability to learn new programs.
 
A SUCCESSFUL CANDIDATE WILL HAVE

• A strong desire to learn and develop new technical skills.
• Curiosity and an interest in understanding how data and systems work.
• A strong customer service mindset with a value placed on relationships.
• Demonstrated problem-solving and critical-thinking skills.
• The ability to take directions, receive feedback, and apply what they have learned.
• The willingness to ask questions and seek help when needed.
• An innovative mindset and willingness to explore new ideas.
• Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work effectively with others.
• A high level of personal integrity.
• The ability to adapt to changing priorities and unfamiliar challenges.
• The ability to work in a team environment.
 
WORK ENVIRONMENT
This position operates in an office environment, working at a personal computer where you may sit or stand. Most of our Sioux Falls office workspace consists of an open-concept design intended to promote open communication and collaboration.

GROWTH & DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES
At POET, we encourage internal development and growth by allowing team members to carve their own path to success. Leaders support team members with the necessary resources to develop their skills, achieve goals, and create the most value. We believe in developing our team members to their highest potential and recognizing contributions that add value to the organization. Each new team member’s position and compensation are carefully determined by considering their unique qualifications and skillset.

PERKS
• A multifaceted wellness program encompassing the whole person – mentally, physically, and spiritually
• On-site fitness centers or fitness reimbursements
• Safety and cold-weather gear reimbursements

POET is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to maintaining a workplace free from discrimination and harassment. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, abilities, merit, and other legitimate business factors, without regard to any legally protected characteristic. This policy applies to all aspects of employment, including recruitment, hiring, compensation, benefits, working conditions, promotion, and termination.

jobs.description:
Job Description
Vacancy Status: 
This posting is not for an existing vacancy within the organization and is open to new applications. (New Head Count)

AI Disclosure:
As part of the application process, Artificial Intelligence will be used in the hiring process for this role.

Work Arrangement: 
Hybrid: This role is categorized as hybrid. This means the successful candidate is expected to report to Markham Elevation Centre (MEC) three times per week at minimum, or other frequency dictated by the business.

The Role:
Our Infotainment team is hiring a software engineer to design and develop software in our Android based Infotainment system. You'll be part of a team working on cutting-edge software solutions including the Software-Defined Vehicle solutions on shipping the latest in vehicle experience to our customers.
 
What You'll Do
GM is developing a breakthrough in the new Software Defined Vehicles, you will directly impact the GM vehicles that drive down the road and improve our customer experience! Your work will contribute directly to GM's vision of a world with ZERO Crashes, ZERO Emissions, and ZERO Congestion. 
 
Key Responsibilities:
• Assist in delivering high-quality software solutions for Software Defined Vehicle – Infotainment Applications and Services 
• Design, development and implementation of Infotainment requirements to continuously improve software functions and user experience using embedded software development frameworks in Android, QNX and Linux environments 
• Adhere to best software design principles, utilizing design patterns and understanding abstractions for effective software solutions. 
• Assist with data handling, analysis, and problem-solving tasks that connect software behavior to real-world system or user outcomes.
• Contribute to application logic, automation, and other internal software used to improve developer efficiency, prototyping speed, or user-facing feature exploration.
• Support software testing and debugging by reproducing issues, validating expected behavior, and documenting results clearly for teammates.
• Work with cross-functional engineers to translate mechatronics- or user-experience-oriented ideas into prototypes and implementation plans.
• Participate in team design reviews, technical discussions, and project planning while communicating progress and open issues effectively.
 
Required Qualifications:
 
• Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in Computer Engineering or Computer Science, Electrical engineering, Mechatronics, Software Engineering or equivalent
• Eligible to work full time hours, 40 hours a week for a term of 12 months (consecutive semesters) starting January 2027

Preferred Skills:
• Demonstrated interest in software-oriented work within engineering, including coursework.
• Strong interest in programming roles that sit at the intersection of software, physical systems, and user experience.
• Proven ability to collaborate with teammates, and communicate effectively on technical projects, leadership experience highly desired.
• Comfortable learning new tools and adapting quickly across technical problem spaces.
• Programming: experience preferably in Kotlin, Java, or C/C++, Jetpack compose
• Experience with JIRA, GIT, and Agile software development framework
• Object-oriented software development experience with knowledge in algorithms and data structures
• Experience with technical project work, coordinating group work, and managing timelines and deliverables.
• Experience gathering stakeholder feedback and iterating solutions based on user needs.
• Strong collaboration, public speaking, adaptability, and teamwork skills.
• Knowledge and experience with CAN, LIN, ARXML, or Ethernet communications protocol.
• Formula SAE, Ecocar, or other Automotive related experience/clubs

NOTE- YOU MUST BE ENROLLED IN A CO-OP PROGRAM AND MEET THE PROGRAM’S ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS. ALL STUDENTS MUST ALSO BE LEGALLY ENTITLED TO WORK IN CANADA.

The monthly salary range for this role is $4,264.00 to $4784.00. The actual base salary a successful candidate will be offered within this range will vary based on factors relevant to the position.

Sponsorship: PLEASE ONLY APPLY IF YOU DO NOT NEED SPONSORSHIP TO WORK IN CANADA NOW OR IN THE FUTURE. WE ARE UNABLE TO CONSIDER CANDIDATES WHO REQUIRE SPONSORSHIP

À propos de Pratt & Whitney Canada
Pratt & Whitney Canada (P&WC) est un leader mondial de l’industrie aérospatiale établi à Longueuil, au Québec. Nous fabriquons des moteurs de nouvelle génération qui équipent la plus grande flotte d’avions et d’hélicoptères au monde dans les segments de l’aviation d’affaires, de l’aviation générale et de l’aviation régionale.

En près de 100 ans, nous avons réalisé de nombreuses percées dans le développement de moteurs qui assurent le transport de marchandises et de matériel, luttent contre les feux de forêt et effectuent le transport de passagers.
 
Un employeur de choix
Pratt & Whitney Canada a été reconnue comme l’un des 10 meilleurs employeurs au Canada en 2025 selon Forbes, en plus d’être classée au premier rang des employeurs dans l’industrie de l’aérospatiale et de la défense au pays! Notre siège social figure sur le palmarès des meilleurs employeurs dans la région de Montréal. Ensemble, ces distinctions confirment notre réputation d’employeur de choix dans la région de Montréal, au Canada et dans le monde.
 
Dates du stage : 5 janvier au 23 avril 2027
Emplacement : Le poste s’effectue à notre établissement de Longueuil du lundi au vendredi, selon des horaires flexibles et exclusivement en présentiel.
Consultez notre chaîne YouTube : https://www.youtube.com/@PrattWhitneyCa
Notre site web : Accueil | Pratt & Whitney

La personne sélectionnée travaillera au sein de l’équipe de Marketing et gestion des comptes, Aviation Générale de Pratt & Whitney Canada. Le candidat sera amené à travailler de manière collaborative avec les membres de l’équipe ainsi que d’autres employés de Pratt & Whitney Canada. Le stagiaire Marketing et gestion des comptes, Aviation Générale se rapporte au Directeur, Marketing Aviation Générale.

• Le stagiaire est appelé à supporter et à être responsable des activités suivantes: Développement de contenu marketing.

• Amélioration continue et développement de processus d'affaires et des documents associés.

Qu’est-ce qu’il vous faut pour réussir ?
• Être éligible à travailler au Canada.
• Être inscrit dans une université canadienne pendant toute la durée de votre stage.
• Être en mesure de travailler sur place dans la province où vous êtes embauché, le cas échéant.

• HTML, Python script, JavaScript et concepts généraux de sites web.
• MS. Office Suite (avancé).
• Expérience de SQL afin de créer et d'exécuter des requêtes.
• Adobe Creative Suite, y compris Photoshop.
 
Atouts :
• Sens de l'organisation et capacité à travailler sous pression avec des priorités concurrentes et variables.
• Compétences en matière de gestion de projet.

Travailler chez Pratt & Whitney Canada

Job Title
Intern – Digital Healthtech Product Management – Bothell, WA – Summer 2027
Job Description
Intern – Digital Healthtech Product Management – Bothell, WA – Summer 2027

Are you interested in an internship opportunity with Philips? We welcome individuals who are currently pursuing an undergraduate (BS) and/or graduate (MS) degree to participate in 3-6 month paid intern opportunities at our site in Bothell, WA. Through this role you will gain meaningful, hands-on experience working for a HealthTech company.

Your role:
• Understand customer needs (from ratings and reviews, competitive intelligence, consumer studies and more)

• Help develop value propositions and business cases for products and solutions that delight customers and meet strategic business goals

• Produce and make strong use of analytics to drive decisions and improve products

• Demonstrate some knowledge of the digital innovation landscape

• Write and communicate product briefings using “jobs to be done” methods and collaborate with design/user experience, product research, and software development teams to plan and drive the continuous delivery of best-in-class products that delight users using Agile and iterative development methodologies and tools to ship software

• Be a self-starter with strong critical thinking skills, written and oral communication skills.

You're the right fit if: 
• Pursuing a bachelor’s degree in a related field. Master’s studies a plus.

• Ideally some experience in Product Management and Marketing; preference that some of this experience is with innovative digital apps and ideally, IoT consumer propositions.

• Consumer health experience would be particularly helpful, especially in solutions driving engagement, behavior change, improved health outcomes

• Demonstrated proficiency in business intelligence and analytics tools to gather and articulate data and correlate/forecast outcomes

• Demonstrate a solid tolerance dealing with ambiguous and complex situations and processes

• You must be able to successfully perform the following minimum Physical, Cognitive and Environmental job requirements with or without accommodation for this Office/Remote position.

Philips Transparency Details 
The hourly pay range for this position is $25.00 to $28.00, plus overtime eligible. The actual base pay offered may vary depending on multiple factors including, job-related knowledge/skills, experience, business needs, geographical location, and internal equity. 

In addition, other compensation, such as an annual incentive bonus, sales commission or long-term incentives may be offered. Employees are eligible to participate in our comprehensive Philips Total Rewards benefits program, which includes a generous PTO, 401k (up to 7% match), HSA (with company contribution), stock purchase plan, education reimbursement and much more. Details about our benefits can be found here. 

At Philips, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top end of the range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent upon the facts and circumstances of each case. 

How we work together
We believe that we are better together than apart. For our office-based teams, this means working in-person at least 3 days per week.
Onsite roles require full-time presence in the company’s facilities.
Field roles are most effectively done outside of the company’s main facilities, generally at the customers’ or suppliers’ locations.
Indicate if this role is an office/field/onsite role.
 
About Philips
We are a health technology company. We built our entire company around the belief that every human matters, and we won't stop until everybody everywhere has access to the quality healthcare that we all deserve. Do the work of your life to help the lives of others.
• Learn more about our business.
• Discover our rich and exciting history.
• Learn more about our purpose.

If you’re interested in this role and have many, but not all, of the experiences needed, we encourage you to apply. You may still be the right candidate for this or other opportunities at Philips. Learn more about our culture of impact with care here.

Additional Information
US work authorization is a precondition of employment. The company will not consider candidates who require sponsorship for a work-authorized visa, now or in the future.
Company relocation benefits will not be provided for this position. For this position, you must reside in or within commuting distance to Bothell, WA.

This requisition is expected to stay active for 45 days but may close earlier if a successful candidate is selected or business necessity dictates. Interested candidates are encouraged to apply as soon as possible to ensure consideration.

Philips is an Equal Employment and Opportunity Employer including Disability/Vets and maintains a drug-free workplace.

 This is a research-engineering internship for individuals operating at or near the post-doctoral level. You will shape the architecture of a multi-target joint probabilistic foundation model designed to solve complex real-world problems. The project focuses on building a system capable of temporal forecasting, unordered tabular regression, classification, and missing-data completion while maintaining coherent joint structure across variables and scenarios. We prioritize creating real value in serious use cases over isolated benchmark optimization. 
 What you'll do 
 
 Design and improve core model architecture, including input encoders for temporal and tabular data, attention mechanisms, and distributional output heads. 
 Implement, train, and evaluate PyTorch models within a production-quality codebase. 
 Run controlled architecture studies, such as ablations, scaling behavior, and throughput profiling, to inform design decisions. 
 Build scalable PyTorch implementations that optimize for memory and throughput. 
 Extend the synthetic-data engine with stochastic dynamics, constraints, and dependence structures. 
 Translate research ideas into robust implementations and credible empirical results. 
 
 What you'll need 
 
 Strong PyTorch skills and hands-on experience building and training deep models. 
 A solid understanding of Transformers, attention variants, and sequence architectures. 
 Experience with probabilistic modeling in neural networks, such as distributional output heads or likelihood-based losses. 
 A strong foundation in probability and statistics to reason about densities, dependence between variables, and calibration. 
 Excellent engineering habits, including readable code, tests, and reproducible experiments. 
 The ability to debug training instability and iterate quickly from hypothesis to evidence. 
 Academic or professional background in Computer Science, Mathematics, or Statistics. 
 Working knowledge of stochastic processes or differential equations, experience with synthetic data generators, or familiarity with tabular/mixed-modality deep learning are considered pluses. 
 
 Location & details 
 
 This is a full-time, paid internship. 
 The role is available on-site in Boston, Massachusetts, or San Francisco, California, as well as remotely within the United States. 
 We accept applications on a rolling basis.

Job Description
GM does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. Do not apply for this role if you will need GM immigration sponsorship now or in the future. This includes direct company sponsorship, entry of GM as the immigration employer of record on a government form, and any work authorization requiring a written submission or other immigration support from the company (e.g., H1-B, OPT, STEM OPT, CPT, TN, J-1, etc.) 

This role is located at the GM Global Technical Center in Warren, Michigan.

The Enterprise Data Governance Office is seeking an early careers Data Governance Engineer to help expand data literacy, data stewardship growth, governance enablement, and community engagement across General Motors. This entry-level role combines technical learning with business and process support. The Data Governance Engineer will help make governance concepts, learning resources, onboarding steps, and practical guidance easier to understand, find, and apply across technical and business audiences.

Working under the guidance of experienced data governance and data literacy team members, the Data Governance Engineer will support steward onboarding, community growth, training coordination, communications, learning-path development, documentation, reporting, stakeholder follow-up, and measurement. This is an opportunity to gain practical experience in enterprise data governance, data literacy, data stewardship, change enablement, and cross-functional program execution.

The Role
At General Motors, data literacy helps employees understand, question, and responsibly use data and artificial intelligence to make informed decisions. Data stewardship helps ensure that data has clear ownership, useful metadata, appropriate classification, measurable quality, and accountable support across its lifecycle. The Data Governance &
Data Literacy team supports these outcomes through role-based learning, steward onboarding, data transfer documentation/tracking, hands-on workshops, enterprise events, communications, community meetings, reusable job aids, reporting, and governance enablement.

The Data Governance Engineer will contribute to the operating work that turns these activities into a repeatable capability. The role is well suited for a student who enjoys connecting technology, business needs, and practical processes; communicating with different audiences; organizing work; using metrics to understand participation and adoption; and learning how governed data is used across a large enterprise.

What You’ll Do
• Coordinate data literacy events, workshops, office hours, community meetings, and learning campaigns, including calendars, registrations, materials, attendance, and follow-up.
• Help grow the Data Stewardship community by supporting invitations, agendas, discussion topics, feedback collection, recaps, and approved collaboration channels.
• Support Data Steward onboarding, including required learning, Atlan onboarding steps, approved access tracking, cataloging activities, office-hours participation, and follow-up actions.
• Assist with intake and triage of data governance, data literacy, and data transfer documentation; route policy, privacy, access, data-quality, and tool-specific questions to the appropriate subject-matter expert.
• Research and organize content on data governance, metadata, ownership, inbound and outbound data exchange documentation/tracking, stewardship, data quality, responsible data use and analytics.
• Create and maintain plain-language communications and reusable materials, including FAQs, job aids, onboarding checklists, quick-start guides, presentations,
announcements, learning paths, recordings, and documentation.
• Under supervision, help verify approved metadata such as ownership, descriptions, and classifications.
• Maintain metric definitions, source notes, reporting trackers, and simple dashboard quality checks; prepare status updates, dashboard summaries, community recaps, and presentations.
• Coordinate with data stewards, domain representatives, technical teams,
communications partners, learning partners, and governance subject-matter experts while following GM requirements for data protection, privacy, cybersecurity, access, and responsible use of data and artificial intelligence.
• Perform other related duties as assigned.

Your Skills & Abilities 
• Currently enrolled in an accredited bachelor’s or master’s degree program in Management Information Systems, Information Systems, Business Analytics, Data Analytics, Computer Information Systems, Business Administration, Computer Science, or a related field.
• Basic understanding of how business processes, information systems, and data support organizational decisions.
• Interest in data governance, data literacy, data stewardship, analytics enablement, responsible artificial intelligence, or related areas.
• Ability to organize information, manage details, follow established processes, and complete assignments on time.
• Strong written, verbal, and visual communication skills, including the ability to explain technical or process topics to non-technical audiences.
• Ability to collaborate with multiple stakeholders and work effectively in a team environment.
• Demonstrated curiosity, willingness to learn, and ability to receive and apply feedback.
• Basic proficiency with Microsoft Office or comparable productivity tools, including document, presentation, spreadsheet, and collaboration applications.
• Ability to work at the GM Global Technical Center in Warren, Michigan and
participate in virtual and in-person meetings as required by the team.

What Can Give You a Competitive Advantage 
• Coursework, project work, or internship experience involving data governance, data stewardship, data quality, business process analysis, learning design, communications, community engagement, or program coordination.
• Familiarity with SQL, spreadsheets, data visualization, survey tools, reporting, or dashboard development.
• Exposure to data catalogs, metadata, ownership, classification, data quality, data privacy, data contracts, or lifecycle concepts.
• Exposure to steward onboarding, communities of practice, office hours,
enablement programs, or adoption measurement.
• Exposure to tools such as Atlan, Immuta, Anomalo, Databricks, Power BI,
Confluence, Degreed, Slack, or similar platforms.
• Strong documentation, collaboration, analytical, and communication skills with both technical and business audiences.

Compensation 
The salary range for this role is from $84,900 - $130,500. The actual base salary a successful candidate will be offered within this range will vary based on factors relevant to the position.

Bonus Potential: An incentive pay program offers payouts based on company performance, job level, and individual performance.

What you’ll get from us (Benefits): 
GM offers a variety of health and wellbeing benefit programs. Benefit options include medical, dental, vision, Health Savings Account, Flexible Spending Accounts, retirement savings plan, sickness and accident benefits, life insurance, paid vacation & holidays, tuition assistance programs, employee assistance program, GM vehicle discounts and more. 

About GM
Our vision is a world with Zero Crashes, Zero Emissions and Zero Congestion and we embrace the responsibility to lead the change that will make our world better, safer and more equitable for all.

Why Join Us 
We believe we all must make a choice every day – individually and collectively – to drive meaningful change through our words, our deeds and our culture. Every day, we want every employee to feel they belong to one General Motors team.

Benefits Overview
From day one, we're looking out for your well-being–at work and at home–so you can focus on realizing your ambitions. Learn how GM supports a rewarding career that rewards you personally by visiting Total Rewards resources.

jobs.title: Memory Systems Architecture & AI Intern - Research
jobs.description:
Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all. 
Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.

The DRAM Systems & Architecture Lab researches next-generation memory architectures that enable future AI, machine learning, and high-performance computing systems. The team explores innovative memory technologies, system architectures, and hardware-software co-design approaches to improve performance, scalability, and efficiency for emerging AI workloads.

As a Research Intern in the DRAM Systems & Architecture Lab, you will conduct research focused on next-generation memory systems for AI accelerators. You will investigate tiered memory architectures, analyze AI workload behavior, develop experimental prototypes, and evaluate architectural innovations across hardware, software, and system-level environments. This role offers the opportunity to contribute to research that may influence future product roadmaps, publications, and advanced memory system designs.

Responsibilities
• Research and evaluate tiered memory architectures designed to improve performance and scalability for AI inference and large language model workloads.
• Develop experimental methodologies, models, simulations, and prototypes to analyze memory system performance, data movement, and workload behavior.
• Investigate memory hierarchy optimizations, data placement strategies, cache management, and memory migration mechanisms across AI computing systems.
• Perform quantitative analysis using hardware platforms, simulation environments, and FPGA-based prototypes to evaluate architectural trade-offs.
• Document research findings, present technical results, and collaborate with architecture teams to contribute to future technology strategies and research initiatives.

Minimum Qualifications

• 0-2 years of relevant experience through PhD research, publications, internships, academic projects, or experimental systems research in computer architecture, memory systems, AI accelerators, or high-performance computing.
• Currently pursuing a PhD in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field.
• Strong understanding of computer architecture, memory hierarchy design, and system performance analysis.
• Experience with systems programming using C++, Python, or similar programming languages.
• Familiarity with performance modeling, simulation, profiling, benchmarking, or experimental system evaluation methodologies.
• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and technical communication skills.
• Experience using AI-enabled tools and large language models (LLMs), such as Claude, Copilot, or similar technologies to support research, development, or engineering workflows.
• Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively within a research-focused team environment.

Preferred Qualifications

• Research experience in memory systems, AI accelerators, GPUs, large-scale inference systems, or high-performance computing architectures.
• Experience developing architectural simulators, analytical models, workload characterization frameworks, or system performance evaluation tools.
• Familiarity with AI inference workloads, large language models, KV cache management, Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures, or memory-centric AI system design.
• Experience with FPGA development, RTL design, High-Level Synthesis (HLS), or hardware prototyping platforms.
• Peer-reviewed publications, conference presentations, patents, or other demonstrated research contributions in computer architecture or systems research.
• Experience working across hardware, software, and runtime layers to evaluate end-to-end system performance and optimization opportunities.
• Demonstrated curiosity, initiative, adaptability, and passion for research and emerging technologies.

Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.

The Signal Integrity (SI) Research & Development team enables the electrical performance of Micron's industry-leading memory and storage products, including DRAM, LPDRAM, NAND, HBM, SSDs, and emerging memory technologies. The team works across silicon, package, PCB, and system-level designs to develop high-speed signaling and power delivery solutions that support next-generation computing, AI, networking, automotive, mobile, and data center applications.

As a Signal Integrity Engineer, you will support the design, analysis, and validation of high-speed memory interfaces and power distribution networks across Micron's product portfolio. Working alongside experienced engineers, you will use modeling, simulation, measurements, and AI-enabled workflows to evaluate signal and power integrity performance, support product development, and contribute to future technology and industry standards initiatives.

• Support signal integrity and power integrity analysis for high-speed memory interfaces and power distribution networks through modeling, simulation, measurement, and correlation activities.

Through deep partnerships with customers, GF delivers differentiated, power-efficient and high-performance solutions for high-growth markets. GlobalFoundries is seeking a Reliability Engineering Intern to support the development and qualification of Silicon Photonics technologies involving CMOS devices and photonic components. Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities. 

At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead. 

This is an existing vacancy.

Your Team, Your Impact
The Central Engineering – AMS Signal Integrity (SI) Team is responsible for establishing and maintaining interconnect Signal Integrity (SI) and Power Integrity (PI) design rules for Marvell's AMS IPs. Day-to-day work includes floorplan and bump assignment studies, Redistribution Layer (RDL) design, interposer and package routing analysis, and PCB layout guidelines to ensure optimal system performance. The team collaborates closely with IP design, physical design, and package/PCB teams across the full product lifecycle by ensuring robust SI/PI solutions at every stage to meet the stringent performance demands of AI, cloud, and hyperscaler data center applications.
What You Can Expect
• Develop Python or similar scripting tools to automate SI/PI simulation workflows and improve team efficiency and throughput
• Build and maintain automated trace/via design rule models for floorplan, RDL, bump patterns, interposer, and package routing to ensure SI/PI compliance
• Perform 2D/3D electromagnetic (EM) modeling and simulation using tools such as Ansys 3D Layout or Cadence Sigrity to characterize high-speed interconnects
• Post-process SI/PI simulation results to extract key metrics, generate summary reports, and support design decision-making

What We're Looking For

jobs.title: Operations Analyst Intern
Engineering Intern
jobs.description:
Why Engineering?

Engineering drives the innovation and solutions that power our growth and success, connecting ideas to real-world impact and delivering value at scale. Our Engineers create cutting-edge solutions that make a real difference for millions of customers. Whether it's enhancing mobile apps, leveraging AI and emerging agentic technologies for personalised experiences, or simplifying core systems, our engineers are shaping the future of banking.

We’re not just building tech, we’re building better customer journeys, smarter systems, and a more secure digital future.

Your internship journey

Our Engineering internship is structured differently to all other internships and is designed to give you a real appreciation of what it means to work for us as an Engineer. The programme emphasises agile ways of working and immerses you in a dynamic and collaborative environment in which you’ll get to work in Scrums on real business projects supported by engineering experts.

At the end of the internship, we’ll assess you on what you’ve learned. Complete this successfully and you could be offered a place on our Engineering graduate programme, where you can carry forward the skills you’ve learnt into the next stage of your career.

Over the course of this eight-week programme, you can look forward to:

• Actively participating and contributing to real engineering projects

• Attending daily stand ups in your scrum project teams to drive real business progress as well as participation in end of sprint demos, retros, and feedback sessions

• Developing your engineering skills and application through agile methodologies, AI-assisted engineering practices and NatWest ways of working

• The opportunity to attend regular business and engineering spotlight so you can understand how our engineers contribute to the broader business and our customers

• Learning about how we operate, and how the contribution of Engineering makes a difference across our business technology functions including Retail, Wealth, Commercial & Institutional and Customer & Operations

• Learning how engineers collaborate with AI tools and emerging agentic technologies to solve complex problems while applying human judgement and critical thinking

• Building an understanding of the products and services we provide for our customers and colleagues

• Attending Engineering specific networking events, social engagements and the opportunity to hear from senior leaders across the bank

How you’ll benefit

We’ll reward you with a starting salary of £29,400 pro rata.

Plus, you can expect to:

• Learn from industry experts and immediately apply your learnings

• Enrich your learning with access to our Learning Academy

• Test and learn new approaches in a safe, inclusive environment

• Start building a professional network

• Grow your confidence, build your resilience, and elevate your presence

• Experience first-hand what it’s like working in a purpose-driven organisation

Entry requirements

To be eligible for our Engineering internship, you’ll need:

• To be in your penultimate year of university

• To be on course to achieving a 2:1 in a STEM subject

• Clear communication skills, and the ability to break down complex problems and explain your ideas

• A curious, logical mindset with a passion for solving problems and exploring emerging technologies, including AI

• Confidence working with data, statistics, and experimentation, and evidence-based decision making

• A flexible attitude, comfortable with change and ambiguity and continuous learning in a rapidly evolving technology landscape

• A drive to learn, grow, and make a real impact

Ready to apply?

The application window for this programme will be open until we receive enough applications to fill our cohort. When that happens, we’ll close the programme to new applications. It’s important to take the time to make sure you’re making the right decision about the programme you want to apply for (you can only apply for one programme) but please complete your application as soon as you can to make sure you don’t miss out!

Have another question?

Head over to our ‘Applying and eligibility support’ page now for answers to some of our most commonly asked questions.

jobs.title: Management Development Program Forward Deployed Digital Product Analyst
jobs.description:
Overview:
Serves as a member of the Management Development Program (MDP) and participates in ten weeks of Core Training and one year of On-the-Job training (OJT). Core Training responsibilities include participation in classroom training, observations of departmental presentations, interaction with senior management, peer networking, and working in teams on group project assignments. OJT responsibilities vary by department and are assigned by the department manager. The position may be responsible for additional projects assigned by the department manager or Leadership Development Manager.

Department Description:
The Wilmington Trust Institutional Services (IS) division is experiencing rapid business growth and has initiated a strategic digital transformation program. The goals of the program are to grow revenue through new and transformed digital-first trust and agency service products, to move from a product-centric to client-centric operating model, to move from market-specific to global solutions, and to dramatically lower the cost to serve.
Wilmington Trust is seeking a Forward Deployed Digital Product Analyst to join its Management Development Program and help accelerate digital transformation across core operations. This early-career role is designed for candidates interested in developing digital products, AI products, business transformation, or client-facing technology leaders.
This role is a hybrid between a junior product manager, business analyst, AI-enabled process analyst, and workflow designer. The role focuses on identifying operational problems, defining user needs, documenting requirements, testing solutions, and using agentic AI tools to rapidly analyze, prototype, and improve business workflows.
Ideal candidates are curious, analytical, hands-on, and comfortable working across business and technology teams. They should have exposure to digital product management concepts such as writing user stories or specifications, mapping process flows, creating simple UI designs or wireframes, testing software or workflows, or using AI tools to improve productivity and solution design.
 
Department Responsibilities:
• Help discover, design, test, and launch digital workflow solutions across Wilmington Trust Institutional Services.
• Sit down with business product owners, operations teams, technology partners, and senior product leaders to learn what is not working today and where automation could help.
• Turn what you hear into clear write-ups: user stories (short descriptions of what a user needs), acceptance criteria (the checklist that says when the work is done), process flows, and wireframes (simple screen sketches).
• Use agentic AI tools (AI that can carry out multi-step tasks for you) to analyze processes, draft documentation, generate test cases, and prototype workflows faster.
• Think through big, unclear problems in a structured way: break them into smaller pieces, get to the root cause, weigh the options, and recommend practical next steps.
• Join working sessions where the team maps how a process runs today versus how it should run, and shape early MVP ideas (a first, simple version of a solution).
• Build quick prototypes using enterprise tools, agentic AI tools, low-code or no-code platforms (build with little or no programming), and design collaboration tools.
• Partner with product owners and delivery teams to keep the backlog (the prioritized list of work) clear, current, and tied to business goals.
• Support QA, UAT (user acceptance testing, where real users confirm a solution works), and production checks by writing test scenarios, logging defects, and confirming fixes.
• Help define and track the numbers that show whether a solution is working, such as user adoption, cycle time, exception rates, and business impact.
• Work with technology partners to understand how systems connect and where data, system limits, or operational risks could get in the way.
• Learn and apply agile, lean, design thinking, process engineering, and product management practices on real transformation work.
• Keep up with new agentic AI capabilities, digital product tools, workflow automation practices, and responsible ways to use AI.
• Share what you find, including requirements, risks, test results, and recommendations, in language that business, product, and technology partners can act on.
• Understand and adhere to the Company’s risk and regulatory standards, policies and controls in accordance with the Company’s Risk Appetite. Identify risk-related issues needing escalation to management.
• Promote an environment that supports belonging and reflects the M&T Bank brand.
• Maintain M&T internal control standards, including timely implementation of internal and external audit points together with any issues raised by external regulators as applicable.
• Complete other related duties as assigned.
 
Department Experience Required:
 
This role is built for junior candidates and anyone interested in a Management Development Program, and recent college graduates are encouraged to apply. Experience from internships, co-ops, capstones, campus consulting projects, fintech labs, digital product projects, or AI projects is welcome, but none of it is required to apply.

• A real interest in digital product management, business transformation, financial technology, AI-enabled operations, or workflow automation.
• Some exposure, through coursework, an internship, a class project, or a job, to product work such as writing user stories, documenting requirements, mapping processes, or sketching wireframes.
• Some hands-on time with agentic AI or AI-assisted tools, such as Open Claw, Hermes, Claude Code, or Codex, used to help plan, build, test, analyze, or automate work.
• Comfort taking an open-ended problem apart, working through the information, spotting patterns, and explaining what you’ve found.
• Some exposure to testing software: QA, UAT (having real users confirm a solution works), writing test cases, logging defects, or checking data.
• The ability to explain things clearly in writing and out loud, from requirements and processes flows to feedback, test results, and recommendations.
• A collaborative style that works well with business, products, operations, design, and technology partners.
• Curiosity about how AI, automation, and digital products can improve business processes, client experiences, and day-to-day operations.
• Attention to detail, good organization, strong follow-through, and a willingness to learn quickly in a fast-paced environment.
 
Department Experience Preferred:
 
• An internship, co-op, project, or first job touching financial services, fintech, banking, wealth management, trust services, capital markets, payments, operations, risk, or compliance.
• Exposure to low-code or no-code workflow tools (platforms that let you build with little or no programming) such as Appian, Power Platform, ServiceNow, Salesforce, Pega, Airtable, Retool, or Mendix.
• Coursework or hands-on work in process mapping, workflow or service design, user journey mapping, or operational improvement.
• Any time spent building, configuring, testing, or documenting workflows and screens in Appian Designer - Appian Level 1 certification or similar exposure is a plus, not a must.
• A general sense of what Appian can do, such as process models, interfaces, records, reports, dashboards, case management, AI features, or RPA (software robots that handle repetitive tasks).
• Using AI tools to help with requirements, prototypes, test generation, documentation, code review, workflow design, or data analysis.
• Exposure to product management methods and agile delivery, including sprint planning, backlog management (keeping the work list prioritized), and retrospectives (short team check-ins on what to improve).
• Practice writing user stories and acceptance criteria that are detailed enough for a team to act on.
• Creating wireframes, user flows, journey maps, proc
